\hypertarget{the-second-law-and-entropy-as-theorems-of-the-mcgucken-principle-dx_4dt-ic}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{4. The Second Law and entropy as theorems of
the McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\)}{4. The Second Law and entropy as theorems of the McGucken Principle dx\_4/dt = ic}}\label{the-second-law-and-entropy-as-theorems-of-the-mcgucken-principle-dx_4dt-ic}}

\textbf{In this section we demonstrate that the Second Law of
thermodynamics and entropy itself are derived from the McGucken
Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\), as theorem chains descending from a common,
foundational, physical principle in the spirit of Newton and Euclid.}
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) is the deeper physical foundation of which entropy and
the Second Law are readings --- a different category from any formal or
diagnostic account of thermodynamics (§1, §3.10). The McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) recognizes our foundational, physical reality: the
fourth dimension expands at c, as a spherically symmetric wavefront,
from every event, with a definite orientation --- the + of +ic. This
oriented expansion is the physical origin of the arrow of time: as the
McGucken Sphere expands, the count Ω of distinguishable states it passes
through increases, and the Boltzmann entropy S = k ln Ω increases with
it. The Second Law dS/dt ≥ 0 is therefore a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\),
exact rather than statistical --- the H-theorem of the forward
Fokker--Planck equation whose retarded propagator the +ic orientation
selects, with equality only at the stationary state and strict
positivity dS/dt = 3k\_B/2t on the unbounded slice --- and with no
Poincaré recurrence because x₄ advances and does not retreat; the
entropy so derived is that of the reduced, environment-traced state
(§6.2.1), the full closed state evolving unitarily. Entropy is the
logarithm of the count of x₄-advance states on the Sphere; the area-law
entropy S = k\_B A/(4ℓ\_P²) is that count read over a bounding surface.
Both the Second Law and the area-law entropy are reproduced in full
below from the flagship {[}29{]} (§19.5--19.6) and the physics-of-time
paper {[}30{]}, each a consequence of \(dx_4/dt = ic\), and both are
used again in §5 as the thermodynamic inputs to the McGucken
Geometric-Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations.

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-second-law-dsdt-0-as-a-theorem-of-dx_4dt-ic}{%
\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{4.1 The McGucken Second Law \(dS/dt > 0\)
as a theorem of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\)}{4.1 The McGucken Second Law dS/dt \textgreater{} 0 as a theorem of dx\_4/dt = ic}}\label{the-mcgucken-second-law-dsdt-0-as-a-theorem-of-dx_4dt-ic}}

The McGucken Second Law is derived directly from the +ic-oriented
expansion of the McGucken Sphere, as follows.

\hypertarget{the-compton-coupling-is-derived-not-assumed-matters-tick-rate-from-the-four-velocity-budget}{%
\paragraph{4.1.0 The Compton coupling is derived, not assumed: matter's
tick rate from the four-velocity
budget}\label{the-compton-coupling-is-derived-not-assumed-matters-tick-rate-from-the-four-velocity-budget}}

The Brownian mechanism below rests on the Compton coupling between
matter and the x₄-advance, and that coupling is a theorem of dx₄/dt =
ic, not an added stochastic postulate. It is reproduced here in full
from the thermodynamics paper {[}24{]} (Theorem 4), so that no step of
the Second Law is left resting on an unexplained assumption.

\textbf{The coupling frequency from the four-velocity budget.} By the
master equation u\^{}μu\_μ = −c² (itself the constitutive content of
dx₄/dt = ic: the four-velocity has fixed magnitude c, GR T1 of
{[}23{]}), a massive particle at spatial rest expends its entire
four-velocity budget on the x₄-advance --- u⁴ = c, with no spatial
component. Its rest-frame x₄-phase therefore accumulates at the rate
\[\omega_C = \frac{mc^2}{\hbar} = \frac{E_{\text{rest}}}{\hbar},\] the
Compton angular frequency --- the unique frequency consistent with both
the Principle's rate ic and the rest-energy quantum ℏ per cycle. This
ω\_C is not an additional postulate imposed on top of dx₄/dt = ic: the
x₄-wavefront already carries the frequency mc²/ℏ at the matter tier,
with c supplying the radial expansion rate and ℏ the action quantum, the
two combining through the rest energy mc². The coupling is doubly
derived --- through the Algebraic Channel (the time-translation
generator's eigenvalue is the rest energy mc², by Stone's theorem and
the Wigner classification on the McGucken-Sphere wavefronts) and through
the Geometric Channel (the Klein--Gordon equation as the unique massive
Huygens extension of the wave equation, whose phase accumulates at ω\_C)
{[}24, Theorem 4{]}. Both routes descend from dx₄/dt = ic alone.

\textbf{The isotropy of each step, also derived.} The spatial projection
of the x₄-driven displacement is instantaneously isotropic at each event
because the x₄-expansion is spherically symmetric from every event
(component (ii) of the Principle) --- each Compton tick displaces the
particle in a direction drawn from the uniform (Haar) measure on S²,
with no preferred direction, precisely because the McGucken Sphere
expands isotropically (Theorem 5 of {[}24{]}). The Brownian motion of
the massive particle is therefore the iterated isotropic Compton
displacement (Theorem 6 of {[}24{]}): the random walk is the
\emph{consequence} of the derived Compton coupling and the derived
isotropy, not a free stochastic posit. What the orthodox reading would
call ``an added universal Brownian motion'' is, in the framework, the
spatial shadow of the one x₄-advance ticking at the Compton rate ω\_C
that the four-velocity budget forces.

\hypertarget{bis-the-random-direction-is-forced-by-the-nonlocality-of-the-expanding-xux2084-the-geometric-ontic-origin-of-probability}{%
\paragraph{4.1.0bis The random direction is forced by the nonlocality of
the expanding x₄: the geometric (ontic) origin of
probability}\label{bis-the-random-direction-is-forced-by-the-nonlocality-of-the-expanding-xux2084-the-geometric-ontic-origin-of-probability}}

The random direction of each Compton-tick displacement is not an added
stochastic assumption --- it is forced by the nonlocality of the
expanding fourth dimension, and this nonlocality is the geometric origin
of probability itself. The mechanism is the identity the framework calls
\emph{i-as-nonlocality, c-as-rate} (thermodynamics paper {[}24{]},
Theorem 19.5.3): in dx₄/dt = ic, the rate c is the speed of the advance
and the imaginary unit i is the nonlocality of the advance. The
x₄-expansion carrying i is intrinsically nonlocal --- it proceeds as a
spherically symmetric wavefront from every event, in all directions at
once, with no single local direction (the McGucken Sphere has no
preferred direction, by the spherical symmetry of the expansion). A
massive particle coupled to this expansion (through the Compton coupling
of §4.1.0) is therefore dragged by a process that has no definite local
direction: the direction in which the particle is displaced at each
Compton tick is drawn from the uniform (Haar) measure on S² precisely
because the expansion it is coupled to is nonlocal --- happening
isotropically everywhere on the Sphere --- and cannot single out one
spatial direction. The randomness of the walk is the shadow, on the
local particle, of the nonlocality of the expanding x₄.

This is the physical origin of probability in the framework, and it is
\emph{geometric and ontic}, not epistemic. Orthodox quantum mechanics
reads probability as epistemic ignorance of a definite underlying value;
the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework reads it as the geometric consequence
of coupling to a nonlocal expansion --- the particle's next displacement
is genuinely undetermined in direction because the expansion dragging it
is nonlocal, not because an observer lacks information. The same
nonlocality of the expanding x₄ that drags the massive particle
isotropically (giving the Brownian walk and the Second Law, §4.1) is the
nonlocality that gives the Born probability its measure over directions
at the event (§3.2, the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure): probability over
detection directions and random-walk displacement direction are the one
nonlocality of the expanding x₄ read at the event and along the
trajectory. Because this geometric origin of probability differs from
the orthodox epistemic reading, it carries an empirical signature ---
the residual, temperature-independent diffusion D\_x = ε²c²Ω/2γ² of a
massive particle coupled to the expansion (§6.2.1), which the epistemic
reading predicts to be exactly zero. The nonlocality that is the i of
dx₄/dt = ic is therefore the common physical source of the random walk,
the Second Law, and the Born measure --- probability itself descending
from the nonlocality of the expanding fourth dimension.

\hypertarget{statement-and-proof-of-the-geometric-second-law}{%
\paragraph{4.1.1 Statement and proof of the Geometric Second
Law}\label{statement-and-proof-of-the-geometric-second-law}}

\textbf{Theorem 19.5.1 (Geometric Second Law of Thermodynamics).} Let
the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) hold at every event {[}so that
spacetime is the McGucken manifold \(M_G\) of expanding Spheres{]}.
Consider an ensemble of \(N\) particles at positions
\(\{r_\alpha\}_{\alpha=1}^N\) on the spatial slice \(\Sigma_t\). The
Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy of the ensemble is
\[S(t) \;=\; -k_B \int P(\vec r, t)\, \ln P(\vec r, t)\, d^3 r, \tag{10.5.1.1}\]
where \(P(\vec r, t)\) is the probability density of the reduced state
(the ensemble with its environment traced out, §6.2.1). Then \(S\) is
non-decreasing in \(t\), with equality only at the stationary state of
the diffusion: \[\frac{dS}{dt} \;\ge\; 0 \tag{10.5.1.2}\] \emph{at every
\(t > t_0\), with \(t_0\) the initial time; on the unbounded spatial
slice there is no stationary state and the inequality is strict,
\(dS/dt = 3k_B/2t > 0\). In a bounded region the same forward diffusion
drives \(P\) to its uniform stationary state and \(dS/dt \to 0\) from
above.}

The monotonicity is \emph{exact} (not statistical): it is the H-theorem
of the forward Fokker--Planck equation, whose retarded propagator the
\(+ic\) orientation selects, and there is no Poincaré recurrence:
\(x_4\) advances and does not retreat. \emph{Proof.} We proceed in four
steps.

By \(dx_4/dt = ic\), \(x_4\) advances at rate \(ic\) from every event of
\(M_G\), isotropically across the spatial three-slice (\(dx_4/dt = ic\)
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), component (ii)). A massive particle of rest mass \(m\)
resolves the advance one Compton tick at a time, \(\Delta t_C = h/mc^2\)
(§4.1.0, Definition 2.2.bis.1 of {[}29{]}): at every tick the McGucken
Sphere of expansion at the particle's position has advanced by
\(c\,\Delta t_C = \lambda_C = h/mc\), one Compton wavelength, and the
particle is displaced by \(\lambda_C\) in a direction \(\hat n\) drawn
uniformly from the unit sphere \(S^2\) --- the displacement being
registered at each tick by the environment coupling of the reduced state
(Theorem 26 of {[}24{]}: every inter-molecular collision is a
registration event). (The Planck-time step
\(\delta t_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^5}\), with \(c\,\delta t_P = \ell_P\), is
the resolution of the horizon mode count of Theorem 12 and §A.3; it is
the step of the massless, horizon-level reading, and is kept there.)

The probability density \(P(\vec r, t)\) evolves under iterated
isotropic Compton displacements with rms step size \(\lambda_C\) per
step. By the Einstein 1905 derivation of Brownian motion applied with
step size \(\lambda_C = c\,\Delta t_C\) and step time \(\Delta t_C\),
the diffusion coefficient is
\[D \;=\; \frac{(c\, \Delta t_C)^2}{6\, \Delta t_C} \;=\; \frac{c^2\, \Delta t_C}{6} \;=\; \frac{h}{6m} \;=\; \frac{\pi\hbar}{3m}, \tag{10.5.1.3}\]
of the order of the Schrödinger--Nelson diffusion constant \(\hbar/2m\)
(the coefficient that the McGucken--Wick rotation \(t \to -i\tau\) turns
\(i\hbar\partial_t\psi = -(\hbar^2/2m)\nabla^2\psi\) into): the
Compton-tick walk and the Wick-rotated Schrödinger equation give the
same diffusion scale, the two differing by the factor \(2\pi/3\) of the
isotropic-step convention. This is a consistency check between the
Geometric Channel (the walk) and the Algebraic Channel (the Schrödinger
equation) of \(dx_4/dt = ic\). The Planck-step value \(c^2\delta t_P/6\)
is mass-independent and belongs to the horizon count, not to the
massive-particle walk, and the probability density satisfies
\[\frac{\partial P}{\partial t} \;=\; D\, \nabla^2 P. \tag{10.5.1.4}\]
This is the isotropic-diffusion equation, derived from the McGucken
Sphere expansion at each Compton tick.

The fundamental solution of (10.5.1.4) with delta-function initial data
\(P(\vec r, 0) = \delta^3(\vec r)\) is the Gaussian
\[P(\vec r, t) \;=\; (4\pi D t)^{-3/2}\, \exp\!\left(-\frac{r^2}{4 D t}\right). \tag{10.5.1.5}\]
Substituting into (10.5.1.1) and evaluating the Gaussian-entropy
integral (standard computation):
\[S(t) \;=\; \tfrac{3}{2} k_B\, \ln(4\pi e\, D t) \;+\; \text{const.} \tag{10.5.1.6}\]

Differentiate (10.5.1.6) with respect to \(t\):
\[\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; \frac{3 k_B}{2 t} \;>\; 0 \tag{10.5.1.7}\] for all
\(t > 0\), since \(k_B > 0\) and \(t > 0\).

The sign of the inequality follows from the \emph{\(+ic\) orientation}
of the principle: \(x_4\) advances at \(+ic\), not \(-ic\), so the
diffusion equation (10.5.1.4) propagates probability forward in \(t\)
with the retarded (forward) propagator and no time-reversed branch ---
the H-theorem of the forward diffusion equation, which for any \(P\)
with decaying or no-flux boundary data reads
\[\frac{dS}{dt} = -k_B\int (1+\ln P)\,D\nabla^2 P\,d^3r = k_B D\int \frac{|\nabla P|^2}{P}\,d^3r \;\ge\; 0,\]
with equality only at the stationary state, which for the unbounded
slice is never reached. The rate \(3k_B/2t\) of (10.5.1.7) is the
point-source value; for Gaussian initial data of width \(\sigma_0\) per
axis, \(\sigma^2(t) = \sigma_0^2 + 2Dt\) and
\(dS/dt = 3k_B D/(\sigma_0^2 + 2Dt) > 0\). Two further conditions enter
the step from the per-tick displacement to (10.5.1.4): the successive
directions \(\hat n\) are independent, which isotropy alone does not
supply (a single direction drawn once and kept is isotropic in
distribution and gives ballistic motion) and which is supplied by the
registration at each tick --- every tick is a fresh collision with the
environment (Theorem 26 of {[}24{]}); and the finite-step walk has a
transition kernel supported within one step, so (10.5.1.4) is its
diffusion (scaling) limit on scales large against \(\lambda_C\) and
\(\Delta t_C\), where the Gaussian's tails stand for many steps. In a
bounded region the same forward propagation drives \(P\) monotonically
to the uniform stationary state, \(dS/dt \to 0^+\), and the relative
entropy of \(P\) to that state decreases monotonically. The textbook
statistical Second Law (a tendency with Poincaré recurrence) reduces to
the McGucken geometric Second Law (a monotonicity without recurrence)
when the \(+ic\)-oriented physical motion underlying \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is
recognised. The \(N\)-particle ensemble whose entropy is (10.5.1.1) is
the reduced state: its full closed state evolves unitarily (§6.2.1), and
the per-tick isotropic displacement is the Lindblad generator of the
environment trace computed there. \(\square\)

\hypertarget{geometric-reading-of-the-geometric-second-law}{%
\paragraph{4.1.2 Geometric reading of the Geometric Second
Law}\label{geometric-reading-of-the-geometric-second-law}}

The Geometric Second Law is \emph{not} the statistical Second Law of
Boltzmann (a tendency with non-zero probability of fluctuations); it is
a theorem about the certain monotonic advance of \(x_4\) and the entropy
it generates. There is no Poincaré recurrence because \(x_4\) does not
recur.

Theorem 19.5.1 is the Geometric Second Law in its general H-theorem form
(used directly in §19.8 in the Jacobson chain). Theorem 19.5.3 below,
importing Proposition 4.5.4 of {[}2, §4.5{]}, is its point-source
specialization for massive-particle ensembles, with the explicit rate
\(dS/dt = (3/2) k_B / t\).

\hypertarget{particle-level-companion-optional-for-the-headline-chapter}{%
\paragraph{4.1.3 Particle-level companion (optional, for the headline
chapter)}\label{particle-level-companion-optional-for-the-headline-chapter}}

\textbf{Theorem 19.5.3 (Strict Second Law for massive-particle
ensembles).} For an ensemble of massive particles undergoing the
Compton-coupling Wiener process generated by the iterated McGucken
Sphere flow on the spatial slice,
\[\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; \frac{3 k_B}{2 t} \tag{10.5.3.1}\] \emph{strictly,
for all \(t > 0\).}

\emph{Proof.} Established at Proposition 4.5.4 of {[}2, §4.5{]}, and
reproduced in mechanism here: the result descends from \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
through the McGucken Sphere. The proof uses Propositions 4.5.1 (Compton
coupling between matter and \(x_4\) at angular frequency
\(\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar\) --- the rate at which a massive particle's
McGucken Sphere ticks), 4.5.2 (spatial-projection isotropy by the
spherical symmetry of the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) expansion --- each Compton
tick displaces the particle isotropically on the spatial slice because
the Sphere expands isotropically), 4.5.3 (Brownian motion as iterated
isotropic Compton displacement, via the central limit theorem applied to
the iid sphere-uniform increments the expanding Sphere generates), and
direct Gaussian-entropy evaluation of \(S = -k_B \int P \ln P \, d^3 r\)
on the resulting Wiener-process density. \emph{LTD reading:} the strict
positivity \(dS/dt = 3k_B/2t > 0\) is the \(+ic\) orientation of the
Sphere's expansion made quantitative --- each Compton tick adds
isotropic spatial spread that can only grow the Gaussian's width, so the
state-count \(\Omega\) (§6) can only increase, never decrease; the
massive-particle Second Law is the Compton-tick expansion of the
McGucken Sphere read on the spatial slice. \(\square\)

The particle-level derivation refines the horizon-level Theorem 19.5.1
with a sharper quantitative content: the specific rate
\(dS/dt = (3/2) k_B / t\).

\hypertarget{entropy-as-the-mcgucken-area-law-s-k_b-a4ell_p2-a-theorem-of-dx_4dt-ic}{%
\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{4.2 Entropy as the McGucken Area Law
\(S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)\), a theorem of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\)}{4.2 Entropy as the McGucken Area Law S = k\_B A/(4\textbackslash ell\_P\^{}2), a theorem of dx\_4/dt = ic}}\label{entropy-as-the-mcgucken-area-law-s-k_b-a4ell_p2-a-theorem-of-dx_4dt-ic}}

\hypertarget{the-area-law-from-x_4-mode-counting-on-mcgucken-spheres}{%
\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{4.2.1 The area law from \(x_4\)-mode counting
on McGucken
Spheres}{4.2.1 The area law from x\_4-mode counting on McGucken Spheres}}\label{the-area-law-from-x_4-mode-counting-on-mcgucken-spheres}}

\textbf{Theorem 19.6.1 (Area law for entropy on McGucken Spheres).} Let
the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) hold at every event {[}so that
spacetime is the McGucken manifold \(M_G\) of expanding Spheres{]}.
{[}The Planck length \(\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3} = \hbar/(m_P c)\) is
the Sphere's wavelength at the horizon tier: the reduced Compton
wavelength of the Planck mass \(m_P = \sqrt{\hbar c/G}\), the one
wavelength that sets the action \(h\) evaluated at the mass for which
the Compton wavelength equals the gravitational radius. It is read off
the Principle, not identified separately.{]} Then the entropy associated
with a McGucken Sphere of area \(A\) is
\[S \;=\; \frac{k_B A}{4 \ell_P^2} \;=\; \frac{k_B A c^3}{4 \hbar G}. \tag{10.6.1.1}\]

\emph{Proof.} The McGucken Sphere associated with a spacetime event
\(O\) is the 2-sphere swept out by \(x_4\)'s spherically symmetric
expansion at radius \(R = ct\) from \(O\) (Definition 2 of the
Introduction). Its area is \(A = 4\pi R^2 = 4\pi c^2 t^2\).

Quantise \(x_4\)'s expansion at the Planck scale: the fundamental
wavelength of \(x_4\)-advance is \(\ell_P\). The number of independent
quantum modes of \(x_4\)-advance crossing the McGucken Sphere is one
mode per Planck-area cell. By the standard mode-counting argument
{[}Bekenstein 1973, Hawking 1975, 't Hooft 1993 (the holographic
principle), Susskind 1995{]},
\[N_{\text{bits}} \;=\; \frac{A}{\ell_P^2} \tag{10.6.1.2}\] up to a
numerical factor of order unity. Identifying entropy with \(k_B\) times
the number of bits, and fixing the numerical factor by demanding
consistency with the Bekenstein-Hawking expression in the limiting case
of a black hole horizon {[}Bekenstein 1973, Hawking 1975{]}:
\[S \;=\; \frac{k_B A}{4 \ell_P^2} \;=\; \frac{k_B A c^3}{4 \hbar G}.\]
The factor \(1/4\) is fixed by the Bekenstein-Hawking matching {[}in the
present paper: fixed in the Geometric Channel by Newtonian matching of
the Clausius relation to the field equations, and computed in the
Algebraic Channel from the derived Einstein--Hilbert action, Theorem
12{]}; the geometric fact \(S \propto A\) (rather than \(S \propto V\))
is forced by the \(x_4\)-mode counting on the McGucken Sphere.
\(\square\)

\hypertarget{geometric-reading-the-area-law-is-mcgucken-sphere-entropy}{%
\paragraph{4.2.2 Geometric reading: the area law is McGucken-Sphere
entropy}\label{geometric-reading-the-area-law-is-mcgucken-sphere-entropy}}

The area law (T10.6.1) is \emph{not} an imported result from black hole
thermodynamics; rather, the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of a black hole
horizon is the \emph{special case} of the McGucken-Sphere entropy when
the McGucken Sphere coincides with the black hole horizon. The priority
statement: \(S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)\) is the entropy of
\(x_4\)-advance modes on any McGucken Sphere, with the black hole
horizon being a particular kind of McGucken Sphere (the apparent horizon
of a Schwarzschild-trapped region; see {[}55, Chapter 22{]}-24).

\hypertarget{the-einstein-field-equations-as-a-theorem-of-the-mcgucken-principle-dx_4dt-ic-two-independent-theorem-chains-along-the-algebraic-and-geometric-channels}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{5. The Einstein field equations as a theorem
of the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\): two independent
theorem-chains along the Algebraic and Geometric
channels}{5. The Einstein field equations as a theorem of the McGucken Principle dx\_4/dt = ic: two independent theorem-chains along the Algebraic and Geometric channels}}\label{the-einstein-field-equations-as-a-theorem-of-the-mcgucken-principle-dx_4dt-ic-two-independent-theorem-chains-along-the-algebraic-and-geometric-channels}}

\textbf{In this section we demonstrate that gravity --- the Einstein
field equations --- is derived from the McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), as theorem chains descending from a common,
foundational, physical principle in the spirit of Newton and Euclid.}
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) is the deeper physical foundation of which gravity is a
reading --- a different category from any formal or diagnostic account
of general relativity (§1, §3.10). The McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) generates at every event the expanding McGucken Sphere.
The Einstein field equations G\_μν + Λg\_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T\_μν are a
theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\), derived along two derivationally disjoint
channels of the McGucken Duality that converge on the same equation
{[}23{]}: the Algebraic Channel (the algebraic-symmetry reading) and the
Geometric Channel (the geometric-propagation reading). This section
reproduces both channels in full from the McGucken general-relativity
paper {[}23{]}. The Einstein field equations are one theorem in a larger
accomplishment: the whole of general relativity is derived and
overdetermined the same way. The McGucken general-relativity paper
{[}23{]} derives all of general relativity as a twenty-four-theorem
chain (GR T1--T24), each theorem descending from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) along
two independent theorem-chains --- the Algebraic Channel (the
algebraic-symmetry reading) and the Geometric Channel (the
geometric-propagation reading). The chain is:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  GR T1 --- the master equation u\^{}μ u\_μ = −c²
\item
  GR T3 --- the weak equivalence principle
\item
  GR T4 --- the Einstein equivalence principle
\item
  GR T5 --- the strong equivalence principle
\item
  GR T6 --- the massless-lightspeed equivalence
\item
  GR T7 --- the geodesic equation
\item
  GR T8 --- the Christoffel connection
\item
  GR T9 --- the Riemann curvature tensor
\item
  GR T10 --- the Ricci tensor, Bianchi identities, and ∇\_μ G\^{}\{μν\}
  = 0
\item
  GR T11 --- the Einstein field equations
\item
  GR T12 --- the Schwarzschild solution
\item
  GR T13 --- gravitational time dilation
\item
  GR T14 --- gravitational redshift
\item
  GR T15 --- perihelion precession
\item
  GR T16 --- light bending
\item
  GR T17 --- gravitational waves
\item
  GR T18 --- FRW cosmology
\item
  GR T19 --- the no-graviton theorem
\item
  GR T20 --- the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy S = A/4ℓ\_P²
\item
  GR T21 --- the Hawking temperature
\item
  GR T22 --- the information-paradox resolution
\item
  GR T23 --- the Penrose process
\item
  GR T24 --- the Strominger--Vafa entropy count Each is derived twice,
  by derivationally disjoint routes sharing no machinery beyond
  \(dx_4/dt = ic\) --- the same convergent-overdetermination signature
  that the whole of quantum mechanics exhibits (§3, {[}38{]}). General
  relativity and quantum mechanics are therefore both complete
  theorem-chains of the one principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\), each derived and
  overdetermined along its Algebraic and Geometric channels, with no
  reconciliation required.
\end{itemize}

The Geometric Channel is the thermodynamic route to gravity: it derives
the Einstein field equations as the equation of state of the McGucken
Sphere's horizon thermodynamics, through the Geometric Second Law, the
area-law entropy, the Unruh temperature, and the Clausius relation δQ =
TδS. The decisive point --- and the difference from Jacobson's 1995
derivation {[}1{]} --- is that none of this thermodynamics is assumed.
Jacobson is explicit that his thermodynamic inputs are assumptions: he
assumes ``the entropy is proportional to horizon area,'' notes that the
proportionality constant η ``is undetermined by anything we have said so
far,'' and takes the temperature to be the Unruh temperature of the
vacuum fluctuations. In Jacobson's derivation the Second Law, the
area-law entropy, and the Unruh temperature are therefore postulated
inputs, whereas here each is itself a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) (the
Second Law and area-law entropy are derived from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) in §4;
the Unruh temperature is derived from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) in §5.4 below,
Theorem 13). The Algebraic Channel, by contrast, derives the same
Einstein field equations from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) with no thermodynamics at
all --- through symmetry and variational machinery only. Gravity is
therefore not derivable only thermodynamically: the Geometric Channel is
the thermodynamic route, the Algebraic Channel is the non-thermodynamic
route, and their convergence on G\_μν + Λg\_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T\_μν through
disjoint machinery is the overdetermined-proof structure of the McGucken
Duality. That gravity, the Second Law, entropy, and temperature are all
theorems of the same principle is precisely why gravity carries a
thermodynamic reading at all, and why ``gravity is entropy'' is a
natural statement (§1): both are \(dx_4/dt = ic\) seen from different
sides.

\hypertarget{why-the-mcgucken-principle-dx_4dt-ic-is-more-foundational-than-jacobsons-thermodynamic-derivation}{%
\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{5.1 Why the McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) is more foundational than Jacobson's thermodynamic
derivation}{5.1 Why the McGucken Principle dx\_4/dt = ic is more foundational than Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation}}\label{why-the-mcgucken-principle-dx_4dt-ic-is-more-foundational-than-jacobsons-thermodynamic-derivation}}

Jacobson's 1995 derivation of the Einstein field equations from δQ = TδS
{[}1{]} is the direct ancestor of the Geometric Channel below, and the
precise sense in which \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is more foundational than that
derivation can be stated exactly, because ``more foundational'' means
``assumes less and derives more.'' Jacobson's construction assumes a
definite list of inputs; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) derives each of them. Seven
contrasts, each anchored to Jacobson's own text, make this precise.

\textbf{1. Jacobson assumes the thermodynamics; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) derives
it.} Jacobson's derivation takes three thermodynamic facts as inputs:
entropy proportional to horizon area, the Unruh temperature T = ℏκ/2π,
and the Clausius relation δQ = TδS. He states their assumed status
plainly --- ``we shall thus assume for most of this letter that the
entropy is proportional to horizon area,'' and the proportionality
constant η ``is undetermined by anything we have said so far'' {[}1{]}.
In the McGucken \(dx_4/dt = ic\) framework these are not inputs but
theorems: the Second Law and the area-law entropy are derived from
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) in §4, and the Unruh temperature is derived from
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) in §5.4 (Theorem 13). Jacobson explains gravity given
thermodynamics; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) explains gravity and the thermodynamics
from one prior fact. Fewer postulates, more output --- the operational
meaning of ``more foundational.''

\textbf{2. Jacobson assumes the null Rindler horizon; \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
generates it.} Jacobson's horizons are pre-existing features of a
spacetime taken as already given: he invokes the equivalence principle
to ``view a small neighborhood of each spacetime point p as a piece of
flat spacetime'' {[}1{]} and then constructs local Rindler horizons on
that assumed background. \(dx_4/dt = ic\) generates the spacetime and
its null structure rather than presupposing them: the McGucken Sphere
expanding at c from every event is the null surface, and the Lorentzian
metric on which the horizon lives is itself a theorem of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) (from (ict)² = −c²t², §2). Jacobson needs a spacetime
in which to place horizons; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) produces the spacetime. His
construction therefore begins one derivational level downstream of the
Principle.

\textbf{3. Jacobson assumes the Unruh effect, which presupposes quantum
field theory, the imaginary unit i, and ℏ; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) supplies
these.} Jacobson's temperature is the Unruh temperature of the quantum
vacuum: ``the Minkowski vacuum state of quantum fields \ldots{} is a
thermal state with respect to the boost hamiltonian at temperature T =
ℏκ/2π'' {[}1{]}. This already presupposes the entire apparatus of
quantum field theory --- the imaginary unit i of the quantum phase, the
KMS thermal structure, and the quantum of action ℏ. \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is
the source of exactly these ingredients: the i is the perpendicularity
of the fourth axis x₄ = ict (§2, §3), and ℏ is the action accumulated
per Compton tick of the McGucken Sphere (§2, §4). The very quantities
Jacobson's temperature depends upon are themselves theorems of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), and the whole of the quantum mechanics his
construction borrows is derived from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) along two channels
(§3, twenty-three results, forty-six derivations {[}38{]}). Jacobson
stands on quantum mechanics; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) derives quantum mechanics.

\textbf{4. Jacobson leaves the cutoff length unexplained;
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) sets it.} Jacobson requires a fundamental cutoff length
l\_c for the entanglement entropy to be finite and area-proportional,
and finds only afterwards, from consistency, that ``l\_c must be of
order the Planck length'' {[}1{]} --- he cannot say why the cutoff takes
that value, remarking that ``given a microscopic theory of spacetime
structure one may someday be able to compute η.'' \(dx_4/dt = ic\) fixes
the resolution scale intrinsically: the x₄-advance proceeds one Compton
tick at a time, one quantum of action h per tick (§2, Definition
2.2.bis.1 of {[}29{]}), and the horizon is tiled by Planck-area cells
set by that quantization (§4.2). The scale Jacobson must assume is
derived, and the ``microscopic theory of spacetime structure'' he defers
to is \(dx_4/dt = ic\).

\textbf{5. Jacobson gives one derivation; \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
overdetermines gravity along two independent channels.} Jacobson
provides a single thermodynamic route to the Einstein field equations.
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) derives the same equations along two derivationally
disjoint channels --- the Geometric Channel (thermodynamic, the
Jacobson-type route, §5.3) and the Algebraic Channel
(foliation-preserving Diff\_McG → Noether's second theorem → Lovelock
uniqueness, with no thermodynamics at all, §5.2). A principle that
reaches the same law by two disjoint routes sharing no intermediate
machinery is more foundational than one that reaches it by a single
route: the convergence is evidence that the principle sits beneath the
law rather than beside it, the convergent-overdetermination signature
that recurs across all of general relativity (§5, GR T1--T24 {[}23{]})
and all of quantum mechanics (§3, QM T1--T23 {[}38{]}).

\textbf{6. Jacobson explains only gravity; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) explains
gravity, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and their interconnections.}
Jacobson's result is confined to gravity as an equation of state.
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) derives general relativity as a twenty-four-theorem
chain (§5, {[}23{]}), quantum mechanics as a twenty-three-theorem chain
(§3, {[}38{]}), and thermodynamics as its own theorem chain (§4,
{[}24{]}), and it explains why these theories connect to one another ---
why ``gravity is entropy,'' ``the Born rule is entropy,'' and finally
``gravity is the Born rule'' (§6). A principle that unifies the separate
theories and accounts for the equivalences the literature finds among
them is more foundational than one that reinterprets a single theory.

\textbf{7. Jacobson points beyond his own construction, and
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) is what he points toward.} Jacobson closes by proposing
that the Einstein equation should not be quantized, being an equation of
state like the wave equation for sound in air, and that there is a
deeper microphysics --- a ``non-equilibrium spacetime'' and an ``unknown
microscopic theory of spacetime structure'' --- that his thermodynamic
derivation does not supply {[}1{]}. \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is exactly that
missing microphysics: the physical substrate --- the fourth dimension
expanding at c, the McGucken Sphere at every event --- whose
state-counting statistics are the thermodynamics Jacobson assumed.
Jacobson's derivation has, in its own concluding words, a gap shaped
like a foundational principle; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) fills it.

\textbf{The structure of the advance.} Jacobson inverted the logic of
general relativity once: where classical relativity runs curvature →
thermodynamics (the horizon area of a solution turns out to behave like
entropy), Jacobson ran thermodynamics → curvature (imposing δQ = TδS on
all local horizons forces the field equations). But he stopped at
thermodynamics as bedrock, assuming the entropy, the temperature, the
horizon, and the cutoff. \(dx_4/dt = ic\) performs the second inversion:
one geometric principle → both thermodynamics and curvature. It derives
the entropy, the temperature, the horizon, and the cutoff that Jacobson
assumed, and names the substrate whose statistics they are. That the
same second inversion also yields quantum mechanics and the Born rule
--- so that gravity and the Born rule emerge as one entropy of the one
McGucken Sphere (§6) --- is why \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is foundational rather
than merely one derivational level deeper: it is the layer of which
Jacobson's thermodynamics is a reading.

\hypertarget{why-the-mcgucken-principle-dx_4dt-ic-is-more-foundational-than-verlindes-entropic-gravity-derivation}{%
\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{5.2 Why the McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) is more foundational than Verlinde's entropic-gravity
derivation}{5.2 Why the McGucken Principle dx\_4/dt = ic is more foundational than Verlinde's entropic-gravity derivation}}\label{why-the-mcgucken-principle-dx_4dt-ic-is-more-foundational-than-verlindes-entropic-gravity-derivation}}

Verlinde's 2011 derivation of Newton's law and the Einstein equations as
an entropic force {[}2{]} stands in the same relation to
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) as Jacobson's, and one identification is worth stating
exactly because it is sharp. Verlinde's foundational postulate --- the
assumption from which, in his words, ``everything else follows'' --- is
that the entropy of the holographic screen changes by one fixed quantum
for a displacement of one Compton wavelength: ΔS = 2πk\_B when Δx = ℏ/mc
{[}2{]}. This postulated Compton-wavelength entropy step is precisely
the McGucken Compton tick. In the McGucken \(dx_4/dt = ic\) framework
the x₄-advance proceeds one Compton wavelength at a time, λ\_C = ℏ/mc,
one quantum of action h per tick (§2, Definition 2.2.bis.1 of {[}29{]}),
and the entropy increment per tick is the state-count increment of the
expanding Sphere (§4). What Verlinde must postulate --- the
Compton-wavelength quantum of entropy --- the framework derives as the
Compton tick of \(dx_4/dt = ic\). Verlinde is moreover explicit that he
cannot explain the quantum of action his derivation contains: ℏ, he
writes, ``just serves as an auxiliary variable that is needed for
dimensional reasons'' and ``can therefore be chosen at will'' {[}2{]}.
In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework ℏ is not auxiliary but the action
accumulated per Compton tick of the Sphere (§2). Verlinde further
assumes, as postulated inputs, the holographic screens, the
equipartition of energy over area-proportional bits N = Ac³/Gℏ, and the
Unruh temperature --- each of which is a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
(§4, §5.3). Verlinde's entropy is S = k\_B log Ω {[}2{]}, the same
Boltzmann state-count S = k ln Ω on which the identity of §7 is built;
his Ω, the configuration-space volume read on a screen, and the
framework's Ω, the count of distinguishable states of the expanding
McGucken Sphere, are the same quantity read on the same kind of surface.
Verlinde, like Jacobson, provides one route and assumes the
thermodynamics; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) derives the thermodynamics --- the
Compton-wavelength entropy step, the quantum of action, the screens, the
equipartition, and the temperature --- and derives gravity along a
second, non-thermodynamic channel besides (§5.2).
