\hypertarget{derived-expansion-versus-primitive-expansion-what-jacobson-hawking-and-verlinde-invoke-and-where-their-expansion-comes-from}{%
\paragraph{5.2.1 Derived expansion versus primitive expansion: what
Jacobson, Hawking, and Verlinde invoke, and where their expansion comes
from}\label{derived-expansion-versus-primitive-expansion-what-jacobson-hawking-and-verlinde-invoke-and-where-their-expansion-comes-from}}

Each of the entropic- and thermodynamic-gravity programs invokes an
\emph{expansion}, but in every case it is a \emph{derived} expansion
that requires an external cause; \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is the
\emph{primitive} expansion from which the others' derived expansions
descend. This is the deepest sense in which the framework is more
foundational, and it can be stated exactly from each author's own
construction.

\textbf{Jacobson and Hawking: the expansion θ of the horizon congruence,
caused by matter.} Jacobson's derivation turns on the expansion θ of the
null geodesic congruence generating the local Rindler horizon, governed
by the Raychaudhuri equation dθ/dλ = −½θ² − σ² − R\_ab k\^{}a k\^{}b,
and the horizon-area variation is δ𝒜 = ∫\_H θ dλ d𝒜 {[}1{]}. This θ is
the horizon's expansion, but it is not primitive: it is \emph{sourced by
matter energy focusing the geodesics} through the Ricci term R\_ab
k\^{}a k\^{}b, which is exactly the term the Einstein equation being
derived converts into T\_ab k\^{}a k\^{}b. Jacobson's expansion is a
derived kinematic quantity of a pre-existing null congruence in a
pre-existing spacetime, caused by the stress-energy. Hawking's area
theorem is the same object read globally: horizon area never decreases
because the generators' expansion θ obeys the same focusing equation
under the null energy condition --- again the horizon's expansion is the
response of the geometry to its matter content, not a foundational fact.
In both, the expansion is an effect whose cause is matter and curvature.

\textbf{Verlinde: the emergent holographic direction, caused by
coarse-graining.} Verlinde posits ``one special direction corresponding
to scale or a coarse graining variable of the microscopic theory\ldots{}
the direction in which space is emergent'' {[}2{]}, with space itself
emerging outward from the holographic screens as the coarse-graining
proceeds. This emergent outward direction is Verlinde's counterpart of
an expansion, but it too is derived: its cause is the
renormalization-group / coarse-graining flow of an underlying theory,
and Verlinde is explicit that the microscopic origin is unknown --- his
construction rests on ``some unknown microscopic theory'' whose
statistics produce the screens and their thermodynamics. His expansion
is an emergent, statistical scale-direction, not a physical expansion at
c, and it points beyond itself to a microphysics he does not supply.

\textbf{\(dx_4/dt = ic\): the primitive expansion, at c, from every
event.} The McGucken Principle does not derive its expansion from
matter, curvature, or coarse-graining. The expansion \emph{is} the
primitive: the fourth dimension advances at the rate c from every
spacetime point, \(dx_4/dt = ic\), and the horizon, the null structure,
the area law, the Unruh and Hawking temperatures, and the entropy all
descend from it (§4, §5, Theorems 11--14). This inverts the order of the
other programs at the decisive point. Where Jacobson's horizon-expansion
θ is \emph{caused} by matter through R\_ab k\^{}a k\^{}b, the McGucken
x₄-expansion is the \emph{cause} from which the Einstein equation ---
and hence the focusing of θ by matter --- is derived (Theorem 14): the
same Raychaudhuri focusing Jacobson feeds with matter is, in the
framework, a consequence of the primitive x₄-advance generating the null
congruence in the first place. Where Verlinde's emergent direction
requires ``some unknown microscopic theory,'' \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is
exactly that missing microphysics --- the physical substrate whose
expansion is the coarse-graining direction Verlinde had to posit.
Jacobson and Verlinde each point explicitly to a deeper layer they do
not provide --- Jacobson to an ``unknown microscopic theory of spacetime
structure,'' Verlinde to an ``unknown microscopic theory'' --- and the
primitive expansion \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is that layer: the expansion the
others find, derived, in the phenomena, stated instead as the
foundational fact from which the phenomena follow. They discover
expansion in the horizon and in emergent space and must ask what causes
it; the McGucken Principle answers that the expansion of the fourth
dimension at c is the cause, and derives the rest.

\hypertarget{why-gravity-and-thermodynamics-are-naturally-related-the-shared-geometric-channel-and-the-channel-asymmetry-between-them}{%
\paragraph{5.2.2 Why gravity and thermodynamics are naturally related:
the shared Geometric Channel, and the channel asymmetry between
them}\label{why-gravity-and-thermodynamics-are-naturally-related-the-shared-geometric-channel-and-the-channel-asymmetry-between-them}}

The observations of §5.2.1 have a consequence that explains, at the
deepest level, why gravity and thermodynamics are related --- and why
the relation is not symmetric. Gravity descends from \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
along \emph{both} channels: the Algebraic Channel (foliation-preserving
Diff\_McG → Noether's second theorem → Lovelock uniqueness, with no
thermodynamics at all, §5.3, Corollary 9.2) and the Geometric Channel
(the thermodynamic route through the Second Law, area law, Unruh
temperature, and Clausius relation, §5.4). The arrow of time --- the
Second Law dS/dt \textgreater{} 0 and the monotone growth of entropy ---
descends from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) along \emph{only} the Geometric Channel
(the time-symmetric relations of thermodynamics, the Onsager reciprocal
relations of §6.2.5 and the conservation form of the Generalized Second
Law of §6.2.6, have Algebraic-Channel readings as well): the strict
Second Law is supplied by the Geometric Channel {[}45{]}, and it cannot
arise in the Algebraic Channel, because the Algebraic Channel is the
channel of what is \emph{preserved} --- symmetry-rich,
Lorentzian-locked, time-symmetric, reversible --- while the arrow of
time and the monotone dS/dt \textgreater{} 0 are the channel of what
\emph{flows} {[}45{]}. A reversible, symmetry-rich description cannot
produce a monotone increase; the Second Law is intrinsically
Geometric-Channel content.

This asymmetry is the reason gravity and thermodynamics are naturally
related. Both descend from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) independently of one
another, and they \emph{share the Geometric Channel} --- the
arrow-carrying, expanding-Sphere channel. Their overlap in that one
channel is where gravity and thermodynamics coincide, and it is why the
literature keeps finding ``gravity is entropy'': Jacobson, Verlinde, and
Padmanabhan are all working in the Geometric Channel, where the
gravitational and thermodynamic derivations run through the same
expanding-Sphere, arrow-carrying structure. They found the overlap
without recognizing it as a channel overlap. It is also why each of
their derivations needs the Second Law (§5.2.1): the thermodynamic route
to gravity is the Geometric-Channel route, and the Second Law is the
Geometric Channel's defining content.

The channel asymmetry also states precisely what is right and what is
incomplete in ``gravity is entropy.'' It is right in the Geometric
Channel: there, gravity is the thermodynamics of the expanding Sphere,
and the identity of §7 --- gravity is the Born rule, both being one
entropy S = k ln Ω --- is a Geometric-Channel statement. It is
incomplete as a claim about gravity as such, because gravity also has
the Algebraic-Channel route with no thermodynamics: the Einstein field
equations are derived there from Diff\_McG-invariance and Lovelock
uniqueness alone, with no entropy, no temperature, and no arrow
(Corollary 9.2). Gravity is therefore not \emph{purely} thermodynamic
--- it is thermodynamic in the Geometric Channel and symmetry-derived in
the Algebraic Channel --- whereas thermodynamics is Geometric-only. The
same Einstein equations arrive with the arrow (Geometric Channel) and
without it (Algebraic Channel), which shows that the arrow of time is
not in the field equations themselves but in the thermodynamic
\emph{route} to them --- exactly because that route runs through the
Geometric Channel, whose expanding-Sphere advance carries the arrow
(§4.1, §5.2.1).

This is the sharpest form of the paper's thesis for the
gravity--thermodynamics relation. The relation is natural and inevitable
because gravity and thermodynamics are both theorem-chains of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) that share the Geometric Channel; the relation is
asymmetric because gravity is a two-channel object and thermodynamics a
one-channel object; and the framework can derive gravity
thermodynamically \emph{without assuming} the thermodynamics precisely
because the expanding-Sphere advance that carries the arrow --- the
Geometric Channel's \(dx_4/dt = ic\) content --- is the foundation from
which the Second Law is a theorem (§4.1), not an input imported to make
the entropy monotone work.

\hypertarget{the-algebraic-channel-the-algebraic-symmetry-reading}{%
\subsubsection{5.3 The Algebraic Channel: the algebraic-symmetry
reading}\label{the-algebraic-channel-the-algebraic-symmetry-reading}}

\textbf{Definition 7 (Algebraic Channel).} Algebraic Channel is the
reading of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) that asks: what transformations leave the
principle invariant?* Since \(x_4\) advances at the same rate \(ic\)
from every spacetime event, in every spatial direction, at every time,
the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is invariant under:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  translations along \(x_4\) itself: \(x_4 \mapsto x_4 + a_4\) for
  \(a_4 \in \mathbb{C}\);
\item
  translations along \(x_1, x_2, x_3\): \(x_j \mapsto x_j + a_j\) for
  \(a_j \in \mathbb{R}\) and \(j = 1, 2, 3\);
\item
  translations along \(t\): \(t \mapsto t + a_0\) for
  \(a_0 \in \mathbb{R}\);
\item
  rotations of the spatial three-coordinates: \(x \mapsto Rx\) for
  \(R \in \mathrm{SO}(3)\);
\item
  Lorentz boosts: \((t, x) \mapsto \Lambda(t, x)\) for
  \(\Lambda \in \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)\), automatic from the \(i\) in
  \(dx_4/dt = ic\) via the integrated identity \(x_4 = ict\) producing
  the Lorentzian signature on the constraint surface.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Theorem 8 (Poincaré invariance of \(dx_4/dt = ic\)).} The
combined invariance group of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) acting on \(M_G\) is the
Poincaré group
\(\mathrm{ISO}(1,3) = \mathbb{R}^4 \rtimes \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)\) at the
four-dimensional level.

\emph{Proof.} By items (i)--(iii) of Definition 7, the McGucken
Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is invariant under the four-dimensional
translation subgroup \(\mathbb{R}^4\). By items (iv) and (v), it is
invariant under the proper orthochronous Lorentz group
\(\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)\). The Lorentzian signature on the constraint
surface arises from the pullback of the holomorphic quadratic form
\(g_E = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2\) on the complexified
cotangent bundle along the embedding
\(\iota: (t, x_1, x_2, x_3) \mapsto (x_1, x_2, x_3, ict)\), producing
\(\iota^* g_E = -c^2 dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2\) (Theorem 4 of
\href{a}{23}). The full derivation of the Poincaré invariance group as
the \emph{derivational product} of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) and the embedding
\(\iota\) appears in {[}7, §2.2, Theorem 12{]}. The
derivational-priority statement --- that \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
\emph{generates} the Poincaré group rather than being a representation
of it --- is the content of {[}4, Theorem 1{]}, where the McGucken
Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is established as the \emph{father symmetry}
from which Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, gauge, quantum-unitary,
CPT, diffeomorphism, and supersymmetry all descend as theorems. The
semidirect-product structure
\(\mathrm{ISO}(1,3) = \mathbb{R}^4 \rtimes \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)\) follows
from the standard composition of translations with Lorentz
transformations. \(\square\)

\textbf{Theorem 9 (Factorisation of Diff(M) via McGucken, imported from
{[}2, §3{]}).} Hilbert's diffeomorphism invariance of the gravitational
action is factored by \(dx_4/dt = ic\) into two physically distinct
derivational components: (a) A kinematic symmetry:
\(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)\)-invariance of the matter action,
where \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)\) is the foliation-preserving
subgroup of \(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\) generated by vector fields
\(\xi^\mu = (\xi^0(x^0), \xi^i(x^0, x^j))\) with \(\xi^0\) depending
only on the time coordinate \(x^0\). (b) A constitutive identity:
\(u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2\) enforced pointwise on every massive worldline.
Off shell, only \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)\) acts as a
symmetry. On shell --- given the matter equations of motion --- the full
\(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\) is recovered, and the Einstein field equations
\(G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)\, T_{\mu\nu}\) follow
from Lovelock uniqueness plus Newtonian matching. \emph{Proof of Theorem
9.} We follow the structure of {[}2, §3{]}, expanding each step.

\textbf{Step 1 (the subgroup \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\)).} The
McGucken Principle the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) fixes the
rate of \(x_4\)-advance to \(ic\) at every point of \(M_G\). Under a
diffeomorphism \(\phi: M_G \to M_G\) generated by a vector field
\(\xi^\mu\), the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) requires
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) to be invariant. The constraint is that \(\xi^0\)
cannot depend on the spatial coordinates \(x^j\) in a way that varies
the rate at different points of the same spatial slice; otherwise the
McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) would be broken because \(dx_4/dt\)
would acquire spatial dependence. Hence
\(\partial \xi^0/\partial x^j = 0\) for \(j = 1, 2, 3\), i.e.,
\(\xi^0 = \xi^0(x^0)\) only. The spatial components \(\xi^j\) are
unconstrained because the spatial sector is deformable (Definition 5 of
\href{b}{23}). The vector field is therefore of the form
\(\xi^\mu = (\xi^0(x^0), \xi^j(x^0, x^k))\), which defines
\(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)\).

\textbf{Lemma 9.1.} \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)\) is a strict
subgroup of \(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\).

\emph{Proof of Lemma 9.1.} The general vector field on \(M_G\) has
\(\xi^0 = \xi^0(x^0, x^i)\) depending on all coordinates. Restricting
\(\xi^0\) to depend only on \(x^0\) yields a strict subgroup, since
vector fields with \(\partial \xi^0/\partial x^j \neq 0\) are not in the
McGucken subgroup. \(\square\)

\textbf{Step 2 (the constitutive identity).} By the McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), every massive particle's worldline \(x^\mu(\tau)\) on
\(M_G\) has \(dx_4/dt = ic\). Parametrising by proper time \(\tau\) via
\(d\tau^2 = -c^{-2} g_{\mu\nu} dx^\mu dx^\nu\), the four-velocity is
\(u^\mu = dx^\mu/d\tau\). The four-velocity budget identity
\[u^\mu u_\mu = g_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu = -c^2\] follows directly from
the definition of \(\tau\): indeed
\(g_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu = (dx^\mu dx_\mu)/d\tau^2 = -c^2\). The
stress-energy tensor of a perfect fluid of such particles is
\[T^{\mu\nu} = (\rho c^2 + p) \frac{u^\mu u^\nu}{c^2} + p\, g^{\mu\nu}, \tag{T}\]
with the constraint \(u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2\) enforced pointwise.

\textbf{Step 3 (Noether's second theorem applied to
\(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\)).} Apply Noether's second theorem
(Noether 1918) to the matter action \(S_M[\phi, g_{\mu\nu}]\) invariant
under \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)\). Noether's second theorem is
here the standard variational result applied to framework-derived
inputs: the McGucken Lagrangian (Lemma 1 of {[}23{]} plus the derived
least-action structure), the \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\)-symmetry,
and the \(+ic\) foliation all descend from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) ({[}2,
Theorem 30\('\){]}; precise status in Remark 10.3.1.1). The variational
theorem itself is general calculus of variations --- a tool, not
re-derived from the Principle; what the Principle supplies are its
inputs. Therefore the Algebraic Channel rests on no \emph{physical}
input external to \(dx_4/dt = ic\) for this step.

The conserved currents associated with
\(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\)-invariance are \emph{weaker} than those
of full \(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\) because the symmetry group is smaller.
Specifically: (S) spatial diffeomorphism invariance (\(\xi^j\)
unconstrained, \(\xi^0 = 0\)) yields the spatial conservation law
\(\nabla_i T^{i\nu} = 0\) on each spatial slice \(\Sigma_t\); (T-int)
time-reparametrisation invariance (\(\xi^0 = \xi^0(x^0)\),
\(\xi^j = 0\)) yields the integrated time-conservation
\(\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\Sigma_t} T^{0\nu} \sqrt{h}\, d^3 x = 0\). The
local conservation \(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0\) in \emph{all} four
directions is \emph{not} given by \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\) alone
because \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\) is a strict subgroup (Lemma
9.1).

\textbf{Step 4 (on-shell enhancement).} Claim: given the matter
equations of motion (relativistic energy equation and Euler equation)
together with the constitutive identity (Step 2), the local conservation
\(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0\) holds in all four directions.

\emph{Proof of the on-shell enhancement.} The perfect-fluid
stress-energy tensor (T) gives, upon differentiation,
\[\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; \nabla_\mu\!\left[(\rho c^2 + p)\,\frac{u^\mu}{c^2}\right] u^\nu \;+\; (\rho c^2 + p)\,\frac{u^\mu}{c^2}\,\nabla_\mu u^\nu \;+\; g^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p. \tag{$\dagger$}\]

\emph{Timelike projection.} Contract (\(\dagger\)) with \(u_\nu\) and
apply the constitutive identity \(u_\nu u^\nu = -c^2\) together with its
consequence \(u_\nu \nabla_\mu u^\nu = 0\) (from differentiating
\(u_\nu u^\nu = -c^2\), a constant on the constraint surface):
\[u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; -c^2 \nabla_\mu\!\left[(\rho c^2 + p)\,\frac{u^\mu}{c^2}\right] \;+\; 0 \;+\; u^\mu \partial_\mu p.\]
Expanding the first term:
\[-c^2 \nabla_\mu\!\left[\frac{(\rho c^2 + p) u^\mu}{c^2}\right] \;=\; -\nabla_\mu[(\rho c^2 + p) u^\mu] \;=\; -(\rho c^2 + p) \nabla_\mu u^\mu \;-\; c^2 u^\mu \partial_\mu \rho \;-\; u^\mu \partial_\mu p.\]
Combining:
\[u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; -(\rho c^2 + p) \nabla_\mu u^\mu \;-\; c^2 u^\mu \partial_\mu \rho.\]
Setting this to zero gives the \emph{relativistic energy equation} (the
perfect-fluid matter EOM for energy conservation along the flow):
\[u^\mu \partial_\mu \rho \;+\; (\rho + p/c^2)\, \nabla_\mu u^\mu \;=\; 0. \tag{Energy-EOM}\]
The timelike projection \(u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0\) is therefore
equivalent to the perfect-fluid energy equation, which is one of the
matter EOMs.

\emph{Spatial projection.} Project (\(\dagger\)) orthogonal to \(u^\nu\)
using the spatial projector
\(h^\nu_\lambda = \delta^\nu_\lambda + u^\nu u_\lambda/c^2\) (with
\(h^\nu_\lambda u^\lambda = 0\) and
\(h^\nu_\lambda h^\lambda_\sigma = h^\nu_\sigma\)):
\[h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} \;=\; (\rho c^2 + p)\,\frac{u^\mu}{c^2}\,(h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu u^\lambda) \;+\; h^{\nu\mu} \partial_\mu p,\]
where the first term of (\(\dagger\)) drops out under the spatial
projection because \(h^\nu_\lambda u^\lambda = 0\), and the third term
contracts to \(h^{\nu\mu}\partial_\mu p\) via
\(h^\nu_\lambda g^{\lambda\mu} = h^{\nu\mu}\). Setting this to zero
gives the \emph{relativistic Euler equation} (the perfect-fluid matter
EOM for spatial momentum):
\[(\rho c^2 + p)\, u^\mu \nabla_\mu u^\nu \;=\; -h^{\nu\mu} \partial_\mu p, \tag{Euler-EOM}\]
where the projection
\(h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu u^\lambda \equiv \nabla_\mu u^\nu\) on the
spatial subspace (using \(u_\lambda \nabla_\mu u^\lambda = 0\))
eliminates the redundant temporal component. The spatial projection
\(h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} = 0\) is therefore equivalent
to the relativistic Euler equation.

\emph{Span and conclusion.} The timelike-projector
\(-u^\nu u^\lambda/c^2\) and the spatial-projector
\(h^\nu_\lambda = \delta^\nu_\lambda + u^\nu u_\lambda/c^2\) together
span the full tangent space at every event:
\[-\frac{u^\nu u_\lambda}{c^2} \;+\; h^\nu_\lambda \;=\; -\frac{u^\nu u_\lambda}{c^2} \;+\; \delta^\nu_\lambda \;+\; \frac{u^\nu u_\lambda}{c^2} \;=\; \delta^\nu_\lambda.\]
Hence the vanishing of \(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu}\) on both subspaces
implies \(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0\) identically. On shell --- given
the relativistic energy equation (Energy-EOM) and the relativistic Euler
equation (Euler-EOM) as the perfect-fluid matter EOMs --- the local
conservation \(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0\) holds in all four directions.
The matter action becomes invariant under arbitrary diffeomorphisms
acting consistently on metric and matter, recovering the full
\(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\) on-shell. \(\square\) (end of Step 4)

\textbf{Step 4′ (full \(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\)-invariance of the
gravitational sector, from the Lorentz covariance of the Sphere).} The
restriction to \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\) in Step 1 is a
restriction on the matter foliation --- on how the coordinate time \(t\)
of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) may be relabelled across a spatial slice --- and it
does not by itself fix the symmetry of the gravitational action. Were
the gravitational action required to be invariant only under
\(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\), Lovelock's theorem would not apply:
the foliation-preserving group is the symmetry group of Hořava--Lifshitz
gravity, whose allowed kinetic term is \(K_{ij}K^{ij} - \lambda K^2\)
with \(\lambda\) a free constant and whose spectrum carries an extra
scalar mode; general relativity is the \(\lambda = 1\) member of that
family, and nothing in \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\) alone selects
it. The McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) supplies the missing
invariance. The McGucken Sphere expands at the same rate \(c\) from
every event in every inertial frame (Theorem 8, the Lorentz covariance
of \(dx_4/dt = ic\); the McGucken Sphere Uniqueness Theorem {[}21{]}),
so the geometry carries no preferred foliation: a preferred spatial
slicing in the gravitational sector would single out a frame in which
the Sphere's expansion rate differed from \(c\), contradicting the
Principle. The gravitational action must therefore be a scalar under the
full \(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\), the foliation entering only through the
matter coupling of Step 2. This forces \(\lambda = 1\) and brings the
gravitational sector within the hypotheses of Lovelock's theorem in Step
5.

\textbf{Step 5 (Einstein field equations from Lovelock).} With
\(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0\) established and the gravitational action
\(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\)-invariant by Step 4′, the geometric side of the
field equations is forced by Lovelock's theorem {[}72{]}: \emph{in four
dimensions, the unique divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensor built
from the metric \(g_{\mu\nu}\) and its first two derivatives, linear in
second derivatives, is
\[L_{\mu\nu} = \alpha\, G_{\mu\nu} + \beta\, g_{\mu\nu}, \tag{Lovelock}\]
where \(G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g_{\mu\nu}\) is the
Einstein tensor and \(\alpha, \beta\) are constants. The derivational
priority of Lovelock as a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) operates through
the McGucken-Invariance Lemma (Lemma 6 of {[}23{]}): the
McGucken-Invariance Lemma restricts the allowed geometric structure to
one in which \(g_{\mu\nu}\) is the }deformable-sector* variable (spatial
sector) coupled to matter through the universal Sphere geometry; the
Lovelock uniqueness then applies to the divergence-free combinations on
the four-dimensional manifold \(M_G\). Setting
\(L_{\mu\nu} = \kappa\, T_{\mu\nu}\) with \(\kappa = 8\pi G/c^4\) and
\(\beta = \Lambda\) gives
\[G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} = \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu}. \tag{Einstein field equations}\]

The tag (the Einstein field equations) is the standard abbreviation for
the Einstein Field Equations: the dynamical equations of general
relativity, relating the geometric curvature of spacetime (encoded in
the Einstein tensor \(G_{\mu\nu}\) and cosmological-constant term
\(\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}\) on the left) to the matter-energy content
(encoded in the stress-energy tensor \(T_{\mu\nu}\) on the right). They
are GR T11 of the book's 24-theorem gravitational chain. \textbf{Step 6
(Newtonian matching fixes \(\kappa\)).} In the weak-field static limit
\(g_{00} = -(1 + 2\Phi/c^2)\), \(g_{ij} = \delta_{ij}\), the dominant
component of (the Einstein field equations) at \(00\) reduces to
Poisson's equation \(\nabla^2 \Phi = 4\pi G \rho\). The coupling
constant \(\kappa = 8\pi G/c^4\) is forced by this matching. \(\square\)
(end of Theorem 9)

\textbf{Corollary 9.2.} The Algebraic Channel derivation of the Einstein
field equations rests on no mathematical input external to
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) and Lovelock's theorem --- applied to a gravitational
sector whose full \(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\)-invariance Step 4′ derives from
the Lorentz covariance of the Sphere --- plus the Newtonian matching
condition fixing the coupling constant. The factorisation (a) of Theorem
9 (Diff-invariance) and (b) (constitutive identity) are both direct
theorems of \(dx_4/dt = ic\). Noether's second theorem, used in Step 3,
operates on framework-derived inputs --- which descend from
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) via {[}2, Theorem 30\('\){]}, with the precise status
stated in Remark 10.3.1.1 (the theorem itself is a standard variational
tool, not re-derived from the Principle). The derivational meaning is
that the McGucken Principle is strictly stronger than Hilbert's
diffeomorphism invariance: the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
determines which diffeomorphisms are off-shell symmetries (only
\(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\)) and explains why the full
\(\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\) is recovered on shell (because the four-velocity
budget is consistent with arbitrary reparametrisation of the worldline).

The Algebraic Channel is the \emph{invariance-group content} of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\). Through Noether's theorem (itself a theorem of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) per {[}4{]}), every continuous symmetry generates a
conservation law: energy (\(t\)-translation), momentum (spatial
translation), angular momentum (spatial rotation), four-momentum
(Lorentz), stress-energy conservation \(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0\) (the
on-shell enhancement of \(\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}\)-invariance).
The Algebraic Channel operates uniformly in Lorentzian signature; the
derivational reason established in {[}2, §5{]} is that the imaginary
unit \(i\) is \emph{interior} to the unitary representations
\(\exp(-isp/\hbar)\), \(\exp(-iHt/\hbar)\) and cannot be exteriorised
without dissolving the algebraic content.

\hypertarget{the-geometric-channel-the-geometric-propagation-reading-the-thermodynamic-route}{%
\subsubsection{5.4 The Geometric Channel: the geometric-propagation
reading (the thermodynamic
route)}\label{the-geometric-channel-the-geometric-propagation-reading-the-thermodynamic-route}}

\textbf{Definition 10 (Geometric Channel).} Geometric Channel is the
reading of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) that asks: what does the principle generate
when applied at every spacetime event?* The McGucken Sphere \(M^+_p(t)\)
of Definition 2 of {[}23{]} is the wavefront generated by
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) at \(p\); by Proposition 3 of {[}23{]}, every point of
\(M^+_p(t)\) is itself a source of a new McGucken Sphere; iterating this
construction generates Huygens' Principle and the iterated-sphere path
structure of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) on \(M_G\). Formally, Geometric Channel is
the wavefront-functor \(p \mapsto M^+_p(\cdot)\) of Definition 2 of
{[}23{]}, together with its iterated composition
\(M^+_p(\cdot) \circ M^+_q(\cdot)\) for \(q \in M^+_p(\cdot)\) as in
Proposition 3.

The Geometric Channel is the \emph{wavefront content} of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\). The Geometric Channel derivation of the Einstein field
equations proceeds through four self-contained theorems, each derived
from \(dx_4/dt = ic\), culminating in the same equation (the Einstein
field equations) that the Algebraic Channel produces. We state each as a
numbered theorem with a complete proof.

\textbf{Theorem 11 (Geometric Second Law).} Given the McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), the Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy of the reduced state of
any ensemble of \(N\) particles is non-decreasing in coordinate time,
\(dS/dt \ge 0\), with equality only at the stationary state of the
forward diffusion; on the unbounded spatial slice the inequality is
strict,
\[\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{3}{2}\, \frac{k_B}{t} > 0 \qquad \text{for all } t > 0.\]
*The monotonicity is exact, not statistical --- the H-theorem of the
forward Fokker--Planck equation whose retarded propagator the \(+ic\)
orientation selects --- and there is no Poincaré recurrence. (The scope
of the statement --- reduced state, bounded versus unbounded domain,
Compton versus Planck step --- is as in Theorem 19.5.1, §4.1.1.)

\emph{Proof.} The proof proceeds in four steps from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) to
the strict monotonicity; the integrated form \(x_4 = ict\) plays no role
in the derivation.

\emph{Step 1 (the physical expansion \(dx_4/dt = ic\) projected onto the
spatial slice).} By the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\), \(x_4\)
advances at rate \(ic\) from every spacetime event \(p \in M_G\) in a
spherically symmetric manner. Projecting this 4-dimensional spherical
expansion onto the spatial three-slice at each event produces the
McGucken Sphere \(M^+_p(t)\) of radius \(c\, \delta t\) about that event
for any infinitesimal time interval \(\delta t\) (Definition 2 of
{[}23{]}). Each particle in the ensemble is therefore displaced by
\(c\, \delta t\) in a direction \(\hat{n}\) drawn from the uniform
measure on \(S^2\) at every Planck-time step
\(\delta t_p = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^5}\) (the fundamental time scale at
which \(x_4\) advances by one Planck length
\(\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^3}\)).

\emph{Step 2 (diffusion equation from isotropic step).} The probability
density \(P(\vec{r}, t)\) of a particle position evolves under iterated
isotropic displacements with rms step size \(c\, \delta t_p\) per step.
The isotropy of each step is a consequence of the McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), component (ii) (Spherical symmetry): the
\(x_4\)-expansion is spherically symmetric from every event, so the
projected displacement direction \(\hat n\) is drawn from the uniform
measure on \(S^2\) with no preferred spatial direction. The standard
derivation of Brownian motion from isotropic random walks (Chandrasekhar
1943) --- here serving only as the computational lemma that turns the
Principle-supplied isotropic step into a diffusion law --- applied with
step size \(c\, \delta t_p\) and step time \(\delta t_p\) gives the
diffusion coefficient
\[D = \frac{(c\, \delta t_p)^2}{6\, \delta t_p} = \frac{c^2\, \delta t_p}{6}\]
and the probability density satisfies the isotropic diffusion equation
\[\frac{\partial P}{\partial t} = D\, \nabla^2 P. \tag{Diff}\]

\emph{Step 3 (Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy of the Gaussian solution).} The
fundamental solution of (Diff) with delta-function initial data
\(P(\vec{r}, 0) = \delta^3(\vec{r})\) is the Gaussian
\(P(\vec{r}, t) = (4\pi D t)^{-3/2}\, \exp(-r^2/(4Dt))\). Direct
evaluation of the Boltzmann--Gibbs differential entropy
\(S(t) = -k_B \int P \ln P\, d^3 r\) on this Gaussian gives
\[S(t) = \frac{3}{2}\, k_B \ln(4 \pi e D t) + \text{const}.\]

\emph{Step 4 (strict monotonicity).} Differentiating with respect to
\(t\):
\[\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{3}{2}\, \frac{k_B}{t} > 0 \qquad \text{for all } t > 0.\]
The monotonicity is \emph{exact}, not statistical, because
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) specifies the \(+ic\) orientation (the McGucken
Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\), component (iii)): \(x_4\) advances and does
not retreat, so (Diff) propagates probability density forward in \(t\)
with no time-reversed branch in the physical dynamics. The textbook
statistical Second Law (a tendency with Poincaré recurrence) reduces to
this strict geometric Second Law when the \(+ic\)-oriented physical
motion underlying the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is recognised.
There is no Poincaré recurrence because \(x_4\) does not recur.
\(\square\)

\textbf{Theorem 12 (Bekenstein--Hawking area law from \(x_4\)-mode
counting).} Given the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) {[}whose
wavelength sets the action \(h\), and which at the horizon tier is the
Planck length \(\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3} = \hbar/(m_P c)\), the
reduced Compton wavelength of the Planck mass{]}, the entropy associated
with a McGucken Sphere of area \(A\) is
\[S = k_B\, \frac{A}{4 \ell_P^2} = k_B\, \frac{A c^3}{4 \hbar G}.\]

\emph{Proof.} By the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\), the fourth
dimension expands at rate \(ic\) from every spacetime event. Quantising
this expansion at the Planck scale, the fundamental wavelength of
\(x_4\)-advance is \(\ell_P\). The number of independent quantum modes
of \(x_4\)-advance crossing the McGucken Sphere of area \(A\) is one
mode per Planck-area cell: \[N_{\text{modes}} = \frac{A}{\ell_P^2}.\]
Identifying entropy with \(k_B\) times the number of modes (one bit per
mode): \(S = k_B A/\ell_P^2\). This mode-counting argument fixes the
\emph{form} of the area law --- entropy proportional to horizon area in
Planck units --- but not its numerical coefficient. The coefficient is
\(1/4\), and its status in the two channels is as follows. In the
Geometric Channel the coefficient \(\eta = 1/(4\ell_P^2)\) is fixed,
exactly as in Jacobson {[}1{]}, by Newtonian matching: the Clausius
relation of Theorem 14 yields a field equation with coupling
\(\eta/2\pi\) in natural units, and identifying that coupling with
Newton's constant through the weak-field limit (Theorem 9 Step 6) gives
\(\eta = 1/4G\), i.e.~\(G = c^3/(4\hbar\eta)\). The Geometric Channel
therefore fixes one constant, the ratio of \(\eta\) to \(G\), and
derives the entropy--area form, the temperature, and the field
equations; it does not derive \(\eta\) and \(G\) separately. In the
Algebraic Channel, where the Einstein--Hilbert action is derived
(Theorem 9), the coefficient is a computed output: the Wick-rotated
\(x_4\)-boost at the horizon supplies the Hawking temperature \(T_H\)
(Theorem 15.4.2 of {[}29{]}), and integrating the first law
\(dE = T_H\, dS\) with the boundary condition \(S(0) = 0\) yields
\(S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)\) (Theorem 15.4.3 of {[}29{]}), the factor
\(\tfrac14\) arising from the \(\tfrac12\) of \(\int M\,dM\) against the
geometric factors carried by \(r_s = 2GM/c^2\); and the Euclidean cigar
computation below (thermodynamics paper {[}24{]}, Theorem 15) obtains
the same \(\tfrac14\) from the Einstein--Hilbert plus
Gibbons--Hawking--York action, with no Bekenstein--Hawking coefficient
posited. Both Algebraic-Channel computations take the Einstein--Hilbert
action as input, and that action is the Algebraic-Channel theorem of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\); they are therefore confirmations that the derived
action reproduces the \(\tfrac14\), and they cannot serve as the
Geometric Channel's input without making the Geometric Channel's
derivation of the field equations circular. In the McGucken
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) framework, therefore, two of Jacobson's three assumed
ingredients --- the entropy--area form \(S \propto A\) (the Compton-tick
Planck-cell count) and the Unruh/Hawking temperature (the Euclidean
\(x_4\)-periodicity) --- are outputs of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) within the
Geometric Channel itself, and the third, the coefficient, is fixed there
by the same Newtonian matching Jacobson uses and derived independently
in the Algebraic Channel {[}24{]}. This is the precise sense in which
the framework is more foundational than the equation-of-state
derivation: what Jacobson assumed, \(dx_4/dt = ic\) derives, with the
single matching constant shared by both.

\textbf{Algebraic-Channel confirmation of the coefficient via the
Euclidean cigar (reproduced from {[}24{]}, Theorems 15--16).} The 1/4 is
computed in full here from the Einstein--Hilbert action derived in
Theorem 9. The derivation proceeds through the McGucken--Wick rotation
of the horizon geometry --- the physical operation of removing the i
from dx₄/dt = ic, which turns the Lorentzian horizon into a smooth
Euclidean geometry (the ``cigar'').

\emph{Step A (the Euclidean cigar and its smoothness period).} Under the
McGucken--Wick rotation τ = x₄/c (the Euclidean reading of the
x₄-advance, §5.5), the Schwarzschild horizon geometry becomes, in the
(ρ, θ) plane near the horizon (ρ the proper radial distance from the
horizon, θ = κτ/c the Euclidean angle), the flat-plane metric ds² = dρ²
+ ρ²dθ². This is smooth at ρ = 0 (the horizon, the tip of the cigar) if
and only if θ is 2π-periodic --- otherwise a conical singularity sits at
the tip. The smoothness requirement θ ∈ {[}0, 2π) fixes the period of
Euclidean time:
\[\kappa\,\tau_{\max}/c = 2\pi \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \beta = \tau_{\max} = \frac{2\pi c}{\kappa},\]
with κ = c⁴/(4GM) the surface gravity of the Schwarzschild horizon.

\emph{Step B (Hawking temperature from the period --- Theorem 16).} By
the Kubo--Martin--Schwinger condition (§C), a quantum state periodic in
Euclidean time with period β is a thermal state at temperature T =
ℏ/(k\_B β). Substituting β = 2πc/κ:
\[T_H = \frac{\hbar}{k_B\,\beta} = \frac{\hbar\,\kappa}{2\pi c\,k_B} = \frac{\hbar c^3}{8\pi G M k_B},\]
the Hawking temperature, derived from the 2π-smoothness of the Euclidean
x₄-circle --- no thermodynamic input assumed, only the geometry of the
Wick-rotated advance.

\emph{Step C (the 1/4 from the Euclidean action --- Theorem 15).}
Evaluate the Euclidean Einstein--Hilbert action, with the
Gibbons--Hawking--York boundary term required for a well-posed
variational problem, on the Ricci-flat Euclidean Schwarzschild manifold.
The bulk Einstein--Hilbert term vanishes (Ricci-flat), leaving only the
GHY boundary contribution, which evaluates to
\[I_E = \frac{\beta M c^2}{2}.\] The standard thermodynamic relation
between the Euclidean action and the entropy --- the free-energy
relation \(\ln Z = -I_E/\hbar\),
\(S = k_B(\beta\langle E\rangle + \hbar\ln Z)/\hbar\), with no
Bekenstein--Hawking input --- is
\(S = k_B\,(\beta\langle E\rangle - I_E)/\hbar\), where β is the
Euclidean period (dimension of time) and \(I_E\) the Euclidean action.
With ⟨E⟩ = Mc² and I\_E = βMc²/2:
\[S = \frac{k_B}{\hbar}\left(\beta M c^2 - \frac{\beta M c^2}{2}\right) = \frac{k_B\,\beta M c^2}{2\hbar}.\]
Substituting β = 2πc/κ = 8πGM/c³ (using κ = c⁴/4GM) gives
\[S = \frac{k_B}{2\hbar}\cdot\frac{8\pi G M}{c^3}\cdot M c^2 = \frac{4\pi G M^2 k_B}{\hbar c} = k_B\,\frac{A}{4\ell_P^2},\]
where the last equality uses the Schwarzschild horizon area A = 4π r\_s²
= 4π(2GM/c²)² = 16πG²M²/c⁴ and ℓ\_P² = ℏG/c³, so that A/4ℓ\_P² =
(16πG²M²/c⁴)/(4ℏG/c³) = 4πGM²/(ℏc). \textbf{The factor 1/4 is the
half-factor of the GHY boundary term (the ½ in I\_E = βMc²/2) carried
through the free-energy relation} --- it is an output of the
Euclidean-cigar geometry of the Wick-rotated x₄-advance evaluated on the
Einstein--Hilbert action of Theorem 9, with no Bekenstein--Hawking
coefficient posited at any step {[}24{]}.

The Bekenstein--Hawking area law's form and the Hawking temperature are
derived from dx₄/dt = ic within the Geometric Channel through the
McGucken--Wick rotation of the horizon; the 1/4 coefficient is fixed
there by Newtonian matching and computed independently in the Algebraic
Channel from the derived action {[}24{]}. The present theorem therefore
delivers the area law's form; Theorem 15.4.3 of {[}29{]} and the cigar
computation deliver its coefficient from the Algebraic-Channel action,
and together they constitute GR T20. \(\square\)

\textbf{Theorem 13 (Unruh temperature from Wick-rotated \(x_4\)-boost).}
Given the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) and Theorem 4 of {[}23{]}
(McGucken--Wick rotation), a uniformly accelerated observer with proper
acceleration \(a\) experiences a temperature
\[T_U = \frac{\hbar a}{2 \pi c\, k_B}.\]

\emph{Proof.} The derivation is self-contained from \(dx_4/dt = ic\). By
the McGucken Principle, the fourth coordinate advances as \(x_4 = ict\)
(integrating \(dx_4/dt = ic\) under the source-origin convention
\(x_4(0)=0\)), so proper time and the fourth coordinate are related by
\(\tau = x_4/c\) and the substitution \(t \mapsto -i\tau\) is the same
advance written in Euclidean units. Under this substitution a Lorentz
boost of rapidity \(\eta\) in the \((x,t)\)-plane ---
\(ct' = ct\cosh\eta + x\sinh\eta\), \(x' = ct\sinh\eta + x\cosh\eta\)
--- becomes, with \(\theta := -i\eta\) (so \(\cosh\eta \to \cos\theta\)
and \(\sinh\eta \to i\sin\theta\)), a Euclidean rotation by angle
\(\theta\) in the \((x, c\tau)\)-plane. A uniformly accelerated observer
of proper acceleration \(a\) follows a worldline of constant
\(x\)-coordinate in Rindler coordinates whose boost parameter advances
at rate \(a/c\) in proper time; on the Euclidean section this is a
circle in the \((x, c\tau)\)-plane, and regularity of the geometry at
the horizon (absence of a conical singularity at the fixed point of the
rotation) requires the Euclidean angle to be \(2\pi\)-periodic. The
corresponding period in Euclidean proper time is
\(\Delta\tau_p = 2\pi c/a\). The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger condition of
quantum statistical mechanics identifies a state periodic in imaginary
time with period \(\hbar\beta\) as a thermal state at inverse
temperature \(\beta\); matching \(\hbar\beta = \Delta\tau_p = 2\pi c/a\)
gives \(\beta = 2\pi c/(\hbar a)\), and hence
\[T_U = \frac{1}{k_B\beta} = \frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c\, k_B}.\] Every step
--- the advance \(x_4 = ict\), the boost-to-rotation, the
\(2\pi\)-regularity, and the KMS periodicity of the Euclidean
\(x_4\)-circle --- is a consequence of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) read on the
Euclidean section; the Unruh temperature is therefore a theorem of the
Principle, not an imported input (the corresponding full
quantum-field-theoretic development is {[}3{]}). \(\square\)

\textbf{Theorem 14 (Geometric Channel output: the Einstein field
equations).} Given the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\), Theorems
11--13, the Clausius relation \(\delta Q = T\, dS\), and the
Raychaudhuri equation for null congruences, the Einstein field equations
\[G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} = \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu}\]
\emph{hold at every spacetime point.}

\emph{Proof.} The derivation follows the thermodynamic route of Jacobson
{[}1{]}, reproduced here in full and underwritten by the McGucken
Geometric-Channel inputs (Theorems 11--13, each proved above from
\(dx_4/dt = ic\)), applied to a local Rindler horizon at every spacetime
event \(p \in M_G\). The local Rindler horizon is not an external
scaffold imposed on the manifold: by the McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), component (ii), \(x_4\) expands spherically at rate
\(c\) from every event, and the null surface this expansion sweeps out
is the McGucken Sphere's null cone (Definition 2 of {[}23{]}); the local
Rindler horizon through \(p\) is precisely a patch of that
Principle-generated null structure as seen by a uniformly accelerated
observer --- the null plane that is the limit of the Sphere's null cone
from a source event at large affine distance behind \(p\), where the
cone's expansion \(\theta = 2/r\) and shear vanish, which is why
Jacobson's equilibrium conditions \(\theta(p) = \sigma(p) = 0\) hold on
it (a Sphere from a nearby event has \(\theta \neq 0\) and is not a
local Rindler horizon). Consider an arbitrary spacetime point \(p\) and
a local Rindler horizon \(H\) through \(p\): a null hypersurface
generated by a null congruence with affine parameter \(\lambda\) and
tangent vector \(k^\mu\). The horizon is the boundary of the past of a
uniformly accelerated observer with proper acceleration \(a\) in the
local neighbourhood of \(p\). The Rindler horizon-generating Killing
vector \(\chi^\mu\) is parallel to \(k^\mu\) on \(H\), with
\(\chi^\mu = -(a/c^2)\,\lambda\, k^\mu\) in the affine parametrisation
(Jacobson {[}1{]}, eq. (1), in SI units with \(\lambda\) an affine
length) --- the Rindler-Killing-vector affine-parameter relation that
supplies the factor of \(a\) canceling against the Unruh temperature.

\emph{Step 1 (heat flux through \(H\)).} The heat flux carried across
\(H\) by matter, defined as the boost-energy flux past the Rindler
observer, is
\[\delta Q \;=\; \int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, \chi^\mu\, d\Sigma^\nu \;=\; -\int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, \frac{a\lambda}{c^2}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA, \tag{Q-flux}\]
where \(d\Sigma^\nu = k^\nu d\lambda dA\) is the null-congruence
area-element-times-affine-parameter measure, and the minus sign comes
from \(\chi^\mu = -(a/c^2)\lambda k^\mu\). \emph{LTD reading:} the
boost-energy flux \(\delta Q\) is the McGucken-Sphere reading of heat
--- the Compton-tick action quanta \(h\) of the matter Spheres (§2)
crossing the Principle-generated null cone of the accelerated observer;
the null generators \(k^\mu\) are the lightfronts of the
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) expansion (Theorem 11), not an external congruence
imposed on the manifold.

\emph{Step 2 (entropy change from the area law).} By Theorem 12, the
entropy associated with the horizon \(H\) at any cross-section is
\(S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)\). The differential entropy change for an area
variation \(\delta A\) is
\[\delta S \;=\; \frac{k_B}{4\ell_P^2}\, \delta A. \tag{S-area}\] On a
null congruence, the area variation along the congruence at parameter
\(\lambda\) relates to the expansion \(\theta\) via
\(d(\delta A)/d\lambda = \theta\, \delta A\), equivalently
\(\delta A = -\int (d\theta/d\lambda) \lambda\, d\lambda\, dA\) in the
focusing limit (Step 3 below). \emph{LTD reading:} the area law
\(S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)\) is the horizon reading of the McGucken Entropy
\(S = k_B\ln\Omega\) (§6, Theorem 6.1), with \(\Omega\) the count of
Compton-tick Planck-area cells the expanding Sphere tiles on \(H\)
(Theorem 12, §A.3); \(\delta S\) is the change in that Sphere
state-count as the horizon area varies.

\emph{Step 3 (area change from Raychaudhuri).} The Raychaudhuri equation
for the null congruence generating \(H\) is
\[\frac{d\theta}{d\lambda} \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}\theta^2 \;-\; \sigma_{\mu\nu}\sigma^{\mu\nu} \;-\; R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu,\]
where \(\theta\) is the expansion, \(\sigma_{\mu\nu}\) the shear, and
\(R_{\mu\nu}\) the Ricci tensor. At the chosen event \(p\) (with
\(\theta(0) = 0\) and \(\sigma(0) = 0\) for the locally-stationary
horizon), the leading-order behaviour is
\(d\theta/d\lambda = -R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu\). \emph{LTD reading:} the
expansion \(\theta\) of the null generators is the focusing of
neighbouring McGucken-Sphere lightfronts (Theorem 11), and its
matter-driven convergence \(R_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu\) is the
Sphere-expansion being lensed by the Compton-tick energy content --- the
Geometric-Channel focusing that the Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) requires
when matter Spheres are present. The integrated area change up to affine
parameter \(\lambda\):
\[\delta A(\lambda) \;=\; \int_0^\lambda \theta(\lambda')\, dA\, d\lambda' \;=\; -\int_0^\lambda \lambda'\, R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu\, dA\, d\lambda', \tag{Ray}\]
where the second equality uses
\(\theta(\lambda) = \int_0^\lambda (d\theta/d\lambda')d\lambda' = -\lambda R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu\)
at leading order.

\emph{Step 4 (Clausius relation).} Equate \(\delta Q = T_U\, \delta S\)
with \(T_U = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)\) from Theorem 13. \emph{LTD reading:}
the Clausius relation here is not imported thermodynamics but the
McGucken identity that the Compton-tick heat crossing the horizon equals
the temperature (the Euclidean \(x_4\)-periodicity of the Sphere,
Theorem 13) times the increment of the Sphere state-count \(\Omega\)
(Theorem 12) --- every factor a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) (§4, §6), so
the equation of state is read entirely in Sphere machinery. Substituting
from (Q-flux), (S-area), and (Ray):
\[-\int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, \frac{a\lambda}{c^2}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; \frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c\, k_B} \cdot \frac{k_B}{4\ell_P^2} \cdot \left(-\int_H \lambda\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA\right).\]
The factor \(a\) on each side cancels; the factor \(\lambda\) inside
each integral cancels; the minus sign on each side cancels; the
\(c^{-2}\) on the left passes to the right:
\[\int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; \frac{\hbar c}{8\pi\, \ell_P^2} \int_H R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA.\]
Using \(\ell_P^2 = \hbar G/c^3\):
\[\frac{\hbar c}{8\pi\, \ell_P^2} \;=\; \frac{\hbar c\cdot c^3}{8\pi\, \hbar G} \;=\; \frac{c^4}{8\pi G}.\]
The same bookkeeping in natural units (\(c = \hbar = k_B = 1\)) reads:
the Unruh temperature is \(T_U = a/2\pi\), the entropy density is
\(\eta = 1/4\ell_P^2 = 1/4G\), the heat flux is
\(\delta Q = -a\int \lambda\, T_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA\),
and the entropy change from the area law is
\(\delta S = \eta\, \delta A = -\eta\int \lambda\, R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA\).
The Clausius relation \(\delta Q = T_U\, \delta S\), after cancelling
the common factor \(a\) and the \(\lambda\)-integrals (which must match
for all local Rindler horizons, i.e.~for all null \(k^\mu\) at every
event), gives
\[T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu \;=\; \frac{\eta}{2\pi}\; R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu \;=\; \frac{1}{2\pi\cdot 4G}\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu \;=\; \frac{1}{8\pi G}\,R_{\mu\nu}k^\mu k^\nu,\]
Jacobson's result {[}1{]}: the coupling is \(\eta/2\pi\), and with
\(\eta = 1/4G\) it is \(1/8\pi G\). Restoring SI units, the two
computations agree:
\[T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu \;=\; \frac{c^4}{8\pi G}\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu \quad \text{for all null } k^\mu, \tag{14.1}\]
the \(c^4\) being carried by the \(c^{-2}\) of the boost Killing vector
together with the \(c^3\) of \(\ell_P^{-2}\) and the \(c^{-1}\) of the
Unruh temperature; it is the unique power of \(c\) for which both sides
carry the dimensions of energy density when \(R_{\mu\nu}\) carries
inverse-length-squared and \(G\) its SI dimensions.

\emph{Step 5 (conclusion: all null vectors → tensor identity).} Equation
(14.1) holds for \emph{every} null vector \(k^\mu\) at \emph{every}
spacetime point. The Newman-Penrose-type completeness of null vectors in
the tangent space, together with the symmetry of both \(T_{\mu\nu}\) and
\(R_{\mu\nu}\), forces
\[T_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \frac{c^4}{8\pi G}\bigl( R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} \bigr),\]
where: - the trace term \(-\tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu}\) is forced by the
requirement \(\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0\) (from Step 4 of Theorem 9, the
on-shell enhancement), which by the contracted Bianchi identity
\(\nabla^\mu G_{\mu\nu} = 0\) singles out the Einstein tensor
\(G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}Rg_{\mu\nu}\) over the bare
Ricci tensor; - the cosmological-constant term \(+\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}\)
enters as an integration constant (allowed because
\(\nabla^\mu g_{\mu\nu} = 0\) identically).

Rearranging the conclusion gives (the Einstein field equations).
\(\square\)

\textbf{Corollary 14.1 (Hilbert--Jacobson agreement).} The Algebraic
Channel derivation of (the Einstein field equations) through Theorem 9
(Diff factorisation + Lovelock + Newtonian matching) and the Geometric
Channel derivation of (the Einstein field equations) through Theorem 14
(Jacobson thermodynamic chain) yield identical field equations with two
shared inputs and otherwise disjoint intermediate machinery. The shared
inputs are the local matter conservation \(\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0\)
(Theorem 9 Step 4, which Theorem 14 Step 5 uses to select the Einstein
tensor over the bare Ricci tensor, exactly as Jacobson does) and the
Newtonian matching that fixes the coupling constant (Theorem 9 Step 6;
in the Geometric Channel it fixes \(\eta = 1/4G\), Theorem 12). The
remaining intermediate-machinery sets are
\(M(\Pi_A) = \{\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}},\, \mathrm{Diff}(M_G)\text{-invariance of the gravitational sector},\, u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2,\, \text{Noether II},\, \text{Lovelock 1971}\}\)
and
\(M(\Pi_B) = \{ S \propto A,\, T_U = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_B),\, \text{Clausius},\, \text{Raychaudhuri},\, \text{KMS} \}\),
with \(M(\Pi_A) \cap M(\Pi_B) = \varnothing\) (the \emph{Dual-Channel
Disjointness} (channel disjointness of the two channels) predicate
\(\mathrm{DCD}(\text{Einstein field equations})\) of Section 5.1, which
asserts that the named intermediate machinery sets of the two derivation
chains intersect only in the McGucken Principle itself and in the two
shared inputs just named).

The Geometric Channel is \emph{bi-signature}: it admits a Lorentzian
reading (with oscillating phase weight \(\exp(iS/\hbar)\) producing the
Feynman path integral) and a Euclidean reading (with real positive
measure weight \(\exp(-S_E/\hbar)\) producing the Wiener process and
horizon thermodynamics). The two are related by the McGucken--Wick
rotation \(\tau = x_4/c\) of Theorem 4. The derivational
\emph{exteriorisability} of the imaginary unit from the
geometric-propagation reading is what permits Geometric Channel to
bridge signatures while the Algebraic Channel remains Lorentzian-locked;
this is the Signature-Bridging Theorem (Theorem 15 below, imported from
{[}2, §5--6{]}).

\hypertarget{the-two-channels-are-disjoint-the-dual-channel-disjointness-of-the-two-gravity-derivations}{%
\subsubsection{5.5 The two channels are disjoint: the dual-channel
disjointness of the two gravity
derivations}\label{the-two-channels-are-disjoint-the-dual-channel-disjointness-of-the-two-gravity-derivations}}

\hypertarget{the-signature-bridging-theorem}{%
\paragraph{5.5.1 The Signature-Bridging
Theorem}\label{the-signature-bridging-theorem}}

\textbf{Theorem 15 (Signature-Bridging Theorem, {[}2, Theorem 5.1{]}).}
Let \(\mathrm{SIG}_L\) denote the Lorentzian metric signature
\((-,+,+,+)\) and \(\mathrm{SIG}_E\) the Euclidean signature
\((+,+,+,+)\). The McGucken--Wick rotation \(t \mapsto -i\tau\) with
\(\tau = x_4/c\) (Theorem 4 of {[}23{]}) is the unique coordinate
identification on the real four-dimensional McGucken manifold that:
\emph{(i) is induced by a single physical principle (the McGucken
Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\));}

\emph{(ii) maps Lorentzian and Euclidean signatures onto one another;}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{(\roman{enumi})}
\setcounter{enumi}{2}
\tightlist
\item
  preserves the physical content of \(x_4\)-expansion (the rate \(c\) is
  invariant under the identification);
\item
  supports two independent derivations of \(G_{\mu\nu}\) --- Algebraic
  Channel in \(\mathrm{SIG}_L\) and the Geometric Channel in
  \(\mathrm{SIG}_E\) --- that yield identical field equations.
  Properties (i)--(iv) are jointly satisfied by no other coordinate
  identification known to physics. The standard Wick rotation of quantum
  field theory is the formal shadow of (i)--(iv) when the physical
  reality of \(x_4\) is suppressed. \emph{Proof.} All three properties
  follow from integrating \(dx_4/dt = ic\). \textbf{(i) The rotation.}
  Integrating \(dx_4/dt = ic\) under the source-origin convention
  \(x_4(0)=0\) gives \(x_4 = ict\); written in proper-time units
  \(\tau = x_4/c\) this is the substitution \(t \mapsto -i\tau\), the
  McGucken--Wick rotation, a coordinate identification on the real
  manifold \(M_G\) rather than an analytic continuation into a complex
  plane. \textbf{(ii) The Lorentzian signature.} On the constraint
  surface parametrised by the embedding
  \(\iota:(t,x_1,x_2,x_3)\mapsto(x_1,x_2,x_3,ict)\), the pullback of the
  Euclidean four-metric \(g_E = dx_1^2+dx_2^2+dx_3^2+dx_4^2\) is
  \[\iota^* g_E = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + d(ict)^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2\,dt^2,\]
  since \(d(ict) = ic\,dt\) and \((ic)^2 = -c^2\): the Lorentzian line
  element of signature \((-,+,+,+)\). The single algebraic fact
  \(i^2 = -1\) converts the Euclidean fourth term into the Lorentzian
  time term. \textbf{(iii) The boost--rotation bridge and KMS
  periodicity.} A Lorentz boost of rapidity \(\eta\) in \((x,t)\)
  becomes, under \(t\mapsto -i\tau\) with \(\theta:=-i\eta\), a
  Euclidean rotation by angle \(\theta\) in \((x,c\tau)\)
  (\(\cosh\eta\to\cos\theta\), \(\sinh\eta\to i\sin\theta\)); the
  \(2\pi\)-periodicity of that Euclidean rotation angle is, by the
  Kubo--Martin--Schwinger condition, the thermal periodicity in
  imaginary time that underlies the Unruh and Hawking temperatures
  (Theorem 13). The signature bridge, the Wick rotation, and the KMS
  thermal periodicity are thus one structure --- the Euclidean reading
  of the \(x_4\)-advance --- all forced by \(dx_4/dt = ic\). \(\square\)
\end{enumerate}

The Wick-rotation paper {[}3{]} establishes that thirty-four independent
inputs of quantum field theory, QM, and symmetry physics --- including
the Wick substitution itself, the convergence of the Euclidean path
integral, the \(+i\epsilon\) prescription, the Schrödinger-to-diffusion
correspondence, Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity, the KMS
condition, Gibbons--Hawking horizon regularity, the Hawking temperature,
the Matsubara formalism, the canonical commutator
\([\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar\), the path-integral weight
\(e^{iS/\hbar}\), the Minkowski--Euclidean action bridge
\(iS_M = -S_E\), the U(1) gauge phase, the Dirac spinor structure, and
the Born rule \(P = |\psi|^2\) --- descend from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) as
theorems.

\hypertarget{sec:channels-wick}{%
\paragraph{1.5.3.1 The Wick Rotation as a Theorem of the McGucken
Principle}\label{sec:channels-wick}}

Both Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel descend from
\(dx_4/dt = ic\). The Wick rotation \(\tau = x_4/c\) is itself a theorem
of the principle (Theorem 4 of {[}23{]}). The principle contains the
imaginary unit; the coordinate identification \(x_4 = ict\) is already
the Wick-rotated coordinate, with \(i\) absorbed into the relationship
between \(x_4\) and the real time \(t\). Integration of \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
along any worldline (null, timelike, spacelike) produces
\(x_4 = ic(t - t_0)\), with the imaginary unit appearing as a
derivational feature of the integration rather than as a separate
analytic-continuation procedure.

\hypertarget{are-the-algebraic-channel-and-the-geometric-channel-derivations-of-a-given-theorem-related-by-a-wick-rotation}{%
\subsubsection{Are the Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel
derivations of a given theorem related by a Wick
rotation?}\label{are-the-algebraic-channel-and-the-geometric-channel-derivations-of-a-given-theorem-related-by-a-wick-rotation}}

A natural reading of the dual-channel architecture is to ask whether the
two derivations of a given theorem are \emph{Wick rotations of each
other} --- whether applying the Wick rotation to the Algebraic Channel
derivation produces the corresponding Geometric Channel derivation, or
vice versa. The answer is no, and the reasons are worth stating
directly.

Applying the Wick rotation to the Algebraic Channel derivation produces
a Wick-rotated Algebraic Channel derivation. The Algebraic Channel
reasons through symmetry-group arguments --- the Lorentz and Poincaré
groups, the action functional, the Euler-Lagrange equations, Noether's
theorems, Lovelock uniqueness, operator algebra with canonical
commutators. Wick-rotating the Algebraic Channel argument changes the
signature of the metric, the form of the action functional, and the
phase of the path integral, but it does not change the \emph{mode of
reasoning}. The argument is still algebraic-symmetry reasoning; it is
just operating in Euclidean signature now.

Applying the Wick rotation to the Geometric Channel derivation produces
a Wick-rotated Geometric Channel derivation. The Geometric Channel
reasons through iterated-Sphere wavefront propagation, Huygens
construction, mode-counting on the Sphere surface, Brownian-motion
diffusion, Compton-phase rotation along \(x_4\). The McGucken Sphere as
a 2-surface with radius \(c(t - t_0)\) and the iterated-Sphere flow at
universal rate \(c\) are signature-invariant geometric objects: the
Sphere is the same Sphere whether one labels the time axis \(t\)
(Lorentzian) or \(\tau = x_4/c\) (Euclidean). Wick-rotating the
Geometric Channel argument transforms the time label but leaves the
iterated-Sphere geometric content invariant.

The Algebraic Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations
(Lovelock uniqueness from action variation, Algebraic Channel) and the
Geometric Channel derivation (Jacobson's thermodynamic chain on the
McGucken Sphere horizon, Geometric Channel) share no intermediate
machinery. The Geometric Channel derivation uses the Geometric Second
Law \(dS/dt > 0\), the Bekenstein--Hawking area law
\(S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)\) as \(x_4\)-mode counting on the horizon
sphere, the Unruh temperature \(T_U = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)\) as the
Wick-rotated \(x_4\)-boost periodicity, and the Clausius relation
\(\delta Q = T_U \delta S\) integrated through the Raychaudhuri equation
on a local Rindler horizon. None of these objects appears in the
Algebraic Channel Lovelock-uniqueness derivation. The two derivations
are \emph{channel-disjoint} at the level of intermediate machinery ---
the channel disjointness (dual-channel-disjoint) signature recorded in
{[}1, Part VII{]}. The Wick rotation, applied to either derivation, does
not produce the other.

What relates the two derivations is \emph{common descent from the
principle}. Both Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel trace back
to \(dx_4/dt = ic\). The cross-channel agreement on the same observable
theorem (here: the Einstein field equations
\(G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}\)) follows from both channels
deriving from the same principle, with no Wick-rotational relationship
between the two derivation chains themselves.

\hypertarget{where-the-mcguckenwick-rotation-enters-the-two-channel-derivation-the-four-distinct-derivational-levels-at-which-t-iux3c4-appears-as-a-theorem-of-dx_4dt-ic}{%
\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{5.5.2 Where the McGucken--Wick rotation
enters the two-channel derivation: the four distinct derivational levels
at which t → −iτ appears as a theorem of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\)}{5.5.2 Where the McGucken--Wick rotation enters the two-channel derivation: the four distinct derivational levels at which t → −iτ appears as a theorem of dx\_4/dt = ic}}\label{where-the-mcguckenwick-rotation-enters-the-two-channel-derivation-the-four-distinct-derivational-levels-at-which-t-iux3c4-appears-as-a-theorem-of-dx_4dt-ic}}

The Wick rotation enters the framework at four distinct derivational
levels:

\begin{enumerate}
\item *As a theorem of the principle (Theorem 4 of [23])*. The Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ is derivable from $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the imaginary-unit content of the rate. It is built into the integration of the principle, with no need to be postulated as an external analytic-continuation device.

\item *Used internally by the Algebraic Channel during its own derivations*. The Algebraic Channel derivation of the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy uses the Gibbons--Hawking--York Euclidean Schwarzschild action --- a Wick rotation applied within the Algebraic Channel argument to make the partition-function-periodicity computation work. The Algebraic Channel is not strictly Lorentzian; it Wick-rotates internally when the algebraic argument requires Euclidean signature.

\item *Used internally by the Geometric Channel during its own derivations*. The Geometric Channel derivation of the Geometric Second Law uses the Wick-rotated Brownian-motion diffusion equation, with $x_4 \to ic\tau_E$ converting the iterated-Sphere wavefront propagation into a heat-equation reading on the deformable spatial sector. The Geometric Channel is not strictly Euclidean either; it Wick-rotates internally when the geometric argument requires Lorentzian signature for the wavefront reading.

\item *As the differential diagnostic between the two channels*. The Algebraic Channel objects (the algebraic content of the master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, the Schrödinger time-derivative $i\hbar\partial_t$, the path-integral phase $e^{iS/\hbar}$) are signature-specific: they transform under the Wick rotation ($-c^2 \to +c^2$, $i\hbar\partial_t \to -\hbar\partial_\tau$, $e^{iS/\hbar} \to e^{-S_E/\hbar}$). The Geometric Channel objects (the McGucken Sphere as a 2-surface, the iterated-Sphere flow at universal $c$, the Sphere-mode count, the wavefront propagation) are signature-invariant. This is the QM corpus result [3, Theorem on Channel--Wick Asymmetry]: the Wick rotation acts as a derivational diagnostic by transforming Algebraic Channel content while preserving Geometric Channel content.
\end{enumerate}

The first three are \emph{uses} of the Wick rotation within or by the
principle. The fourth is the differential response of the two channels'
content under the rotation. None of the four is the standard
``Wick-rotate Algebraic Channel to get Geometric Channel'' relationship
that the bridge framing would suggest, because that relationship does
not hold: the two derivation chains are channel-disjoint at the level of
their intermediate machinery, and the Wick rotation does not bridge
between them.

\hypertarget{how-the-algebraic-and-geometric-channels-absorb-the-imaginary-unit-i-of-dx_4dt-ic-differently-explicit-i-in-the-algebraic-route-versus-geometric-absorption-in-the-wavefront-route}{%
\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{5.5.3 How the Algebraic and Geometric
channels absorb the imaginary unit i of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) differently:
explicit i in the algebraic route versus geometric absorption in the
wavefront
route}{5.5.3 How the Algebraic and Geometric channels absorb the imaginary unit i of dx\_4/dt = ic differently: explicit i in the algebraic route versus geometric absorption in the wavefront route}}\label{how-the-algebraic-and-geometric-channels-absorb-the-imaginary-unit-i-of-dx_4dt-ic-differently-explicit-i-in-the-algebraic-route-versus-geometric-absorption-in-the-wavefront-route}}

The two channels exploit the same dynamical principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
--- whose mere integrated coordinate shadow is the static identity
\(x_4 = ict\) --- through different absorptions of the imaginary unit:

\begin{itemize}
\item
  \emph{Algebraic Channel} absorbs \(i\) into the metric signature and
  operator coefficients: the Lorentzian signature \((-,+,+,+)\), the
  canonical commutator \([\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar\), the Schrödinger
  time-derivative \(i\hbar\partial_t\), the path-integral phase
  \(e^{iS/\hbar}\).
\item
  \emph{Geometric Channel} absorbs \(i\) into the rate of the
  fourth-dimension expansion: \(dx_4/dt = ic\) as the active rate, the
  iterated-Sphere wavefront propagation at universal \(c\), the Compton
  phase \(\Phi = \exp(-imc^2\Delta\tau/\hbar)\) along worldlines.
\end{itemize}

Both readings produce the same observable predictions because both
descend from the same principle.

\hypertarget{the-defining-characteristics-of-each-channel-the-algebraic-symmetry-reading-of-dx_4dt-ic-versus-the-geometric-propagation-reading-of-dx_4dt-ic}{%
\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{5.5.4 The defining characteristics of each
channel: the algebraic-symmetry reading of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) versus the
geometric-propagation reading of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\)}{5.5.4 The defining characteristics of each channel: the algebraic-symmetry reading of dx\_4/dt = ic versus the geometric-propagation reading of dx\_4/dt = ic}}\label{the-defining-characteristics-of-each-channel-the-algebraic-symmetry-reading-of-dx_4dt-ic-versus-the-geometric-propagation-reading-of-dx_4dt-ic}}

\textbf{Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry reading):} The Algebraic
Channel reads the integrated shadow \(x_4 = ict\) of the McGucken
Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) as a coordinate label and derives theorems
from the symmetry group of the label. The Lorentz group
\(\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)\), the Poincaré group \(\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)\), the
diffeomorphism group \(\mathrm{Diff}(M)\) and its factorisation,
Noether's theorems, Lovelock's uniqueness, variational principles with
action functionals, operator algebra with canonical commutators. The
master equation \(u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2\) in its Lorentzian-signature form
is the standard Algebraic Channel reading; the Wick-rotated Euclidean
form \(|u^\mu|^2_E = +c^2\) is also the Algebraic Channel object, used
internally when the partition-function argument requires Euclidean
signature. The defining feature is the \emph{mode of reasoning}:
symmetry-group arguments with algebraic operations on tensor fields.

\textbf{Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation reading):} The
Geometric Channel reads \(dx_4/dt = ic\) as an active wavefront
expansion and derives theorems from the iterated-Sphere flow. The
McGucken Sphere \(M^+_p(t)\) as a 2-surface in 3-space with radius
\(c(t-t_0)\) centred at the source apex, Huygens-Feynman wavefront
construction, Compton-phase uniformity
\(\Phi(q;p) = \exp(-i m c^2 \Delta\tau/\hbar)\) on the Sphere,
proper-time integrals \(\Delta\tau = \int dt' \sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}\) along
worldlines, the iterated-Sphere composition of the Feynman path
integral, the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy via mode-counting on the
horizon Sphere. The defining feature is the \emph{mode of reasoning}:
geometric-propagation arguments with wavefront content on a 2-surface.

The Algebraic Channel/Geometric Channel distinction is \emph{not} the
Lorentzian/Euclidean distinction; both channels operate in either
signature as the internal argument requires. The distinction is between
\emph{algebraic-symmetry reasoning on a coordinate label} and
\emph{geometric-propagation reasoning on an active wavefront}. These are
different modes of reasoning, not different signature conventions.

\hypertarget{what-each-channel-of-dx_4dt-ic-can-and-cannot-derive-on-its-own-and-why-the-einstein-field-equations-require-the-convergence-of-both}{%
\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{5.5.5 What each channel of \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
can and cannot derive on its own, and why the Einstein field equations
require the convergence of
both}{5.5.5 What each channel of dx\_4/dt = ic can and cannot derive on its own, and why the Einstein field equations require the convergence of both}}\label{what-each-channel-of-dx_4dt-ic-can-and-cannot-derive-on-its-own-and-why-the-einstein-field-equations-require-the-convergence-of-both}}

\textbf{Algebraic Channel alone} can derive every theorem of GR that
depends on the symmetry-group structure (Einstein field equations via
Lovelock, geodesic equation via variational principle, Killing-vector
conserved quantities, Lorentz invariance of \(c\) at the level of the
metric, light cone causal structure). The Algebraic Channel cannot
directly visualise what is dynamically active in the fourth dimension.
It presents the metric signature as a given, the four-velocity
normalisation as a constraint, and the imaginary unit \(i\) as appearing
in specific formulas without supplying a geometric content.

\textbf{Geometric Channel alone} can derive the iterated-Sphere
structure of wave propagation, the Huygens-Feynman path-integral
composition, the wavefront-realist reading of quantum mechanics, the
geometric content of the active fourth-dimension expansion, the
Bekenstein--Hawking entropy via mode-counting on the horizon Sphere, the
Jacobson thermodynamic derivation of the Einstein field equations. The
Geometric Channel cannot directly produce the operator-algebra structure
of quantum field theory (canonical commutators, raising and lowering
operators, S-matrix elements) without invoking Algebraic Channel reading
at specific points.

\textbf{Together}, the two channels supply the complete dual-channel
architecture: Algebraic Channel delivers the algebraic-symmetry content
underlying GR and QM; Geometric Channel delivers the
geometric-propagation content underlying the same theorems; the
cross-channel agreement on observables (the dual-channel-disjoint
signature, channel disjointness) is the derivational overdetermination
establishing the principle's physical reality.

\hypertarget{the-historical-record-how-the-disjoint-threads-the-wick-rotation-xux2084-ict-iux210fux209c-the-lorentzian-cuxb2-the-euclidean-path-integral-and-the-bekensteinhawking-wick-rotation-are-unified-as-readings-of-dx_4dt-ic}{%
\paragraph{\texorpdfstring{5.5.6 The historical record: how the disjoint
threads --- the Wick rotation, x₄ = ict, iℏ∂ₜ, the Lorentzian −c², the
Euclidean path integral, and the Bekenstein--Hawking Wick rotation ---
are unified as readings of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\)}{5.5.6 The historical record: how the disjoint threads --- the Wick rotation, x₄ = ict, iℏ∂ₜ, the Lorentzian −c², the Euclidean path integral, and the Bekenstein--Hawking Wick rotation --- are unified as readings of dx\_4/dt = ic}}\label{the-historical-record-how-the-disjoint-threads-the-wick-rotation-xux2084-ict-iux210fux209c-the-lorentzian-cuxb2-the-euclidean-path-integral-and-the-bekensteinhawking-wick-rotation-are-unified-as-readings-of-dx_4dt-ic}}

The recognition that all of these threads --- Wick rotation,
\(x_4 = ict\), \(i\hbar\partial_t\), the Lorentzian \(-c^2\), the
Euclidean path integral, the Bekenstein-Hawking Wick-rotated action, the
Compton phase \(e^{-imc^2\Delta\tau/\hbar}\) --- share the same
derivational content was invisible in the pre-McGucken physics
literature for the reasons identified in §6.0.9 below. The quantum field
theory community (Schwinger, Symanzik, Osterwalder-Schrader) developed
the Wick rotation as a formal analytic-continuation device without
recognising that it descends from a single physical principle. The GR
community (MTW, Wald, Carroll) abandoned the fourth coordinate
\(x_4 = ict\) at the textbook level (§6.3). The QM community read the
Schrödinger evolution's \(i\) as a calculational device without
identifying it with the perpendicularity of \(x_4\) to the spatial
three.

\subsubsection{5.6 Jacobson's own stated open problems, each resolved by

ic}\label{jacobsons-own-stated-open-problems-each-resolved-by-the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic}}
