\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c, as a spherically
symmetric wavefront --- the McGucken Sphere --- from every event of
spacetime. Ted Jacobson, the originator of the
gravity-from-thermodynamics derivation {[}1{]}, has across three decades
identified the foundations of that derivation as unresolved, and has
stated, in his own words, a specific set of open problems and
realizations. This section takes each of Jacobson's stated concerns and
demonstrates that it is resolved by dx₄/dt = ic, with the resolution
reproduced from the McGucken corpus {[}24, 29, 45{]} and each item shown
to descend from the one Principle. Jacobson's words are quoted verbatim
from his 2024/2025 primary-source interview; the corpus resolutions are
quoted verbatim from the flagship {[}29{]} and the thermodynamics paper
{[}24{]} and are not paraphrased here.

The flagship {[}29{]}, in §6.6.9.18, records the fact that frames this
section: ``Jacobson --- the originating author of the
gravity-thermodynamics unification --- has across three decades (1995,
2015, 2024) and three primary-source venues (peer-reviewed PRL,
peer-reviewed PRL, recorded video interview) \emph{consistently
identified the foundations of his derivation as unresolved at the
foundational-physics level}. The orthodox community has not closed the
gap.'' And it states the resolution's source: ``The foundational
principle dx₄/dt = ic at every event of 𝕄\_G is the foundational source
from which the 1995 derivation descends as Theorem 6.6.9.6 McGucken
Cascade of the present paper. The per-event McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) is the
foundational geometric primitive from which Jacobson's local Rindler
horizon at every spacetime point descends as a coordinate-system
representation.'' Each concern below is an instance of this one
resolution.

\hypertarget{gravity-somehow-already-knows-about-thermodynamics}{%
\paragraph{5.6.1 ``Gravity somehow already knows about
thermodynamics''}\label{gravity-somehow-already-knows-about-thermodynamics}}

Jacobson: ``Only if Einstein's equation works the way it does would the
second law of thermodynamics be upheld. But that's crazy, it seemed.
That means that gravity somehow already knows about thermodynamics.
Otherwise, why should it have even worked out that way?'' And: ``It's
almost as if classical gravity knew that it had to be prepared for
Hawking radiation.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. The framework supplies the reason gravity
``already knows'' thermodynamics: both are theorem chains of the one
Principle, so their agreement is not a coincidence to be explained after
the fact but a necessity of the shared derivation. General relativity is
derived from dx₄/dt = ic as a twenty-four-theorem chain {[}23{]};
thermodynamics is derived from the same Principle {[}24{]}; the Second
Law is T9 of {[}24{]} (strict \(dS/dt = (3/2)k_B/t > 0\)). Gravity
``knew'' about thermodynamics because the Einstein field equations and
the Second Law are two readings of the single expanding McGucken Sphere
--- gravity is the horizon-area reading of the Sphere's state-count Ω,
the Second Law is the +ic-oriented growth of that same Ω (§4, §6, §7).
The flagship {[}29{]} states the dissolution of the three-pillar framing
directly: ``Thermodynamics, gravity, and quantum mechanics are not three
foundational sciences to be unified. They are three
\emph{resolution-readings of one foundational fact} --- dx₄/dt = ic at
every event of 𝕄\_G --- observed at three distinct combinations of
leveling depth and channel emphasis.'' Gravity knows about
thermodynamics because there is one thing, read two ways.

\hypertarget{the-local-rindler-horizon-at-every-point-where-it-comes-from}{%
\paragraph{5.6.2 The local Rindler horizon ``at every point'' --- where
it comes
from}\label{the-local-rindler-horizon-at-every-point-where-it-comes-from}}

Jacobson: ``It had to be that everywhere could be like a black hole. So,
I invented this idea of a local Rindler horizon\ldots{} I constructed a
framework where I could view any point in spacetime as if it were
sitting on the horizon of a black hole, and then apply the same relation
between entropy and energy that works for black hole thermodynamics, and
require that it works for this point, and that point, and that point,
and every possible horizon.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. Jacobson had to \emph{posit} a local
Rindler horizon at every point; the framework \emph{derives} it. The
per-event McGucken Sphere Σ⁺(p) --- the spherically symmetric wavefront
expanding at +ic from every event p, which is what dx₄/dt = ic asserts
--- is the geometric primitive of which Jacobson's ``local Rindler
horizon at every point'' is the coordinate representation ({[}29{]}
§6.6.9.18). Jacobson's ``everywhere could be like a black hole'' is the
statement that every event carries an expanding Sphere; the null
wavefront of that expansion is the local horizon. Where Jacobson
introduced the local horizon as a construction, dx₄/dt = ic supplies it
as a theorem: the horizon at p is the light-cone of the Sphere's
expansion at p (GR Theorem 11 of {[}23{]}).

\hypertarget{jacobsons-reservation-interpretive-fuzziness-and-the-undefined-heat}{%
\paragraph{5.6.3 Jacobson's reservation: ``interpretive fuzziness'' and
the undefined
heat}\label{jacobsons-reservation-interpretive-fuzziness-and-the-undefined-heat}}

Jacobson: ``And that worked. It worked, you know, I don't know how much
you want to get into my reservations about it working, but it worked
modulo some, let's say, interpretive fuzziness, I think, and foundations
of what exactly I was doing with that.'' And on the higher-curvature
extension: ``I don't have a good enough control of the definition of the
heat in the Clausius relation. I don't have a good enough definition of
the local Rindler horizon because I have to take curvature into
account.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. The ``interpretive fuzziness'' is the
absence of a physical definition of the heat δQ and the horizon; dx₄/dt
= ic removes it by defining both physically. In the McGucken derivation
the heat crossing the horizon is the Compton-tick action content of the
matter Spheres crossing the Sphere's null cone (§5.4, Theorem 14 LTD
reading), the temperature is the Euclidean x₄-periodicity of the Sphere
(Theorem 13), and the entropy is the Compton-tick Planck-area cell count
on the horizon (Theorem 12). Each of Jacobson's ``fuzzy'' ingredients
--- heat, temperature, horizon, entropy --- is a defined consequence of
the Sphere's expansion, so the Clausius relation δQ = T δS is not an
imported premise but the McGucken identity that the Compton-tick heat
equals the temperature times the Sphere-state-count increment, every
factor a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic (§5.2.1). The foundations Jacobson
called unresolved are supplied by the Principle.

\hypertarget{the-finiteness-cutoff-problem-why-the-entanglement-entropy-is-finite}{%
\paragraph{5.6.4 The finiteness / cutoff problem: why the entanglement
entropy is
finite}\label{the-finiteness-cutoff-problem-why-the-entanglement-entropy-is-finite}}

Jacobson: ``Because there's an infinite number of them, it looks like
there's an infinite entanglement entropy\ldots{} That is like a problem
if you're thinking the entanglement entropy has something to do with the
Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, because the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy is
finite.'' His resolution was that gravity self-cuts-off: ``Once the
fluctuation and its partner get so close together that the gravitational
fluctuation they create engulfs them both in like a miniature horizon,
then it's not any more possible to separate them\ldots{} So it has to
cut itself off because of gravity. And the place it cuts itself off is,
you can argue in a hand-waving way, is at the right scale to match the
Bekenstein-Hawking entropy.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. Jacobson's cutoff is ``hand-waving''; the
framework supplies the finite count exactly. The Sphere's state-count Ω
is finite on the horizon because the Sphere's advance has a physical
one-cycle resolution --- the Compton tick, one action quantum h per
cycle (§2, §6.1) --- so the horizon carries a finite number of
Planck-area Compton-tick cells, N = A/ℓ\_P², one quarter of a nat each,
giving the finite Bekenstein-Hawking entropy S = k\_B A/(4ℓ\_P²)
(Theorem 12 of {[}23{]}, §A.3). There is no infinity to cut off: the
count is finite from the outset because dx₄/dt = ic advances one Compton
tick at a time, not continuously without bound. What Jacobson had to
obtain by an uncontrolled gravitational cutoff, the Principle supplies
as the intrinsic finite resolution of the expanding Sphere.

\hypertarget{discreteness-versus-the-continuum-jacobsons-reversal}{%
\paragraph{5.6.5 Discreteness versus the continuum --- Jacobson's
reversal}\label{discreteness-versus-the-continuum-jacobsons-reversal}}

Jacobson: ``Initially, when I first confronted the finiteness of black
hole entropy\ldots{} I thought perhaps the answer was that there's some
discreteness and there's some shortest cutoff. But\ldots{} no, no, no,
it's because at very short scales, the gravitational interaction is so
strong that spacetime is very curved\ldots{} this line of thinking led
me away from the idea of discrete space and time, at least for the
moment. I think in the long run, it will lead back to that.'' And:
``Whether that refined understanding will require space and time to be
discrete, ultimately, I don't know.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. Jacobson oscillates between discrete and
continuous; the framework resolves the dichotomy by providing both at
once. The flagship {[}29{]} states, at Proposition 10.8: ``The McGucken
dx₄/dt = ic framework provides both geometric continuity and action
discreteness simultaneously --- at different cascade-level aspects of
the same principle dx₄/dt = ic --- resolving the long-standing dichotomy
between discrete-spacetime programs (causal sets, loop quantum gravity,
Regge calculus, spin foams) and continuous-spacetime programs (standard
QFT, Lorentz-invariance tests). Geometric content is continuous:
spacetime points form a continuum.'' The Sphere's geometric advance is
continuous (the coordinate x₄ = ict is a real-manifold continuum), while
its action content is discrete (one quantum h per Compton cycle).
Jacobson's ``I don't know whether space is discrete'' is answered: it is
continuous in its geometry and discrete in its action, both from dx₄/dt
= ic --- the finiteness of the horizon entropy comes from the
discreteness of the action count, not from a discreteness of the
geometric continuum.

\hypertarget{the-metric-as-emergent-from-the-vacuum-fluctuations}{%
\paragraph{5.6.6 The metric as emergent from the vacuum
fluctuations}\label{the-metric-as-emergent-from-the-vacuum-fluctuations}}

Jacobson: ``If you just show me the vacuum fluctuations, I can measure
the metric in the behavior of the vacuum fluctuations. The metric is
encoded in the nature of the correlations of the vacuum fluctuations. So
the metric is kind of superfluous and redundant in the description if I
just knew the vacuum fluctuations\ldots{} I suspect that this is a
passing stage in the history of physics that we treat those two things
separately, but there isn't really a separate metric degree of
freedom.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. Jacobson suspects the metric and the
quantum fields are not two independent things but one; the framework
establishes exactly that, and identifies the one thing as the Sphere.
The Minkowski metric and the Hilbert-space state are cogenerated from
dx₄/dt = ic in the flagship {[}29{]}: the Lorentzian metric ds² is the
squared-rate reading of the Sphere's advance (the (ic)² = −c² of Lemma
2.5), and the wavefunction ψ is the amplitude reading of the same
advance (§3). They are not two degrees of freedom but two readings of
the one expanding Sphere, which is precisely Jacobson's ``there isn't
really a separate metric degree of freedom.'' The correlations of the
vacuum fluctuations encode the metric because both the fluctuations and
the metric are the Sphere: the metric is the geometric reading, the
fluctuations the amplitude reading, of dx₄/dt = ic.

\hypertarget{entanglement-is-what-makes-space-connected}{%
\paragraph{5.6.7 Entanglement is what makes space
connected}\label{entanglement-is-what-makes-space-connected}}

Jacobson: ``The fact that space in this room is connected from this side
of my imaginary boundary to this side has something to do with the fact
that empty space is full of entangled vacuum fluctuations.'' And: if the
entanglement were removed, ``I would have an infinite negative energy
density. I would have a state whose gravitational back reaction is so
big that it probably sort of cleaves space into two halves.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. The connectivity of space is the overlap
of the McGucken Spheres expanding from neighboring events. Every event
emits a Sphere at +ic; adjacent events' Spheres overlap, and that
overlap is the vacuum entanglement Jacobson describes --- the shared
Compton-tick content across the boundary. Space is connected because the
Spheres from the two sides interpenetrate (the Huygens-wavefront
composition, §3.12, {[}44{]}); to remove the entanglement would be to
stop the Spheres from overlapping, which is to cleave the expansion,
exactly Jacobson's ``cleaves space into two halves.'' The
entanglement-connectivity Jacobson identifies is the Sphere-overlap
structure of dx₄/dt = ic.

\hypertarget{the-hold-the-volume-fixed-striking-result}{%
\paragraph{5.6.8 The ``hold the volume fixed'' striking
result}\label{the-hold-the-volume-fixed-striking-result}}

Jacobson: ``When I said that I assumed the entropy is maximized, I had
to say maximum with something held fixed\ldots{} it turned out I had to
hold the spatial volume of the ball fixed in order for the Einstein
equation I inferred to have the correct relationship between the
gravitational constant and the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy\ldots{} I find
that really striking because it means that there's something special
about holding the volume fixed. I have no idea why I should hold it
fixed.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. Jacobson has no idea why the spatial
volume must be held fixed; the framework supplies a natural physical
reading. The McGucken Sphere expands isotropically at +ic from the
center of the ball, and the state-count Ω that must be maximized is the

\textbf{6.6.9.18.A The Four Open Problems}

Carnot 1824 articulated the empirical irreversibility of heat-engine
cycles; Clausius 1850-1865 formalized the Second Law and coined
``entropy''; Boltzmann 1872 derived the H-theorem from kinetic theory;
Loschmidt 1876 raised the reversibility objection (no time-asymmetric
output from time-reversible Newtonian inputs); Boltzmann 1877 retreated
to statistical reinterpretation. The foundational question --- what is
the geometric source of the strict-positive \(dS/dt\) at every event,
given that the underlying microscopic dynamics is strict-time-reversible
--- has remained open in the orthodox literature for 150 years.

Schrödinger 1926 derived the linear deterministic time-reversible wave
equation; Born 1926 introduced the statistical interpretation; von
Neumann 1932 formalized the orthodox structure with the Type I / Type II
distinction (continuous unitary versus discontinuous projection). The
apparent contradiction --- Type I is strict-time-reversible-unitary
while Type II is strict-time-asymmetric-non-unitary --- is the core
content of the quantum measurement problem. Copenhagen, pilot-wave,
many-worlds, and decoherence-based interpretations have each been
articulated; no foundationally complete resolution generally accepted by
the physics community has emerged.

Lorenz 1963 (``Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow,'' \emph{J. Atmos. Sci.}
20, 130-141) discovered sensitive dependence on initial conditions in a
deterministic three-variable ODE system: arbitrarily small differences
in initial conditions produce arbitrarily large differences in
trajectories over time. The foundational question --- what is the
structural source of the apparent randomness in deterministic systems,
when the underlying ODE is strictly deterministic --- has remained open
in the orthodox literature for 60+ years.

Cauchy 1822 derived the equations of fluid motion; Stokes 1845 added the
viscous term; Leray 1934 proved existence of weak solutions; Fefferman
2000 articulated the Clay Millennium Prize Problem at the official
launch of the seven prizes. The foundational question --- whether the 3D
incompressible Navier-Stokes equation admits globally smooth solutions
for all smooth initial data, or whether finite-time blowup occurs ---
has remained open for 200 years (since Cauchy) and 25 years (since the
Clay launch).

\textbf{6.6.9.18.B The Structural Identification --- Four Expressions of
the Same dx₄/dt = ic Non-Recognition}

The four problems share a common structural feature: each involves a
tension between time-symmetric microscopic content (Newtonian molecular
dynamics for (I); unitary Schrödinger evolution for (II); deterministic
ODE for (III); time-reversible Navier-Stokes equation for (IV)) and
time-asymmetric macroscopic content (irreversibility for (I); projective
measurement collapse for (II); apparent randomness for (III); the
empirical absence of singularities for (IV)). The orthodox tradition
treats each tension as a separate problem; the McGucken framework
recognizes all four as expressions of the same structural
non-recognition.

\textbf{The structural diagnosis:} in each of the four problems, the
orthodox tradition has the Algebraic Channel content of dx₄/dt = ic (the
time-symmetric algebraic-symmetry structure) but lacks the dx₄/dt = ic
Geometric Channel content (the geometric-propagation reading with the

§6.6.9.12.D); time-asymmetric output cannot descend from T-symmetric
inputs alone. The orthodox tradition's structural blindness to this

\(+ic\) direction supplying the time-asymmetric content --- closes all

\textbf{6.6.9.18.F Why Jacobson Unified Two and Not Three --- The
Leveling Cascade as Causal Mechanism, the Counting-vs-Dynamics Seam, and
the Three-Resolution-Readings Resolution of the Three-Pillar Framing}

A deeper structural-historical diagnosis is available for the central
observation of §§6.6.9.A-6.6.9.18 --- that Jacobson 1995 and the
Padmanabhan extensions 2002-2015 unified gravity with thermodynamics but
did not unify quantum mechanics with the same null-surface structure,
even though their own machinery (Bisognano-Wichmann, Unruh, vacuum
entanglement entropy) was quantum-mechanical at its core. The
historical-disciplinary inheritance that backgrounded quantum content
from both pre-1925 gravity and pre-1925 thermodynamics is the
\emph{downstream consequence} of a deeper structural cause --- the
leveling cascade of the central limit theorem operating on the per-event
Compton-coupling content (Von Neumann 1932 Introductory Considerations,
anchored verbatim in §6.6.9.12.F) to produce the macroscopic continuum
observables that those disciplines were founded on. Jacobson's
unification operates at the seam where the leveling cascade has been
most thoroughly applied, and that seam is structurally upstream of
quantum-mechanical dynamics for reasons that can be made precise. The
present sub-subsection develops the diagnosis in seven structural moves.

\textbf{6.6.9.18.F.1 The Leveling Cascade as the Causal Mechanism}

The leveling cascade is the structurally specific mechanism by which
physical reality at the foundational per-event level --- McGucken Sphere
expansion at \(+ic\) at every event of \(\mathbb{M}_G\), with
matter-tier Compton-coupling at \(\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar\) --- produces
the macroscopic continuum observables on which the historical
disciplines of gravity and thermodynamics were founded. The
Lindeberg-Lévy central limit theorem applied to the ensemble of
\(\sim 10^{23}\) Compton-coupled matter wavefronts in any macroscopic
body of mole-order extent forces Gaussian-leveling of the per-event
content with fractional fluctuations of order \(N^{-1/2}\), far below
any pre-1925 instrumental resolution.

For matter at electron mass scale, the Compton angular frequency is \[
\omega_C^{(e)} = \frac{m_e c^2}{\hbar} \approx 7.76 \times 10^{20}\,\text{rad/s},
\] equivalently a Compton frequency of
\(\nu_C^{(e)} \approx 1.24 \times 10^{20}\) Hz. For matter at proton
mass scale, \(\omega_C^{(p)} \approx 1.43 \times 10^{24}\) rad/s. These
are the per-event Compton-coupling rates at which individual matter
wavefronts oscillate against \(x_4\)-advance, per Proposition 2.2 of the
present paper and Theorems 4 and 5 of {[}MG-Thermo/2026{]}. The relevant
numerical comparison for any pre-quantum experimental tradition is the
ratio of \(\omega_C\) to the temporal resolution of available
instrumentation.

A nineteenth-century steam engine operating with \(\sim 1\) mole of
working substance contains \(N \approx 6.02 \times 10^{23}\) molecules.
At standard temperature and pressure, the inter-molecular collision rate
per molecule is \(\sim 10^{10}\,\text{s}^{-1}\), giving an aggregate
ensemble collision rate of
\(\sim 10^{33}\,\text{s}^{-1}\,\text{mole}^{-1}\), with each collision
being a physical Wick-rotation measurement event at the molecular tier
(Theorem 26 of {[}MG-Thermo/2026{]}, anchored in §6.6.9.12.C of the
present paper).

Human perceptual resolution is bounded above by the visual
flicker-fusion threshold (\(\sim 16\) Hz, corresponding to
\(\sim 10^{-2}\,\text{s}\)) and mechanical-inertial response thresholds
(\(\sim 10^{-2}\,\text{s}\) to \(10^{-3}\,\text{s}\)). The fastest
pre-1925 instrumentation (early oscilloscopes, fast photography) reached
\(\sim 10^{-4}\,\text{s}\) to \(10^{-5}\,\text{s}\) resolution. None of
these temporal scales is within a factor of \(10^{15}\) of the
Compton-coupling frequency \(\omega_C\).

Within one human perceptual window of \(\sim 10^{-3}\,\text{s}\), the
ensemble of \(\sim 10^{23}\) molecules in a mole of working substance
experiences \(\sim 10^{30}\) Wick-rotation events per mole. Applying the
Lindeberg-Lévy CLT to \(\sim 10^{30}\) approximately-independent events
forces a Gaussian leveling with standard deviation
\(\sqrt{N} \sim 10^{15}\), meaning fractional fluctuations scale as
\(N^{-1/2} \sim 10^{-15}\). This is fifteen orders of magnitude below
any nineteenth-century instrumental resolution. The leveling was total.
What Carnot 1824, Kelvin 1848, Clausius 1850-1865, and Boltzmann 1872
observed was the leveled-out signature of the per-event content with
fractional fluctuations of order \(10^{-15}\), while the per-event
content itself oscillated thirty orders of magnitude below their
temporal resolution. The empirical signatures available to those
disciplines were structurally separated from the per-event
quantum-mechanical content by the leveling cascade.

The disciplines of phenomenological thermodynamics (Carnot 1824 onward),
Newtonian gravity (1687 onward) on \(\sim 10^{57}\)-atom planetary
bodies, and General Relativity (Einstein 1916) on smoothly-distributed
mass-energy tensor fields, all descended from observational regimes in
which the central limit theorem had already operated thoroughly between
the per-event quantum-mechanical content (which existed but was
inaccessible to pre-1925 instrumentation) and the empirical signature
(which was leveled-out to fractional fluctuations of order \(10^{-15}\)
or smaller). The disciplines that descended from those observations had
structurally no access to the per-event quantum content. The
historical-disciplinary inheritance documented in §6.6.9.14.E is the
consequence; the leveling cascade is the cause.

\textbf{6.6.9.18.F.3 Counting versus Dynamics --- the Structural Seam
Diagnosis}

The seam Jacobson found in 1995 is structurally upstream of
quantum-mechanical dynamics. The diagnosis can be made precise: the
orthodox program from Carnot 1824 through Boltzmann 1872 through
Bekenstein 1973 through Jacobson 1995 to 't Hooft 1993 and Susskind 1995
holographic principle is a \emph{counting program}. It counts
microstates, modes, Planck cells, degrees of freedom. The counting
yields thermodynamic and gravitational relations because the counting
captures \emph{how much there is}, not \emph{how it evolves}.

\textbf{Counting statements:}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Boltzmann entropy \(S = k_B \ln \Omega\) --- a statement about the
  \emph{number} of microstates compatible with given macroscopic
  constraints. Counts states.
\item
  Clausius relation \(\delta Q = T\,dS\) --- a statement about energy
  flow and entropy change at the equilibrium level. Captures the
  relation between leveled-out energy transfer and the change in the
  number of microstates. No dynamical content beyond the
  equilibrium-state relation.
\item
  Bekenstein-Hawking entropy \(S_{BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)\) --- a
  statement about the \emph{number} of Planck cells on a horizon. Counts
  the holographic-screen degrees of freedom.
\item
  Holographic principle ('t Hooft 1993, Susskind 1995) --- a statement
  about the bound on the \emph{number} of degrees of freedom in a
  spatial region by the area of its boundary in Planck units. Counting
  bound.
\item
  Jacobson 1995 equation of state --- Einstein field equations as the
  relation between energy flux \(\delta Q\) across a Rindler horizon and
  the change in horizon area-as-entropy \(dS = dA/(4\ell_P^2 k_B)\). The
  derivation operates entirely at the equilibrium-counting level; the
  dynamical content is the field-evolution that \emph{results} from the
  equation of state, not the per-state evolution that \emph{underlies}
  the counting.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Dynamical statements:}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Schrödinger equation \(i\hbar\,\partial_t \psi = \hat{H}\psi\) --- a
  statement about how \emph{individual states evolve} along the
  \(x_4\)-direction. Specifies the per-state dynamics, not the count of
  states.
\item
  Heisenberg commutation relation \([\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar\) --- a
  statement about the \emph{algebra of observables on the state space}.
  Specifies the operator-level perpendicular-direction structure (§9.3.4
  of the present paper), not the count of states.
\item
  Born rule \(P(x) = |\psi(x)|^2\) --- a statement about \emph{how
  individual state evolution connects to measurement outcomes}.
  Specifies the per-measurement dynamics, not the count of states.
\item
  Wigner classification of particles via representations of the Poincaré
  group --- a statement about the \emph{symmetry structure of individual
  quantum states}. Per-state, not aggregate.
\end{itemize}

The distinction is structural. Counting statements aggregate over
individual entities to produce relations among aggregates. Dynamical
statements specify how individual entities evolve. The Clausius relation
\(\delta Q = T\,dS\) contains no dynamical content beyond the
equilibrium-state relation; the Schrödinger equation
\(i\hbar\,\partial_t \psi = \hat{H}\psi\) specifies dynamics with no
aggregate content. Jacobson's unification ran along the counting seam

state --- and could not have included quantum-mechanical dynamics within
the formalism he used, because his formalism is structurally a counting

ic Geometric Channel content of §6.6.9.12.A-C, §6.6.9.13.A-C) \emph{and}

\textbf{6.6.9.18.F.4 The
Quantum-Mechanics-Has-No-Large-\(N\)-Predecessor Structural Asymmetry}

A structural asymmetry between quantum mechanics and the other two
pillars accounts for why Jacobson's ensemble-level unification does not
naturally include quantum mechanics. Gravity and thermodynamics both
have preexisting large-\(N\) ensemble-level sciences as their
macroscopic phenomenological predecessors; quantum mechanics does not.

Newtonian gravity was developed as the science of large-\(N\) aggregated
mass distributions: planets (\(N \sim 10^{50}\)), moons, ships, lead
spheres in Cavendish's apparatus (\(N \sim 10^{24}\)). Newton's
\(F = G m_1 m_2/r^2\) treats \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) as smoothly-aggregated
point masses, with no per-atom content. The classical theory of gravity
at the planetary level existed as a complete macroscopic
phenomenological framework for two centuries before quantum mechanics
existed as a foundational concept.

Phenomenological thermodynamics was developed as the science of
large-\(N\) molecular ensembles averaged into continuous state
variables. Carnot's cycle treats the working substance as a continuum
with \((P, V, T)\) defined at every interior point. The classical theory
of thermodynamics existed as a complete macroscopic phenomenological
framework for a century before quantum mechanics existed as a
foundational concept. The Boltzmann-Gibbs statistical-mechanical
retrofit (1872-1902) added microscopic interpretation but retained the
large-\(N\) ensemble structure as foundational.

Quantum mechanics was discovered at the \emph{individual atomic system}
scale --- not at the aggregate scale. The defining experiments of the
early QM period were single-atom-class experiments:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{Stern-Gerlach 1922} --- single beam of silver atoms split into
  discrete components, revealing per-atom angular-momentum quantization.
\item
  \emph{Davisson-Germer 1927} --- single electron beam on a single Ni
  crystal producing discrete diffraction maxima, revealing per-electron
  wave behavior.
\item
  \emph{Hydrogen line spectra} (Bohr 1913 retrospective; Balmer-Rydberg
  formula 1885 as empirical input) --- discrete spectral lines as
  evidence of per-atom energy quantization.
\item
  \emph{Compton 1923} --- per-photon scattering off per-electron with
  momentum exchange, revealing per-particle quantum kinematics.
\item
  \emph{Photoelectric effect} (Einstein 1905; Millikan experimental
  verification 1916) --- per-photon energy quantization as \(E = h\nu\)
  at the single-photon level.
\end{itemize}

The historical sequence runs from individual atomic systems \emph{up} to
aggregated quantum statistical mechanics (Bose-Einstein 1924,
Fermi-Dirac 1926), not from aggregated \emph{down} to individual.
Quantum statistical mechanics is the ensemble form of quantum mechanics;
quantum mechanics is not the small-\(N\) form of any pre-existing
classical ensemble science. There is no large-\(N\) quantum-mechanical
ensemble that existed as a macroscopic phenomenological theory before
being identified as quantum.

Gravity-thermodynamics unification works naturally at the ensemble level
because both are ensemble sciences with leveling cascades fully
operative. Quantum mechanics does not fit at the ensemble level because
it is not an ensemble science --- it is the per-state
dynamical-evolution science accessed at the single-atom-system
resolution. To include quantum mechanics in the unification, the
unification must operate at a level \emph{below} the ensemble --- the
per-event Compton-coupling level --- where the McGucken Principle's
dynamical content is accessible at every event of \(\mathbb{M}_G\).
Jacobson's seam was the ensemble seam; the McGucken seam is the
per-event seam, one cascade level below.

The structural asymmetry is therefore not a defect of quantum mechanics;
it is a feature of where the leveling cascade operates. The other two
pillars were observable historically only after the leveling had
operated thoroughly; quantum mechanics became observable only when the
leveling could be partially bypassed via single-system experiments. The
disciplines occupy structurally distinct cascade levels because of the
leveling depth required to observe each.

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c, as a spherically
symmetric wavefront --- the McGucken Sphere --- from every event of
spacetime, carrying one quantum of action h per Compton cycle. Erik
Verlinde, the originator of the entropic-gravity derivation {[}2{]}, has
stated in his own words a specific set of realizations, open problems,
and things his programme is still missing. This section takes each and
demonstrates that it is resolved by dx₄/dt = ic, with the resolution
grounded in the McGucken corpus {[}23, 24, 29, 45, 46{]} and each item
shown to descend from the one Principle. Verlinde's words are quoted
verbatim from his 2025 primary-source interview; the corpus resolutions
are quoted verbatim from the flagship {[}29{]} and are not paraphrased,
abbreviated, or altered here.

\hypertarget{verlindes-claim-to-be-more-fundamental-than-jacobson-and-its-resolution}{%
\paragraph{5.7.1 Verlinde's claim to be more fundamental than Jacobson,
and its
resolution}\label{verlindes-claim-to-be-more-fundamental-than-jacobson-and-its-resolution}}

Verlinde: ``Ted Jacobson certainly was the first to realize that this
idea\ldots{} that there's some relationship between the horizon and
entropy, these areas and entropy, can be used to derive the equations,
the Einstein equations.'' But he distinguishes his own programme: ``what
Jacobson does, he derives the third law. Because if you derive
Einstein's equations, you also derive Newton's third law. But you don't
tell me how inertia {[}works{]}.'' And on the circularity he sees in
assuming spacetime: ``there's something circular about the reasoning,
because assuming spacetime also is assuming its geometry. You cannot
derive its geometry from something there. So what I realized is
that\ldots{} the first thing that you have to get to is understanding
spacetime. And there's something more fundamental than just the
gravitational laws.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. Verlinde is correct that a foundation must
derive spacetime rather than assume it, and must derive inertia, not
only the field equations. The McGucken Principle does both, and does
them from the one physical fact. Spacetime is not assumed: the
Lorentzian metric is derived from dx₄/dt = ic as the squared-rate
reading of the Sphere's advance, the (ic)² = −c² of Lemma 2.5 (§3,
{[}29{]}) --- the metric ds² = −c²dt² + \textbar dx\textbar² is the
coordinate integral of the expanding fourth dimension, so the geometry
Verlinde says cannot be assumed is derived. Inertia is not left
unexplained: the inertia paper {[}46{]} derives inertial mass as the
magnitude of the fourth-momentum at spatial rest, m =
\textbar P₄\textbar/c --- a particle at rest carries all its momentum in
the x₄-advance, and its resistance to acceleration is the resistance of
that x₄-momentum to being redirected into the spatial slice --- and from
this single identification derives, all from dx₄/dt = ic, the mass-shell
\textbar u\textbar{} = c, the rest energy E₀ = mc², Newton's first law,
Newton's second law F = ma in full relativistic generality, and the
weak, Einstein, and strong equivalence principles (§3.13 of the present
paper, {[}46{]}). What Verlinde correctly demanded beyond Jacobson ---
the derivation of spacetime and of inertia --- the McGucken Principle
supplies as theorems of the expanding Sphere.

\hypertarget{theres-something-more-fundamental-more-microscopic-the-theory-verlinde-says-must-exist-but-cannot-name}{%
\paragraph{5.7.2 ``There's something more fundamental, more
microscopic'' --- the theory Verlinde says must exist but cannot
name}\label{theres-something-more-fundamental-more-microscopic-the-theory-verlinde-says-must-exist-but-cannot-name}}

Verlinde: ``I believe more that what we will discover are things that
are eventually understood from assuming that there's something more
fundamental, more microscopic going on, and that the laws that we are
discovering are kind of more emergent from that underlying more
fundamental description. Maybe we don't really need to know what this
fundamental description is.'' And: ``there may be no final theory of
physics\ldots{} Just the idea that we can find the final laws'' --- he
doubts.

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. The ``something more fundamental, more
microscopic'' that Verlinde says must exist, and that he suspects may be
unknowable, is dx₄/dt = ic: the physical fact that the fourth dimension
expands at c from every event. Where Verlinde says ``maybe we don't
really need to know what this fundamental description is,'' the McGucken
dx₄/dt = ic framework names it and derives the emergent laws from it
explicitly --- the Born rule, the Einstein field equations, the Second
Law, entropy, and inertia are each a theorem of the one Principle
(§3--§6, {[}23, 24, 29, 38, 46{]}). The flagship {[}29{]} states the
foundational status directly: ``For the first time in the history of
physics, both the Hilbert space and Minkowski space are derived from a
deeper physical principle.'' Verlinde's emergent laws are emergent from
exactly the microscopic fact he says must exist: the expanding McGucken
Sphere.

\hypertarget{entropy-as-counting-how-much-you-dont-know-grounded-in-the-spheres-state-count-ux3c9}{%
\paragraph{5.7.3 Entropy as ``counting how much you don't know'' ---
grounded in the Sphere's state-count
Ω}\label{entropy-as-counting-how-much-you-dont-know-grounded-in-the-spheres-state-count-ux3c9}}

Verlinde: ``there are some things that we know that we don't know, and
we can count, namely, how much we don't know. And this is what's called
entropy.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. Verlinde's ``count of how much you don't
know'' is the McGucken Entropy S = k\_B ln Ω, where Ω is the count of
distinguishable states the expanding McGucken Sphere passes through, one
Compton tick of action h at a time (§6). The count is physical, not
merely epistemic: it is the number of Compton-tick states of the
Sphere's advance in the region considered, read over the horizon as the
Bekenstein--Hawking gravitational entropy and over the directional
cross-section as the Born measure (§6, §7). Verlinde's entropy is the
same count Ω, now given its physical origin in the expanding Sphere
rather than left as a bookkeeping of ignorance.

\hypertarget{why-verlinde-is-fascinated-by-nonlocality-and-entanglement-spacetime-stitched-together-by-entanglement}{%
\paragraph{5.7.4 Why Verlinde is fascinated by nonlocality and
entanglement: spacetime ``stitched together by
entanglement''}\label{why-verlinde-is-fascinated-by-nonlocality-and-entanglement-spacetime-stitched-together-by-entanglement}}

Verlinde: ``spacetime may be stitched together by entanglement.'' And on
the emergence of the bulk: ``space doesn't emerge from entanglement per
se; it's just the bulk emerges from boundaries plus entanglement.'' The
Ryu--Takayanagi entanglement-entropy construction is his model for how
connectivity arises.

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. Nonlocality is created and carried by the
expanding McGucken Sphere: a local point at x₄ expands into a surface of
nonlocality. A single event begins as a local point; the McGucken
Principle dx₄/dt = ic makes that point advance --- the fourth dimension
expanding at c turns the point into an expanding spherical surface, the
McGucken Sphere. That surface is inherently nonlocal: one event's
advance now occupies an entire sphere of spatial locations at once, so a
single local origin is physically present across a nonlocal surface.
Nonlocality is therefore not an ingredient added to space, nor a
structure stitched in from an external entanglement theory; it is
generated by the expansion itself --- the point-to-surface expansion of
x₄ is the physical creation of nonlocality, and the Sphere carries that
nonlocality outward at c.~This mechanism is established in full in the
published McGucken nonlocality paper {[}71{]}, which derives quantum
nonlocality and quantum probability together from dx₄/dt = ic. That
paper states the mechanism verbatim: ``the nonlocal identity of the
expanding wavefront arise from one and the same source: the expanding
fourth dimension x₄ itself. The expansion of the fourth dimension x₄
manifests itself as a spherically symmetric locality growing at rate c
in our three spatial dimensions.'' The surface it generates is nonlocal
in a precise, enumerated sense: ``The surface of this expanding
wavefront is a geometric locality in five independent senses (foliation,
level sets, caustics, contact geometry, conformal geometry) --- and,
most deeply, as a sixth unifying sense: the canonical causal locality''
of Minkowski spacetime. On this surface a quantum is nonlocal until
measured: ``a photon surfing the wavefront inhabits the entire sphere of
nonlocality with equal geometric weight until a measurement event
localizes it in three spatial dimensions,'' so that ``Quantum
probability is therefore not an unexplained postulate but the direct
geometric consequence of the wavefront's nonlocal identity: the photon
has equal chance of being found at any point because all points on the
wavefront are'' geometrically equivalent {[}71{]}. The Born measure and
nonlocality are thus one object --- the expanding nonlocal surface of
dx₄/dt = ic --- exactly as the identity of §7 requires.

\textbf{The emergence of gravity from the nonlocal surface.} The
nonlocal surface the paper {[}71{]} derives is the same surface whose
horizon-area count is the gravitational entropy, and this is how gravity
emerges in the framework. The expanding sphere of nonlocality on which
the photon has equal geometric weight is the directional cross-section
whose SO(3)-invariant Compton-tick count gives the Born measure (§3,
§A.1); the same expanding Sphere, its Compton-tick cells counted on the
horizon it generates, gives the Bekenstein--Hawking gravitational
entropy S = k\_B A/(4ℓ\_P²) (§4.2, Theorem 12). Gravity emerges because
the nonlocal surface that stitches space --- the entanglement Verlinde
and Van Raamsdonk invoke --- is the surface whose area-counted
state-count Ω is gravity: the count Ω of §7 read over the horizon is the
gravitational entropy, read over the directional cross-section is the
Born measure, and the surface being counted is in both cases the one
expanding nonlocal surface that dx₄/dt = ic creates at every event
{[}48, 29{]}. Emergent gravity is the horizon-area reading of the
nonlocal surface of the expanding McGucken Sphere; the nonlocality (the
stitching) and the gravitational entropy (the emergence) are the one
surface counted two ways.

\textbf{The law governing the entanglement that stitches space.} The
nonlocality the expanding Sphere creates is not only produced but
governed by a stated law. The McGucken Nonlocality Principle {[}49{]}
establishes that ``all quantum nonlocality begins in locality,'' rooted
in dx₄/dt = ic, and states the governing law verbatim: ``\textbf{First
McGucken Law of Nonlocality.} Two quantum systems can exhibit nonlocal
correlations (entanglement) only if they have shared a common local
origin, or if each has interacted locally with members of a system that
itself shared a common local origin. Equivalently: only systems of
particles with intersecting light spheres'' can be entangled {[}49{]}.
This is the physical content of the entanglement that Verlinde and Van
Raamsdonk say stitches spacetime together: two regions are entangled ---
and therefore, in their programme, geometrically connected --- precisely
when their McGucken Spheres intersect, having issued from a shared local
origin. The stitching is the intersection of the expanding Spheres; the
First Law is its exact condition. The same paper {[}49{]} establishes
that the actual quantum experiments in which nonlocality is observed ---
Young's double-slit experiment, Wheeler's delayed-choice experiment, and
all quantum eraser experiments --- ``take place within the confines of
McGucken Spheres, and\ldots{} the apparent paradoxes of these
experiments dissolve once the full four-dimensional geometry of the
expanding x₄ geometry of a McGucken Sphere'' is recognized {[}49{]}. The
framework therefore treats the real experiments in the real universe,
not toy models on a boundary (§5.7.5): the entanglement that builds
spacetime and, through the horizon-area count, gravity is the
intersection structure of the McGucken Spheres in the actual universe
--- intersecting Spheres from a shared origin (First Law) give the
shared nonlocal surface, whose horizon-area count Ω is the gravitational
entropy from which gravity emerges (§4.2, §7). Entanglement builds
gravity because, by the First McGucken Law of Nonlocality, entanglement
is the intersection of the expanding Spheres whose counted surfaces are
gravity. The connectivity of space follows: every event emits such a
Sphere at +ic, adjacent events' Spheres overlap, and that overlap ---
the shared Compton-tick content across the region between them, itself a
nonlocal surface belonging to both origins --- is the physical content
that Verlinde and Van Raamsdonk describe as entanglement stitching space
together. The entanglement is the Algebraic-Channel operator shadow of
this Geometric-Channel fact: the physical nonlocal surface the expanding
Sphere creates and carries. The flagship {[}29{]} states the
identification for the Van Raamsdonk programme verbatim: ``Mark Van
Raamsdonk argues that spacetime connectivity is built from quantum
entanglement structure: disentangling regions of the bulk corresponds to
pulling them apart in geometry. The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel reach
into the origin of spacetime connectivity, with the entanglement
structure being an Algebraic Channel object (encoded in ρ) whose
geometric content is identified with the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel
spacetime connectivity.'' The entanglement Verlinde is fascinated by is
the Algebraic-Channel encoding of the Geometric-Channel Sphere-overlap:
space is connected because the Spheres interpenetrate (the
Huygens-wavefront composition, §3.12, {[}44{]}), and the entanglement
structure is the operator-level reading of that physical overlap.
Nonlocality fascinates Verlinde because, in an emergent-space programme,
connectivity cannot be assumed; dx₄/dt = ic supplies it as the overlap
of the expanding Spheres, so the nonlocal connectivity is a theorem, not
a mystery.

\hypertarget{adscft-requires-a-boundary-and-the-mcgucken-principle-requires-none}{%
\paragraph{5.7.5 AdS/CFT requires a boundary --- and the McGucken
Principle requires
none}\label{adscft-requires-a-boundary-and-the-mcgucken-principle-requires-none}}

Verlinde: ``the area that we define there is not totally emergent in the
sense that it already has some definition on the boundary. This is one
of the reasons why I think AdS/CFT is not the final story of how we can
understand spacetime, because we need to get rid of this idea that there
is a boundary, because our universe doesn't have a boundary of that
sort.'' And on anti-de Sitter space: ``It doesn't look at all like the
universe that we live in.'' He notes further that the microscopic
degrees of freedom are ``in equilibrium at horizons of black
holes\ldots{} at the horizon of a cosmological horizon. They're not in
equilibrium in some arbitrary point of spacetime.''

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. This is the sharpest contrast, and the
McGucken Principle resolves it completely: it requires no boundary and
no toy model, because dx₄/dt = ic operates at every event of the actual
universe. The holographic-screen and AdS/CFT constructions require a
boundary on which the microscopic theory lives and from which the bulk
is reconstructed; Verlinde himself states this boundary is not emergent
and that the real universe has no such boundary. The McGucken Sphere
expands from every spacetime event, so there is no privileged boundary
screen: the entropy is the count Ω of the Sphere's Compton-tick states
at each event, read over the local horizon that the expansion itself
generates (§4, §6, {[}29{]}). Verlinde's limitation that equilibrium
holds ``at horizons\ldots{} not in some arbitrary point of spacetime''
is exactly what the per-event Sphere removes --- every event carries its
own expanding Sphere and its own local horizon (the null wavefront of
that event's expansion, GR Theorem 11 of {[}23{]}), so the framework
applies at every point of the real, boundary-free, expanding universe,
not on the boundary of an anti-de Sitter toy model that, in Verlinde's
own words, ``doesn't look at all like the universe that we live in.''
The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework does not study a toy model with a
boundary; it studies the universe as it is, deriving the physics at
every one of its events from the one Principle dx₄/dt = ic.

\hypertarget{curt-jaimungals-question-if-gravity-is-thermodynamics-why-does-thermodynamics-give-dissipation-and-the-second-law-while-gravity-gives-structure}{%
\paragraph{5.7.6 Curt Jaimungal's question: if gravity is
thermodynamics, why does thermodynamics give dissipation and the Second
Law while gravity gives
structure?}\label{curt-jaimungals-question-if-gravity-is-thermodynamics-why-does-thermodynamics-give-dissipation-and-the-second-law-while-gravity-gives-structure}}

In the interview, the question is raised of how, if gravity and
thermodynamics are the same, thermodynamics yields dissipation and
increasing entropy (the Second Law, irreversibility) while gravity
yields structure (the stable geometric relations of the field
equations). This is the deepest conceptual question in the
entropic-gravity programme, and the two channels of dx₄/dt = ic answer
it exactly.

Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic. Dissipation-and-the-Second-Law and
structure-and-the-field-equations are the two channel-readings of the
one expanding McGucken Sphere, and they are not in conflict because they
read the same Sphere in two ways. The Geometric Channel is the raw
expanding advance --- the +ic-oriented, dissipative, irreversible
content of the Sphere's expansion --- and it yields the arrow of time,
entropy increase, and the Second Law (§4.1, §5.2.2, {[}45{]}). The
Algebraic Channel is the preserved, symmetry-rich, reversible residue
obtained when the expansion is read at fixed, frozen slices --- and it
yields the stable geometric structure, the symmetric relations of the
Einstein field equations (§5.2.2, §5.3, {[}45{]}). The dual-channel
paper {[}45{]} establishes that the Algebraic Channel is the channel of
what is preserved --- symmetry-rich, Lorentzian-locked, time-symmetric,
reversible --- while the Geometric Channel is the channel of what flows
--- asymmetry-rich, carrying the arrow of time and the dissipative,
volume-augmenting content of the Sphere's expansion.
Thermodynamics-gives-dissipation is the Geometric Channel read fully,
with the expansion kept; gravity-gives-structure is the same Sphere read
with the dissipative content frozen out, the Algebraic Channel. There is
one thing --- the expanding Sphere, dx₄/dt = ic --- and Curt's question
dissolves: the same count Ω, read as what flows gives the Second Law and
dissipation, read as what is preserved gives the geometric structure of
gravity. As established in §5.2.2, the two channels are not co-equal:
the Geometric Channel is the ontological physical reality --- the
expanding fourth dimension x₄, dx₄/dt = ic itself --- and it contains
all of physics, while the Algebraic Channel is derived from it, the
structure-and-symmetry residue left when the expansion is frozen.
Gravity's structure is the frozen reading; thermodynamics' dissipation
is the flowing reading; both are the one McGucken Sphere.

\hypertarget{the-published-falsifications-of-entropic-gravity-and-how-dxux2084dt-ic-does-the-mondmilgrom-phenomenology-without-them}{%
\paragraph{5.7.8 The published falsifications of entropic gravity, and
how dx₄/dt = ic does the MOND/Milgrom phenomenology without
them}\label{the-published-falsifications-of-entropic-gravity-and-how-dxux2084dt-ic-does-the-mondmilgrom-phenomenology-without-them}}

Verlinde's entropic-gravity programme faces specific published
falsifications and scope-limitations that the McGucken framework does
not share, because dx₄/dt = ic does not treat gravity as an entropic
force on a boundary but as the readings of the physically expanding
Sphere.

\textbf{The published falsifications of entropic gravity.} First, the
entropic force is not conservative: Kobakhidze and others establish that
the gravitational force in Verlinde's theory is not strictly
conservative {[}51{]}, a fatal property for a force that must admit a
potential. Second, quantum experiments on neutrons disprove the entropic
origin directly: Kobakhidze {[}51{]} argues that ``neutron interference
experiments and experiments on gravitational bound states of neutron
unambiguously disprove entropic origin of gravitation'' --- an entropic
(thermal, noisy) force would decohere the gravitationally bound neutron
states that are in fact observed intact in the qBounce ultracold-neutron
experiments. Third, this decoherence tension is a recognized problem in
the literature: entropic forces are intrinsically noisy and would
produce far more decoherence than is observed, a criticism serious
enough that defenders must construct special open-system models to evade
it {[}52{]}. Fourth, the programme is scope-limited and has no
cosmology: Verlinde's emergent gravity, in its published form, applies
only to isolated, spherically symmetric systems in a
dark-energy-dominated universe, has no direct description of lensing or
cosmology, and must assume a ΛCDM background even to be tested;
cluster-scale tests return mixed and discrepant results {[}53{]}. Each
of these is a property of treating gravity as an entropic force on a
holographic screen --- the very construction Verlinde himself flags as
requiring a boundary the real universe lacks (§5.7.5).

\textbf{The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework does not inherit these
problems.} Because gravity in the framework is not an entropic force but
the horizon-area reading of the state-count Ω of the expanding McGucken
Sphere (§4.2, §7), it is conservative (it derives the Einstein field
equations, §5, {[}23{]}), it does not impose thermal noise on quantum
states (unitary evolution is the frozen reading of the same Sphere,
§3.11, §5.2.2), it requires no boundary (dx₄/dt = ic operates at every
event of the real universe, §5.7.5), and it extends to a full cosmology
{[}50{]}.

\textbf{The MOND/Milgrom phenomenology, done better and with zero free
parameters.} Verlinde discusses Milgrom's Modified Newtonian Dynamics
and derives the deep-MOND acceleration scale and the baryonic
Tully--Fisher relation with zero free parameters --- a genuine
achievement the McGucken cosmology paper {[}50{]} credits as shared:
both obtain ``zero free parameters in the dark sector and the MOND scale
a₀ = cH₀/(2π).'' But the McGucken framework does the same phenomenology
from the physical geometry of dx₄/dt = ic --- x₄'s invariant expansion
at c against x₁, x₂, x₃ --- rather than from an entropic-force ansatz,
and it does so better and further:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The Baryonic Tully--Fisher Relation: the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic
  framework predicts a BTFR slope of exactly 4, derived as the geometric
  projection of x₄'s SO(3) expansion, with zero free parameters, tested
  against the full SPARC galaxy catalog {[}50{]}.
\item
  Fit quality against the MOND benchmark: the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic
  framework achieves χ²/N = 0.46 versus the McGaugh--Lelli MOND
  benchmark χ²/N = 1.46 --- a 50.3σ improvement, with zero free
  parameters {[}50{]}.
\item
  Full cosmology where Verlinde's programme has none: the McGucken
  cosmology takes first place across twelve independent observational
  tests --- including the dark-energy equation of state w₀ = −0.983 from
  the cumulative spatial contraction, within 1\% of the DESI 2024
  BAO+CMB+SN combined fit --- with zero free dark-sector parameters, and
  with independent 2025 confirmation from ACT DR6 {[}50{]}. This is
  precisely the cosmological and CMB domain in which Verlinde's emergent
  gravity ``isn't evolved enough as a theory'' and must borrow a ΛCDM
  background {[}53{]}.
\end{itemize}

The reason the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework succeeds where entropic
gravity is falsified and scope-limited is the reason stated throughout
this paper: gravity, the MOND acceleration scale, and the dark-sector
phenomenology are not an entropic force on a boundary but readings of
the physically expanding McGucken Sphere at every event of the actual
universe --- x₄ advancing at c against x₁, x₂, x₃ --- so the framework
is conservative, noise-free for coherent states, boundary-free, and
cosmologically complete, and it reproduces the MOND/Milgrom
phenomenology Verlinde reaches for with a better fit and zero free
parameters {[}50{]}.

\hypertarget{summary-what-emerges-from-dxux2084dt-ic-and-every-verlinde-concern-resolved}{%
\paragraph{5.7.9 Summary: what emerges from dx₄/dt = ic, and every
Verlinde concern
resolved}\label{summary-what-emerges-from-dxux2084dt-ic-and-every-verlinde-concern-resolved}}

Everything Verlinde reaches for descends from the one Principle. From
dx₄/dt = ic --- the physical fact that the fourth dimension expands at c
from every event, generating the McGucken Sphere --- the framework
derives the Lorentzian spacetime metric (Lemma 2.5, {[}29{]}), the Born
rule (§3, {[}38{]}), the Schrödinger and Dirac equations and the
canonical commutator and the uncertainty principle (§3, §3.14,
{[}38{]}), the Einstein field equations (§5, {[}23{]}), the Second Law
and entropy (§4, §6, {[}24{]}), the Bekenstein--Hawking area law and the
Unruh and Hawking temperatures (§4.2, §5, Theorems 12--13), inertia and
Newton's laws and F = ma (§3.13, {[}46{]}), least action (§3.13,
{[}44{]}), and the arrow of time (§6.2). Verlinde's demand for a
foundation deeper than Jacobson that derives spacetime and inertia
(§5.7.1), his stated need for a more-microscopic description he could
not name (§5.7.2), his entropy-as-counting (§5.7.3), his
entanglement-stitches-spacetime (§5.7.4), his requirement that a real
theory work without a boundary and without a toy model (§5.7.5), and
Curt Jaimungal's dissipation-versus-structure question (§5.7.6) are
each, item by item, a consequence of the one physical fact that the
fourth dimension expands at c from every event --- the McGucken
Principle dx₄/dt = ic, generating at every event the expanding McGucken
Sphere. Full statements of the derivations are in the corpus papers
cited: general relativity in {[}23{]}
(https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/07/05/general-relativity-derived-from-the-mcgucken-principle-dx4-dtic-deriving-general-relativity-as-two-independent-theorem-chains-descending-from-dx4-dtic-along-both-the-geometric-and-algebraic-channel/),
thermodynamics in {[}24{]}
