\hypertarget{full-reproduction-the-head-to-head-mcgucken-versus-verlinde-comparison-vi.5-of-50-verbatim}{%
\paragraph{5.7.10 Full reproduction: the head-to-head
McGucken-versus-Verlinde comparison (§VI.5 of {[}50{]},
verbatim)}\label{full-reproduction-the-head-to-head-mcgucken-versus-verlinde-comparison-vi.5-of-50-verbatim}}

The following is reproduced verbatim and in full from the McGucken
cosmology paper {[}50{]}, §VI.5
(https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/05/19/the-mcgucken-cosmology-dx\%e2\%82\%84-dt-ic-outranks-every-major-cosmological-model-in-the-combined-empirical-record-and-mcgucken-accomplishes-this-with-zero-free-dark-sector-parameters-first-place-3/),
the corpus source for the McGucken-versus-Verlinde results summarized
above. It is quoted complete and unaltered.

\textbf{VI.5 Head-to-Head: McGucken Versus Verlinde --- dx₄/dt = ic's
Asymmetry of x₄ Expanding against x₁, x₂, x₃ as the Decisive Structural
Difference}

The McGucken framework and Verlinde's emergent gravity are the only two
zero-free-parameter dark-sector theories in the literature. This makes
the head-to-head comparison between them the central content of the
empirical analysis. Where these two frameworks make different
predictions, the empirical record discriminates between them, and that
discrimination directly tests the invariance of x₄'s expansion at c
against x₁, x₂, x₃.

\textbf{VI.5.1 The shared structural achievements of McGucken and
Verlinde: zero free parameters in the dark sector and the MOND scale a₀
= cH₀/(2π)}

Both frameworks succeed where the rest of the dark-sector literature has
failed in three structurally important ways. Both unify dark matter and
dark energy through one underlying mechanism (sensitivity amplification
of δφ in McGucken; emergent gravity from de Sitter horizon entanglement
entropy in Verlinde). Both predict a₀ ≈ cH₀/(2π) for the MOND
acceleration scale. Both predict the radial acceleration relation shape.
These are agreements at the level of the macroscopic predictions of the
two frameworks.

These agreements have a structural explanation that the {[}174{]} paper
makes explicit: \textbf{Verlinde's entropic gravity is the macroscopic
thermodynamic limit of the McGucken Principle.} The two frameworks agree
on Newton's law, Einstein's equations, the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy
formula, and the basic dark-sector phenomenology because Verlinde's
predictions in this domain \emph{are} the thermodynamic shadow of the
McGucken Principle's microscopic mechanism. The McGucken Principle
supplies what Verlinde's framework requires but does not derive: the
microscopic degrees of freedom (quanta of x₄'s oscillation on the
McGucken Sphere), the entropy increase mechanism (x₄'s irreversible
spherically symmetric expansion), the holographic-screen geometry (the
McGucken Sphere is the surface of x₄'s expansion), the Planck-area
information density (one quantum of x₄'s oscillation per Planck-area
cell), the Unruh temperature (x₄'s oscillation rate as perceived by an
accelerating observer), and the volume-law entropy contribution
(baseline entropy density of x₄'s zero-point Planck-scale oscillation).

So the agreement of the two frameworks on macroscopic predictions is not
the agreement of two independent theories converging on the same answer.
It is the agreement of a microscopic theory (McGucken) with its own
thermodynamic limit (Verlinde). The McGucken framework supplies the
microscopic mechanism that Verlinde's framework has been seeking but has
not been able to specify on its own.

\textbf{VI.5.2 The foundational ontological structure: x₄'s invariant
expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃}

But the deeper question is not where the two frameworks agree; it is
where they disagree, and \emph{why}.

\textbf{Verlinde's framework operates on a standard symmetric
four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold.} The Lorentzian-manifold structure
is taken as input --- assumed from the start. Verlinde applies the
holographic principle to closed surfaces in this manifold, derives
entropy gradients, and recovers gravity as a thermodynamic equation of
state given that the underlying spacetime already has the right
structure. The four dimensions are on equal footing; there is no
preferred direction along which something is moving while the others
remain static.

\textbf{The McGucken framework operates on a manifold with the
invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃ built in.} The
fourth dimension x₄ moves at the invariant rate ic; the three spatial
dimensions x₁, x₂, x₃ are stationary but stretchable. The
Lorentzian-manifold structure is not input but \emph{output} --- derived
as a theorem from the single principle dx₄/dt = ic {[}159{]}. The metric
signature (−,+,+,+) emerges from i² = −1 applied to the moving x₄ axis.
The four-velocity normalization u\^{}μu\_μ = −c² is a chain-rule theorem
\emph{forced by} the McGucken Principle when the worldline is
proper-time-parametrized (per (R3) of Appendix B; the norm is a
downstream consequence of the Principle dx₄/dt = ic in (R1), not
identical to it). All six standard postulates of general relativity are
theorems descending from one geometric principle.

This is the foundational ontological difference. Verlinde uses general
relativity; McGucken derives general relativity. Verlinde's framework
operates at the thermodynamic-emergent level above the Lorentzian
manifold, taking it as given; the McGucken framework operates at the
geometric-foundational level beneath the Lorentzian manifold, deriving
it.

\textbf{VI.5.3 The eight specific divergences flow from x₄'s invariant
expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃}

The invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃ produces
specific predictions that Verlinde's symmetric-spacetime framework
cannot make. We enumerate eight.

\textbf{Divergence 1: The H₀ tension.} Verlinde's framework treats H₀ as
a single cosmological parameter with no structural distinction between
local and cosmic-average measurements. The McGucken framework predicts
that dx₄/dt = ic is strictly invariant --- x₄'s rate never varies ---
but mass grips the spatial three (x₁x₂x₃) and contracts them slowly
across cosmic time as cumulative baryonic mass aggregates. The Hubble
parameter H = dx₄/(x₁x₂x₃·dt) measures the ratio of the invariant x₄
rate to the spatial scale at the time of measurement; CMB-anchored
measurements use the recombination-epoch (larger, less contracted)
spatial scale propagated forward through ΛCDM, while local measurements
use the present-epoch (smaller, more contracted) spatial scale directly.
The 8.3\% gap between Planck and SH0ES is consistent with the predicted
cumulative spatial contraction ψ(recombination)/ψ(today) ≈ 1.08 since
recombination --- a direct measurement of how much mass has aggregated
and tightened its grip on x₁x₂x₃ since z = 1100. \textbf{Empirical
record: the H₀ tension is robust at 5σ and persists with improved
measurements. McGucken predicts this; Verlinde does not.}

\textbf{Divergence 2: The dark-energy w(z) functional form.} Verlinde's
framework gives w ≈ −1 (cosmological-constant-like) without a sharp
parameter-free functional form. The McGucken framework predicts the
specific form w(z) = −1 + Ω\_m(z)/(6π) with the 6π geometric factor
forced by x₄'s spherical expansion. \textbf{Empirical record: McGucken's
w₀ = −0.983 matches DESI BAO-alone w = −0.99 ± 0.14 at 0.05σ. The DESI
direction (w₀ \textgreater{} −1) matches the McGucken direction. DESI
Year-3+ in non-CPL parametrizations will test the specific shape.}

\textbf{Divergence 3: The radial profile of dark matter near galaxies.}
Verlinde's volume-law-entropy mechanism gives flat rotation curves but
no sharp radial profile. The McGucken framework predicts the
asymmetry-derived form g\_McG = g\_N + √(g\_N · a₀), with the
cosmological coupling term √(g\_N · a₀) forced by the asymmetry's
introduction of the cosmological scale a₀ = cH₀/(2π) into the metric.
\textbf{Empirical record: the SPARC RAR analysis (χ²/N = 0.59 with the
asymmetry-derived form, vs.~χ²/N = 1.60 for the simple MOND
interpolation, both with the McGucken-predicted a₀) confirms the
asymmetry-derived functional form predicted by McGucken.}

\textbf{Divergence 4: The dwarf-galaxy regime.} Verlinde's framework
predicts deviations from MOND in dwarf galaxies (lower-acceleration
regime). The McGucken framework predicts the universal asymmetry-derived
form g\_McG = g\_N + √(g\_N · a₀) across all galactic regimes; dwarf
galaxies operate in the deep-MOND limit where g\_N \textless\textless{}
a₀ and g\_McG → √(g\_N · a₀), but with the same functional form as
massive galaxies. \textbf{Empirical record: the SPARC sample shows a
universal RAR with no clean dwarf-galaxy deviations {[}20{]}. McGucken's
prediction is supported; Verlinde's is in tension.}

\textbf{Divergence 5: Cluster-scale dark matter and the Bullet Cluster.}
The Bullet Cluster (1E 0657-56) shows a \textasciitilde25 kpc spatial
offset between the X-ray gas peak and the weak-lensing reconstructed
total-mass peak, with the lensing peak coincident with the galaxy
distribution. This is the canonical ``smoking gun for dark matter''
because it appears to show the gravitating mass tracking the
collisionless tracers (galaxies) rather than the dominant baryonic
component (gas).

\textbf{MOND cannot account for this.} MOND modifies inertia or
Poisson's equation at each spatial point as a function of the local
acceleration scale, treating space symmetrically. In MOND, the
missing-mass signal is sourced by the local baryonic acceleration, which
is dominated by the gas (\textasciitilde85-90\% of cluster baryons).
MOND therefore predicts the lensing peak should coincide with the gas
peak --- contradicted by observation.

\textbf{The McGucken framework predicts this offset structurally.} The
invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃ is the foundational
feature: x₄ advances invariantly while x₁x₂x₃ stretch around mass. The
asymmetric stretching is sourced by baryonic mass \emph{intrinsically}
--- each galaxy's stretching is part of its own self-gravitating system,
traveling with the galaxy as a coherent unit. During a violent merger
like the Bullet Cluster, three things happen:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  Galaxies pass through collisionlessly, carrying their own intrinsic
  asymmetric coupling with them. Each galaxy's gravitating-mass profile
  (stars + the integrated asymmetric stress-energy that sources the
  galactic dark-matter-like signal) travels with the galaxy as a
  self-consistent unit.
\item
  Hot gas is decelerated by ram pressure, lagging behind. The asymmetric
  coupling sourced by the gas itself travels with the gas.
\item
  The total lensing signal at the galaxy peak is dominated by the sum of
  all individual galaxies' gravitating-mass profiles plus the smaller
  stellar-mass-sourced contribution. The total lensing signal at the gas
  peak is dominated by the gas-sourced asymmetric coupling alone, which
  is more diffuse and produces a weaker lensing peak per unit baryonic
  mass.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{The lensing peak therefore follows the galaxies (where most of
the gravitating-mass content of the cluster ended up), with the gas peak
lagging behind.} This is exactly what the Bullet Cluster shows.

\textbf{Empirical record: the Bullet Cluster offset matches the McGucken
prediction; MOND and Verlinde's symmetric-spacetime frameworks face
unresolved tension here.}

This is the structural payoff of treating space as asymmetric rather
than symmetric. In a symmetric-spacetime framework, the modified-gravity
signal must be a function of the local baryonic acceleration \emph{at
each point} --- so it follows the most baryonic-rich location (the gas
peak). In the asymmetric framework, the modified-gravity signal is
sourced by the baryonic mass \emph{wherever those baryons are
concentrated}, including their dynamical history (collisionless
vs.~shocked).

\textbf{Divergence 6: Structure formation.} Verlinde's framework has
difficulty fitting into N-body cosmological simulations; deriving
large-scale structure formation is an open problem. The McGucken
framework predicts straightforward baryon-led structure formation, with
dark-matter signal following the growing baryonic gravitational
potentials. The framework predicts no primordial dark-matter halos.
\textbf{Empirical record: large-scale-structure simulations using
baryon-led formation are consistent with McGucken's prediction;
Verlinde's predictions are less sharply specified.}

\textbf{Divergence 7: Voids.} Verlinde's volume-law entropy fills space
uniformly, with predictions for void interiors not sharply specified.
The McGucken framework predicts essentially no dark-matter signal in
voids: no baryonic potential means no spatial stretching, which means no
amplification. \textbf{Empirical record: void-lensing analyses {[}84,
85{]} are converging toward baryon-dominated voids, supporting
McGucken's prediction.}

\textbf{Divergence 8: Multi-channel correlation through one parameter.}
Verlinde's framework predicts a₀, dark-energy density, and cluster
dark-matter distributions through largely independent mechanisms within
the holographic-entropy structure. The McGucken framework predicts a₀,
w(z), the H₀ tension, and the BTFR slope of 4 through the single
parameter δ\ensuremath{\dot{\psi}}/ψ ≈ −H₀ --- the rate at which x₁x₂x₃ are contracting under
cumulative mass aggregation. \textbf{Empirical record: all four
observables are consistent with current data within the same parameter
value, providing multi-channel correlation that Verlinde's framework
structurally cannot match.}

\textbf{Divergence 9: The CMB preferred frame.} Verlinde's framework
operates on a symmetric four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold with no
structural distinction between any reference frames. The CMB rest frame
in Verlinde's framework is at best contingent initial conditions of the
Big Bang --- a label rather than a mechanism. The McGucken framework
predicts the CMB rest frame as the physical realization of absolute rest
in x₁x₂x₃, the geometric ground state defined by dx₄/dt = ic {[}176{]}.
The Local Group's measured peculiar velocity of 627 km/s relative to the
CMB rest frame is a direct measurement of our tilt from absolute rest at
θ = arcsin(627/299,792.458) = 0.11994°. \textbf{Empirical record: the
CMB preferred frame is observed at extraordinary precision by COBE,
WMAP, and Planck. Its very existence is a problem for
symmetric-spacetime frameworks (which include Verlinde's) and a forced
consequence of the McGucken asymmetry. This is direct empirical evidence
for the invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃.}

\textbf{Divergence 10: The holographic screen --- McGucken horizon
vs.~Hubble horizon.} Verlinde's framework uses the Hubble horizon
(proper radius c/H(t)) as the holographic screen. The McGucken framework
uses the McGucken horizon (proper radius R₄(t) = ct in the early
universe, asymptoting to c/H\_∞ in late de Sitter epochs) {[}179{]}.
These are \emph{different surfaces} with different areas in
non-de-Sitter epochs. The distinguishing ratio ρ(t) = R₄(t)·H(t)/c
equals unity only in the asymptotic de Sitter regime; in the
radiation-dominated and matter-dominated eras, ρ(t) differs from 1
measurably. \textbf{Quantitative prediction: at recombination (z ≈
1100), ρ(t\_rec) ≈ 2.6, giving an entropy ratio S\_McG/S\_Hub ≈ 7. This
is a sharp, computable, quantitative distinction between McGucken
holography and Verlinde-style Hubble-horizon holography, with empirical
consequences in the CMB power spectrum, the Silk damping scale, and the
BAO acoustic scale.}

\textbf{Divergence 11: The horizon and flatness problems --- resolved
without inflation.} Verlinde's framework inherits the horizon problem
(why is the CMB so homogeneous given that distant regions were causally
disconnected at recombination in standard FRW cosmology?) and the
flatness problem (why is Ω\_k so close to zero?) from standard ΛCDM.
Both require inflation in Verlinde's framework. The McGucken framework
resolves both as geometric consequences of dx₄/dt = ic {[}177{]}. The
McGucken radius R₄(t) = ct is \emph{always} greater than or equal to the
standard causal horizon at every epoch, so all regions of the CMB sky
have always been within the McGucken Sphere of every emission event ---
they share x₄-locality through the McGucken-Sphere structure even when
separated in x₁x₂x₃. The flatness is a geometric consequence of x₄'s
expansion being spherically symmetric and the spatial slices being
three-dimensional. \textbf{No inflation required. Verlinde's framework
cannot make this prediction; it inherits the standard cosmological
problems.}

\textbf{Divergence 12: Lab-scale Compton coupling.} Verlinde's framework
has no lab-scale prediction beyond what it inherits from standard QM and
standard GR. The qBOUNCE neutron-state experiments and other lab-scale
tests have been argued to ``tightly constrain'' Verlinde's framework,
contributing to its ``long-shot'' status in mainstream physics. The
McGucken framework predicts a sharp lab-scale signature: a
mass-independent zero-temperature diffusion residual D\_x\^{}(McG) =
ε²c²Ω/(2γ²) detectable in cold-atom and trapped-ion laboratories
{[}180{]}. Particles couple to x₄'s expansion at their Compton frequency
ω\_C = mc²/ℏ, producing observable consequences at lab scales.
\textbf{Empirical record: this is a unique testable signature of the
invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃ that Verlinde's
framework structurally cannot produce. Future cold-atom and trapped-ion
experiments will discriminate between the frameworks at lab scales --- a
domain where Verlinde is already in tension.}

\textbf{VI.5.4 The inferential argument from the McGucken-vs-Verlinde
divergences: how data supporting McGucken's predictions over Verlinde's
establishes dx₄/dt = ic's Asymmetry of x₄ Expanding against x₁, x₂, x₃
as a real structural feature of physics}

These twelve divergences, taken together, constitute the empirical case
for the invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃ as a real
structural feature of physics.

The argument is direct. Both frameworks have zero free parameters in the
dark sector. Both unify dark matter and dark energy through one
mechanism. Both reproduce the basic galactic phenomenology (BTFR, RAR
shape, a₀ scale). Where they differ is precisely the structural content:
McGucken has the invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃,
Verlinde does not. Where the predictions diverge, McGucken's predictions
arise specifically from the asymmetry; Verlinde's framework has no
analogous mechanism to produce them.

So when the data favors McGucken's predictions over Verlinde's --- when
the H₀ tension persists, when the universal RAR is observed without
dwarf-galaxy deviations, when the Bullet Cluster lensing-gas offset
matches McGucken's prediction (and contradicts symmetric-spacetime
alternatives), when DESI BAO-alone gives w₀ in the McGucken direction
--- the empirical evidence is not ambiguous between ``McGucken happens
to be right'' and ``Verlinde happens to be wrong.'' It points
specifically to the structural feature that distinguishes them: the
invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃.

This is the form of inferential argument that established the major
structural commitments of twentieth-century physics. The equivalence
principle was inferred from the bending of starlight, an empirical
signature of the principle that Newtonian frameworks could not produce.
Quantization was inferred from atomic spectral lines, an empirical
signature of quantization that classical-physics frameworks could not
produce. The existence of antimatter was inferred from Anderson's
positron observation, an empirical signature that Schrödinger-equation
frameworks could not produce.

In each case, the structural feature was inferred from empirical
successes of frameworks that incorporated it, against empirical
limitations of frameworks that lacked it. The structural feature was not
directly observable; its empirical consequences were.

\textbf{The invariance of x₄'s expansion at c against x₁, x₂, x₃ is in
the same logical position today.} It is not directly observable --- one
cannot watch x₄ moving while the spatial three stretch. But it has
multiple specific empirical consequences (H₀ tension, universal RAR,
w(z) functional form, multi-channel correlation, Bullet Cluster
lensing-gas offset, void physics), and those consequences are observed.
Each empirical success that distinguishes McGucken from Verlinde is
therefore an indirect detection of the asymmetry.

Three features of the situation amplify the inferential force.

\textbf{First, the asymmetry is a sharp, testable structural
commitment.} It is not vague: it is the specific claim that one
direction moves while three remain stationary but stretchable. This is
the kind of claim that either survives empirical testing or does not,
with no wiggle room.

\textbf{Second, the asymmetry has multiple independent empirical
consequences.} The H₀ tension, the universal RAR shape, the w(z)
profile, the Bullet Cluster lensing-gas offset, the void physics, the
CMB preferred frame, the McGucken-vs-Hubble horizon entropy ratio, the
no-inflation horizon-and-flatness resolution, and the lab-scale
Compton-coupling prediction are not derivable from each other. Each
separately tests the asymmetry; the combined evidence is multiplicative
rather than additive across nine essentially independent empirical
channels.

\textbf{Third, the asymmetry is the unique structural feature
distinguishing McGucken from Verlinde.} Both frameworks have zero free
parameters. Both unify the dark sector. Both reproduce the basic
phenomenology. The only foundational difference is the asymmetry ---
with everything else flowing from it. The empirical evidence therefore
points cleanly at the asymmetry rather than diffusely across many
candidate structural differences.

\textbf{VI.5.5 The seven additional structural achievements of the
McGucken framework}

Beyond the eight predictive divergences, the McGucken framework extends
beyond Verlinde's framework in seven additional structural ways, each a
domain of fundamental physics that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
generates as a theorem while Verlinde's emergent gravity does not. These
are not predictive divergences in the dark sector but foundational
achievements that the asymmetry makes possible.

\textbf{(1) Foundational integration with general relativity.} The
McGucken Principle derives all six standard postulates of general
relativity as theorems descending from dx₄/dt = ic {[}159{]}: the
Lorentzian-manifold structure (P1), the Equivalence Principle in its
Weak, Einstein, Strong, and Massless-Lightspeed forms (P2), the geodesic
hypothesis (P3), the metric-compatibility of the connection (P4),
stress-energy conservation (P5), and the Einstein field equations
through two mathematically independent routes (P6). Verlinde's framework
derives gravity from holographic screens but does not derive the full
Lorentzian-manifold structure of spacetime from the same principle.

\textbf{(2) Foundational integration with quantum mechanics.} The same
dx₄/dt = ic principle that produces the dark sector also produces the
entire structure of quantum mechanics as a chain of theorems {[}160{]}:
the Born rule, the Schrödinger equation, {[}\(\hat{q}\), \(\hat{p}\){]}
= iℏ, Heisenberg uncertainty, Pauli exclusion, the Feynman path
integral, the Dirac equation, the CHSH inequality, and the full
Feynman-diagram apparatus. Verlinde's framework is a gravitational
theory; it does not derive quantum mechanics from the same underlying
mechanism.

\textbf{(3) Foundational integration with thermodynamics.} The McGucken
Principle derives the Second Law, entropy as the count of x₄-stationary
configurations, the thermodynamic arrow of time from x₄'s monotonic
advance, the Boltzmann distribution, and the Stefan-Boltzmann law as
theorems descending from dx₄/dt = ic {[}161{]}. The arrow of time is not
postulated separately but emerges as the directional content of x₄'s
expansion. Verlinde's framework engages thermodynamics through its
emergent-gravity-from-entropy mechanism but does not derive
thermodynamics itself from one geometric principle.

\textbf{(4) The McGucken Symmetry generates all of physics's symmetry
structure.} {[}162{]} establishes that the symmetry generated by dx₄/dt
= ic --- the McGucken Symmetry --- is the father symmetry of physics,
completing Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme. The McGucken Principle
generates the Klein pair (G, H) = (ISO(1,3), SO⁺(1,3)) of Minkowski
spacetime through two structurally independent routes {[}163{]}.
Verlinde's framework does not address the foundational origin of
physics's symmetry structure or complete the Erlangen Programme.

\textbf{(5) The McGucken Lagrangian forces the unique structure of all
four sectors of fundamental physics.} {[}164{]} establishes that the
unique simplest and most complete Lagrangian of physics is forced by
dx₄/dt = ic. Across all four sectors --- free-particle kinetic, Dirac
matter, Yang-Mills gauge, and Einstein-Hilbert gravitational --- the
structure is forced rather than chosen. Verlinde's framework does not
derive the structure of the Standard Model or the Einstein-Hilbert
action from a single underlying principle.

\textbf{(6) Mathematical universality at the categorical level.}
{[}172{]} establishes the McGucken Principle as the initial object in a
specific category of moving-dimension geometries. {[}171{]} establishes
that dx₄/dt = ic generates simultaneously the McGucken Space (geometric
content) and the McGucken Operator (algebraic content) as categorically
dual aspects of the same single principle. Verlinde's framework has no
analogous categorical-universality result.

\textbf{(7) The Jacobson-Verlinde-Marolf microscopic foundation.}
{[}175{]} establishes that the McGucken Principle resolves the central
open question of the thermodynamic-gravity programme: what are the
microscopic degrees of freedom whose statistical behavior produces
gravity as an equation of state? Jacobson stated in 2025: ``I don't know
what it is, frankly. I think it's sort of beyond my conceptual
horizon.'' The McGucken Principle specifies the microscopic degrees of
freedom: they are the quanta of x₄'s oscillation on the McGucken Sphere,
with the framework also satisfying Marolf's 2014 nonlocality constraint
structurally through global x₄-invariance.

\textbf{The summary picture.} Verlinde's emergent gravity matches the
McGucken framework on dark-sector parameter count (zero) and on the
unification of dark matter and dark energy through one mechanism. On the
twelve predictive divergences and the seven structural achievements
enumerated above --- totaling \textbf{nineteen specific dimensions} on
which the McGucken framework extends beyond Verlinde's --- the McGucken
framework generates results that Verlinde's framework does not.
\textbf{All nineteen flow from the invariance of x₄'s expansion at c
against x₁, x₂, x₃.} The McGucken Principle is structurally a more
comprehensive foundational object: it is the same single principle
dx₄/dt = ic that does all of this work, not a separate principle for
each domain.

\hypertarget{causal-set-theory-its-motivations-resolved-and-the-mcgucken-derivation-of-lorentz-invariance-together-with-nonlocality}{%
\subsubsection{5.8 Causal set theory: its motivations resolved, and the
McGucken derivation of Lorentz invariance together with
nonlocality}\label{causal-set-theory-its-motivations-resolved-and-the-mcgucken-derivation-of-lorentz-invariance-together-with-nonlocality}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c, as a spherically
symmetric wavefront --- the McGucken Sphere --- from every event of
spacetime. Causal set theory is the discrete-spacetime approach to
quantum gravity founded by Bombelli, Lee, Meyer, and Sorkin in 1987
{[}54{]}. This section states what causal set theory was created to
solve, where it succeeded and where it did not, and shows that its
central motivations are resolved by dx₄/dt = ic --- including the two
properties it most prizes, Lorentz invariance and a controlled
nonlocality, which the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies together
from the one Principle.

\textbf{Where causal set theory started and what it was created to
solve.} The program rests on a chain of results establishing that causal
order is more fundamental than the metric. Robb (1914, 1936) showed,
shortly after Minkowski, that the causal structure of Minkowski
spacetime determines its topology and metric; Kronheimer and Penrose
(1967) formalized causal spaces; and the pivotal theorems of Hawking,
King, and McCarthy (1976) and Malament (1977) established that the
causal structure of a suitable spacetime determines its conformal
geometry --- everything but the overall volume scale. Riemann (1873) and
Finkelstein (1969) supplied the complementary idea that spacetime might
be fundamentally discrete. Bombelli, Lee, Meyer, and Sorkin combined
these in 1987 {[}54{]}: the causal order gives the conformal geometry
(by Malament's theorem), and discreteness supplies the missing volume by
counting, since volume can be identified with the number of elements.
This is Sorkin's slogan, ``Order + Number = Geometry.'' Causal set
theory was created to cure the three infinities of fundamental physics
--- the ultraviolet divergences of relativistic quantum field theory,
the curvature singularities of general relativity, and the divergent
result when the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy is computed directly from
quantum-gravitational degrees of freedom --- by replacing the continuum
with a locally finite partially ordered set, so that every finite region
contains only a finite number of fundamental elements and the infinities
become finite.

\textbf{Where it succeeded.} Causal set theory achieved discreteness
without violating local Lorentz invariance --- its signature result,
obtained because the discrete elements are distributed by a random
Poisson sprinkling that picks out no preferred frame, so the
discreteness is locally Lorentz invariant {[}55{]}. From the discrete
order alone, its practitioners have reconstructed the spacetime
dimension, topological invariants, geodesic distance, the d'Alembertian,
and the Ricci scalar {[}55{]}. And Sorkin's causal-set prediction of a
small, fluctuating cosmological constant of order the observed value ---
the everpresent-Λ prediction --- was made before the 1998 discovery of
dark energy {[}55{]}.

\textbf{Where it did not succeed.} Three difficulties remain open.
First, the entropy or non-manifoldlike problem: if a causal set is
selected by counting, the overwhelming majority of causal sets look
nothing like a spacetime manifold --- they are Kleitman--Rothschild
orders with ``three moments of time,'' utterly non-manifoldlike, and
they dominate by sheer number, so the dynamics must suppress them or no
continuum emerges {[}55, 56{]}; this is, in Carlip's words, ``the
manifestation of the cosmological constant problem in causal set
theory,'' and it is only partially resolved {[}56{]}. Second, the
Hauptvermutung --- the central conjecture that a causal set determines
its continuum spacetime uniquely --- remains unproven {[}55{]}. Third,
causal set theory has a well-developed kinematics but no complete
accepted quantum dynamics of the causal set, and it does not derive
quantum mechanics, the Born rule, or thermodynamics; it is a program for
quantum gravity that presupposes quantum theory.

\textbf{Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic: causal order and volume from the
expanding Sphere.} Causal set theory takes the causal order as an
unexplained primitive and must add discreteness by hand to recover the
volume that Malament's theorem leaves out. The McGucken Principle
supplies both the causal order and the volume from one physical fact.
The causal order is the order of the expanding McGucken Sphere: the null
wavefront advancing at c from each event is the light cone, so the
causal relation ``p precedes q'' is ``q lies on or within the forward
Sphere of p'' --- the causal structure is the expansion structure of
dx₄/dt = ic (GR Theorem 11 of {[}23{]}). The volume that causal set
theory must recover by counting is the count Ω of Compton-tick states of
the expanding Sphere in the region (§6): ``Number ∼ Spacetime Volume''
is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the state-count Ω of the
Sphere, one Compton tick of action h at a time. So ``Order + Number =
Geometry'' is, under dx₄/dt = ic, ``the expanding Sphere's causal cone
plus the expanding Sphere's Compton-tick count equals the geometry'' ---
both order and number descend from the one advance, rather than order
being assumed and number bolted on.

\textbf{The full Lorentzian metric, not only the conformal geometry.}
Malament's theorem gives causal set theory only the conformal geometry
from order; the volume must be supplied separately by discreteness, and
the reconstruction of a definite spacetime rests on the unproven
Hauptvermutung. The McGucken Principle derives the full Lorentzian
metric outright: the pullback of the Euclidean four-metric under the
embedding carrying x₄ = ict gives ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c²dt², the
complete Lorentzian line element including its scale, from the single
algebraic fact (ic)² = −c² (Lemma 2.5, {[}29{]}). The metric --- volume
and all, not merely the conformal class --- is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic,
so there is no missing volume to supply by counting and no
Hauptvermutung to prove: the manifold is the expanding Sphere's
coordinate integral, not a random poset hoped to approximate a manifold.
The non-manifoldlike problem does not arise, because the McGucken dx₄/dt
= ic framework does not select a spacetime by counting equally weighted
orders; the spacetime is the integrated advance of the fourth dimension
at every event.

\textbf{Lorentz invariance and nonlocality, together, from the one
Principle.} Causal set theory's proudest achievement is that
discreteness need not break Lorentz invariance, and it discovered that
the price of discreteness-with-Lorentz-invariance is a characteristic
nonlocality --- in a causal set approximating Minkowski spacetime, each
element has infinitely many nearest neighbours. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic
framework provides both Lorentz invariance and nonlocality, and provides
them together, as two consequences of the same expanding Sphere. Lorentz
invariance is derived: the Lorentz and Poincaré groups descend from
dx₄/dt = ic as theorems (GR Theorem 8 of {[}23{]}, {[}45{]}), because
the invariant expansion of x₄ at the rate c against the spatial slice is
exactly the invariance of c that the Lorentz group encodes --- the
metric ds² of Lemma 2.5 is Lorentz-invariant by construction, so no
preferred frame is introduced. Nonlocality is derived from the same
advance: the McGucken Principle turns each local event into an expanding
spherical surface, so a single local origin is physically present across
a nonlocal surface at once (§5.7.4), and the entanglement and
connectivity of space are the intersections of these expanding Spheres
(First McGucken Law of Nonlocality, {[}49{]}). Where causal set theory
finds Lorentz invariance and nonlocality as a linked pair --- one the
price of the other --- the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework derives them
as the two faces of the one expansion: the invariance of the rate c of
the advance is Lorentz invariance, and the expansion of the local point
into a surface is the nonlocality. Both are theorems of dx₄/dt = ic,
obtained together, with the full Lorentzian metric and without the
non-manifoldlike sea, the unproven Hauptvermutung, or the missing
dynamics that causal set theory still confronts, and with quantum
mechanics and thermodynamics derived from the same Principle that causal
set theory must presuppose.

\hypertarget{full-reproduction-the-static-light-cone-tradition-versus-the-active-sphere-reading-and-the-sorkindowker-causal-set-lineage-from-29-verbatim}{%
\paragraph{5.8.1 Full reproduction: the static-light-cone tradition
versus the active-Sphere reading, and the Sorkin--Dowker causal-set
lineage (from {[}29{]},
verbatim)}\label{full-reproduction-the-static-light-cone-tradition-versus-the-active-sphere-reading-and-the-sorkindowker-causal-set-lineage-from-29-verbatim}}

The following is reproduced verbatim and in full from the flagship
Minkowski--Hilbert paper {[}29{]}
(https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/07/05/minkowski-space-and-hilbert-space-derived-and-unified-via-the-mcgucken-principle-dx\%e2\%82\%84-dt-ic-how-the-born-rule-schrodinger-equation-hilbert-space-lorentzian-spacetime-metric-einstein-fiel/),
the corpus treatment of the causal-set lineage and the two senses of
locality. It is quoted complete and unaltered.

The historical-comparison table in §1.1bis.1 catalogues a wide range of
prior programs that have engaged with the null cone, locality, Lorentz
invariance, or nonlocality in various combinations. The structural
framing in v36 (this paper's earlier version) characterized the
Sorkin--Dowker causal-set lineage as the ``closest near-miss'' to
identification (I), and identified the trinity-conflict-vs-biconditional
distinction as the structural axis. On closer examination --- with the
verified primary sources read in full (Bombelli--Lee--Meyer--Sorkin
1987, Sorkin 1991, Sorkin 2009, Dowker--Glaser 2013,
Belenchia--Benincasa--Dowker 2015, Boguñá--Krioukov 2025) --- that
framing is correct in detail but mis-located in level. The deeper
structural distinction is between \textbf{the entire static-light-cone
tradition of orthodox physics} and \textbf{the active-Sphere reading of
the McGucken framework}. This subsection develops the deeper distinction
with verbatim primary-source content.

\emph{The static-light-cone tradition.} Across twentieth-century and
early-twenty-first-century physics, the null cone of the Lorentzian
metric is treated as a \textbf{frozen, passive, kinematical surface} in
a pre-given Lorentzian manifold. Penrose's twistor program (1967 and
subsequent decades) constructs twistors as complex coordinates
parameterizing the existing null structure of an existing Minkowski
spacetime; the null cone is given, the twistors are built from it.
Reeh--Schlieder's theorem {[}\emph{Nuovo Cimento} 22, 1051 (1961){]}
establishes the cyclic-vector property of local QFT algebras on regions
of an existing Lorentzian manifold; the metric and its null structure
are background, the QFT algebraic content is layered on top. The
Bombelli--Lee--Meyer--Sorkin 1987 {[}PRL 59, 521{]} founding paper of
causal-set theory proposes spacetime as a locally finite partial order,
with the partial order encoding the causal structure of an
\emph{approximating} Lorentzian manifold --- \emph{``the metric must be
Lorentzian, because no other signature than \((-,+,...,+)\) has the
two-napped light cones from which the continuum's causal order is
derived''} --- treating the existence of light cones as the geometric
fact that justifies the partial-order discretization. The Sorkin--Dowker
causal-set lineage (Sorkin 1991, 2007, 2009; Dowker--Glaser 2013;
Belenchia--Benincasa--Dowker 2015; Boguñá--Krioukov 2025)
Poisson-sprinkles discrete points into a pre-existing Lorentzian
manifold whose light cones are taken as the kinematical given; the
hyperboloid Belenchia--Benincasa--Dowker 2015 identify as the locus of
\(L_1(x)\) near \(\partial J^-(x)\) is a region of the static,
pre-existing light cone, populated by discrete points. Jacobson's
null-thermodynamics derivation of Einstein's equations {[}PRL 75, 1260
(1995); PRL 116, 201101 (2015){]} treats Rindler horizons as
pre-existing null surfaces at which equilibrium conditions are imposed;
the null structure is given, the thermodynamic argument is applied on
it. Maldacena's holographic correspondence {[}Adv. Theor. Math. Phys. 2,
231 (1998){]} and the broader AdS/CFT literature treat bulk and boundary
Lorentzian/conformal metrics as fixed inputs; the holographic
identification operates between QFTs defined on these pre-given
backgrounds. Light-front quantization, conformal compactification
(Penrose 1965), Bondi--Metzner--Sachs (BMS) symmetries at null infinity,
Strominger's ``null asymptotic'' celestial-amplitude program --- every
one of these orthodox approaches treats the null cone as a frozen
kinematical structure, a passive object that physics happens on or near
or across, but not itself dynamical.

\emph{The active-Sphere reading of the McGucken framework.} The McGucken
Principle dx₄/dt = ic of the present paper makes a structurally distinct
claim: the null cone of the Lorentzian metric is \textbf{not} a
primitive object in its own right; it is the \emph{integrated coordinate
shadow} of an active spherically symmetric wavefront --- the McGucken
Sphere \(\mathcal{M}_E(t)\) --- propagating from every event
\(E \in \mathbb{M}_{1,3}\) at velocity \(c\) in the \(x_4\)-direction.
The McGucken Sphere is an \emph{active} geometric primitive carrying
wavelength, frequency \(\omega = E/\hbar\), phase, and action \(\hbar\)
per Planck-frequency oscillation built into its propagation. The static
light cone \(\partial J^{\pm}(E)\) of the orthodox tradition is the
\emph{locus traced} as the McGucken Sphere has propagated outward; the
null cone is the geometric record of where the active wavefront has
been, not a primitive in its own right. \emph{The dynamics are in the
premise.} (See the central content paragraph of §1.1, the inset
following Principle 2.1 of §2.1, and the cascade derivation of §§2--9,
packaged in Theorem 6.6.7.6.) This distinction is foundational: every
static-light-cone program treats geometric kinematics as the primitive
input and must add the quantum-mechanical formalism (Hilbert space, Born
rule, entanglement, Bell-violation correlations) as separate structure
layered on top of the static metric. The McGucken framework treats the
active wavefront --- and the dynamical content built into it --- as the
primitive, and derives BOTH the quantum-mechanical formalism AND the
Lorentzian spacetime formalism of relativity as cascade-level theorems
from this dynamical premise. The static null cone of orthodox physics
and the active McGucken Sphere are \textbf{not the same geometric
object}: the former is a passive locus, the latter is a propagating
wavefront with frequency, phase, and action content built in. They share
a region of spacetime, in the way that the trail of a moving particle
shares a region of spacetime with the particle's trajectory, but the
trail is not the particle.

\emph{The two senses of locality, disambiguated.} The locality
discussion in the static-light-cone tradition refers to
\textbf{local-Lagrangian locality}: the form of action
\(S = \int \mathcal{L}(x) d^4x\) where \(\mathcal{L}(x)\) depends on
field values and finitely many derivatives at the single point \(x\).
The Einstein--Hilbert action of GR, the Yang--Mills action of QFT, the
Klein--Gordon and Dirac Lagrangians, and the continuum d'Alembertian
\(\Box\) all have this property; the action is an integral over the
spacetime manifold of a density that depends only on
infinitesimally-nearby field content at each point.
\textbf{Bell-violation locality}, by contrast, is the
no-spacelike-correlation property: measurements at spacelike-separated
events have factorizable joint probabilities, the property
\(P(A,B|a,b,\lambda) = P(A|a,\lambda) P(B|b,\lambda)\) for some hidden
variable \(\lambda\). The two senses are structurally distinct: standard
continuum QFT on Minkowski spacetime has local-Lagrangian locality
(every QFT textbook builds the Lagrangian to satisfy this) but lacks
Bell-violation locality (the empirical record of nonlocality, falsifying
Bell-CHSH inequalities, has been confirmed by Aspect 1982, Tittel et
al.~1998, Hensen et al.~2015 loophole-free, Big Bell Test Collaboration
2018, and every Bell test since). Standard physics is local in sense (1)
and nonlocal in sense (2), simultaneously, with no formal contradiction
within the orthodox treatment.

\emph{Which sense the Sorkin--Dowker lineage addresses.} The
Sorkin--Dowker causal-set lineage addresses \textbf{local-Lagrangian
locality at the operator level}. Their concern is that the
Poisson-sprinkling discretization scheme --- which is required to
preserve Lorentz invariance --- produces discrete d'Alembertians whose
kernels depend on infinitely many discrete events distributed on the
past-light-cone hyperboloid. The discrete operator \(B^{(d)}\phi(x)\)
does not have the local-Lagrangian form (it does not depend only on
field values at infinitesimally-nearby events to \(x\)); it depends on
field values at an infinite set of events one Planck unit of proper time
in the past. The 18-year engineering arc --- Sorkin 2007 {[}``Does
locality fail at intermediate length-scales?'', arXiv:gr-qc/0703099{]},
Benincasa--Dowker 2010, Dowker--Glaser 2013,
Belenchia--Benincasa--Dowker 2015, Boguñá--Krioukov 2025 --- is the
construction project of finding discrete operators that \emph{behave
nonlocally on the discrete substrate} but \emph{converge to the
local-Lagrangian continuum d'Alembertian} \(\Box\) in the right limit.
Boguñá--Krioukov 2025 {[}arXiv:2506.18745{]} state the engineering goal
verbatim: \emph{``This approach thus reconciles locality with Lorentz
invariance, and paves a way toward defining converging discrete
approximations to locality-based differential operators even in theories
that are inherently nonlocal.''} The phrase ``Lorentzian nonlocality''
in this lineage refers to this operator-kernel nonlocality, treated as a
discretization artifact to be tamed so that the continuum limit recovers
standard local-Lagrangian physics. The lineage does \emph{not} address
Bell-violation nonlocality, does not offer a physical explanation of EPR
correlations, and does not engage with the quantum-mechanical
nonlocality of standard QM at any structural level --- the
quantum-mechanical formalism is treated as a separate framework layered
on the causet background (Sorkin 2011 ``Scalar Field Theory on a Causal
Set in Histories Form'' J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 306, 012017; Johnston 2008
``Particle propagators on discrete spacetime'' Class. Quant. Grav. 25,
202001; Albertini et al.~2024 in-in correlators Phys. Rev.~D
109.106014).

\emph{Which sense McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1 addresses.} McGucken Theorem
6.6.8.1 addresses \textbf{Bell-violation locality} --- the structural
source of the no-spacelike-correlation property that empirical Bell
tests have falsified. The theorem identifies the null cone of the
continuous Lorentzian metric --- \emph{not} a discretization artifact,
\emph{not} an operator-kernel property --- as the structural-geometric
source of the Bell-violation correlations of standard quantum mechanics.
The McGucken Sphere wavefront \(\mathcal{M}_E(t)\) from event \(E\)
propagates at null on the light cone \(\partial J^+(E)\); correlations
between measurements at spacelike-separated events \(E_1, E_2\) in the
chronological future of a common-source event \(E_I\) are present in the
Sphere wavefront from \(E_I\) onward (Theorem 6.6.7.7 no-signaling
theorem); the same null structure that the static-light-cone tradition
treats as locality-supplying is in fact the nonlocality-source of the
empirical Bell-violation record. The McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1
biconditional content (null vectors ⇔ Sphere ⇔ Lorentzian signature ⇔
nonlocality) is a statement about sense (2) --- Bell-violation locality
--- and the structural-geometric source of its failure in nature.

\emph{The two programs are addressing structurally different phenomena
that share a word.} The Sorkin--Dowker lineage works on local-Lagrangian
operator-kernel locality (sense 1) as a continuum-recovery engineering
problem; the McGucken framework works on Bell-violation locality (sense
2) as a structural-geometric identification. Both use the word
``locality'' and both invoke the null cone; the geometric objects, the
physical content, and the structural claims are different. The
Sorkin--Dowker ``Lorentzian nonlocality'' terminology is not a near-miss
to the McGucken claim because the two phrases denote different physical
phenomena. A near-miss would require sharing the physical phenomenon
being addressed; sharing vocabulary is necessary but not sufficient.

\emph{Why no published near-miss exists to McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1.}
The categorical structural reason is now clear: \textbf{every published
program engaging with the null cone treats it as static kinematics, not
as the integrated trail of an active wavefront.} A static null cone
cannot be the source of Bell-violation correlations because it has no
dynamical content --- no wavefront, no oscillation, no frequency, no
phase, no action quantum, nothing that could carry the structural
information required to \emph{produce} the correlations rather than
merely \emph{be the kinematic stage} on which the correlations are
observed. To identify the metric's null structure as the physical source
of Bell-violation nonlocality, one needs the null cone to be dynamical
--- to have wavefront content built in. The static-light-cone tradition
cannot, by structural construction, make this identification. The
McGucken framework can, and does, via Theorem 6.6.8.1, precisely because
the active McGucken Sphere wavefront carries the dynamical content built
into the geometric primitive itself. To our knowledge, no published
physics theorem prior to the McGucken corpus offers a physical-geometric
explanation of Bell-violation nonlocality as the structural content of
the Lorentzian metric --- because the structural framework required to
ask the question (active wavefront as geometric primitive) is the
categorical break the McGucken framework introduces.

\emph{Categorical novelty of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic programme.} The
novelty established by Theorems 6.6.7.4, 6.6.7.6, and 6.6.8.1 is
therefore a structural break with the entire orthodox tradition.
\emph{(a) Dynamical premise.} dx₄/dt = ic is an active dynamical
principle --- every event has an active spherically symmetric expansion
in \(x_4\) at velocity \(c\), with action \(\hbar\) per Planck-frequency
oscillation --- not added separately at a later stage. \emph{(b) Active
wavefront as geometric primitive.} The McGucken Sphere
\(\mathcal{M}_E(t)\) is the geometric primitive; the static null cone of
the orthodox tradition is the integrated coordinate shadow. The
relationship is one-way: the active Sphere generates the static null
cone as its trail, but the static null cone does not generate the active
Sphere. \emph{(c) Biconditional structural identity.} Theorem 6.6.8.1
establishes that null vectors, McGucken Sphere, Lorentzian signature,
frame-invariance of \(c\), Lorentz group structure, and Bell-violation
nonlocality are biconditionally tied to one another --- they are aspects
of one structure, not separate axiomatic ingredients. \emph{(d) Cascade
derivation of QM as forced theorem chain.} Quantum mechanics is not
added as separate structure; the cascade Sphere → Hilbert → inner
product → Born rule → Bell-violation correlations runs as a sequence of
forced theorems from the active wavefront content of dx₄/dt = ic
(Theorem 6.6.7.6, packaged with proof-level audit). \emph{(e) Physical
explanation of quantum nonlocality.} The Lorentzian metric's null
structure is identified as the structural-geometric source of the
empirical Bell-violation record. This is the foundational answer to the
EPR question Einstein, Podolsky, Rosen posed in 1935 and that Bell
sharpened in 1964: the source of the spooky action at a distance is the
active McGucken Sphere wavefront, identical to the null cone of the same
Lorentzian metric that produces relativistic locality at the
local-Lagrangian level.

The static-light-cone tradition, taken as a whole, was the right
framework to investigate within the kinematical paradigm of
twentieth-century physics --- and it produced enormous results (twistor
theory, causal sets, holography, BMS symmetries, null infinity,
conformal field theory at null asymptotic boundaries). The McGucken
framework operates one level upstream, treating the null cone as the
integrated shadow of an active wavefront whose dynamical content is what
generates the quantum-mechanical structure of nature. This is the
categorical structural distinction. McGucken Theorems 6.6.7.4, 6.6.7.6,
and 6.6.8.1 do not extend, sharpen, or near-miss any prior theorem; they
state structurally new content made possible by the categorical break
with the static-light-cone tradition.
