\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c, as a spherically
symmetric wavefront --- the McGucken Sphere --- from every event of
spacetime. Jacob Barandes's stochastic-quantum correspondence {[}57{]}
is a recent and serious attempt to reformulate quantum mechanics as
ordinary probability theory over particles with definite positions. This
section states what that program achieves, identifies what it re-encodes
rather than removes, and shows that the entangled pair its formalism
describes is, under dx₄/dt = ic, a single expanding McGucken Sphere
measured at two points.

\textbf{What the program is and what it seeks.} Barandes proves an exact
correspondence between quantum theory and a class of ``indivisible''
(non-Markovian) stochastic processes: every quantum system corresponds
to a stochastic process over an ordinary configuration space, whose
transition matrix Γ(t ← t₀) is generically indivisible, meaning it does
not factorize through intermediate times. The two supporting theorems
--- the Born Representation Theorem, that any stochastic matrix can be
written Γ\_ij = tr(E\_i P\_j) in Born-rule trace form, and the
Unistochastic Theorem, that any stochastic matrix can be obtained by
marginalization from a unistochastic matrix Γ\_ij =
\textbar U\_ij\textbar² --- establish that the Born and unitary forms
are the universal representation of any probability process. The stated
goal is deflationary: the correspondence ``demotes the wave function
from a primary ontological ingredient to a secondary mathematical tool
and yields a deflationary account of exotic quantum phenomena, such as
interference, decoherence, entanglement, noncommutative observables, and
wave-function collapse'' {[}57{]}. The aim is to remove the physical
reality of the wavefunction, not to remove nonlocality; Barandes retains
definite particle positions at all times.

\textbf{The double slit, in Barandes's own account.} For single-particle
interference Barandes states that ``the particle always fundamentally
has a single location and is never in both holes simultaneously,'' and
that ``the final interference pattern on the detection screen is not due
to any purported physical reality of Schrödinger waves, but due to the
generic indivisibility of time evolution'' --- ``interference is nothing
more than a generic discrepancy between the actual indivisible
stochastic dynamics and a heuristic-approximate divisible stochastic
dynamics'' {[}57{]}. The particle is local; the interference is carried
by the non-factorizable (``indivisible'') transition dynamics, which
Barandes characterizes as a nonlocality in time that manifests as an
apparent nonlocality across space.

\textbf{What the exactness of the correspondence entails, by Bell's
theorem.} A reformulation that reproduces quantum theory must reproduce
Bell-inequality violations, which are experimentally confirmed. Bell's
theorem establishes that no theory with definite outcomes that is local
in Bell's sense and satisfies statistical independence can reproduce
those violations. Barandes's processes have definite configurations at
all times; his correspondence to quantum theory is exact. These two
facts together force a conclusion: the nonlocal entanglement
correlations are already present inside the indivisible stochastic
processes --- carried by the non-factorizable joint transition matrix
over the two-system configuration space. If the correspondence is exact,
the nonlocal correlations are in the formalism, because Bell guarantees
they must be; if the processes were genuinely local, the correspondence
to quantum theory would not be exact. The exactness of the
correspondence is therefore not evidence that nonlocality has been
removed --- it is proof that the nonlocal entanglement has been
retained, re-encoded as the indivisibility of the joint dynamics and
renamed. ``Quantum theory as an ordinary stochastic process'' is
nonlocal entanglement re-described in stochastic vocabulary, not
eliminated. The program achieves its actual goal --- demoting the
wavefunction --- but it does not, and by Bell cannot, produce quantum
theory from processes lacking nonlocal entanglement; and it supplies a
mathematical re-encoding of the entanglement, not a physical mechanism
for it, with the indivisibility that carries the correlation left as an
unexplained primitive.

\textbf{Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic: the entangled pair is one Sphere.}
The McGucken framework supplies the physical mechanism that the
stochastic-quantum correspondence names but does not provide. Two
entangled photons emitted from a common source are not two systems that
establish a correlation across a distance; they are one expanding
McGucken Sphere, measured at two points. The common emission is one
event; dx₄/dt = ic expands that one event into one spherically symmetric
surface advancing at c; both photons are features of that one surface
(§5.7.4). Their correlation is perfect and requires no signal because
there is only one object: measuring one photon reads the one Sphere, and
the other photon is the same Sphere read at its antipodal point (§7.9,
§3.12). The measurements are spacelike separated, but the entity
measured is single, so no superluminal influence is needed and Bell's
verdict is honored --- the nonlocality is real, and it is the unity of
one expanding surface, not communication between two. This is the
general content of the First McGucken Law of Nonlocality {[}49{]}, for
which entangled systems are those with intersecting light spheres from a
common local origin; the shared-origin pair is the pure case, in which
the two light spheres are not merely intersecting but identical --- one
Sphere. Where Barandes houses the entanglement in the indivisibility of
a joint transition matrix, a mathematical property left unexplained,
dx₄/dt = ic derives it: the joint system is indivisible because it is
one Sphere, and ``indivisibility'' is the stochastic-language
description of what being one expanding surface looks like. Barandes
removes the wavefunction and pays for the entanglement with an
unexplained non-factorizable dynamics; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic
framework keeps a physically real expanding wavefront --- the Sphere ---
and derives the entanglement from it, as the unity of the one surface on
which both photons ride.

\hypertarget{barandess-questions-his-causally-local-proposal-his-open-admissions-and-the-co-generation-of-probability-and-nonlocality-by-dxux2084dt-ic}{%
\paragraph{5.9.1 Barandes's questions, his causally-local proposal, his
open admissions, and the co-generation of probability and nonlocality by
dx₄/dt =
ic}\label{barandess-questions-his-causally-local-proposal-his-open-admissions-and-the-co-generation-of-probability-and-nonlocality-by-dxux2084dt-ic}}

In his 2025 interview {[}57{]}, Barandes poses a specific set of
questions and states his motivation and his proposed resolutions in his
own words; they are reproduced here verbatim, followed by the point on
which the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework diverges.

\textbf{The questions Barandes asks.} The interview is organized around
eight questions: what the wavefunction is --- a physical entity or, as
Born held, ``a tool for computing measurement probabilities'' {[}57{]};
what wave-particle duality really is; what entanglement is and what its
misconceptions are; what the measurement problem is; what quantum
systems are ``made out of,'' given that in textbook quantum theory
``there's just nothing'' {[}57{]} as a substrate; whether gravity is
quantum; what nonlocality and Bell's theorem establish; and what
indivisible stochastic processes are.

\textbf{His motivation: take probability seriously.} Barandes's stated
aim is to build a foundation on ordinary probability --- to treat
quantum theory as a genuine stochastic process over configurations with
definite values at all times, and to demote the wavefunction
accordingly: in the indivisible stochastic approach, in his words,
``there's no wave function. So the wave function is not what the
ontology is. The wave function is whatever your choice of configurations
are'' {[}57{]}. This motivation --- to honor the probabilistic character
of nature and to found quantum theory on it --- is correct and is
shared, as a starting recognition, by the present framework: the Born
measure is a genuine physical probability, the state-count Ω of the
expanding Sphere (§6, §7).

\textbf{Barandes's stated novel contribution: the continuous-time
interpolation of a discrete permutation process.} Barandes identifies
his own central technical novelty in the interview {[}57{]}. Starting
from a discrete-time deterministic process modeled by repeated
multiplication by a permutation matrix, he asks whether it can be
smoothly interpolated to continuous time: ``can we interpolate them? Is
there some smooth way to interpolate this to continuous time? \ldots{}
Turns out there's a very natural way to do it. Um as best I can tell I
think I'm the first person to write this down. Although I'm not sure. I
don't want to claim priority because it's very hard to search in the
literature'' {[}57{]}. This interpolation is what turns a plain
classical permutation into a smoothly evolving unitary flow, from which
a Hamiltonian, energy eigenvalues, and a Schrödinger-type equation are
then read off. It is the technical heart of the program --- the step
that manufactures continuous unitary quantum structure out of a discrete
classical shuffle. Under the reading of the present paper it is also the
clearest instance of the construction pattern noted above: the
continuity and the unitarity are supplied by \emph{interpolating} the
discrete classical process --- built to connect the classical states
smoothly --- not derived from a physical mechanism. The McGucken dx₄/dt
= ic framework does not interpolate a discrete classical dynamics into
continuous unitary time; the continuous evolution is physical from the
outset --- the actual expansion of the fourth dimension at c, dx₄/dt =
ic, whose smoothness is the smoothness of the advancing McGucken Sphere
and whose unitarity is the frozen reading of that advance (§3.11,
§5.2.2). Where Barandes interpolates a permutation to obtain a
continuous unitary and reads a Hamiltonian off the result, the McGucken
dx₄/dt = ic framework begins with the continuous physical advance and
derives the Hamiltonian, the Schrödinger equation, and the unitary flow
as its theorems (§3, {[}38{]}).

\textbf{His proposal for nonlocality: make the theory causally local.}
Where Barandes's program turns is on nonlocality. Rather than accept
nonlocality as a physical feature, he seeks to reclassify quantum theory
as causally local. In his 2024 paper, ``New Prospects for a Causally
Local Formulation of Quantum Theory'' {[}57{]}, he proposes, in his
words, that ``what it means for a theory to be causally local is that
when you have two systems that are at space-like separation\ldots{} then
there's a clean factorization of the conditional probabilities between
them'' {[}57{]}. He supports this with the no-signaling theorem ---
``the steering does not send signals\ldots{} cannot deliberately send
controllable messages'' {[}57{]} --- with Reichenbachian common-cause
factorization, and even with the suggestion that if ``there's no
causation there's no superluminal causation and then the problem is just
solved'' {[}57{]}.

\textbf{His open admissions.} Barandes is candid that his program leaves
foundational questions open. On ontology: ``if we think there's never
going to be some fundamental theory at the bottom of all of this, what
really is out there in nature, that's\ldots{} an open question''
{[}57{]}; the framework may be ``a tower of these theories,'' or ``tap
out to some ultimate quantum field theory or\ldots{} string theory,''
and --- his words --- ``I don't know'' {[}57{]}. On quantum gravity: the
stochastic formulation requires a notion of time-slices and space-like
directions, so ``if the space-time itself is\ldots{} fluctuating, how do
I do this?'' --- which he identifies as ``a gap.'' These are the same
category of admission recorded for Jacobson and Verlinde (§5.6, §5.7):
the originator states that the foundation is not yet supplied.

\textbf{The asymmetry, and its resolution under dx₄/dt = ic.} Barandes
accepts one experimentally established feature of nature --- its
probabilistic character --- and takes it as the foundation, while
resisting a second experimentally established feature --- its
nonlocality, confirmed by Bell-inequality violations --- which he seeks
to reclassify as causal locality. But probability and nonlocality stand
on the same experimental footing: both are what measurement shows. A
foundation that honors the one must honor the other. The McGucken dx₄/dt
= ic framework supplies exactly the reason the two cannot be separated:
probability and nonlocality are co-generated by the same act, the
expansion of the fourth dimension x₄. As established in this paper
(§5.7.4), the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic turns each local event into
an expanding spherical surface, so that ``the point-to-surface expansion
of x₄ is the physical creation of nonlocality, and the Sphere carries
that nonlocality outward at c'' (§5.7.4); and the same expanding surface
carries the Compton-tick state-count Ω whose antipodal overlap is the
Born measure (§7.9, the head-on x₄-collision of two McGucken spheres).
The nonlocality is the expanding surface; the probability is the count
of that surface's states; they are one object seen twice, not two
features to be adopted and discarded independently. Two entangled
photons from a common source are one expanding McGucken Sphere measured
at two points, so their nonlocal correlation and their Born
probabilities are the same Sphere read two ways (§5.9). This is why
Barandes's program can honor probability but cannot, consistently, shed
nonlocality: in the physical mechanism from which both descend --- the
expansion of x₄ at c --- to take the probability is to take the
nonlocality, because the expanding surface that is the one is the
expanding surface that is the other. Barandes takes probability
seriously, as he should, and seeks to remove the nonlocality, which the
shared origin of the two in the expanding McGucken Sphere does not
permit.

\hypertarget{the-maudlinbarandes-debate-the-markov-condition-the-imposition-charge-and-the-single-outcome-problem}{%
\paragraph{5.9.2 The Maudlin--Barandes debate: the Markov condition, the
imposition charge, and the single-outcome
problem}\label{the-maudlinbarandes-debate-the-markov-condition-the-imposition-charge-and-the-single-outcome-problem}}

The 2025 Maudlin--Barandes discussion {[}58{]} brings the governing
assumption of the stochastic-quantum program into the open and exposes
precisely where the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework parts from it.

\textbf{Why Barandes requires the abandonment of the Markov condition.}
Maudlin states the condition plainly: the Markov condition ``is just the
idea that earlier events can only be causally relevant to later events
via intermediate events'' {[}58{]} --- the present screens off the past
from the future. This screening-off, together with locality, is exactly
what generates the factorization conditions underlying Bell's theorem.
Barandes's indivisible stochastic process is defined by the failure of
this condition: the transition matrix does not factorize through
intermediate times, except at isolated ``division events'' where it
momentarily does. The abandonment of Markovianity is the single device
on which the entire program turns: it is what allows Barandes to keep
definite configurations, deny the physical reality of the wavefunction,
and still claim a ``causally local'' account that reproduces
Bell-violating statistics, because the Reichenbach--Bell factorization
that would force genuine nonlocality no longer applies when the process
is non-Markovian. This is why the Markov condition is the recurring
focus: non-Markovianity is the mechanism carrying interference,
entanglement, and the ``causal locality'' claim all at once.

\textbf{Maudlin's imposition charge.} Maudlin presses that the
stochastic-classical reading is stipulated rather than earned. On the
identification of quantum expectation values with classical averages ---
the category problem --- he objects: ``It's not enough just to put
little brackets around a quantity and say it's an average and then say
that therefore it's the same kind of average that we would think of
classically. There's more work that needs to be done'' {[}58{]}. On what
the theory is about, he presses the ontology question directly ---
``what is the ontology? What is the theory saying exists?'' {[}58{]} ---
noting that an indivisible stochastic process is a formal recipe, not an
account of what exists. And on the division events by which the
non-Markovian process is made to yield definite outcomes, the debate
exhibits the difficulty in Barandes's own description: at a measurement
``the indivisible unistochastic matrix factorizes across the two times
and suddenly we get the spontaneous generation of a new division event
that wasn't there before'' {[}58{]}. A division event is introduced
where the theory needs an outcome to actualize, rather than derived ---
the imposition that Maudlin's critique targets: machinery adjusted to
protect the non-Markovian picture, with the justification, in Maudlin's
words, still owed.

\textbf{The single-outcome problem, which the division event papers
over.} The sharpest form of the difficulty is the symmetric-detection
case: a source that can trigger one of many equivalent detectors --- in
the limiting case, a source at the center of a sphere of detectors,
every detector reached with identical weight, exactly one firing. The
indivisible process assigns the outcome probabilities, but the
actualization of one detector rather than another is carried by the
``spontaneous generation of a new division event'' --- a device that
records that one outcome occurs without supplying what selects it. This
is the same gap that appears in the Transactional Interpretation's
symmetric handshake (§7.5) and in the collapse postulate it was meant to
replace: the probabilities are given, but the single actualization among
equal alternatives is left as a primitive.

\textbf{Where the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework sides, and what it
supplies.} On each of Maudlin's three points, the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic
framework sides with the critique and supplies what Barandes leaves
owed. On the category problem, the quantum measure is not a stipulated
classical average: \textbar ψ\textbar² is the physical overlap-count Ω
of the expanding McGucken Sphere, the head-on x₄-collision of two
Spheres (§6, §7.9), a definite physical quantity rather than a classical
average asserted by placing brackets around it. On the ontology, what
exists is the expanding fourth dimension --- the McGucken Sphere at
every event (the Geometric Channel is the physical reality, §5.7) ---
the account of what the theory is about that an indivisible stochastic
process does not provide. On the imposition charge and the
single-outcome problem, the indivisibility that Barandes must posit is,
physically, the unity of one expanding Sphere: an entangled pair is one
Sphere measured at two points (§5.9), so the joint process is
indivisible because it is literally one object, not because a
non-factorizing matrix and ad hoc division events were introduced; and
the single actualization in the sphere-of-detectors case is the physical
Wick rotation localizing the one Sphere at the detector where its
expanding surface collides head-on (§7.9, §7.4), rather than a
spontaneously generated division event. Barandes abandons the Markov
condition to escape nonlocality and inserts division events to recover
definite outcomes; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework derives the
nonlocality as physically real (the point-to-surface expansion of x₄,
co-generated with probability, §5.9.1) and derives the definite outcome
as the physical localization of the one Sphere, so neither the
abandonment nor the insertion is needed. On the reading of this
framework, Maudlin's demand --- that more work is needed to earn the
classical-probabilistic picture, and that the theory must say what
exists --- is met not by imposing a stochastic reading on quantum
mechanics but by deriving quantum mechanics, with its probability and
its nonlocality together, from the expanding McGucken Sphere dx₄/dt =
ic.

\hypertarget{schullers-constructive-gravity-what-the-peer-reviewed-paper-claims-versus-the-gravity-from-electromagnetism-popularization-the-maxwell-circularity-and-dxux2084dt-ic-as-the-physical-principle-underlying-maxwell-the-lorentzian-metric-quantum-mechanics-general-relativity-and-thermodynamics}{%
\subsubsection{5.10 Schuller's constructive gravity: what the
peer-reviewed paper claims versus the ``gravity from electromagnetism''
popularization, the Maxwell circularity, and dx₄/dt = ic as the physical
principle underlying Maxwell, the Lorentzian metric, quantum mechanics,
general relativity, and
thermodynamics}\label{schullers-constructive-gravity-what-the-peer-reviewed-paper-claims-versus-the-gravity-from-electromagnetism-popularization-the-maxwell-circularity-and-dxux2084dt-ic-as-the-physical-principle-underlying-maxwell-the-lorentzian-metric-quantum-mechanics-general-relativity-and-thermodynamics}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c, as a spherically
symmetric wavefront, from every event of spacetime. Frédéric Schuller's
constructive-gravity programme {[}61, 62{]} determines gravitational
dynamics, and selects the Lorentzian signature, from the requirement
that matter be predictive, interpretable, and quantizable on an a priori
general tensorial background. This section separates what the
peer-reviewed paper claims from the popularization headline, identifies
the point at which Maxwell's equations enter, shows that because
Maxwell's equations already contain the invariant speed of light --- one
of the two postulates from which Einstein derived Lorentzian spacetime
in 1905 --- the recovery of the Lorentzian metric from electromagnetism
returns to electromagnetism's own starting point, and shows that dx₄/dt
= ic derives the invariant c, the Lorentzian metric, and Maxwell's
equations from the expansion of the fourth dimension, together with
quantum mechanics, general relativity, and thermodynamics.

\textbf{What the peer-reviewed paper claims.} The peer-reviewed paper
(Giesel, Schuller, Witte, and Wohlfarth, Physical Review D 85, 104042,
2012 {[}61{]}) is titled ``Gravitational dynamics for all tensorial
spacetimes carrying predictive, interpretable and quantizable matter.''
The title makes no claim of deriving gravity from electromagnetism. Its
claim, in the abstract's own words, is that ``only a severely restricted
class of tensor fields can provide classical spacetime geometries,
namely those that can carry matter field equations that are predictive,
interpretable and quantizable,'' that ``these three conditions on matter
translate into three corresponding algebraic conditions on the
underlying tensorial geometry, namely to be hyperbolic, time-orientable
and energy-distinguishing,'' and that ``Lorentzian metrics, on which
general relativity and the standard model of particle physics are built,
present just the simplest tensorial spacetime geometry satisfying these
conditions'' {[}61{]}. The operative word is simplest: the Lorentzian
metric is the simplest member of a class of admissible geometries,
selected rather than forced uniquely. The paper's stated deliverable is
that ``the search for modified gravitational dynamics is reduced to a
clear mathematical task'' {[}61{]} --- a system of linear partial
differential equations, the gravitational-closure equations, whose
solutions yield the action governing a given geometry.

\textbf{The popularization headline.} The video presentation of the work
carries the title ``The Physicist Who Derived Gravity From
Electromagnetism'' {[}61, popularization note{]}. This is a
popularization headline, not the paper title, and it claims more than
the paper does. The peer-reviewed paper determines gravitational
dynamics for a matter model's causal structure and selects Lorentzian
signature as the simplest admissible geometry; the video headline states
that gravity was derived from electromagnetism. The gap between the two
framings is the gap between the careful hedged result the paper
establishes and the strong claim the popularization asserts.

\textbf{What the paper does.} The construction is a procedure ---
gravitational closure, built on the Hojman--Kuchař--Teitelboim
geometrodynamics apparatus {[}62{]} --- that takes a matter model's
causal structure as input and returns the gravitational dynamics
compatible with it. A matter model must be specified before the geometry
can be constrained, and Schuller states this explicitly. In the master
recipe of {[}61{]}, step 2 is: ``Decide on matter dynamics to define the
causal structure impressed on the geometry. These matter equations may
well be of phenomenological nature, as were the Maxwell equations before
1905. This is where the theory gets its vital injection from realistic
physics.'' For the Maxwell input the closure output is the
Einstein--Hilbert action; for non-Maxwell matter models --- area-metric
and weakly birefringent electrodynamics --- the closure output is a
modified gravitational dynamics on a non-Lorentzian geometry. What the
paper does, therefore, is supply a general machine mapping matter causal
structure to gravitational dynamics, with Maxwell to Einstein--Hilbert
as the flagship case; it does not derive gravity from electromagnetism
with nothing else supplied.

\textbf{The Maxwell circularity: electromagnetism already contains one
of the two postulates of special relativity.} Maxwell's equations fix
the speed of electromagnetic waves as c = 1/√(ε₀μ₀), a constant
determined by the equations themselves with no reference to any observer
or frame. The frame-independence of that speed is the empirical content
that broke Galilean relativity, and it is the second postulate of
Einstein's 1905 special relativity --- the constancy of the speed of
light --- from which, with the principle of relativity, the Lorentz
transformations and the Lorentzian metric follow. Einstein's 1905 paper
is titled ``On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies''; Lorentzian
spacetime was derived from electromagnetism. The paper's conclusions
state the dependence in full: ``it was Maxwell theory that justified
Einstein to promote Lorentzian manifolds to the status of a spacetime
geometry'' {[}61{]}. Consequently a construction that feeds ordinary
Maxwell electrodynamics in as its matter model and recovers the
Lorentzian metric as the geometry that renders that matter predictive
recovers the Lorentzian structure from the theory in which it
originated. The invariant c that makes Maxwell's equations predictive in
a signature-selecting way is the same invariant c that is the seed of
the Lorentzian metric. The generalized programme escapes this loop where
it treats non-Maxwell matter --- area-metric and birefringent
electrodynamics, whose causal structure is not the standard light cone
--- and there the selected geometry is genuinely non-Lorentzian; but the
Maxwell case, on which the ``gravity from electromagnetism''
popularization rests, takes as its input the theory that already carries
the invariant c from which the Lorentzian output descends.

\textbf{Resolution under dx₄/dt = ic: the physical principle beneath
Maxwell and the metric alike.} The McGucken Principle does not take the
invariant c from Maxwell's equations. It takes c as the rate of the
expansion of the fourth dimension --- a physical-geometric primitive,
prior to electromagnetism and to any field theory. The constancy of the
speed of light is derived from the Principle as a theorem (Theorem
2.4.5, clause P2): the rate of x₄-advance is \textbar ic\textbar{} = c
at every event by the universality clause of Principle 2.1, the photon's
null worldline reads the slope of the null cone, and the null cone is
Lorentz-invariant, so c is the same in every inertial frame. The
Lorentzian metric is derived by the pullback (ic)² = −c² (Lemma 2.5),
signature and volume and all, rather than selected as the simplest
admissible option once a matter model has impressed a causal structure.
And Maxwell's equations themselves are derived from the Principle: the
U(1) gauge structure of electromagnetism is the phase-cycle of the
x₄-advance, so electromagnetism is a downstream sector of dx₄/dt = ic
rather than the input from which the geometry is recovered. The order of
derivation is the reverse of constructive gravity's. Schuller: specify
Maxwell electrodynamics, which contains the invariant c, and determine
the Lorentzian-Einstein dynamics that the invariant c's geometry
supports. McGucken: state the expansion of the fourth dimension at c,
and derive the invariant c, the Lorentzian metric, Maxwell's equations,
and the U(1) gauge structure, with none of them presupposed. Where
constructive gravity's Maxwell case determines gravitational dynamics on
the Lorentzian geometry that electromagnetism historically produced,
dx₄/dt = ic supplies the physical principle beneath both
electromagnetism and the metric --- and, as the theorem chains of this
paper and the corpus establish, beneath quantum mechanics, general
relativity, and thermodynamics as well. The invariant c that
constructive gravity must take from Maxwell, and that Einstein read off
Maxwell in 1905, is in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework the rate of
the one expansion from which Maxwell, the metric, and the rest descend.

\hypertarget{northeys-quaternionic-spinor-gravity-matter-makes-space-and-the-born-rule-as-spinorgeometry-rigidity-approached-from-the-opposite-direction-to-dxux2084dt-ic}{%
\subsubsection{5.11 Northey's quaternionic spinor gravity: ``matter
makes space'' and the Born rule as spinor--geometry rigidity, approached
from the opposite direction to dx₄/dt =
ic}\label{northeys-quaternionic-spinor-gravity-matter-makes-space-and-the-born-rule-as-spinorgeometry-rigidity-approached-from-the-opposite-direction-to-dxux2084dt-ic}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c, as a spherically
symmetric wavefront, from every event of spacetime; the Lorentzian
metric and the Dirac spinor both descend from that expansion. Julian
Northey's quaternionic spinor gravity {[}63, 64{]} reaches the Born rule
from the opposite direction: it takes the spinor as primitive and builds
spacetime from it. This section states Northey's construction and
direction of derivation, notes the point on which it agrees with the
present framework, and identifies the point on which the two are
inverse. The account here is drawn from the abstracts of {[}63{]} and
{[}64{]}, which state the thesis and method in full; the internal proofs
of {[}63{]} were not consulted, and none is required to establish the
relation, which turns on the direction of derivation the abstracts state
explicitly.

\textbf{Northey's construction and its direction.} Northey works within
a quaternionic Einstein--Cartan--Kibble--Sciama framework, representing
the Dirac field as a biquaternionic spinor --- an internal SU(2) doublet
of complex Dirac spinors --- and takes the spinor as the primitive
object from which geometry is built. The founding paper is titled
``Matter Makes Space'' {[}64{]}, and its abstract states the direction:
``By recasting Dirac spinors as bi-quaternionic fields and spacetime
geometry as emergent from their non-commutative algebra, the
long-standing tensions are resolved between quantum nonlocality and
geometric gravity'' {[}64{]}; a companion statement records that ``from
this single field, spacetime geometry---both metric and affine
structure---emerges naturally.'' The metric and the affine connection
are composite, constructed from spinor bilinears; the spinor is the
bedrock. On this base the Born rule is derived {[}63{]}: probability is
the hypersurface flux of a conserved current Jμ{[}Ψ{]}, and imposing
locality, internal gauge invariance, observer-independent positivity,
on-shell conservation, dimensional consistency, and universality selects
the Dirac current Jμ ∝ \(\bar{\Psi}\)γμΨ, yielding ρ = −Jμnμ and hence ρ
= Ψ†Ψ in the local rest frame, with deformed measures excluded. The Born
rule is, in Northey's words, ``a rigidity property of the
spinor--geometry correspondence rather than a phenomenological
postulate'' {[}63{]}.

\textbf{Where the two frameworks agree.} Two agreements are physical
rather than incidental. Both derive the Born rule as a
uniqueness-and-exclusion result: a set of physical requirements selects
the \textbar ψ\textbar² measure, and amplitude rescalings that would
deform it are excluded. Northey imposes six requirements --- locality,
internal gauge invariance, observer-independent positivity, on-shell
conservation, dimensional consistency, and universality --- that select
the Dirac current and exclude Harrison-style amplitude rescalings
{[}63{]}. The present framework's uniqueness theorem (§3.4) imposes the
four requirements (R1)--(R4) --- reality, non-negativity, phase
invariance, and bilinearity --- that force P = \textbar ψ\textbar², and
§3.5 excludes precisely the deformed densities: \textbar ψ\textbar,
\textbar ψ\textbar³, ψ², and the quartic (ψ*ψ)² are each ruled out by
(R1)--(R4). Northey's excluded Harrison rescalings and the present
framework's excluded \textbar ψ\textbar\^{}k deformations are the same
family, and both derivations turn on forcing the exponent 2 and
excluding every rescaling of it. Neither derivation uses Gleason's
theorem: Northey forces the exponent from a conserved-current
variational argument, and the present framework forces it five
derivationally disjoint ways --- the Metric Route from the rank-2
Lorentzian metric (§3.1), the Haar Route from the SO(3) symmetry of the
Sphere (§3.2), the Norm Route from the parallelogram identity (§3.3),
the Collision Route from the two-Sphere head-on collision (§3.8), and
the PT-Symmetry Route --- where §3.6 places Gleason among the prior
programs that instead derive the rule on a postulated Hilbert space.
Both papers also cite the operational-redundancy result of Masanes,
Galley, and Müller as the modern statement that the measurement
postulate is not independent (§3, §3.6). And both hold that quantum
structure and spacetime geometry are aspects of one object rather than
separate posits. The Born rule as a rigidity forced by physical
requirements, not a postulate, is a conclusion the two frameworks reach
in common.

\textbf{Where the two frameworks are inverse.} The frameworks differ on
what is primitive, and the difference is exact. Northey takes the
biquaternionic Dirac spinor as primitive and builds spacetime --- metric
and connection --- from its non-commutative algebra: matter makes space.
The McGucken Principle takes the expanding fourth dimension as primitive
and derives both the Lorentzian metric (Lemma 2.5, the pullback (ic)² =
−c²) and the Dirac spinor (the quantum chain, the Dirac sector) from the
expansion: the expansion makes both space and the spinor. Northey's
bedrock --- the spinor --- is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, a
derived structure, one of the objects the expansion produces; and the
composite metric he constructs from spinor bilinears is, in the McGucken
dx₄/dt = ic framework, the coordinate integral of the advance, prior to
the spinor rather than built from it. The Dirac current Jμ =
\(\bar{\Psi}\)γμΨ whose rest-frame flux Northey identifies as the Born
density is, under dx₄/dt = ic, itself a consequence of the x₄-advance,
so the object from which he begins is one the Principle derives. The two
constructions therefore approach the Born rule from opposite ends of the
same correspondence: Northey from the spinor upward to the geometry, the
McGucken Principle from the expansion downward to both the geometry and
the spinor. Where ``matter makes space'' takes the quaternionic spinor
as given and lets geometry emerge, dx₄/dt = ic supplies the physical
principle beneath the spinor and the metric alike, and derives the Born
rule as the state-count of the expanding Sphere (§6) and as the head-on
collision of two Spheres (§3.8, §7.6) rather than as the rigidity of a
map whose primitive term --- the spinor --- is itself left underived.

\hypertarget{doraumuchs-derivation-of-the-semiclassical-einstein-equations-from-quantum-relative-entropy-each-input-a-theorem-of-the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic}{%
\subsubsection{5.12 Dorau--Much's derivation of the semiclassical
Einstein equations from quantum relative entropy, each input a theorem
of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt =
ic}\label{doraumuchs-derivation-of-the-semiclassical-einstein-equations-from-quantum-relative-entropy-each-input-a-theorem-of-the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states the physical reality that the fourth dimension expands at the
rate c, as a spherically symmetric wavefront --- the McGucken Sphere,
whose wavelength carries one quantum of action h per Compton cycle ---
from every event of spacetime. Gravity and the quantum field's
information measure are both theorem chains of that Principle (§5, §3),
so Dorau and Much's derivation of the Einstein equations from the
quantum relative entropy of the vacuum is another reading of the one
expanding McGucken Sphere, and this section shows that each quantity
they take as input is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic.

\textbf{What Dorau and Much establish.} Dorau and Much {[}65{]} derive
the semiclassical Einstein equations from the Araki--Uhlmann relative
entropy of a scalar quantum field on a bifurcate Killing horizon. Their
abstract states the result verbatim: ``the relative entropy between the
vacuum state and coherent excitations of a scalar quantum field on a
bifurcate Killing horizon is given by the energy flux across the
horizon,'' and ``under the assumption of the Bekenstein-Hawking
entropy-area formula, this energy flux is proportional to a variation in
the surface area of the horizon cross section,'' so that ``the
semiclassical Einstein equations follow automatically from this
identification'' {[}65{]}. They name the construction ``a quantum field
theoretic generalization of Jacobson's thermodynamic derivation of the
Einstein equations, replacing classical thermodynamic entropy with the
well-defined quantum relative (Araki-Uhlmann) entropy'' {[}65{]}, and
conclude that ``the semiclassical Einstein equations, and thus local
spacetime curvature, can be interpreted as arising from quantum
information, namely the distinguishability between vacuum and excited
states on local horizons'' {[}65{]}. The chain is: the relative entropy
of a coherent excitation against the vacuum equals the energy flux
across the horizon, S\_rel = −2π ∫ U ⟨:T\_ab:⟩ ξ\^{}a ξ\^{}b dU dvol
(their Eq. 13); matched to the Raychaudhuri area focusing δA = −∫ U
R\_ab ξ\^{}a ξ\^{}b dU dvol (their Eq. 24), the two give the
semiclassical Einstein equations R\_ab − ½ R g\_ab + Λ g\_ab = α
⟨:T\_ab:⟩ (their Eq. 28), with the proportionality constant fixed to α =
8π ``if we assume in analogy to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy-area
relation \ldots{} that the relative entropy is equal to one fourth of
the area variation'' {[}65{]}. The inputs they take as given are the
local Minkowski metric g\_ab ≈ η\_ab (their Eq. 1, via the equivalence
principle), the Bekenstein--Hawking area law, the geometric modular flow
Δ\^{}\{it\} = D\_\{2πt\} with the vacuum a KMS state at the Unruh
temperature (Bisognano--Wichmann {[}68{]}, Summers--Verch), the
quasifree Hadamard vacuum, and the bifurcate Killing horizon; Dorau
remarks that ``most of the ingredients for our work have been known for
decades'' {[}65{]}.

\textbf{LTD reading.} Dorau and Much set a quantum distinguishability
measure --- the Araki--Uhlmann relative entropy of the vacuum against a
coherent excitation --- at the horizon, proportional to the horizon area
variation, and read the Einstein equations off that proportionality. In
the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework the relative entropy that
distinguishes vacuum from excitation and the horizon area variation are
the same count Ω of distinguishable Compton-tick states of the one
expanding McGucken Sphere: the distinguishability count read at the
event, and the Bekenstein--Hawking count read over the horizon, proven
one entropy S = k ln Ω in Theorem 7.3. Dorau and Much match the two by
the assumed proportionality S\_rel = δA/4; the McGucken Principle
derives that proportionality as the one count read over two surfaces
(§6, §7). Every input they take as given is a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic:
the local Minkowski metric is the exact pullback (ic)² = −c² of the
advancing Sphere (Lemma 2.5, §2); the Bekenstein--Hawking area law is
the Compton-tick Planck-area count of the Sphere (§4.2); the geometric
modular flow and its Unruh/KMS temperature are the Euclidean x₄-period
of the Sphere under the McGucken--Wick rotation (§7.4, Appendix C); the
quasifree vacuum is the overlap of the Spheres expanding at +ic from
neighboring events; and the bifurcate Killing horizon is the null
wavefront of the Sphere at the event (§4.1, §5.8). The derivation that
the Araki--Uhlmann relative entropy itself, the modular flow it rests
on, and the horizon it is defined on are each theorems of dx₄/dt = ic is
given in full in Appendix D, where the wedge algebra of the McGucken
field is shown to be the setting in which relative entropy replaces the
von Neumann entropy, the modular flow is the x₄-advance read in the
accelerated frame, and the relative-entropy functional is the count Ω.
Dorau and Much's statement that ``most of the ingredients \ldots{} have
been known for decades'' {[}65{]} is the reading this paper supplies:
the ingredients are the several readings of the one expanding McGucken
Sphere, and dx₄/dt = ic is the Principle from which they descend. Their
result reaches the gravity-to-quantum-information link --- local
spacetime curvature from the distinguishability of quantum states ---
one step short of ``gravity is the Born rule,'' because for them the
quantum measure and the horizon area are matched at a boundary by the
assumed proportionality, where dx₄/dt = ic derives both as the one count
Ω of the one Sphere.

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-chandrasekarans-an-algebraic-quantization-of-gravity-from-the-null-cone-2026-the-null-cone-as-the-mcgucken-sphere-the-gravitational-clock-as-its-radius-the-area-count-as-its-planck-cells-the-hilbert-space-and-the-lorentzian-manifold-as-its-cogenerated-structures-and-the-arrow-of-time-his-axioms-exclude}{%
\subsubsection{5.13 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of
Chandrasekaran's ``An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null
cone'' (2026): the null cone as the McGucken Sphere, the gravitational
clock as its radius, the area count as its Planck cells, the Hilbert
space and the Lorentzian manifold as its cogenerated structures, and the
arrow of time his axioms
exclude}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-chandrasekarans-an-algebraic-quantization-of-gravity-from-the-null-cone-2026-the-null-cone-as-the-mcgucken-sphere-the-gravitational-clock-as-its-radius-the-area-count-as-its-planck-cells-the-hilbert-space-and-the-lorentzian-manifold-as-its-cogenerated-structures-and-the-arrow-of-time-his-axioms-exclude}}

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding
at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically
symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose
volume defines a nonlocality. This section reads Chandrasekaran's
quantization of vacuum general relativity on intersecting null cones
{[}83{]}, with his seminar on the same work {[}84{]}, against the
theorems of the Principle established in §§2--5 of this paper and in the
corpus papers {[}23{]}, {[}24{]}, {[}29{]}, {[}46{]}, {[}49{]}, and
{[}85{]}. Every statement attributed to {[}83{]} below is quoted from
its text with its equation or section number; every statement attributed
to {[}84{]} is quoted with its timestamp; every corpus theorem is
reproduced verbatim from its source with the source named, and the
restatements and proofs that follow a quotation are the present paper's.
Evidence levels: {[}83{]} verified-read in full (abstract, §§1--6,
Appendices A--E, references; the footnote bodies are absent from the
copy read); {[}84{]} verified-read to 1:10:45, where the available
transcript ends; {[}24{]}, {[}46{]}, {[}49{]}, {[}85{]} verified-read
for the theorems quoted; {[}29{]} verified-read in its v203 text for the
theorems quoted.

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic makes the following
predictions about a construction of the kind in {[}83{]}. (i) A
quantization carried out on null cones is carried out on McGucken
Spheres, because the future null cone of an event p is the locus swept
by x₄'s spherical expansion at c from p, Σ₊(p), of radius r = ct (§2),
and the past null cone of an event q is the locus of the events p whose
McGucken Spheres Σ₊(p) arrive at q. (ii) The data needed on such a cone
are the transverse shape of the McGucken Sphere alone, because the
radial advance is fixed at c, and the interior at t + dt is determined
by the data on Σ₊(p) at t (§6.2.8, Theorem 21 of {[}24{]}). (iii) A
clock defined by affine advance along a generator from the apex is the
radius r = ct = x₄/i of the McGucken Sphere; it increases in one
direction because the rate is +ic, and it has a period, one Compton
wavelength per cycle with action h per cycle (§2; Proposition 2.2.bis.1
of {[}85{]}). (iv) A state count bounded by the area of a cut is the
Planck-cell count of the McGucken Sphere, S = k\_B A/4ℓ\_P² (Theorem 12;
Theorem 19.6.1), and a thermal weight obtained by continuing a corner
boost through 2π arises from the Euclidean period of the advance
(Theorem 13) taken over that count. (v) The canonical commutator, the
Hilbert space, and the Lorentzian manifold on which such a construction
is set are theorems of the Principle, derived together (Lemma 2.5,
Theorems 5.1, 6.1, 10.6 of {[}29{]}, reproduced in §5.13.2). (vi)
Entanglement across a corner and across a bifurcation surface is the
nonlocality of the McGucken Sphere whose generators pass through them
({[}49{]}; §5.9). (vii) The field equations obtained in the classical
limit are those derived in Theorem 9 and Theorem 14. (viii) Any
orientation of time used in such a construction enters as a convention,
because its equations read the squared form (ic)² = −c² of the rate
(Theorem 15; Theorem 16.2 of {[}85{]}), while the Principle derives the
orientation from the sign of +ic (Theorem 11; Theorem 4.6.4 of
{[}29{]}). Each prediction is verified against {[}83{]} below.

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-what-chandrasekaran-constructs-in-his-words}{%
\paragraph{5.13.1 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of what
Chandrasekaran constructs, in his
words}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-what-chandrasekaran-constructs-in-his-words}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic predicts that the
objects defined in {[}83{]} --- causal diamond, null cones, corner,
clock, area, boost charge, Fock space, Hilbert space of the diamond,
entropy, axioms --- are readings of one McGucken Sphere and of the
Hilbert space it cogenerates; the definitions are reproduced here so
that each later theorem of this section refers to {[}83{]}'s own
sentences.

The claim of {[}83{]} (abstract): ``We propose a background independent
quantization of vacuum general relativity on four dimensional Lorentzian
spacetimes. Starting from first order gravity, we solve the
gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones of a bulk subregion
and obtain the reduced phase space at finite G\_N. We promote its
canonical Poisson brackets to commutation relations and use deformations
of the reduced action to define an algebra of observables. Equipped with
this, we use Gaussian wavefunctions of canonical pairs to construct a
nonperturbative Hilbert space representation, for which this algebra
generates a type I factor. By composing amplitudes between states
prepared on null cones, we then obtain a Lorentzian path integral in
which each sum over intermediate states converges absolutely. As a
check, we compute the amplitude for graviton pair creation and
annihilation on a null cone nonperturbatively in G\_N and find a finite
closed form expression, even though expanding first in G\_N yields a
logarithmic divergence. We next use diffeomorphism invariance of the
path integral to show that a macroscopic causal diamond with a given
maximum size has a finite dimensional Hilbert space. From the Lorentzian
trace we obtain the Bekenstein Hawking entropy for marginally trapped
surfaces and calculate its logarithmic correction for large
Schwarzschild black holes, recovering at one loop the coefficient Sen
obtained through Euclidean methods. We end by deriving the semiclassical
Einstein equations to one loop as the low energy limit of this theory.''

The region ({[}83{]} §1): ``In a causal diamond we can dress these
observables to a dynamical reference frame at the spacelike corner where
the future null cone from its past tip intersects the past null cone
from its future tip.'' The reason for the null boundary ({[}83{]} §1):
``A description of the interior in terms of boundary observables is
particularly natural when the boundary is null. To specify a classical
solution inside a null cone, we can choose two functions along its
generators together with data at its cuts and solve the null
constraints.'' The orientation of the generators ({[}83{]} Figure 7
caption): ``The arrows ℓ\_p\^{}a and ℓ\_q\^{}a are the future directed
null generators of these boundaries at S.''

The clock ({[}83{]} §2): ``We likewise define a gravitational clock for
a causal diamond by following an incoming null generator from the
spacelike cap Σ₀ that cuts off the past tip to the corner S where it
meets the outgoing null cone. Fixing the tangent vector in a local
Lorentz frame on Σ₀ sets the scale of the affine parameter, so if we
take it to vanish there its value at the corner defines the clock
reading.'' Its monotonicity ({[}83{]} §2.1): ``its reading increases
strictly from zero.'' Its formula ({[}83{]} equation (3.27)): u*(y) =
p\_\{ε,y\}{[}u(1, y) − u(ε, y){]} = ϱ\_S(y) ∫\_ε\^{}1 e\^{}\{Ξ\_y(v)\}
dv, with Ξ\_y(v) ≥ 0 the shear integral of equation (3.26c), ϱ\_S(y) the
areal radius at the corner, and ε the cap cut-off; its angular average
({[}83{]} equation (3.28)): ū* = ∫\_S ϱ\_S u* ϵ₀ / ∫\_S ϱ\_S ϵ₀, with
∫\_S ϵ₀ = 4π. Its value on a shear-free cone ({[}83{]} §5.1): ``On this
null cone the shear vanishes and ϱ\_S(y) = b on every null generator, so
the classical clock reads (1 − ε)b,'' with corner area 𝒜 = 4πb². Its
value on the Schwarzschild horizon cone ({[}83{]} equation (5.52b)): ū*
= (1 − ε)√(𝒜/4π). Its commutation with the area ({[}83{]} §5.2):
``{[}\(\hat{\bar{u}}^{*}\), \(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\){]} = 0.''

The area and the boost ({[}83{]} equation (3.43)): 𝒦 = ∫\_S ϵ₀ 𝒦(y) =
𝒜/8πG\_N, with 𝒦(y) = ϱ\_S(y)²/8πG\_N the boost charge aspect. The
quantum of area ({[}83{]} equation (4.12b)): \(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\)
a\textbar i⟩ = (𝒜\_i + 8πG\_Nħk) a\textbar i⟩, for an insertion a of
definite boost frequency k. The thermal weight ({[}83{]} equations
(5.23a)--(5.23b)): C\_𝒟 = U e\^{}\{−\(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\)/8G\_Nħ\} P\_𝒟,
C\_𝒟†C\_𝒟 = P\_𝒟 e\^{}\{−\(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\)/4G\_Nħ\} P\_𝒟, obtained
by continuing the corner boost rapidity to iπ on each of two glued
copies.

The state space ({[}83{]} equation (4.10c)): 𝒦\_𝒜 ≃ ⊕\emph{\{m=0\}\^{}∞
Sym\^{}m ℓ²(ℕ), the Fock space of the two radiative polarizations at
fixed corner area; the Hilbert space of the diamond ({[}83{]} equations
(5.1)--(5.2)): ℋ\_𝒟 = P\_𝒟 ℋ\_ω with P\_𝒟 = 𝟏}\{{[}0,
ℓ(𝒟){]}\}(\(\hat{\bar{u}}^{*}\)); the bound on area ({[}83{]} equation
(5.21d)): 0 ≤ P\_𝒟 \(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\) P\_𝒟 ≤ {[}4π ℓ(𝒟)²/(1 − ε)²{]}
P\_𝒟; the dimension ({[}83{]} §5.2): ``Hence ℋ\_𝒟 is finite
dimensional''; and ({[}83{]} equation (5.39c) and the sentence
following): ``The corner area can therefore take at most d\_𝒟 distinct
values.''

The entropy ({[}83{]} equation (5.50)): S(ρ\_𝒟) = −Tr(ρ\_𝒟 log ρ\_𝒟) =
⟨\(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\)⟩/4G\_Nħ + log Z\_\{𝒟,1\}, with the corner a
marginally trapped surface ({[}83{]} equation (5.51)):
Θ\_(ℓ)\textbar{}\emph{S = 0, Θ}(n)\textbar\_S \textless{} 0. The
logarithmic correction ({[}83{]} equations (5.68)--(5.69)): q = 257/302
and q/2(1 − q) − 1/2 = 106/45.

The classical limit ({[}83{]} §6): ``In this limit, invariance of the
amplitude under field shifts in the interior yields the Einstein
equations in each subregion''; ({[}83{]} equation (6.4)) R\_ab − ½R
g\_ab + Λ g\_ab = 0; the backreaction ({[}83{]} equation (6.16) and the
sentence introducing it): ``With the initial and boundary data fixed,
the retarded solution for ḡ = g₀ + Δg obeys Δg = Δg₀ −
𝒢\_R⟨E\^{}\{(2)\}{[}h, h{]}⟩\_𝒢 + O(ħ²), where 𝒢\_R is the retarded
Green's function of the linearized Einstein equations on the reduced
phase space.''

The axioms ({[}83{]} Appendix E.1): ``1. Diffeomorphism invariance. We
require invariance under diffeomorphisms that preserve the boundary
conditions and under changes of intermediate cuts.'' ``2. Reality and
positivity.'' ``3. Factorization.'' ``4. Continuous unitary time
evolution. Real time evolution U from Σ to Σ′ has inverse U† and
preserves the inner product.'' ``5. Spectrum and finiteness.'' The
purpose of the axioms ({[}83{]} Appendix E): ``We would like to recover
that Hilbert space and its operator algebra from the amplitudes
themselves.''

The author's description of the method ({[}84{]}, 11:53--12:00):
``nothing I'm going to talk about is particularly novel. Like it's not
like the ingredients are like make use of some super new thing. These
are all ingredients that have been there for a while.'' The guiding
premise ({[}84{]}, 1:28--1:53): ``we know that black holes have an area
law entropy order 4G \ldots{} I kind I want to basically take this kind
of thing as sort of a guiding principle for how should we build states
of spacetime.'' The reason for the null cone ({[}84{]}, 7:26--7:40):
``Maybe we should be looking at light cones or like null cones because
on a null cone the constraints are like transport equations or
characteristic equations \ldots{} because it's null you kind of get
space and time together for free.'' The clock ({[}84{]}, 58:19--58:51):
``an important part of this construction is the existence of a clock
that's just given to you by gravity \ldots{} I can integrate
Raychaudhuri's equation to get like area as a function of like an affine
parameter \ldots{} from one spacetime to another the amount of time it
takes to get from say the corner to the cap will fluctuate.'' The
nonlocality ({[}84{]}, 56:17--56:25): ``this theory is non-local in the
sense that everything lives on the cone and there are no pointlike
objects.'' The aim ({[}84{]}, 55:42): ``we will basically take these
abstract null cone algebras and build space and build time roughly
speaking.''

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-the-corpus-theorems-this-section-uses-reproduced-verbatim}{%
\paragraph{5.13.2 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of the

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic is the single premise of
each theorem below; the theorems are reproduced from {[}29{]}, {[}46{]},
{[}49{]}, and {[}85{]} without alteration, so that the comparisons in

From {[}29{]}, Lemma 2.5 (Lorentzian signature on the constraint
surface), as reproduced with its proof in {[}85{]} §2.7: ``The
constraint surface Φ\_M⁻¹(0) ⊂ E₄, equipped with the metric induced from
the four-dimensional Euclidean line element ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² +
dx₄², is the Lorentzian spacetime Minkowski Space 𝕄\_\{1,3\} with
signature (−,+,+,+).'' Proof: ``On the constraint surface, x₄ = ict, so
dx₄ = ic dt and dx₄² = (ic)² dt² = −c² dt². Substitution into the
four-dimensional Euclidean line element yields dℓ² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃²
+ dx₄² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c² dt², which is the Minkowski metric with
signature (−,+,+,+). ∎''

From {[}85{]}, Proposition 2.2.bis.1 (Three exact substrate-tick
identifications): ``During one Compton substrate tick of a massive
particle of rest mass m at event p ∈ Minkowski Space 𝕄\_(1,3), the
following three quantities are given exactly: (i) The fourth-dimensional
advance: Δx₄ = ic · Δt\_C = iλ\_C, where λ\_C = h/mc is the Compton
wavelength. (ii) The action accumulation: ΔS = E · Δt\_C = mc² · 2πħ/mc²
= 2πħ = h. (iii) The oscillation phase advance: ω\_C · Δt\_C = mc²/ħ ·
2πħ/mc² = 2π (one full cycle).''

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 5.1 (Canonical commutation relation from dx₄/dt =
ic): ``The canonical commutation relation {[}\(\hat{q}\), \(\hat{p}\){]}
= iℏ follows from the McGucken Principle as a single foundational

quantization of x₄-advance per Planck-frequency oscillation (Proposition
2.2).''

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 6.1 (Hilbert space from dx₄/dt = ic): ``The
Hilbert space 𝓗 of nonrelativistic single-particle quantum mechanics is
the unique irreducible separable Hilbert-space representation of the
Weyl form of the McGucken-derived canonical commutator algebra: U(a)
V(b) = exp(−i (a · b)/ℏ) V(b) U(a), a, b ∈ ℝ³, with iℏ supplied by

ψ)(x) = exp(i (a · x)/ℏ) ψ(x), (V(b) ψ)(x) = ψ(x + b).'' (The bracketed
numbers {[}108{]} and {[}109{]} are the reference numbers internal to
{[}29{]}.)

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 6.1.5 (Hilbert space from McGucken-Sphere

of nonrelativistic single-particle quantum mechanics is the Cauchy

superpositions of McGucken-Sphere wavefronts on the spatial slice ℝ³ at

the spatial slice of the pointwise product of two wavefronts' complex

inherited from McGucken structures already established in the dx₄/dt =
ic framework: rank-2 sesquilinearity from Lemma 7.1 (rank-2 metric
pairing), conjugate symmetry from Theorem 7.11 (PT-symmetry through the

L²(ℝ³, d³x), the same Hilbert space supplied by the Algebraic Channel's
Stone--von Neumann derivation.''

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 10.6 (Hilbert space and Minkowski space as one

(i)--(iii) of five: ``The Hilbert space 𝓗 of quantum mechanics derived
in Theorem 6.1 of the present paper and the Minkowski spacetime manifold

𝕄\_\{1,3\} at parameter time t, with the rigged-Hilbert-space inner
product ⟨x \textbar{} y⟩ = δ³(x − y) reproducing in distributional form
the spatial-distance content of the Minkowski metric on the slice.''

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 16.15.1 (W1 as McGucken cascade theorem): ``The

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 9.5.11 (Wick rotation as coordinate

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 4.6.4 (Sign-orientation: +ic is derivational, not

of the x₄-advance as +i, not −i. The orientation +ic is fixed at the

into its causal future; the time-reversed branch dx₄/dt = −ic generates

From {[}85{]}, §16.3, the decomposition of the Principle's right-hand
side: ``The decomposition +ic = +· i · c makes the content of the
principle explicit: i marks geometric perpendicularity --- x₄ is
perpendicular to the spatial slice x₁ x₂ x₃. This is what makes the
metric Lorentzian rather than Euclidean. Sign-symmetric: (−i)² = i² =

contracts at −ic. The Sphere goes outward in time, not inward.
Sign-asymmetric: this is the unique content that is T-anti-invariant.
Algebraic Channel does not read this content; dx₄/dt = ic Geometric
Channel does.''

From {[}85{]}, Theorem 16.2 (Algebraic Channel's Sign-Blind Independence
and Empirical Insufficiency), statement: ``Algebraic Channel's
sign-blind algebraic apparatus --- the Hilbert space 𝓗 with Hermitian
operator algebra, the canonical commutator {[}\(\hat{q}\),
\(\hat{p}\){]} = iħ, Stone's theorem with unitary one-parameter groups,

variational Lagrangian-Hamiltonian formalism, Noether's first and second

constructively independent of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel: the
apparatus can be built from algebraic foundations (Hilbert space,

primitive as input. This constructive independence is established by the
historical record of 1925--1957: Heisenberg-Born-Jordan (1925), Dirac
(1925), Stone (1932), von Neumann (1932), Bargmann (1957), and the first
five Wightman axioms (1956) constructed this apparatus from algebraic
foundations alone. However, Algebraic Channel's sign-blind construction
is empirically insufficient: the sign-blind apparatus does not pick out
positive-energy spectrum vs.~negative-energy spectrum, does not
distinguish future light cone Σ₊(p) from past light cone Σ₋(p) as

\textgreater{} 0, does not give the radiative arrow (retarded over
advanced Green's function), does not give the cosmological expansion
direction H₀ \textgreater{} 0, and does not produce matter dominance.
Empirical adequacy of the algebraic apparatus requires importing the
Spectrum Condition (Wightman 1956 sixth axiom: Spec(P\^{}μ) ⊂
\(\bar{V}_{+}\), the closed forward light cone in momentum space), which
explicitly breaks the +ic ↔ −ic symmetry by selecting positive-energy
states. The Spectrum Condition is not a theorem of the other Algebraic
Channel axioms; it must be imposed externally. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic
framework identifies the Spectrum Condition as the algebraic residue of
the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel's +ic orientation surviving the
projection Π\_A: the orientation cannot live in the sign-blind algebra,
but it must be imported for the algebra to be empirically adequate.''

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 16.6 (No-go theorem for entropy-decreasing

with the McGucken-Sphere Brownian coupling D\_x = ε²c²Ω/(2γ\_L²)
{[}MG-Thermodynamics §III, McGucken-Brownian coupling identity{]}, no
entropy-decreasing macroscopic trajectory in the universe's Sphere chain
exists.''

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 6.6.7.6 (Cascade-level equivalence: McGucken

generated by dx₄/dt = ic at each event E ∈ 𝕄\_\{1,3\} simultaneously

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 6.6.7.7 (No-signaling as null propagation of

From {[}29{]}, Theorem 6.6.9.2 (Spacetime Thermodynamics Requires Null

From {[}49{]}, the abstract: ``The expansion of x₄ is the single
geometric process that transforms locality into nonlocality: it
distributes every local point into a nonlocal expanding wavefront
(Huygens' Principle), generates the nonlocal correlations observed in
entanglement experiments, and limits the growth of nonlocality to the
velocity of light. Two particles can become entangled only if they have
shared a common local origin, or if they have each interacted locally
with members of a system that itself originated locally. The geometric
object at the center of this framework is the McGucken Sphere --- a
sphere whose radius expands at c, representing the expansion of x₄. In
the simplest case, entangled particles sharing a common origin exist
within a single McGucken Sphere: they share a common x₄ wavefront
because they originated at the same local event. Entanglement can also
be transferred via mediating particles (as in entanglement swapping),
and the interaction of those mediating particles represents intersecting
McGucken Spheres --- each carrying its own wavefront from its own local
origin, with entanglement transferred where the spheres intersect.'' And
its Theorem 4.2 (Nonlocality of the light cone's surface): ``The surface
of the forward light cone emanating from any spacetime event is a
geometric nonlocality: its spatially separated points share a common
quantum identity.''

From {[}24{]}, the Huygens-equals-Holography theorem (Theorem 21 of
{[}24{]}, as §6.2.8 of the present paper names it): ``Under the McGucken
Principle dx₄/dt = ic, Huygens' Principle and the holographic principle
of `t Hooft and Susskind are two formulations of the same geometric

of Huygens' Principle.''

From {[}46{]}, Theorem 7.1 (McGucken-Invariance Lemma): ``The physical
fact of the fourth-dimension expansion at c holds globally on ℳ,
regardless of the gravitational field. Formally: 1. ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g\_μν = 0
for all metric components. 2. In any chart (t, x₁, x₂, x₃) adapted to
the foliation 𝓕 such that the coordinate x₄ along worldlines descends
from the integrated form of Axiom 2.1 (x₄ = ict), the timelike block of
the metric is gauge-fixed: g\_tt = −c², g\_tj = 0. 3. Only the

six.'' From {[}46{]}, Corollary 7.4 (Gravitational time dilation,
redshift, and the no-graviton conclusion), clause (iii): ``There is no
graviton: gravity is the geometry of h\_ij, not a force mediated by
