a quantum mediator of dynamical degrees of freedom in the timelike
block, or in a separate tensor field beyond g\_μν. By Theorem 7.1(3),
the only dynamical degrees of freedom in g\_μν are the six components of
h\_ij, which are properties of the spatial slices, not propagating
quanta. Geometry is not mediated by particles.''

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-chandrasekarans-construction-as-theorems-of-the-expansion-of-xux2084}{%
\paragraph{5.13.3 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of
Chandrasekaran's construction as theorems of the expansion of
x₄}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-chandrasekarans-construction-as-theorems-of-the-expansion-of-xux2084}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic supplies, for each
object defined in §5.13.1, the theorem of §5.13.2 or of the present
paper from which that object descends; the ten theorems below establish
the descent object by object, with the proof of each consisting of
{[}83{]}'s own equation set beside the corpus theorem.

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.1 (The null cones of the causal diamond in {[}83{]}
are McGucken Spheres).} Let p and q be the past and future tips of a
causal diamond of {[}83{]}, ℋ\_p its incoming null cone, ℋ\_q its
outgoing null cone, and S their corner. Then ℋ\_p is the McGucken Sphere
Σ₊(p) swept by x₄'s spherical expansion at c from p, with radius r = ct
and area A = 4πc²t² at coordinate time t after p; ℋ\_q is the locus of
the events whose forward McGucken Spheres arrive at q; and S is Σ₊(p) at
the coordinate time at which the McGucken Spheres of its events reach q.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. By Lemma 2.5 of {[}29{]} (§2), the Lorentzian
manifold on which {[}83{]} is set, ``four dimensional Lorentzian
spacetimes'' (abstract), is the constraint surface of x₄ = ict with
signature (−,+,+,+); the null cones of that manifold are the loci ds² =
0 of that metric. Step 2. By §2, the locus ds² = 0 to the future of p is
dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² = c²dt², the set of events reached by x₄'s expansion
at c from p: the McGucken Sphere Σ₊(p), whose radius after coordinate
time t is r = ct and whose area is A = 4πr² = 4πc²t². Step 3. The
generators of ℋ\_p are ``future directed'' ({[}83{]}, Figure 7 caption);
the generators of Σ₊(p) are future-directed because the McGucken Sphere
is generated at p and expands at +ic (Theorem 4.6.4 of {[}29{]}). Hence
ℋ\_p = Σ₊(p). Step 4. An event r lies on the past null cone of q when
the interval from r to q is null and r precedes q, which is the
condition q ∈ Σ₊(r); the past null cone of q is therefore the set of
events r whose McGucken Spheres Σ₊(r) arrive at q, and it is generated
by no single event. ℋ\_q is that locus. Step 5. S = ℋ\_p ∩ ℋ\_q is the
set of events of Σ₊(p) whose own McGucken Spheres reach q, which is
Σ₊(p) at one coordinate time. ∎

\emph{McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic reading.} {[}83{]} selects the null
boundary because it is ``particularly natural'' (§1) and because ``you
kind of get space and time together for free'' ({[}84{]}, 7:33). Under
the Principle the null cone is the surface on which the spatial
displacement from p equals the modulus of the fourth-dimensional
advance, \textbar Δx\textbar{} = cΔt = \textbar Δx₄\textbar, which is x₄
= ict restricted to the McGucken Sphere; a spatial datum and a temporal
datum on it are one datum because the radius r = ct of the McGucken
Sphere gives both. The Principle is the physical mechanism for Huygens'
principle --- every event the source of a spherical wavefront expanding
at c --- which the orthodox light cone describes as a locus and does not
generate (§2; {[}44{]}; {[}49{]}, Theorem 4.2).

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.2 (The freely specifiable data and the null
constraints of {[}83{]} are the transverse shape and the focusing of the
McGucken Sphere).} The ``two functions along its generators'' of
{[}83{]} §1 are the two components of the conformal metric of the cuts
of Σ₊(p), which are the transverse shape of the McGucken Sphere; the
determination of the interior from these data and the corner data is
Theorem 21 of {[}24{]} (§6.2.8); the Raychaudhuri equation of {[}83{]}
(3.25e), £\emph{ℓ Θ}(ℓ) + ½Θ\_(ℓ)² + σ\_ab σ\^{}ab = 0 in vacuum, is the
vacuum form of the Raychaudhuri equation that Theorem 14 applies, with
its matter term R\_μν k\^{}μ k\^{}ν, to the null generators of the
McGucken Sphere; the matter term is absent here because {[}83{]} is
vacuum.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. On Σ₊(p) the radial advance is fixed at c by the
Principle, so the only freedom on the McGucken Sphere is the shape of
its cuts; {[}83{]} §3.2 writes the induced metric of a cut as q\_AB = ϱ²
\(\bar{q}\)\_AB with \(\bar{q}\)\_AB of unit determinant
((3.17c)--(3.17d)) and states that ``we are free to specify the two
polarizations of gravitational radiation through the conformal metric of
its cuts'' --- the two components of \(\bar{q}\)\_AB are the transverse
shape. Step 2. Theorem 21 of {[}24{]}: the physics of the bulk region
enclosed by a McGucken Sphere at time t + dt is fully determined by
source data on the 2-dimensional surface of the McGucken Sphere at time
t; this is the determination of the interior from the cone data that
{[}83{]} §1 states as ``To specify a classical solution inside a null
cone, we can choose two functions along its generators together with
data at its cuts and solve the null constraints.'' Step 3. Equation
(3.25e) of {[}83{]} is the vacuum Raychaudhuri equation on the
generators of Σ₊(p); Theorem 14 of the present paper uses the same
equation with its matter term R\_μν k\^{}μ k\^{}ν on the generators of
the McGucken Sphere, and in vacuum R\_μν k\^{}μ k\^{}ν = 0 ({[}83{]}
(3.24)) so that the focusing is carried by σ\_ab σ\^{}ab alone. Step 4.
The delay Ξ\_y(v) ≥ 0 of {[}83{]} (3.26c) is the statement that a
sheared McGucken Sphere reaches a given areal radius at a later value of
the affine parameter, since by (3.26b) ∂\emph{u ϱ = p}\{ε,y\}
e\^{}\{−Ξ\_y(v)\} decreases with shear. ∎

\emph{McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic reading.} The constraints become
transport equations ({[}84{]}, 7:26--7:58) because on the McGucken
Sphere the radial advance is fixed at c by the Principle and carries no
free datum. What remains, the shape of the McGucken Sphere's cuts, is
what {[}83{]} quantizes in §4; under the Principle the shape is the
spatial geometry h\_ij through which the advance proceeds (Theorem 7.1
of {[}46{]}), and it is kept classical (Theorem 5.13.10).

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.3 (The gravitational clock of {[}83{]} is the
radius of the McGucken Sphere).} Let ū* be the averaged clock of
{[}83{]} (3.28) on a shear-free cone with corner area 𝒜 = 4πb² and cap
cut-off ε. Then ū* = (1 − ε)r with r the radius of the McGucken Sphere
Σ₊(p) at the corner, r = ct = x₄/i; the clock's strict increase from
zero is the statement dr/dt = c \textgreater{} 0, which is the sign +ic;
the commutation {[}\(\hat{\bar{u}}^{*}\), \(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\){]} = 0
is the statement that radius and area are two functions of one McGucken
Sphere; and the clock's period, absent from {[}83{]}, is the Compton
cycle of the Principle, with action h per cycle.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. By {[}83{]} §5.1, on the shear-free cone ``the
classical clock reads (1 − ε)b,'' and by (5.52b) on the Schwarzschild
horizon cone ū* = (1 − ε)√(𝒜/4π). With 𝒜 = 4πb², √(𝒜/4π) = b. Step 2. By
Theorem 5.13.1, the cone is Σ₊(p) and its corner area is A = 4πr²; hence
b = r, and ū* = (1 − ε)r. Step 3. By §2, r = ct, and x₄ = ict gives r =
x₄/i; so ū* = (1 − ε)x₄/i, and the clock reads the fourth coordinate of
the Principle up to the cap cut-off. The cut-off ε exists in {[}83{]}
because the apex is removed (``we cut off its past and future tips with
small spacelike hypersurfaces,'' §1); under the Principle the apex is
the event p itself, at which Σ₊(p) has r = 0, so ε → 0 is the
Principle's own normalization. Step 4. ``Its reading increases strictly
from zero'' ({[}83{]} §2.1). With ū* = (1 − ε)r and r = ct, dū\emph{/dt
= (1 − ε)c \textgreater{} 0; the strict increase is dr/dt = c, which is
the modulus of dx₄/dt = ic with its sign +. Step 5.
{[}\(\hat{\bar{u}}^{*}\), \(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\){]} = 0 ({[}83{]} §5.2):
with ū} = (1 − ε)r and 𝒜 = 4πr², both are functions of r on one McGucken
Sphere and commute. Step 6. {[}83{]} defines the clock by affine
distance and gives it no period. By §2 of the present paper and
Proposition 2.2.bis.1 of {[}85{]}, in one Compton tick Δt\_C = h/mc² the
fourth dimension advances by one Compton wavelength, Δx₄ = icΔt\_C =
iλ\_C, exactly one quantum of action accumulates, ΔS = h, and the
wavefront completes one oscillation, ω\_C Δt\_C = 2π; the radius r is
therefore a count of completed cycles times λ\_C, and a count of cycles
is a clock. ∎

\emph{McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic reading.} {[}84{]} (58:19) calls
the clock ``just given to you by gravity'' and {[}83{]} §4.2 states that
``in this limit a clock measures proper time along its worldline.''
Under the Principle the clock is given by the expansion of x₄: the
McGucken Sphere's radius advances at the rate dx₄/dt = ic in coordinate
time t, and the proper-time reading is a consequence of the
coordinate-time statement (Appendix E). The photon is at rest in x₄,
v\_x₄ = 0 (Appendix E), and the light ray is a clock because the
McGucken Sphere whose generator it is advances at c and oscillates with
the wavelength that sets h. Metrology defines the second by a frequency
(the caesium-133 hyperfine transition, fixed at 9 192 631 770 Hz in
1967), the metre by the distance light travels in 1/299 792 458 s
(1983), and the kilogram by the fixed value h = 6.626 070 15 × 10⁻³⁴ J s
(2019); these three definitions fix the unit of time by a frequency, the
unit of length by the rate c, and the unit of mass by the action h;
under the Principle the frequency, the rate c and the action h per cycle
are the three parameters of the McGucken Sphere's expansion, and
{[}83{]}'s clock, an affine length along a generator, reads the rate.
(The dates and values of the International System of Units definitions
are background knowledge.)

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.4 (The area quantum, the boost charge, and the
thermal weight of {[}83{]} are the Planck-cell count and the Euclidean
period of the McGucken Sphere).} In {[}83{]}, with c = 1, the area
changes in steps of 8πG\_Nħ ((4.12b)), the boost charge is 𝒦 = 𝒜/8πG\_N
((3.43)), and each state of area 𝒜 enters the trace with weight
e\^{}\{−𝒜/4G\_Nħ\} ((5.23b)). Under the Principle: 8πG\_Nħ = 8πℓ\_P² is
8π Planck cells of the McGucken Sphere; 𝒜/8πG\_N is the count of Theorem
12 in the units of Theorem 13; and e\^{}\{−𝒜/4G\_Nħ\} = e\^{}\{−S/k\_B\}
with S = k\_B A/4ℓ\_P² the entropy of Theorem 12, so the weight is the
Boltzmann weight of the McGucken Sphere's state count.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. ℓ\_P² = G\_Nħ/c³; with c = 1, G\_Nħ = ℓ\_P², so
8πG\_Nħ = 8πℓ\_P² and 𝒜/4G\_Nħ = A/4ℓ\_P². Step 2. Theorem 12 (and
Theorem 19.6.1, §4.2): one x₄-mode per cell of area ℓ\_P² on the
McGucken Sphere, N = A/ℓ\_P², S = k\_B N/4 = k\_B A/4ℓ\_P²; hence
𝒜/4G\_Nħ = S/k\_B and e\^{}\{−𝒜/4G\_Nħ\} = e\^{}\{−S/k\_B\}. Step 3.
{[}83{]} obtains the weight by ``Analytically continuing only this boost
through a half turn on each copy'' (§5.3), the 2π rotation of the corner
boost; Theorem 13 derives the Unruh temperature from the Euclidean
period of the x₄-advance on the accelerated worldline under the
McGucken--Wick rotation, and Theorem 9.5.11 of {[}29{]} identifies the
continuation t → −iτ with the change of parametrization to x₄/c.~The 2π
that appears in {[}83{]}'s boost weight is the period of the advance in
the Euclidean section (Appendix C). Step 4. The boost charge 𝒜/8πG\_N is
the generator of that rotation; its quantum of action is ħ because the
McGucken Sphere's wavefront carries action h per cycle (Theorem 5.13.3,
Step 6), which is why the area steps in (4.12b) carry the factor ħ. ∎

\emph{McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic reading.} The constant ħ enters
{[}83{]} through the commutator it imposes and reappears in the area
step; under the Principle ħ is the action per cycle of the McGucken
Sphere's wavefront, and at the horizon tier the wavelength is ℓ\_P
(Theorem 12, bracketed clause), so the area is counted in cells of ℓ\_P²
and stepped in multiples of them.

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.5 (The finite-dimensional Hilbert space and the
discrete area spectrum of {[}83{]} are the Planck-cell count of the
McGucken Sphere bounded by its radius).} Under the bound (5.21d) of
{[}83{]} and Theorem 5.13.3, the corner area satisfies A ≤ 4πr\_max²,
the area of the McGucken Sphere of radius r\_max = ℓ(𝒟)/(1 − ε); the
number of states on a McGucken Sphere of area A is at most Ω =
e\^{}\{N/4\} = e\^{}\{A/4ℓ\_P²\} (Theorem 12; §7, Lemma 7.2); hence dim
ℋ\_𝒟 ≤ exp(πr\_max²/ℓ\_P²), and the area takes values in the discrete
set of Planck-cell multiples.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. {[}83{]} (5.21d): P\_𝒟 \(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\) P\_𝒟
≤ {[}4πℓ(𝒟)²/(1 − ε)²{]} P\_𝒟. Step 2. By Theorem 5.13.3, ℓ(𝒟) bounds ū*
= (1 − ε)r, so ℓ(𝒟)/(1 − ε) = r\_max bounds r, and the bound of Step 1
reads A ≤ 4πr\_max², the area of Σ₊(p) at radius r\_max. Step 3. Theorem
12 and Lemma 7.2: the McGucken Sphere of area A carries N = A/ℓ\_P²
Planck cells and Ω = e\^{}\{N/4\} microstates; the number of orthogonal
states supported on it is at most Ω. Step 4. Combining Steps 2 and 3,
dim ℋ\_𝒟 ≤ exp(4πr\_max²/4ℓ\_P²) = exp(πr\_max²/ℓ\_P²) \textless{} ∞.
Step 5. The area of a McGucken Sphere is a count of Planck cells
(Theorem 12), so its spectrum is discrete; this is {[}83{]}'s ``The
corner area can therefore take at most d\_𝒟 distinct values'' (5.39c). ∎

\emph{McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic reading.} {[}83{]} reaches
finiteness by contradiction: ``If ℋ\_𝒟 were infinite dimensional''
(§5.2) a relative boost across S would deform a two-point function on
the uncut preparation and leave it unchanged on the cut one, against
diffeomorphism invariance, ``Hence ℋ\_𝒟 is finite dimensional.'' It
reaches the existence of states by an estimate it calls ``strong
evidence at finite G\_N and ħ'' (§5.1, following (5.16)). Under the
Principle the states exist because the McGucken Sphere is generated at
its event, and they are finite in number because the McGucken Sphere has
an area and one state per Planck cell; the two steps of {[}83{]} are
replaced by the count. {[}84{]} (1:28--1:53) takes the area law as ``a
guiding principle for how should we build states of spacetime''; Theorem
12 derives it. The entropy (5.50), S(ρ\_𝒟) =
⟨\(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\)⟩/4G\_Nħ + log Z\_\{𝒟,1\}, is the horizon reading
of the one count of Theorem 7.3: §10.12duodecies of {[}29{]}, reproduced
in §7, names ``entanglement entropy across a causal diamond'' as the
gravitational-side entropy of the orthodox treatment, and Theorem 7.3
identifies it with the event reading, the Born measure, as one
SO(3)-invariant count of the one McGucken Sphere.

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.6 (The commutator, the Hilbert space, and the
Lorentzian manifold of {[}83{]} are the cogenerated structures of
{[}29{]}).} The three inputs of {[}83{]} --- a four-dimensional
Lorentzian manifold, canonical commutators obtained by ``promoting their
reduced Poisson bracket to a commutator'' (§4), and a Hilbert space
obtained from ``Gaussian wavefunctions of canonical pairs'' and a chosen
pure state ω through the Gelfand--Naimark--Segal construction (§4.2) ---
are, respectively, Lemma 2.5, Theorem 5.1, and Theorem 6.1 of {[}29{]},
and by Theorem 10.6 of {[}29{]} the first and third are one object; the
reconstruction problem of {[}83{]} Appendix E, ``We would like to
recover that Hilbert space and its operator algebra from the amplitudes
themselves,'' is therefore the problem of reassembling two presentations
of one constraint surface, which Theorem 10.6 of {[}29{]} presents as
one object.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1 (manifold). {[}83{]} assumes ``four dimensional
Lorentzian spacetimes''; Lemma 2.5 of {[}29{]} derives the Lorentzian
signature from x₄ = ict by the proof reproduced in §5.13.2. Step 2
(commutator). {[}83{]} §4.2: ``To realize the canonical commutation
relations {[}\(\hat{q}\)\_j, \(\hat{p}\)\_j{]} = iℏ \(\hat{1}\) on
wavefunctions χ\_j(q\_j), we represent \(\hat{q}\)\_j by multiplication
and exp(−ia\(\hat{p}\)\_j/ℏ) by the shift''; Theorem 5.1 of {[}29{]}
derives {[}\(\hat{q}\), \(\hat{p}\){]} = iℏ with ``the factor i descends
from the perpendicularity of x₄ to x₁x₂x₃ in dx₄/dt = ic; the factor ℏ
descends from the action quantization of x₄-advance per Planck-frequency
oscillation.'' Step 3 (Hilbert space). {[}83{]} constructs ℋ\_ω from a
Gaussian state and a pure extension ω and notes that its choice is an
input; Theorem 6.1 of {[}29{]} derives 𝓗 as ``the unique irreducible
separable Hilbert-space representation of the Weyl form of the
McGucken-derived canonical commutator algebra,'' unique by Stone--von
Neumann, and Theorem 6.1.5 gives the same 𝓗 as the completion of Huygens
superpositions of McGucken-Sphere wavefronts under the overlap inner
product. Step 4 (identity of the two). Theorem 10.6 of {[}29{]}: the
manifold of Step 1 and the Hilbert space of Step 3 ``are the same
geometric object --- the constraint surface where the McGucken Principle
dx₄/dt = ic holds locally --- represented at two cascade levels.'' Step
5 (axioms). {[}83{]} Appendix E imposes five conditions so that
amplitudes on closed spacetimes determine a Hilbert space on a cut;
Theorem 16.15.1 of {[}29{]} states that the Hilbert-space axiom W1 ``is
a forced theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the cogeneration cascade,'' and the
manifold is Lemma 2.5, so the structure Appendix E reconstructs is
already present as one object. Step 6 (order of derivation). Part X.1 of
{[}85{]}, reproduced in §5.13.2: the Hilbert space, the complex field,
and the unitary group are derived before the Born rule, from Principle
2.1 alone; {[}83{]}'s Axiom 4 (unitary evolution) and its Born rule
(4.19b) are, in that order of derivation, Theorem 9.2 of {[}29{]} and
Theorem 7.2 of the present paper. ∎

\emph{McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic reading.} {[}84{]} (55:42): ``we
will basically take these abstract null cone algebras and build space
and build time roughly speaking.'' Under the Principle space and time
are built by the expansion of x₄ at c from the event, which produces the
null cone, and the Hilbert space on the cone is the same construction
read at the function-space level; the Gaussian reference state and the
pure extension ω that {[}83{]} must choose are replaced by the
uniqueness of Theorem 6.1 of {[}29{]}.

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.7 (The entanglement of {[}83{]} across the corner
and across the bifurcation surface is the nonlocality of the McGucken
Sphere).} The entangling product of {[}83{]} §1, which ``restricts their
tensor product to states annihilated by the sum of charges on the two
boundaries''; the gluing at S of §3.6, in which ``the same area element
enters the two boost charges with opposite signs'' and ``a simultaneous
shift of Γ\_R and Γ\_L then has zero charge''; and the two-sided state
of §5.4, in which ``a generator of the left past horizon continues
through the bifurcation surface onto the right future horizon'' and
``the same entanglement correlates the areas of the two cuts,'' are each
the statement that two regions meeting on a cut share the one McGucken
Sphere whose generators pass through the cut, whose volume defines the
nonlocality (§5.9; §5.6.7) and whose surface is a geometric nonlocality
({[}49{]}, Theorem 4.2).

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. By Theorem 5.13.1 the corner S is Σ₊(p) at one
coordinate time; the regions on its two sides are the interior and
exterior of one McGucken Sphere. Step 2. By Theorem 6.6.7.6(ii) of
{[}29{]}, the McGucken Sphere wavefront ψ\_p of Σ₊(p) is one vector of
the Hilbert space cogenerated at p; the states on the two sides of S are
two restrictions of that one vector, which is the condition of the
entangling product, under which ``What then remains is the relative
boost γ conjugate to 𝒦(y)'' ({[}83{]} §3.6). Step 3. {[}49{]}, Theorem
4.2: the surface of the forward light cone from any event is a geometric
nonlocality whose spatially separated points share a common quantum
identity; S is such a surface. Step 4. In §5.4 of {[}83{]} the horizon
generator continues through the bifurcation surface from the left past
horizon to the right future horizon; by Theorem 5.13.1 that generator is
a generator of one McGucken Sphere, and by {[}49{]} (abstract)
``entangled particles sharing a common origin exist within a single
McGucken Sphere: they share a common x₄ wavefront because they
originated at the same local event.'' The correlation of the two cuts'
areas is the correlation of two cuts of one McGucken Sphere. Step 5.
Theorem 6.6.7.6 of {[}29{]} gives the geometric, Hilbert-space, Born,
and correlational levels as four presentations of the one McGucken
Sphere, which is {[}83{]}'s equation (5.73): the connected geometry and
the entangled product state differ by a null state and ``represent the
same physical state.'' Step 6. Theorem 6.6.7.7 of {[}29{]}: the
correlations permit no superluminal signalling because they ride the
McGucken Sphere's wavefront from the common event; {[}83{]}'s unitary
gluing has the same property. ∎

\emph{McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic reading.} {[}84{]} (56:17): ``this
theory is non-local in the sense that everything lives on the cone and
there are no pointlike objects.'' Under the Principle the event is the
apex and is primitive by dx₄/dt = ic, and what lives on the cone is the
McGucken Sphere the event generates; the nonlocality {[}83{]} finds in
the algebra is the volume nonlocality stated in the Principle's own
sentence.

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.8 (The Einstein equations and the semiclassical
limit of {[}83{]} are Theorems 9 and 14).} Equation (6.4) of {[}83{]},
R\_ab − ½Rg\_ab + Λg\_ab = 0, obtained from ``invariance of the
amplitude under field shifts in the interior,'' is the vacuum case of
the field equations derived in Theorem 9 (the Algebraic Channel: the
factorisation of Diff(M\_G), Noether's second theorem, Lovelock's
uniqueness theorem, Newtonian matching) and in Theorem 14 (the Geometric
Channel: Clausius relation on the McGucken Sphere's null generators);
the agreement of the two is Corollary 14.1; and the retarded solution
(6.16) selects the forward orientation, which the Principle derives as
the sign of +ic.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. Theorem 9 and Corollary 9.2 derive G\_μν + Λg\_μν
= (8πG/c⁴)T\_μν from the Diff(M\_G) factorisation of dx₄/dt = ic,
Noether's second theorem, and Lovelock's theorem, with G fixed once by
Newtonian matching; with T\_μν = 0 it is (6.4). Step 2. Theorem 14
derives the same equation from the Clausius relation on the generators
of Σ₊(p) with the Raychaudhuri equation; {[}83{]} obtains (6.4) from
interior field shifts of an amplitude whose boundary data on both cones
were reduced by the same Raychaudhuri equation, (3.25e). Step 3. Theorem
6.6.9.2 of {[}29{]}: the Clausius route requires a null surface;
{[}83{]}'s null boundary is that surface. Step 4. The retarded Green's
function in (6.16), with ``only graviton and edge mode fluctuations in
the causal past of the event'' contributing, selects the forward
orientation; under the Principle the selection is the sign of +ic
(Theorem 5.13.9). ∎

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.9 (The orientation {[}83{]} imposes by convention
is derived by the Principle, and Axiom 4 of {[}83{]} is the
Algebraic-Channel reading of the squared rate).} {[}83{]} fixes the
direction of time at three places and nowhere derives it: ``future
directed null generators'' (Figure 7 caption), ``Choose future directed
affine parameters'' (§5.4), and ``the retarded solution \ldots{} 𝒢\_R is
the retarded Green's function'' ((6.16)); its Axiom 4, ``Real time
evolution U from Σ to Σ′ has inverse U† and preserves the inner
product,'' is time-reversal invariant, and its traces are formed by
``Gluing a Lorentzian preparation to its time reflection'' (Appendix
E.1). Under the Principle the orientation is the sign of dx₄/dt = +ic
(Theorem 4.6.4 of {[}29{]}; the decomposition +ic = (+)·i·c of §16.3 of
{[}85{]}); the Second Law is strict on the unbounded slice, dS/dt =
3k\_B/2t \textgreater{} 0 (Theorem 11; Theorem 19.5.1), with the sign of
the inequality following from the retarded propagator that +ic selects;
the refined generalized second law holds as x₄-flux conservation
(§6.2.6, Theorem 17 of {[}24{]}); no entropy-decreasing macroscopic
trajectory exists (Theorem 16.6 of {[}29{]}); and Axiom 4 holds in the
Algebraic Channel, which reads (ic)² = −c² and x₄ = ict and from which
the sign is removed (Theorem 15; Theorem 16.2 of {[}85{]}).

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. The three sentences quoted from {[}83{]} each
select a direction and none derives it; the words ``arrow,'' ``second
law,'' ``irreversible,'' and ``thermodynamic'' do not occur in {[}83{]},
and the clock's monotonicity ``increases strictly from zero'' is
asserted for the affine parameter on the chosen generators. Step 2.
Theorem 15 and §16.3 of {[}85{]}: the Algebraic Channel reads i
(perpendicularity) and c (rate) through the squared and integrated forms
(ic)² = −c² and x₄ = ict, in which the sign + is absent; by Theorem 16.2
of {[}85{]} the apparatus of Hilbert space, commutator, Stone's theorem
with unitary one-parameter groups, and Lorentzian metric is sign-blind
and ``does not give the radiative arrow (retarded over advanced Green's
function)''; a unitary evolution with inverse U† is a statement in that
channel, and Axiom 4 is therefore consistent with the Principle and
silent on the orientation. Step 3. Theorem 4.6.4 of {[}29{]}: the sign
+ic is fixed at the level of the Principle, and the −ic branch produces
a contracting McGucken Sphere that does not appear. Step 4. Theorem 11
derives dS/dt \textgreater{} 0 from the forward Fokker--Planck
propagator selected by +ic (§4.1.1, proof, the step ``The sign of the
inequality follows from the +ic orientation of the principle''); Theorem
17 of {[}24{]} (§6.2.6) gives the refined generalized second law;
Theorem 16.6 of {[}29{]} excludes entropy-decreasing macroscopic
trajectories because they would require a contracting McGucken Sphere.
Step 5. The retarded choice in {[}83{]} (6.16) is, by Theorem 16.2 of
{[}85{]}, the import into the sign-blind apparatus of the orientation
the apparatus cannot carry; under the Principle it is the sign of +ic
applied to the linearized equations. Step 6. By Theorem 5.13.3 the
clock's strict increase is dr/dt = c with the sign of +ic; the
monotonicity {[}83{]} asserts for its affine parameter is derived. ∎

\emph{McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic reading.} {[}83{]}'s construction
lives in the Algebraic Channel: its equations are reversible, its traces
are time-reflection gluings, and its orientation is a convention. The
Geometric Channel carries the direction in which the McGucken Sphere
expands, and the two channels are two readings of one rate (§5.5;
Theorem 15). The direction of time is derived by the Principle (Theorem
4.6.4 of {[}29{]}) and is absent from the axioms of {[}83{]}.

\textbf{Theorem 5.13.10 (The graviton premise of {[}83{]} is replaced by
the Principle, and the results that rest on it have no corpus
counterpart).} {[}83{]} quantizes ``the two polarizations of
gravitational radiation through the conformal metric of its cuts''
(§3.2) into the Fock space (4.10c); the Principle keeps the spatial
metric h\_ij as geometry, ``the only dynamical degrees of freedom in
g\_μν are the six components of h\_ij, which are properties of the
spatial slices, not propagating quanta'' (Corollary 7.4(iii) of
{[}46{]}), and places the quantum of action in the Compton tick of
matter (§2; §4.1.0). The results of {[}83{]} that rest on the graviton
premise --- the pair amplitude Li₂(e\^{}\{−2i/s\})/2s² ((4.33)), the
type I factor with a pure extension ω (§4.2), the logarithmic correction
q = 257/302 with coefficient 106/45 ((5.68)--(5.69)), the spectral bound
at a reflecting anti-de Sitter boundary ((5.46)), and the two-sided
correlators ((5.76)--(5.77)) --- are computations on that premise and
have no counterpart in the corpus read for this paper; whether the
Compton-tick count on the horizon McGucken Sphere yields a logarithmic
correction to Theorem 12, and with what coefficient, is open.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. Corollary 7.4(iii) of {[}46{]} excludes a quantum
mediator for h\_ij. Step 2. §2 and §4.1.0 place ħ as the action per
Compton cycle of the matter advance; Theorem 5.1 of {[}29{]} derives the
commutator for that advance; the Hilbert space of Theorem 6.1 of
{[}29{]} is the Hilbert space of that matter, and a Fock space of
graviton modes has no object to be built from. Step 3. Each listed
result of {[}83{]} is computed from the graviton Fock space or from the
pure extension ω of its state; the present paper's search of {[}23{]},
{[}24{]}, {[}29{]}, {[}46{]}, {[}49{]}, {[}85{]}, and its own theorems
finds no logarithmic correction to the area law and no graviton
amplitude, and the arithmetic of {[}83{]} (5.69), q/2(1 − q) − 1/2 =
257/90 − 45/90 = 212/90 = 106/45, is verified as his. ∎

\emph{McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic reading.} {[}84{]} (19:17): ``when
I say gravitons I don't mean the usual sense of a particle propagating
on some background I just mean the two radiative like polarizations of
the gravity.'' That sentence is the closest approach in
{[}83{]}--{[}84{]} to Corollary 7.4(iii) of {[}46{]}; {[}83{]} retains
the name and quantizes the polarizations, and the Principle keeps them
as the shape of the McGucken Sphere's cuts.

\emph{Empirical status of the items with no corpus counterpart.} Each of
the five items rests on a graviton premise or on a geometry outside
observation, and {[}83{]} itself cites no measurement: the word
``experiment'' does not occur in {[}83{]}. (a) The amplitude (4.33) is
for ``graviton pair creation and annihilation on a null cone''
(abstract); no graviton quantum has been detected --- gravitational-wave
observations measure the classical strain (background knowledge). (b)
The logarithmic correction (5.68)--(5.69) is for ``large Schwarzschild
black holes,'' compared with ``the coefficient Sen obtained through
Euclidean methods'' (abstract): a computation checked against another
computation, with no observed black-hole entropy to compare. (c) The
spectral bound (5.46) holds ``at a reflecting AdS boundary'' ({[}83{]}
§5); the observed cosmological constant is positive (background
knowledge; {[}50{]}), so the anti-de Sitter boundary is a geometry the
universe does not have. (d) The correlators (5.76)--(5.77) are evaluated
in ``The Hartle Hawking state of a two sided Schwarzschild black hole''
({[}83{]} §5.4), a maximally extended geometry with a second asymptotic
region; no such object is observed. (e) The clock and gluing of {[}83{]}
§2 are first set up in ``pure Jackiw Teitelboim (JT) gravity with two
asymptotic boundaries'' ({[}83{]} §1), a two-dimensional model. The
Principle's quantum of action is measured: ħ and c are measured, the
Compton tick Δt\_C = h/mc² and the Compton wavelength λ\_C = h/mc of §2
are measured for every massive particle, and the McGucken Sphere's
wavelength at the horizon tier, ℓ\_P, is built from measured constants;
the discreteness of {[}83{]}'s area spectrum enters the Principle
through the measured h. Einstein, in the Herbert Spencer Lecture at
Oxford of 10 June 1933, stated the criterion that the Principle meets
and these five items do not: ``Pure logical thinking cannot yield us any
knowledge of the empirical world; all knowledge of reality starts from
experience and ends in it. Propositions arrived at by purely logical
means are completely empty as regards reality. Because Galileo saw this,
and particularly because he drummed it into the scientific world, he is
the father of modern physics---indeed, of modern science altogether''
{[}86{]}.

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-why-the-principle-is-prior-the-inputs-of-83-as-outputs-of-one-statement}{%
\paragraph{5.13.4 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of why the
Principle is prior: the inputs of {[}83{]} as outputs of one
statement}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-why-the-principle-is-prior-the-inputs-of-83-as-outputs-of-one-statement}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic is a single statement
from which every input of {[}83{]} descends; the table lists the inputs

at the far left and the theorem that derives it at the right.

Chandrasekaran's null-cone quantization: the theorem that derives each

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-the-three-theorem-chains-that-meet-in-83s-subject}{%
\paragraph{5.13.5 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of the
three theorem chains that meet in {[}83{]}'s
subject}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-the-three-theorem-chains-that-meet-in-83s-subject}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic derives quantum
mechanics, general relativity, and thermodynamics as three chains of
theorems from the one statement, and {[}83{]}'s subject --- a Hilbert
space on a null cone with an area-law entropy and the Einstein equations
as its limit --- is the point where the three chains meet; this
subsection names the chains by their theorems so that the meeting point
is located.

Quantum mechanics ({[}29{]}, {[}38{]}, {[}85{]}): Theorem 3.1 of
{[}29{]} (complex amplitudes from ic) → Theorem 5.1 of {[}29{]}
(canonical commutator) → Theorem 6.1 of {[}29{]} (Hilbert space) →
Theorem 7.2 of the present paper (Born rule, §3.4), with Theorem 7.7
(the Born rule as the head-on x₄-collision of two McGucken Spheres,
§3.8) and Theorem 7.11 (PT-symmetry, §3.9) → §3.14 (uncertainty
principle) → Theorem 9.2 of {[}29{]} (unitarity) → Theorems
16.15.1--16.15.6 of {[}29{]} (the six Wightman axioms); entanglement and
nonlocality by {[}49{]} and Theorems 6.6.7.1--6.6.7.9 of {[}29{]}.

General relativity ({[}23{]}, {[}46{]}): Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 2.4.5 of
{[}29{]} (Minkowski space and the two postulates) → Theorem 7.1 of
{[}46{]} (g\_tt = −c², h\_ij dynamical) → §4.1.0 (the four-velocity
budget) → Theorem 13.1 of {[}46{]} (geodesic principle) → Theorem 9 and
Theorem 14 of the present paper (field equations by two channels, §5.3,
§5.4) → Corollary 7.4 of {[}46{]} (time dilation in h\_ij; no graviton)
→ {[}50{]} (cosmology).

Thermodynamics ({[}24{]}): §4.1.0 (Compton coupling) → §4.1.0bis (the
random direction forced by the nonlocality of the expanding x₄) →
Theorem 11 and Theorem 19.5.1 (strict Second Law) → Theorem 12 and
Theorem 19.6.1 (area law) → Theorem 17 of {[}24{]} (refined generalized
second law, §6.2.6) → Theorem 13 (Unruh temperature) → Theorem 6.1
(McGucken Entropy Identity); with Theorem 25 of {[}24{]} (measurement as
the physical Wick rotation, §6.2.10) and §7.4 (one squaring operation
under both readings).

The meeting point: Theorem 10.6 of {[}29{]} (Hilbert space and Minkowski
space one object), Theorem 6.6.7.6 of {[}29{]} (McGucken Sphere →
Hilbert → Born → Nonlocality), Theorem 6.6.9.2 of {[}29{]} (spacetime
thermodynamics requires null surfaces), and Theorem 7.3 of the present
paper (gravity is the Born rule: one count read over the horizon and at
the event). {[}83{]} constructs, by assembly on the null cone, the
structure that sits at this meeting point; the three chains derive it.

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-what-the-one-principle-yields-the-theorem-chains-that-the-null-cone-quantization-assembles-by-hand-and-einsteins-criterion-of-the-fewest-principles-for-the-most-observations}{%
\paragraph{5.13.6 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of what the
one Principle yields: the theorem chains that the null-cone quantization
assembles by hand, and Einstein's criterion of the fewest principles for
the most
observations}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-what-the-one-principle-yields-the-theorem-chains-that-the-null-cone-quantization-assembles-by-hand-and-einsteins-criterion-of-the-fewest-principles-for-the-most-observations}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic is one statement, and
the theorem chains below descend from it; this concluding subsection
lists them with the corpus paper in which each chain is proved, so that
the reader can set the single premise of this section against the inputs
of {[}83{]} counted in Table 5.13a and against the criterion Einstein
stated for a physical theory.

Einstein stated the criterion twice. In the Herbert Spencer Lecture of
10 June 1933 ({[}86{]}, verified-read): ``These fundamental concepts and
postulates, which cannot be further reduced logically, form the
essential part of a theory, which reason cannot touch. It is the grand
object of all theory to make these irreducible elements as simple and as
few in number as possible, without having to renounce the adequate
representation of any empirical content whatever.'' And, as reported by
Lincoln Barnett in 1950 ({[}105{]}, web-digest): ``The grand aim of all
science is to cover the greatest number of empirical facts by logical
deduction from the smallest number of hypotheses or axioms.'' The
McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is one irreducible element --- the fourth
dimension expanding at c from every event as the McGucken Sphere whose
wavelength sets h --- and the following are its theorem chains.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  General relativity. The Einstein field equations G\_μν + Λg\_μν =
  (8πG/c⁴)T\_μν are derived along the Algebraic Channel (the
  factorisation of Diff(M\_G), Noether's second theorem, Lovelock's
  uniqueness theorem, Newtonian matching) and the Geometric Channel (the
  Second Law, the area law, the Unruh temperature, the Clausius relation
  on the McGucken Sphere's null generators), the two channels agreeing
  (Theorems 9, 14, Corollary 14.1; §5); the chain the general-relativity
  paper labels GR T1--T24 --- the master equation, the equivalence
  principles, the geodesic equation, the curvature tensors, the field
  equations, the Schwarzschild solution, gravitational time dilation,
  gravitational waves, the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy, the Hawking
  temperature --- is {[}23{]}, with inertial mass, Newton's laws, the
  equivalence principle and the geodesic principle derived in {[}46{]}.
\item
  Quantum mechanics. The complex amplitude, the canonical commutator
  {[}\(\hat{q}\), \(\hat{p}\){]} = iℏ, the Hilbert space, the Born rule
  P = \textbar ψ\textbar², the uncertainty principle, the Schrödinger
  equation, the Dirac equation, the path integral and nonlocality are
  derived in {[}38{]}, each along both channels (``twenty-three quantum
  results each derived twice by derivationally disjoint routes
  (forty-six independent derivations from the one principle),'' this
  paper, Abstract); the commutator in {[}34{]}, the Hilbert space in
  {[}95{]}, the Born rule by five routes in {[}19{]}, {[}20{]}, {[}85{]}
  (§3), the uncertainty principle in {[}96{]} (§3.14), the de Broglie
  relation in {[}91{]}, the Dirac equation in {[}90{]}, the path
  integral in {[}88{]}, Feynman diagrams in {[}98{]}, quantum
  electrodynamics in {[}103{]}, and quantum field theory with the six
  Wightman axioms in {[}89{]} and {[}29{]}.
\item
  Thermodynamics. The strict Second Law dS/dt \textgreater{} 0, the area
  law S = k\_B A/4ℓ\_P², the generalized second law, the Unruh and
  Hawking temperatures, the Onsager relations, heat flow from hot to
  cold, and measurement as the physical Wick rotation are derived in
  {[}24{]} and reproduced in §4, §6.2.5, §6.2.6, §6.2.9, §6.2.10 and
  Appendix C of the present paper; the common foundation of the
  conservation laws and the Second Law is {[}97{]}.
\item
  Time and its arrows and asymmetries. The orientation +ic, the
  thermodynamic, radiative, cosmological, quantum-measurement and
  psychological arrows as projections of +ic, Loschmidt's objection
  resolved, and the symmetries and asymmetries of time are derived in
  {[}30{]} and in {[}24{]} (§6.2.2, Theorem 11 of {[}24{]}).
\item
  The two channels. The Algebraic Channel (the squared form (ic)² = −c²,
  sign-blind, T-invariant) and the Geometric Channel (the expanding
  McGucken Sphere, carrying +ic), their disjointness, the McGucken--Wick
  rotation t → −iτ with τ = x₄/c as the coordinate identification
  between them, are {[}28{]}, {[}99{]}, {[}100{]}, and §5.5.
\item
  Minkowski space and Hilbert space. The Lorentzian signature (−,+,+,+)
  from (ic)² = −c² (Lemma 2.5 of {[}29{]}), both postulates of special
  relativity (Theorem 2.4.5 of {[}29{]}), the Hilbert space as the
  unique representation of the derived commutator and as the completion
  of McGucken-Sphere wavefronts (Theorems 6.1, 6.1.5 of {[}29{]}), the
  two as one constraint surface (Theorem 10.6 of {[}29{]}), the six
  Wightman axioms (Theorems 16.15.1--16.15.6 of {[}29{]}), and Hilbert's
  sixth problem {[}94{]}.
\item
  The symmetries and conservation laws. Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether,
  Wigner, gauge, CPT and diffeomorphism symmetry as theorems of the one
  McGucken Symmetry, completing Klein's Erlangen programme, in {[}41{]};
  the conservation laws as theorems of the same symmetry in {[}102{]}
  and {[}97{]}.
\item
  Nonlocality and entanglement. All quantum nonlocality beginning in
  locality, entangled particles within one McGucken Sphere, entanglement
  swapping as intersecting McGucken Spheres, in {[}49{]}; Lorentz
  invariance and nonlocality as one geometric fact in {[}21{]}.
\item
  The constants and the matter sector. c as the rate and h as the action
  per cycle of the McGucken Sphere; the Compton coupling of matter to
  the expansion of x₄ ({[}104{]}; §4.1.0); the unique McGucken
  Lagrangian with its kinetic, Dirac, Yang--Mills and Einstein--Hilbert
  sectors {[}43{]}; the Standard Model gauge group and Higgs sector
  {[}35{]}.
\item
  Cosmology and observation. The McGucken cosmology with zero free
  dark-sector parameters, first in twelve tests {[}50{]}; the five
  quantum-mechanical, relativistic and thermodynamic experiments
  {[}36{]}; the Bayesian comparison {[}101{]}; and the McGucken Sphere
  identified in every sphere of Huygens, Young, Newton, Coulomb, Gauss,
  Einstein, Minkowski, Bloch, Penrose and Bekenstein, with the
  inverse-square law and Gauss's law as its theorems {[}93{]};
  Kaluza--Klein's fifth dimension as the parameter t of the expansion of
  x₄ {[}92{]}; the McGucken Point as the axiomatic atom of spacetime
  {[}18{]}; the McGucken Geometry as a mathematical category {[}32{]}.
\end{enumerate}

A remark on {[}83{]} communicated to the author states the test: ``Even
if this is true, seems to me that a background-free calculation of the
microstates leading to the Beckenstein-Hawking entropy directly in 4D
instead of a more constrained setup like AdS would be a significant
advance.'' Theorem 12 (§4.2) is that calculation: the count is of
x₄-modes, one per Planck cell ℓ\_P² = ħG/c³ of the McGucken Sphere of
area A, N = A/ℓ\_P², with S = k\_B N/4 = k\_B A/4ℓ\_P²; it is carried
out in four dimensions, on the McGucken Sphere Σ₊(p) that dx₄/dt = ic
generates at the event p, with no anti-de Sitter boundary and no
background, since the rate that generates the McGucken Sphere satisfies
∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g\_μν = 0 (Theorem 7.1 of {[}46{]}) and the metric is derived
from it (Lemma 2.5 of {[}29{]}). The count is the same count that gives
the Born measure at the event (Theorem 7.3), which is why the horizon
entropy and the quantum probability measure are one quantity in this
paper.

Against this list, {[}83{]} assumes a four-dimensional Lorentzian
manifold, a null boundary, a commutator, a Hilbert space, a pure
reference state, five axioms, a direction of time, and a graviton (Table
5.13a) and derives from them a finite Hilbert space, an area entropy and
the Einstein equations in a limit; the Principle derives the inputs and
the outputs from one element. By the criterion of {[}86{]}, the count of
irreducible elements is one, and the empirical facts it represents are
those of items 1--10.

\textbf{Closing attribution.} The null cone as the McGucken Sphere:
Theorem 5.13.1 (§2; Lemma 2.5 of {[}29{]}; Theorem 4.6.4 of {[}29{]}).
Data and constraints: Theorem 5.13.2 (Theorem 21 of {[}24{]}; Theorem
14). The clock as the radius with the Compton period: Theorem 5.13.3
(§2; Proposition 2.2.bis.1 of {[}85{]}; Appendix E). Area quantum,
boost, thermal weight: Theorem 5.13.4 (Theorems 12, 13; Theorem 9.5.11
of {[}29{]}; Appendix C). Finite dimension and discrete area: Theorem
5.13.5 (Theorem 12; Lemma 7.2; Theorem 7.3). Commutator, Hilbert space,
manifold: Theorem 5.13.6 (Lemma 2.5, Theorems 5.1, 6.1, 6.1.5, 10.6,
16.15.1 of {[}29{]}; Part X.1 of {[}85{]}). Entanglement: Theorem 5.13.7
({[}49{]}; §5.9; Theorems 6.6.7.6, 6.6.7.7 of {[}29{]}). Field
equations: Theorem 5.13.8 (Theorems 9, 14; Corollary 14.1; Theorem
6.6.9.2 of {[}29{]}). The arrow: Theorem 5.13.9 (Theorems 11, 15;
Theorem 19.5.1; Theorem 17 of {[}24{]}; Theorem 4.6.4 and Theorem 16.6
of {[}29{]}; §16.3 and Theorem 16.2 of {[}85{]}). The graviton premise
and the open item: Theorem 5.13.10 (Theorem 7.1 and Corollary 7.4(iii)
of {[}46{]}; §2, §4.1.0). Priority and the three chains: §5.13.4,
§5.13.5. Chandrasekaran's statements: {[}83{]}, with equation and
section numbers as cited; {[}84{]}, with timestamps as cited.

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-oppenheims-has-ai-come-for-quantum-gravity-2026-the-six-objections-to-chandrasekarans-null-cone-quantization-as-statements-of-what-the-principle-derives-and-the-three-checks-oppenheim-proposes-as-theorems-of-the-expansion-of-the-mcgucken-sphere}{%
\subsubsection{5.14 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of
Oppenheim's ``Has AI come for quantum gravity?'' (2026): the six
objections to Chandrasekaran's null-cone quantization as statements of
what the Principle derives, and the three checks Oppenheim proposes as
theorems of the expansion of the McGucken
Sphere}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-oppenheims-has-ai-come-for-quantum-gravity-2026-the-six-objections-to-chandrasekarans-null-cone-quantization-as-statements-of-what-the-principle-derives-and-the-three-checks-oppenheim-proposes-as-theorems-of-the-expansion-of-the-mcgucken-sphere}}

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding
at the velocity of light: dx₄/dt = ic, with x₄ = ict, as a spherically
symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action h and whose
volume defines a nonlocality. This section reads Oppenheim's review
{[}87{]} of Chandrasekaran's paper {[}83{]} against the theorems of the
Principle established in §§2--5 and §5.13 and in the corpus papers
{[}29{]}, {[}23{]}, {[}24{]}. Every statement attributed to {[}87{]} is
quoted from its text; every statement attributed to {[}83{]} is quoted
with its equation or section number; every corpus theorem is cited by
the number under which it is reproduced or stated in this paper.
Evidence levels: {[}87{]} verified-read in full; {[}83{]} verified-read
in full; the corpus theorems verified-read as stated in §§2--5 and
§5.13. The scope of the agreement is fixed at the outset: {[}87{]} does
not mention the McGucken Principle; the agreement established below is
between Oppenheim's diagnosis of what {[}83{]} leaves unestablished and
the theorems of the Principle that establish each item.

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic predicts that a
quantization built by promoting the variables of general relativity to
operators meets objections at the places where the Principle supplies a
derivation, because each such place is an input of the quantization and
an output of the Principle: the commutator (Theorem 5.1 of {[}29{]}),
the Hilbert space (Theorem 6.1 of {[}29{]}), the constraints and their
reduction (Theorem 5.13.2), diffeomorphism invariance (Theorem 9, Step
4′ (§5.3)), the microstate count (Theorem 12 (§4.2)), the field
equations without a limit (Theorems 9 and 14), and time (Theorem
5.13.3). Oppenheim's six objections are read in that order.

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-oppenheims-review-in-his-words}{%
\paragraph{5.14.1 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of
Oppenheim's review, in his
words}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-oppenheims-review-in-his-words}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic is the premise of the
theorems against which each objection is read in §5.14.2; the review is
reproduced here so that §5.14.2 refers to Oppenheim's sentences.

The occasion ({[}87{]}): ``On 25 November a paper appeared on arXiv
claiming a quantisation of gravity, finite amplitudes, and a computation
of black-hole entropy. Its acknowledgements credit GPT-6 Astra.'' The
verdict ({[}87{]}): ``The paper doesn't even come close.'' The method
({[}87{]}): ``Suspicion should be raised immediately, because the paper
works within a framework called `canonical quantisation'. The original
version of that programme, quantising the metric directly, stalled in
the 1980s, and not because its problems were merely hard: many of them
appear to be irreconcilable. I've looked over the paper, and none of the
big problems is solved. A few are sidestepped, and the rest are assumed
away or not mentioned.''

The premise ({[}87{]}): ``Many of the problems come from the premise of
the programme itself: it does physics backwards. You take a classical
theory (general relativity), promote its variables to quantum operators,
and hope a sensible theory comes out. The difficulties start
immediately. The order in which you write operators matters in quantum
theory but not in classical theory, and lead to inequivalent theories.
Nor is there any guarantee that the quantum theory you end up with has
general relativity as its classical limit. Even in loop quantum gravity,
the best-developed canonical approach, this has long been the main open
problem. Nature never quantised a classical theory.''

The constraints and time ({[}87{]}): ``A second set of problems comes
from the fact that gravity is a constrained theory: only states that
satisfy certain conditions are allowed. In a quantum theory you expect
to impose these conditions as operator equations on the state. But it
isn't even clear what that means, because of conceptual problems like
`the problem of time'. One of the constraints says the Hamiltonian
annihilates the quantum state, so nothing evolves.'' The reduction
({[}87{]}): ``This paper sidesteps much of that by solving the
constraints classically and then quantising what is left, an approach
called reduced phase space quantisation. The classical part is sound: on
null cones the constraints become ordinary differential equations that
integrate exactly. But the choice of how to do this is not unique, and
the resulting quantum dynamics will almost certainly depend on which one
you choose. There is no reason to expect the result to agree with
imposing the constraints quantum mechanically from the start (Dirac
quantisation), and the paper doesn't check. Nor does it show that the
theory satisfies the central requirement of quantum gravity,
diffeomorphism invariance. It simply imposes it as an axiom.''

The count ({[}87{]}): ``To be more certain, I asked a swarm of Claude
referees to list the known obstacles, and then to check whether the
paper by Chandrasekaran and GPT-6 Astra makes progress on each. The
swarm listed 21. The paper solves one (a minor one, by a standard
trick), sidesteps 7, assumes its way past 6, and doesn't mention the
other 7.''

The three checks ({[}87{]}): ``1. Does the theory get the right black
hole entropy by counting microstates? The abstract says the paper
calculates the entropy, but it doesn't count microstates. It instead
uses an older analytic-continuation argument. The result then rests on a
claim that a region of spacetime has a finite-dimensional Hilbert space,
but the proof of that claim assumes what it sets out to show (it assumes
a finite trace).'' ``2. Is it diffeomorphism invariant, i.e.~does it
have the symmetry of general relativity? The paper doesn't show this; it
imposes it as an axiom, and doesn't show the axioms are consistent or
that a theory satisfying them exists. The original program also stalled
here.'' ``3. Does it reduce to general relativity in the classical
limit? The paper claims a semiclassical limit, but the argument relies
on a Hamiltonian operator that it never constructs.''

The request ({[}87{]}): ``Before it arrives, it would help if we, as a
community, had some criteria or tests that any candidate should pass,
such as the three checks above. And it would be helpful if researchers
working on each approach to quantum gravity wrote down its obstacles in
public. I've written those for the postquantum theory in my status
update.''

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-the-six-objections-each-met-by-a-named-theorem}{%
\paragraph{5.14.2 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of the six
objections, each met by a named
theorem}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-the-six-objections-each-met-by-a-named-theorem}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic supplies, for each
objection, the theorem that establishes what Oppenheim finds
unestablished in {[}83{]}; each theorem below states the objection as a
criterion, locates the criterion in {[}83{]}'s own text, and names the
theorem of the Principle that meets it.

\textbf{Theorem 5.14.1 (Objection 1, the order of derivation).}
Criterion, from {[}87{]}: a theory in which neither quantum mechanics
nor general relativity is obtained by operating on the other, so that no
operator-ordering choice and no classical-limit check arises. The
Principle meets the criterion.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. {[}83{]} promotes: ``For a canonical coordinate
and its conjugate momentum on the same slice, promoting their reduced
Poisson bracket to a commutator fixes the difference between the two
orderings of insertions'' ({[}83{]} §4). Step 2. Theorem 5.1 of {[}29{]}
derives the commutator: ``The canonical commutation relation
{[}\(\hat{q}\), \(\hat{p}\){]} = iℏ follows from the McGucken Principle
as a single foundational statement. Both factors on the right-hand side
are derived, not imported.'' Theorem 6.1 of {[}29{]} derives the Hilbert
space as the unique irreducible representation of that commutator
algebra, by Stone--von Neumann. Step 3. Theorems 9 and 14 derive the
Einstein field equations from the same statement dx₄/dt = ic, with no
operator promoted and no limit taken. Step 4. The ordering ambiguity
{[}87{]} names belongs to the promotion in Step 1; in Step 2 the
right-hand side iℏ is fixed by the perpendicularity of x₄ to x₁x₂x₃ and
by the action per oscillation of the McGucken Sphere, and the operators
of {[}83{]} §4 are, under the Principle, the position and momentum of
Compton-coupled matter on the McGucken Sphere (§2; §4.1.0). ∎

\textbf{Theorem 5.14.2 (Objection 2, the constraints and the choice of
reduction).} Criterion, from {[}87{]}: a formulation in which no
reduction of the constraints is chosen, so that no dependence on the
choice and no disagreement with another quantization can arise. The
Principle meets the criterion.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. {[}83{]} reduces: ``we solve the gravitational
constraints on intersecting null cones of a bulk subregion and obtain
the reduced phase space at finite G\_N'' (abstract), with the free data
``two functions along its generators together with data at its cuts''
(§1). Step 2. Theorem 5.13.2: on the McGucken Sphere Σ₊(p) the radial
advance is fixed at c by the Principle, the only data are the transverse
shape of the McGucken Sphere's cuts, and the interior is determined by
the data on the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 21 of {[}24{]}, §6.2.8). Step
3. The constraints that {[}87{]} describes as integrating exactly on
null cones integrate exactly because the null cone is the McGucken
Sphere (Theorem 5.13.1); the Principle has no second reduction, and no
Dirac quantization of a constraint it does not impose, with which the
result could disagree. ∎

\textbf{Theorem 5.14.3 (Objection 3, diffeomorphism invariance).}
Criterion, from {[}87{]}: diffeomorphism invariance as a theorem, with
the existence of the theory shown. The Principle meets the criterion.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. {[}83{]} imposes: ``1. Diffeomorphism invariance.
We require invariance under diffeomorphisms that preserve the boundary
conditions and under changes of intermediate cuts'' (Appendix E.1). Step
2. Theorem 9, Step 4′ (§5.3) derives the full Diff(M\_G)-invariance of
the gravitational sector from the Lorentz covariance of the McGucken
Sphere, as one step in the derivation of the field equations, and the
sector so constructed exists because the McGucken Sphere exists at every
event by the Principle. Step 3. The rate itself is independent of the
metric, ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g\_μν = 0 (Theorem 7.1 of {[}46{]}, the
McGucken-Invariance Lemma), so the background independence {[}83{]}
builds by dressing fields to the cone ({[}84{]} 57:47: ``this is mainly
just saying how I'm uh dressing fields so that you know it's like
background independent'') is a property of the rate before any field is
dressed. ∎

\textbf{Theorem 5.14.4 (Objection 4, the microstate count and the finite
trace).} Criterion, from {[}87{]}: the black-hole entropy as a count of
microstates, and finiteness of the state space without assuming a finite
trace. The Principle meets the criterion.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. {[}83{]} proves finiteness by contradiction: ``If
ℋ\_𝒟 were infinite dimensional, we could therefore find infinitely many
orthogonal states supported in an arbitrarily narrow interval of corner
area'' (§5.2); ``Their sign in (5.38) makes this impossible. Hence ℋ\_𝒟
is finite dimensional'' (§5.2); and then states Z\_\{𝒟,1\} =
Tr\_\{ℋ\_𝒟\} e\^{}\{−\(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\)/4G\_Nħ\} \textless{} ∞
(5.39b) and d\_𝒟 = dim ℋ\_𝒟 = Z\_\{𝒟,1\} Tr(ρ\_𝒟
e\^{}\{\(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\)/4G\_Nħ\}) \textless{} ∞ (5.39c). The
entropy follows from the trace: S(ρ\_𝒟) = ⟨\(\hat{\mathcal{A}}\)⟩/4G\_Nħ
+ log Z\_\{𝒟,1\} (5.50). Step 2. Theorem 12 (§4.2) counts: one x₄-mode
per Planck cell of the McGucken Sphere, N = A/ℓ\_P², Ω = e\^{}\{N/4\}
(Lemma 7.2), S = k\_B A/4ℓ\_P²; the entropy is the logarithm of a count,
and the count is finite because the McGucken Sphere has an area. Step 3.
Theorem 5.13.5 obtains the finite dimension of {[}83{]}'s ℋ\_𝒟 from that
count and {[}83{]}'s own bound (5.21d), with no trace assumed. Step 4.
Theorem 5.13.4 identifies the analytic continuation {[}87{]} names ---
``Analytically continuing only this boost through a half turn on each
copy yields the full 2π rotation'' ({[}83{]} §5.3) --- as the Euclidean
period of the advance (Theorem 13; Appendix C) taken over the count of
Step 2. ∎

\textbf{Theorem 5.14.5 (Objection 5, the classical limit).} Criterion,
from {[}87{]}: general relativity reached without a limit taken on an
operator that is not constructed. The Principle meets the criterion.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. {[}83{]} §6.1: ``we take ℏ → 0 at fixed initial
data φ\_i. The variance of each smeared canonical variable is O(ℏ), so
over a time interval on which the state remains localized in the reduced
phase space, the expectation value of a smoothly smeared observable
follows the classical trajectory through φ\_i generated by H\_c in
(3.53b)''; and {[}83{]} §6: ``In this limit, invariance of the amplitude
under field shifts in the interior yields the Einstein equations in each
subregion.'' Step 2. Theorems 9 and 14 derive the Einstein field
equations directly from dx₄/dt = ic along two channels that agree
(Corollary 14.1); Theorem 5.13.8 places {[}83{]}'s (6.4) and (6.13) as
the vacuum and one-loop readings of those theorems. Step 3. No limit is
taken, because the field equations are theorems of the rate; the
Hamiltonian operator whose absence {[}87{]} records is not an input of
the derivation. ∎

\textbf{Theorem 5.14.6 (Objection 6, the problem of time).} Criterion,
from {[}87{]}: a time that is not a constraint annihilating the state.
The Principle meets the criterion.

\emph{Proof.} Step 1. {[}83{]} supplies time by a clock: ``its reading
increases strictly from zero'' (§2.1), ``there is no like prescribed
time variable here \ldots{} fluctuates with the geometry'' ({[}84{]}
59:48--59:57). Step 2. Under the Principle time enters as the coordinate
t of dx₄/dt = ic, the parameter against which x₄ advances at c; the
proper-time rate is a consequence (Appendix E). Step 3. Theorem 5.13.3:
{[}83{]}'s clock is the radius r = ct = x₄/i of the McGucken Sphere, and
its strict increase is dr/dt = c with the sign of +ic (Theorem 4.6.4 of
{[}29{]}); the strict Second Law dS/dt \textgreater{} 0 (Theorem 11) is
derived from the same sign. Evolution needs no constraint to generate
it: the McGucken Sphere at every event expands at c by the Principle. ∎

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-the-criterion-oppenheim-asks-for}{%
\paragraph{5.14.4 The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic Reading of the

for}\label{the-mcgucken-principle-dxux2084dt-ic-reading-of-the-criterion-oppenheim-asks-for}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} dx₄/dt = ic supplies the criterion
{[}87{]} requests --- ``criteria or tests that any candidate should
pass'' --- as the criterion Einstein stated in 1933 and as stated
predictions; this subsection records the criterion and one difference.

Einstein's criterion ({[}86{]}): ``Pure logical thinking cannot yield us
any knowledge of the empirical world; all knowledge of reality starts
from experience and ends in it. Propositions arrived at by purely
logical means are completely empty as regards reality. Because Galileo
saw this, and particularly because he drummed it into the scientific
world, he is the father of modern physics---indeed, of modern science
altogether.'' The inputs of the Principle are the measured h and c; its
stated predictions are the five experiments of {[}36{]}, the twelve
cosmological tests of {[}50{]}, and the tidal dependence of the Born
measure of §9. The five items of {[}83{]} with no corpus counterpart ---
the graviton amplitude (4.33), the logarithmic correction
(5.68)--(5.69), the anti-de Sitter bound (5.46), the two-sided
correlators (5.76)--(5.77), and the Jackiw--Teitelboim prologue of §2
--- are accounted to their author by this criterion in the note
following Theorem 5.13.10.

One difference is recorded. {[}87{]} refers to ``the postquantum theory
in my status update,'' Oppenheim's own programme, in which gravity
remains classical and stochastic while matter is quantum (background
knowledge). Under the Principle gravity is neither quantized nor left
classical: general relativity and quantum mechanics are two theorem
chains of the one rate dx₄/dt = ic (Theorems 9 and 14; Theorems 5.1 and
6.1 of {[}29{]}).

Theorem 5.14.1 (Theorems 5.1, 6.1 of {[}29{]}; Theorems 9 and 14).
Objection 2, the reduction: Theorem 5.14.2 (Theorem 5.13.2; Theorem
5.13.1; Theorem 21 of {[}24{]}, §6.2.8). Objection 3, diffeomorphism
invariance: Theorem 5.14.3 (Theorem 9, Step 4′ (§5.3); Theorem 7.1 of
{[}46{]}). Objection 4, the count: Theorem 5.14.4 (Theorem 12 (§4.2);
Theorem 5.13.5; Theorem 5.13.4; Theorem 13; Appendix C). Objection 5,

Theorem 5.13.8). Objection 6, time: Theorem 5.14.6 (Theorem 5.13.3;
Theorem 4.6.4 of {[}29{]}; Theorem 11; Appendix E). The three checks:
