\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-entropy-s-k-ln-ux3c9-of-the-state-count-ux3c9-of-the-expanding-sphere-of-which-gravity-the-born-rule-and-thermodynamics-are-all-readings}{%
\subsection{6. The McGucken Entropy S = k ln Ω of the state-count Ω of
the expanding Sphere, of which gravity, the Born rule, and
thermodynamics are all
readings}\label{the-mcgucken-entropy-s-k-ln-ux3c9-of-the-state-count-ux3c9-of-the-expanding-sphere-of-which-gravity-the-born-rule-and-thermodynamics-are-all-readings}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) states the physical reality that the fourth dimension
expands at the rate \(c\), as a spherically symmetric wavefront --- the
McGucken Sphere --- from every event of spacetime, carrying one quantum
of action \(h\) per Compton oscillation. Everything in this section is a
direct consequence of that Principle: the McGucken Entropy is the
entropy of the state-count of that expanding Sphere, its logarithm
\(S = k_B\ln\Omega\); its strict monotonicity is the \(+ic\) orientation
of the expansion; and each named entropy of physics is a reading of the
one Sphere state-count \(\Omega\) that \(dx_4/dt = ic\) generates. The
section defines the McGucken Entropy, states the McGucken Entropy
Identity unifying the entropies of physics as readings of \(\Omega\),
and shows how the McGucken Entropy resolves Loschmidt's objection (§6.2)
and supplies the constructive foundation Einstein sought (§6.3) --- each
a consequence of the one Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\).

\textbf{Definition (McGucken Entropy).} The \emph{McGucken Entropy} is
the entropy of the McGucken Sphere's SO(3)-invariant Haar measure on the
spatial-projection two-sphere W(t), under the Compton-coupling
matter-interaction mechanism:
\[S_{\text{McG}} = k_B \ln \Omega, \qquad \Omega = \text{the count of distinguishable states of the expanding McGucken Sphere,}\]
where Ω is the number of distinguishable configurations the Sphere's
SO(3)-invariant advance passes through --- one per Compton tick, each
carrying one quantum of action h --- resolved on the region under
consideration. This is the foundational entropy of the framework: every
entropy in physics is a reading of S\_McG, and the identity of §7
(gravity is the Born rule) is the statement that the gravitational and
quantum readings of S\_McG are one quantity.

Because S\_McG is defined by the Haar measure on the Sphere, it inherits
the Sphere's two-channel structure (§5.2.2): read through the Algebraic
Channel it is a time-symmetric algebraic invariant; read through the
Geometric Channel it is a time-asymmetric geometric quantity carrying
the +ic monotonic orientation, whence dS\_McG/dt \textgreater{} 0
(§4.1). The apparently distinct entropy formulas of physics are the
readings of S\_McG in the several empirical sectors, established as a
theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) in the thermodynamics paper {[}24{]}.

\textbf{Theorem 6.1 (The McGucken Entropy Identity, after {[}24{]}).}
\emph{Under \(dx_4/dt = ic\), the entropy formulas of five distinct
sectors of physics are five readings of the one McGucken Entropy S\_McG
= k\_B ln Ω on the expanding McGucken Sphere:}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{(1) Information theory --- Shannon entropy} H = −Σ\_i p\_i log
  p\_i, the Algebraic-Channel algebraic-symmetry reading of the Sphere's
  Haar measure partitioned into pointer-basis cells.
\item
  \textbf{(2) Statistical mechanics --- Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy} S\_BG
  = −k\_B Σ\_i p\_i log p\_i, the Geometric-Channel Euclidean reading,
  time-asymmetric with dS/dt \textgreater{} 0.
\item
  \textbf{(3) Quantum mechanics --- von Neumann entropy} S\_vN = −Tr(ρ
  log ρ), the Algebraic-Channel reading of the density matrix's spectral
  probabilities (the same reading Carcassi's equivalence identifies with
  the Born rule, §3.11).
\item
  \textbf{(4) Black-hole thermodynamics --- Bekenstein--Hawking entropy}
  S\_BH = k\_B A/(4ℓ\_P²), the Geometric-Channel Euclidean reading on
  the horizon McGucken Sphere (§4.2, §5), the gravitational reading of
  Ω.
\item
  \textbf{(5) Stochastic processes --- Wiener differential entropy} S\_W
  = (3/2)k\_B ln(4πeDt/λ\_C²), the Geometric-Channel reading on Brownian
  paths (the Gaussian entropy of the Compton-tick diffusion, §4.1), with
  the reference length λ\_C the Compton step, required because the
  argument of the logarithm must be dimensionless (§6.4.1).
\end{itemize}

\emph{All five are projections of the one SO(3)-invariant Haar-measure
entropy of the McGucken Sphere onto the five sectors, related pairwise
by the Klein correspondence, with the two Algebraic-Channel readings
(Shannon, von Neumann) time-symmetric and the three Geometric-Channel
readings (Boltzmann--Gibbs, Bekenstein--Hawking, Wiener) time-asymmetric
with the +ic orientation forcing strict positivity of the entropy
time-derivative.}

\emph{Proof (after {[}24{]}, six steps).} Each of the five expressions
reduces to the McGucken-Sphere Haar-measure entropy S\_McG.
\textbf{(Step 1, Shannon).} The Born-rule derivation (§3) establishes
that the probability density on the Sphere's directional cross-section
is the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure; partitioned into pointer-basis
cells with weights p\_i, its information content is H = −Σ p\_i log
p\_i, the algebraic-symmetry reading. \textbf{(Step 2,
Boltzmann--Gibbs).} Theorem 19.5.1 (§4.1) established dS/dt =
(3/2)k\_B/t \textgreater{} 0 via the Compton-coupling Brownian
mechanism; the microstate count of that diffusion on the spatial slice
gives S\_BG = −k\_B Σ p\_i log p\_i, the Geometric-Channel reading.
\textbf{(Step 3, von Neumann).} The density matrix ρ = Σ λ\_i
\textbar φ\_i⟩⟨φ\_i\textbar{} has spectral weights λ\_i that are the
Born probabilities on the Sphere (§3), so S\_vN = −Tr(ρ log ρ) = −Σ λ\_i
log λ\_i is the algebraic reading of the same Haar measure.
\textbf{(Step 4, Bekenstein--Hawking).} Theorem 19.6.1 / §4.2
established S\_BH = k\_B A/(4ℓ\_P²) as the Compton-tick mode count tiled
on the horizon Sphere, the Geometric-Channel reading over the bounding
area. \textbf{(Step 5, Wiener).} The Wiener process on M is the
Euclidean reading of the iterated Huygens--McGucken-Sphere displacement;
its differential entropy S\_W = (3/2)k\_B ln(4πeDt/λ\_C²), referred to
the Compton-step cell, is the continuous-path form of the same Gaussian
count (§4.1). \textbf{(Step 6, Klein correspondence).} The five readings
are related pairwise --- Shannon ↔ Boltzmann--Gibbs (same −Σp log p,
algebraic vs.~geometric reading), von Neumann ↔ Bekenstein--Hawking
(spectral probabilities on Hilbert space vs.~mode count on the horizon
Sphere), Boltzmann--Gibbs ↔ Wiener (discrete vs.~continuous Gaussian
entropy), Shannon ↔ Wiener (discrete vs.~continuous information), and
all five ↔ the McGucken-Sphere Haar measure via the Compton-coupling
mechanism --- completing the identification of the five as one quantity.
\(\square\)

\textbf{Scope of the identity.} The five readings are of one source
count under a specified state, measurement, and coarse-graining, and
they are numerically equal only when those are the same: the von Neumann
entropy of the pure state (\textbar0⟩ + \textbar1⟩)/√2 is zero while the
Shannon entropy of its z-measurement is k\_B ln 2, the difference being
the coarse-graining the measurement basis imposes; and for a nonuniform
distribution e\^{}\{S/k\_B\} is an effective number of states, an
integer only for the uniform case. Theorem 6.1 identifies the Sphere's
count as the common source of the five functionals, and the two-state
probability--entropy correspondence of §7 (the equal mixture ρ =
½(\textbar ψ⟩⟨ψ\textbar{} + \textbar φ⟩⟨φ\textbar) has eigenvalues (1 ±
√p)/2 with p = \textbar⟨ψ\textbar φ⟩\textbar², so its entropy is an
invertible function of the Born probability) is the exact form the
correspondence takes.

\textbf{Consequence.} The seventy-six-year-old observation that the same
functional form −Σ p\_i log p\_i appears in information theory (Shannon
1948), statistical mechanics (Boltzmann 1872, Gibbs 1902), and quantum
mechanics (von Neumann 1932) --- treated in the orthodox literature as a
coincidence supported only by Shannon's three axioms --- is not
coincidental but forced: all are readings of the one McGucken Entropy
S\_McG = k\_B ln Ω of the expanding Sphere {[}24{]}. This reading is
corroborated externally and independently: the Born measure is derived
as an entropy-minimization result in frameworks unconnected to the
corpus --- Carcassi--Aidala's equivalence of the Born rule with the von
Neumann entropy {[}39, 42{]} and Zaghi's derivation of the Born rule as
the minimizer of the Umegaki relative entropy {[}47{]} --- each
confirming, from a different direction, that the Born rule is entropy,
as the McGucken Entropy Identity states. These are external
corroborations of the equivalence, not corpus results and not
gravity-side derivations; the McGucken contribution is to identify the
one entropy S\_McG of the expanding Sphere of which the Born measure and
the gravitational entropy are both readings (§7), which no external
program addresses. This is why ``gravity is entropy,'' ``the Born rule
is entropy,'' and ``gravity is the Born rule'' all hold (§6): the
gravitational entropy (reading 4), the Born measure (readings 1/3), and
the thermodynamic entropy (readings 2/5) are one entropy S\_McG of the
one Sphere, counted over the horizon, the event, and the diffusion
respectively --- the Universe's foundational entropy, the logarithm S =
k ln Ω of the count Ω of states of the expanding McGucken Sphere.

\hypertarget{the-mcgucken-entropy-resolves-loschmidts-reversibility-objection-the-150-year-arrow-of-time-impasse-dissolved}{%
\subsubsection{6.2 The McGucken Entropy resolves Loschmidt's
reversibility objection: the 150-year arrow-of-time impasse
dissolved}\label{the-mcgucken-entropy-resolves-loschmidts-reversibility-objection-the-150-year-arrow-of-time-impasse-dissolved}}

The McGucken Entropy resolves a tension that has stood since 1876.
Loschmidt's reversibility objection (Umkehreinwand) to Boltzmann's
H-theorem is that the microscopic dynamics of mechanics are
time-symmetric --- for every entropy-increasing trajectory there is a
time-reversed, entropy-decreasing one of equal validity --- so no
strictly monotonic Second Law dS/dt \textgreater{} 0 can follow from
reversible microdynamics alone. For 150 years this stood as an
unresolved impasse: reversible micro-dynamics and the monotone
macroscopic Second Law were two facts whose coexistence was
mathematically permitted but physically unexplained.

The two-channel structure of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) dissolves the objection,
and the resolution runs directly through the McGucken Entropy. The
time-symmetric microscopic dynamics Loschmidt invoked is the
Algebraic-Channel reading: the unitary evolution U(t) has its inverse
U(−t) in the same group, and the Heisenberg relation {[}\(\hat{q}\),
\(\hat{p}\){]} = iℏ is invariant under t → −t (§5.2.2). On that channel
Loschmidt was correct: reversible microdynamics cannot derive a strict
monotone, because the Algebraic Channel is sign-symmetric on the +ic
orientation. But the strict Second Law dS/dt \textgreater{} 0 is
Geometric-Channel content --- the +ic orientation of the McGucken
Sphere's expansion, which is not present in the Algebraic Channel at all
(§4.1, §5.2.2). The McGucken Entropy S\_McG = k\_B ln Ω carries the
arrow because Ω is the count of states of the \emph{expanding} Sphere,
and the expansion is oriented at +ic (never −ic): the Sphere expands
outward, never inward, so Ω increases, never decreases, giving
dS\_McG/dt \textgreater{} 0 (Theorem 19.5.1, §4.1). This is the content
of the Loschmidt no-go theorem of the corpus {[}45{]}: under
\(dx_4/dt = +ic\) with the McGucken-Sphere Compton-coupling Brownian
mechanism, no entropy-decreasing macroscopic trajectory exists --- the
time-reversed trajectory Loschmidt constructed on the Algebraic Channel
has no realization on the Geometric Channel, whose expansion is chirally
+ic-oriented.

There was therefore never an actual conflict. Loschmidt and Boltzmann
were each right within their respective channels: Loschmidt on the
Algebraic-Channel time-symmetric algebra, where unitary mechanics cannot
produce monotonicity, exactly as he argued; Boltzmann on what is, in
modern reading, the Geometric-Channel +ic-oriented geometry, which
carries the monotonicity through the orientation of the active expansion
{[}45{]}. The unitary evolution and the monotone entropy increase hold
simultaneously at every instant, as the two channels of the one
principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) --- the frozen (reversible) reading and the
expanding (dissipative) reading of the one McGucken Entropy (§3.11). The
150-year impasse was the signature of a physics operating entirely in
the Algebraic Channel's time-symmetric algebra without access to the
Geometric Channel's +ic orientation; the McGucken Entropy supplies the
missing orientation, and the objection dissolves. The five (or six)
conventionally distinguished arrows of time --- thermodynamic,
cosmological, radiative, quantum-measurement, psychological, and
Penrose's Weyl-curvature arrow --- are, in the same reading, projections
of the single +ic orientation of the Sphere's expansion that the
McGucken Entropy records {[}45{]}.

\textbf{The low-entropy past is derived, not posited: the Past
Hypothesis as a geometric necessity.} A standard objection to any
arrow-of-time account is that it must still explain why the early
universe had low entropy --- the Past Hypothesis, which Boltzmannian
mechanics must add as a separate brute stipulation because its
reversible microdynamics cannot supply it, and which Penrose quantifies
as a 1-in-10\textsuperscript{(10}123) fine-tuning of the initial state.
The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework does not posit the low-entropy past;
it derives it as a theorem (thermodynamics paper {[}24{]}, Theorem 13).
The x₄-origin is geometrically, necessarily, the lowest-entropy moment
of any system participating in the x₄-expansion: at the origin the
McGucken Sphere has zero radius, so the state-count Ω is minimal (Ω → 1,
a single distinguishable cell, ln Ω → 0), and the Sphere can only expand
from there, so Ω can only grow. There is no smaller sphere than the
initial point and no configuration of lower count than the single cell;
the lowest-entropy state is not a fine-tuned initial condition selected
from a uniform prior but the unique geometric starting point of the
expansion itself. Penrose's 10\textsuperscript{(10}123) improbability
measures the unlikeliness of the low-entropy past \emph{under a uniform
prior over phase space} --- but the geometry of x₄-expansion does not
use that prior: it starts every system at the origin of the advance,
which is the minimum-Ω point by construction. The Past Hypothesis, an
unexplained stipulation in orthodox cosmology, is in the McGucken
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) framework a consequence of the same +ic-oriented
expansion that gives the Second Law --- the two are one theorem for the
x₄-advance count: the Sphere starts at minimum count and expands, so
this entropy starts low and rises, necessarily and without fine-tuning.
The scope of this theorem is stated exactly. It derives the low initial
value of the x₄-advance count of each Sphere. Penrose's
10\textsuperscript{(10}123) measures a further quantity --- the
Weyl-curvature (gravitational-clumping) entropy of the initial matter
configuration, the count over matter microstates that Boltzmann's
formula takes --- and the minimum-Ω origin of the Spheres does not by
itself fix that configuration: a universe of Spheres all at their
origins can carry an arbitrary matter distribution. The homogeneity of
the initial matter distribution across the sky is addressed in the
McGucken cosmology {[}50{]} (the horizon and flatness problems resolved
without inflation, §5.7.10, Divergence 11, through the McGucken radius
R₄ = ct exceeding the standard causal horizon at every epoch); the full
Weyl-curvature statement of the Past Hypothesis --- the smoothness of
the initial gravitational field --- is the open item that remains, and
it is not supplied by the present theorem.

\hypertarget{one-generator-not-two-the-full-state-is-unitary-diffusion-is-the-reduced-state-reading-with-a-computed-lindblad-generator-and-a-falsifiable-residual}{%
\subsubsection{6.2.1 One generator, not two: the full state is unitary,
diffusion is the reduced-state reading, with a computed Lindblad
generator and a falsifiable
residual}\label{one-generator-not-two-the-full-state-is-unitary-diffusion-is-the-reduced-state-reading-with-a-computed-lindblad-generator-and-a-falsifiable-residual}}

The two-channel reading raises a precise dynamical question that must be
answered with one generator, not two labels: a single physical system
--- a hydrogen atom, an interferometer, a closed box of gas --- has one
history, evolved by one law. Either that law is unitary
(volume-preserving on the full Hilbert space) or it is the diffusive
process of the Second Law (volume-augmenting). It cannot be exactly
both, for the same closed state, at every instant. The resolution is not
a duality of labels but a standard open-system reduction, and the
McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework computes it in full {[}24{]}; it is
reproduced here because it is the answer to the apparent contradiction.

\textbf{The full closed state evolves unitarily.} The generator of the
full state is the McGucken-derived Schrödinger/unitary evolution (§3,
{[}38{]}): the closed system's evolution is exactly unitary, phase-space
volume is exactly conserved on the full state, interference is exact,
energy is exactly conserved. There is no per-particle contractive law on
the full closed state. The apparent diffusion is \emph{not} a property
of the full state.

\textbf{Diffusion is the reduced-state reading, and its generator is
computed.} When the environment is traced out --- as it must be for any
system that is not the entire universe --- the reduced state obeys a
Lindblad equation whose generator is derived from dx₄/dt = ic through
the Compton coupling. The Compton-coupling interaction with the
x₄-modulation produces, at second order (computed two independent ways
--- the Floquet--Magnus expansion of {[}24{]} and the
Langevin/fluctuation--dissipation route, which cross-validate), a
momentum-diffusion term
\[D_p = \tfrac{1}{2} m^2 \varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega,\] with ε the
dimensionless x₄-coupling, Ω the modulation rate, c the expansion
velocity. This is the Lindblad generator the reduction requires: the
reduced state decoheres and acquires the diffusion, the full state stays
unitary. The decoherence timescale is τ\_dec \textasciitilde{} 1/(N\_env
ω\_C), and --- this is the decisive point the critic's objection asks
for --- the randomness ``is only apparent on the reduced state, not the
full state. Decoherence does not produce randomness in principle; it
produces randomness in practice, through the unobservability of the
environment'' {[}24{]}. The Second Law's dS/dt \textgreater{} 0 is the
entropy of the reduced state; the full-state unitarity and the
reduced-state diffusion are not two generators of one state but the
exact generator of the full state and its trace onto a subsystem --- the
ordinary structure of quantum statistical mechanics, with the generator
supplied by dx₄/dt = ic.

\textbf{The residual is falsifiable and confronted with data.} After the
ordinary environmental damping γ is included
(Langevin/Ornstein--Uhlenbeck reduction), the framework predicts a
residual zero-temperature spatial diffusion coefficient
\[D_x^{(\mathrm{McG})} = \frac{\varepsilon^2 c^2 \Omega}{2\gamma^2}\]
for any massive particle coupled to the x₄-expansion --- a specific,
mass- and temperature-structured coefficient that is the empirical
signature distinguishing the framework from standard quantum mechanics
(where it is exactly zero). This residual is the answer to ``how does an
interferometer stay coherent if every particle is kicked each tick'':
the kicks are the reduced-state decoherence, their un-decohered residual
is D\_x above, and it is bounded by present optical-clock and
trapped-ion-interferometry precision (fractional frequencies
\textasciitilde10⁻¹⁸--10⁻¹⁹). The framework does not assert exact
unitarity and exact per-particle diffusion of the same state; it
computes the unitary full-state generator, the Lindblad reduced-state
generator, the decoherence time, and the residual --- and stakes itself
on the residual as a falsifiable number {[}24{]}.

\textbf{Wick rotation is not the reduction.} The McGucken--Wick rotation
(§5.5) relates the Lorentzian and Euclidean \emph{presentations} of the
geometry; it is not the mechanism that turns the unitary full-state law
into the diffusive reduced-state law. That mechanism is the
environmental trace above, with the computed Lindblad generator. The
Wick rotation and the open-system reduction are distinct operations, and
the resolution of the one-generator question rests on the reduction, not
on the analytic continuation.

\hypertarget{the-five-arrows-of-time-as-projections-of-ic-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-11-of-24}{%
\paragraph{6.2.2 The Five Arrows of Time as projections of +ic
(thermodynamics paper {[}24{]}, Theorem 11 of
{[}24{]})}\label{the-five-arrows-of-time-as-projections-of-ic-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-11-of-24}}

\textbf{Theorem (Five-fold unification of arrows of time).} Under the
McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = +ic\), the following five empirically
distinct arrows of time are projections onto distinct sectors of
physical observation of one and the same underlying monotonic geometric
advance:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{Thermodynamic arrow}: \(dS/dt > 0\) for closed isolated systems.
\item
  \emph{Cosmological arrow}: the universe expands, \(\dot{a}(t) > 0\).
\item
  \emph{Radiative arrow}: electromagnetic radiation propagates outward
  from sources (retarded, not advanced, Green's function).
\item
  \emph{Quantum-measurement arrow}: measurement projects a superposition
  onto a single eigenvector; the inverse process is not observed.
\item
  \emph{Psychological arrow}: subjective experience of memory and
  anticipation is asymmetric (we remember the past, not the future).
\end{enumerate}

The unique common source is the geometric monotonicity \(dx_4/dt = +ic\)
(sign \(+\), not \(-\)).

\emph{Proof.} \textbf{Step 1 (One-way geometric advance).} The McGucken
Principle \(dx_4/dt = +ic\) asserts that the fourth dimension expands at
velocity \(c\) in the \(+ic\) direction at every spacetime event. The
McGucken Sphere \(\Sigma_+(p_0)\) grows monotonically with radius
\(R(t) = c(t-t_0)\), never shrinking (Theorem 3 of {[}24{]}). This is
the one-way geometric advance.

\textbf{Step 2 (Thermodynamic projection).} Theorem 9 of {[}24{]}
establishes \(dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0\) for massive-particle ensembles,
with the strict positivity forced by the monotonicity of the McGucken
Sphere's volume and the Compton-coupled diffusion that follows from
\(dx_4/dt = ic\). Theorem 10 of {[}24{]} establishes
\(dS/dt = 2\kB/(t-t_0) > 0\) for photon ensembles on the spherical
wavefront. The thermodynamic arrow is thus the projection of \(+ic\)
onto the entropy sector.

\textbf{Step 3 (Cosmological projection).} In the FRW geometry, the
scale factor \(a(t)\) is the spatial projection of the cosmological
McGucken expansion. The CMB rest frame is selected as a commitment of
the framework by condition (P4) of the privileged-element conditions
{[}Def.~5.4{]}, which fixes the empirically observed cosmic microwave
background rest frame as the privileged frame of \(V\)'s flow rather
than as a state-dependent derived consequence. The spatial slicing
within which the universe-scale Sphere expands isotropically is
therefore fixed. Then \(\dot{a}(t) > 0\) follows from the monotonicity
of \(R(t)\): spatial slices at later \(t\) are at larger radii on the
cosmological Sphere. This is the cosmological projection of \(+ic\).
Theorem 18 of {[}24{]} develops the FRW thermodynamics in detail.

\textbf{Step 4 (Radiative projection).} The wave equation of Theorem 1
of {[}24{]} admits two independent fundamental solutions: the retarded
Green's function
\(G_{\mathrm{ret}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \delta(t-r/c)/(4\pi r)\) and the
advanced Green's function
\(G_{\mathrm{adv}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \delta(t+r/c)/(4\pi r)\). The
McGucken Sphere is \(\Sigma_+(p_0)\) (notation: the subscript \(+\)
carries the orientation) corresponding to \(r = +c(t-t_0)\) for
\(t > t_0\); the time-reversed sphere \(\Sigma_-(p_0)\) corresponding to
\(r = -c(t-t_0)\) (i.e., \(t < t_0\)) is geometrically excluded by
\(dx_4/dt = +ic\) (with sign \(+\)). Physical electromagnetic radiation
propagates along the McGucken Sphere \(\Sigma_+(p_0)\), selecting the
retarded Green's function. The radiative arrow is thus the projection of
\(+ic\) onto the electromagnetic-propagation sector. The standard
\(+i\varepsilon\) prescription of QFT (with \(\varepsilon \to 0^+\)) is
identified by Theorem 12 of {[}19{]} as the infinitesimal Wick rotation
at angle \(\theta = \varepsilon\) in the \((x_0, x_4)\) plane: the
substitution \(t \to (1 - i\varepsilon)t\) corresponds to
\(\tau = x_4/c\) rotated by an infinitesimal angle in the \((x_0, x_4)\)
Euclidean plane, with the full Wick rotation the completion at
\(\theta = \pi/2\). The Feynman \(+i\varepsilon\) prescription and the
full Wick rotation are therefore the same geometric operation at two
different angles of rotation in the \((x_0, x_4)\) plane (Corollary 13
of {[}19{]}). The sign \(+i\varepsilon\) (not \(-i\varepsilon\)) is the
integral-shadow image of the same \(+ic\) structure, selecting the
retarded prescription consistent with the McGucken Sphere
\(\Sigma_+(p_0)\).

\textbf{Step 5 (Quantum-measurement projection).} On the McGucken dx₄/dt
= ic framework, quantum measurement is the projection of the
spacetime-distributed wavefunction \(\psi(\mathbf{x},t,x_4)\) onto a
spatial hypersurface at fixed \(t\) (the Born rule as projection onto
the \(x_1 x_2 x_3\) slice; the McGucken Sphere projection). The
measurement-time direction is the same \(+ic\) direction: measurements
occur at later \(t\), never at earlier \(t\) relative to the system
preparation. Wavefunction collapse (or, on a unitary interpretation,
decoherence) is the projection of the spacetime structure onto a spatial
slice at later \(t\) on the McGucken Sphere. The quantum-measurement
arrow is thus the projection of \(+ic\) onto the measurement sector.
Detailed development is in the QM companion paper {[}18{]}.

\textbf{Step 6 (Psychological projection).} The psychological arrow of
time is the empirically observed asymmetry between memory (we recall the
past) and anticipation (we predict, but do not remember, the future). On
the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, biological systems are open
thermodynamic systems embedded in the expanding McGucken geometry. The
accumulation of memory traces requires monotonic entropy increase in the
environment (Landauer's principle: information storage requires entropy
export). The thermodynamic arrow (Step 2) thus forces the psychological
arrow: memory accumulation is correlated with environmental entropy
increase, which is correlated with \(x_4\)'s advance at \(+ic\). The
psychological arrow is thus the projection of \(+ic\) onto the
cognitive-biological sector.

\textbf{Step 7 (Unification).} Steps 2-6 establish that each of the five
arrows is the projection of one underlying geometric fact,
\(dx_4/dt = +ic\) with sign \(+\). The five arrows are not five
independent empirical facts requiring five independent explanations;
they are five projections of one geometric monotonicity. This is the
unification: \emph{one source, five projections}.

\textbf{Step 8 (Counterfactual confirmation).} Suppose instead
\(dx_4/dt = -ic\) (the time-reversed McGucken Principle). Then all five
arrows would reverse: entropy would decrease, the universe would
contract, radiation would converge inward (advanced Green's function),
measurements would un-collapse wavefunctions, and memory would record
the future. The empirical observation that the five arrows point in a
common direction is exactly the empirical content of the sign \(+\) in
\(dx_4/dt = +ic\). The McGucken Principle thus passes a strong
counterfactual test: it forces the observed direction of all five arrows
simultaneously. \(\Box\)

\hypertarget{ergodicity-as-a-huygens-wavefront-identity-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-8-of-24}{%
\paragraph{6.2.3 Ergodicity as a Huygens-wavefront identity
(thermodynamics paper {[}24{]}, Theorem 8 of
{[}24{]})}\label{ergodicity-as-a-huygens-wavefront-identity-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-8-of-24}}

\textbf{Theorem (Ergodicity as Huygens-Wavefront Identity).}
Ergodicity--the equality of time-averages and ensemble-averages--is a
geometric identity of the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Geometric Channel
Huygens-wavefront propagation: for any continuous observable \(F\) on
phase space, the time-average along any trajectory equals the
ensemble-average over the McGucken Sphere's wavefront cross-section. The
identity is independent of metric transitivity and unaffected by
KAM-tori obstruction. This closes Einstein's second gap (T2).

\hypertarget{proof-theorem-8-of-24}{%
\subsubsection{Proof (Theorem 8 of
{[}24{]})}\label{proof-theorem-8-of-24}}

\emph{Proof.} The proof proceeds via the direct Huygens-wavefront
identity of {[}Theorem 3 of {[}24{]}{]} applied to the McGucken Sphere
structure of \(dx_4/dt = ic\). Birkhoff's 1931 pointwise ergodic theorem
is not used in the present derivation: the equidistribution-on-\(S^2\)
result of Step (b) of the Huygens-Wavefront Identity Lemma below follows
from the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Geometric Channel spatial-projection isotropy
alone, which is a geometric content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) (condition (P3)
of {[}Definition 5.4 of {[}24{]}{]}) and does not depend on the orbital
structure of the underlying dynamical system. Birkhoff 1931 appears in
the comparison block of the Theorem 8 of {[}24{]} comparison as the
orthodox antecedent that the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supersedes;
it does not appear in the present derivation.

\textbf{Step 1 (The geometric setup).} From Theorem 3 of {[}24{]}, the
geometric-propagation content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is the McGucken Sphere
expanding from every spacetime event with Huygens-wavefront propagation.
The wavefront at time \(t\) from event \(p_0 = (\mathbf{x}_0, t_0)\) is
the two-sphere \(W(t) = \Sigma_+(p_0)\cap\Sigma_t\) of radius
\(R(t) = c(t-t_0)\).

\textbf{Step 2 (The Huygens-wavefront identity).} Consider a particle
initially at \(p_0\). At time \(t > t_0\), the McGucken Sphere from
\(p_0\) has area \(A(t) = 4\pi R^2(t) = 4\pi c^2 (t-t_0)^2\). By the
Iterative McGucken Sphere Lemma, every point on this Sphere is itself
the source of a new McGucken Sphere by Huygens' Principle (Theorem 3 of
{[}24{]}).

\textbf{Step 3 (Ensemble realization on the Sphere).} The continuous
family of intermediate Spheres along the trajectory from \(p_0\)
physically realizes the ensemble over which the trajectory's ``possible
histories'' spread. At time \(t\), the ensemble of realizations is
parameterized by the surface of the McGucken Sphere with the uniform
rotation-invariant measure on \(S^2\) -- the unique SO(3)-invariant
normalized measure forced directly by condition (P3) of {[}Definition
5.4 of {[}24{]}{]}, with no external Haar machinery required. This
ensemble is the geometric content of the trajectory, not a fictional
bookkeeping device imposed by the theorist.

\textbf{Step 4 (The McGucken-framework strengthening over Birkhoff
1931).} The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework's central observation:
\emph{the ensemble-average is geometrically realized by the
Huygens-wavefront cross-section at each instant, not merely by the
long-time limit of the trajectory}. The Birkhoff 1931 pointwise ergodic
theorem is the orthodox result that the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework
supersedes: the orthodox argument requires metric transitivity and
applies to the long-time limit of the trajectory under
measure-preserving dynamics, with KAM-tori obstruction breaking the
metric-transitivity hypothesis on positive-measure sets. The McGucken
argument operates on the wavefront at each instant rather than on the
orbit's long-time limit, replacing the Birkhoff machinery with the
Huygens-wavefront identity below.

\textbf{Step 5 (The McGucken-framework strengthening).} The McGucken
dx₄/dt = ic framework strengthens the Birkhoff theorem: \emph{the
ensemble-average is geometrically realized by the Huygens-wavefront
cross-section at each instant, not merely by the long-time limit of the
trajectory.} Specifically:

\textbf{Lemma (Huygens-Wavefront Identity).} Let \(F:M\to\mathbb{R}\) be
a continuous observable. For any spacetime event \(p_0\) and any
\(t > t_0\), let \(W(t) := \Sigma_+(p_0)\cap\Sigma_t\) be the McGucken
Sphere from \(p_0\) at time \(t\), with uniform measure \(d\sigma\) on
\(W(t)\) normalized to total mass 1 (the unique SO(3)-invariant
probability measure on \(W(t) \cong S^2\) as established in Theorem 5 of
{[}24{]} the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Algebraic Channel via Haar uniqueness on
\(S^2 = \mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)\)). Then for any trajectory
\(\gamma\) in phase space (passing through \(p_0\) at time \(t_0\)) and
any continuous observable \(F\),

\[\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_{t_0}^{t_0 + T} F(\gamma(s))\,ds \;=\; \int_{W(t)} F\,d\sigma\]

where the right-hand side is the geometric ensemble-average over the
wavefront cross-section.

\emph{Proof of lemma.} The proof has three parts.

\emph{(a) The trajectory as a Huygens-wavefront propagator.} The
physical-geometric content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) asserts that the fourth
dimension expands at velocity \(c\) in a spherically symmetric manner
from every spacetime event. Any trajectory \(\gamma\) in phase space is,
by Theorem 3 of {[}24{]}, a sequence of McGucken-Sphere apex events
\(\gamma(s_1), \gamma(s_2), \ldots\) each generating a Huygens
wavefront. The four-velocity of \(\gamma\) satisfies
\(u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2\) ({[}Cor.~1.1{]}; the master equation of
Proposition 2.3 of {[}14{]}, {[}a consequence of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) ---
the chain-rule pullback of the Sphere's expansion rate, carrying the
magnitude only, Appendix E (R3) --- with \(dx_4/d\tau = ic\) holding on
the rest worldline where \(d\tau = dt\), Lemma 4.7 of {[}29{]}{]}),
where \(u^4 = c\) ({[}on the rest worldline the four-velocity budget is
wholly in the \(x_4\)-component, as \(dx_4/dt = ic\) states{]}). The
trajectory therefore advances along \(x_4\) at rate \(c\), with its
spatial three-velocity \((u^1, u^2, u^3)\) constrained by the
four-velocity budget to satisfy
\(|\mathbf{u}|^2 + c^2 = c^2 \gamma_L^2\), where \(\gamma_L\) is the
Lorentz factor. The trajectory's spatial position at any time \(t\) lies
within the McGucken Sphere \(W(t)\) of radius \(R(t) = c(t - t_0)\), by
the geometric content of the \(u_\mu u^\mu = -c^2\) constraint: the
spatial-velocity magnitude is bounded by \(c\) on subluminal
trajectories.

\emph{(b) Ergodic equidistribution of \(\gamma\) on \(W(t)\) under
random spatial-direction wandering.} By Theorem 5 of {[}24{]}'s
spatial-projection isotropy, the spatial-direction component of
\(\gamma\)'s velocity is distributed uniformly on \(S^2\) at every
infinitesimal proper-time step in the rest frame; equivalently, the
angular distribution of the trajectory's velocity is a sequence of
i.i.d.~uniform-on-\(S^2\) random variables. Iterating: over a long time
interval \([t_0, t_0 + T]\), the \emph{empirical angular distribution}
of the trajectory converges weakly to the uniform measure on \(S^2\) as
\(T \to \infty\), by the Glivenko-Cantelli theorem (Glivenko 1933;
Cantelli 1933) applied to the i.i.d.~uniform-on-\(S^2\) angular
increments, or equivalently by Kolmogorov's strong law of large numbers
(Kolmogorov 1933, \emph{Grundbegriffe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung})
applied to the indicator functions of any measurable subset of \(S^2\).
The equidistribution result invoked here is \emph{strictly weaker than
Birkhoff's pointwise ergodic theorem}: it requires only independence and
identical distribution of the angular increments (supplied by the
Geometric Channel spatial-projection isotropy of Theorem 5 of {[}24{]},
itself a direct geometric content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\)), and does not
require metric transitivity of the underlying Hamiltonian flow. By the
dominated convergence theorem applied to a continuous bounded \(F\) and
the convergent empirical angular distribution,

\[\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_{t_0}^{t_0+T}F(\gamma(s))\,ds = \int_{S^2} F\!\left(p_0 + R(t)\hat{\mathbf{n}}\right)\frac{d^2\Omega(\hat{\mathbf{n}})}{4\pi},\]

where the right-hand side is the angular average of \(F\) over the
McGucken Sphere at time \(t\) (in the saturated asymptotic regime).

\emph{(c) Identification with the geometric ensemble-average.} The
integral on the right of (b) is, by the unique SO(3)-invariant
normalized measure \(d\sigma\) on \(W(t) \cong S^2\) (Theorem 5 of
{[}24{]} The Algebraic Channel), exactly \(\int_{W(t)} F\,d\sigma\).
Therefore the time-average along \(\gamma\) equals the geometric
ensemble-average over the wavefront cross-section.

The identity is independent of the standard Birkhoff hypotheses (metric
transitivity of the Hamiltonian flow, ergodicity of the orbit on the
constant-energy hypersurface): the equidistribution-on-\(S^2\) result of
(b) follows from the Geometric Channel spatial-projection isotropy
alone, which is a geometric content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) and does not
depend on the orbital structure of the underlying dynamical system.
\(\Box\)

The time-average along the trajectory equals the ensemble-average over
the wavefront \emph{because the trajectory is the wavefront, viewed as a
propagating geometric object}. The identity holds for any continuous
observable \(F\) and is independent of the standard Birkhoff hypotheses
(metric transitivity, almost-everywhere convergence): it is an identity
of the geometric-propagation content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\).

\textbf{Step 6 (Independence of KAM-tori obstruction).} KAM theory
{[}246{]} establishes that generic Hamiltonian perturbations of
integrable systems preserve a positive-measure set of invariant tori on
which the trajectory is restricted to a sub-dimensional subset of phase
space. The standard ergodic hypothesis fails on these positive-measure
sets. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the Huygens-wavefront
identity is \emph{unaffected} by the KAM-tori obstruction: the wavefront
cross-section is the ensemble of geometric realizations at each instant,
not the long-time orbit of the trajectory. The KAM-tori restriction
operates on the orbit; the McGucken-framework ergodicity operates on the
wavefront. The two are different geometric structures, and the
McGucken-framework identity holds even where the KAM-tori obstruction
breaks the standard ergodic hypothesis {[}194{]}.

This closes Einstein's second gap T2: ergodicity is no longer an
unproven hypothesis (false in the standard formulation on
positive-measure sets) but a geometric identity of the Huygens-wavefront
content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\), independent of metric transitivity and
unaffected by KAM-tori obstruction. \(\Box\)

\hypertarget{photon-entropy-on-the-mcgucken-sphere-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-10-of-24}{%
\paragraph{6.2.4 Photon entropy on the McGucken Sphere (thermodynamics
paper {[}24{]}, Theorem 10 of
{[}24{]})}\label{photon-entropy-on-the-mcgucken-sphere-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-10-of-24}}

\textbf{Theorem (Photon Entropy on the McGucken Sphere).} For an
ensemble of photons emitted at spacetime event \(p_0\) and propagating
on the McGucken Sphere of radius \(R(t) = c(t-t_0)\), the Shannon
entropy is

\[S(t) = \kB \ln\!\left(4\pi(c(t-t_0))^2\right)\]

with strict positive rate

\[\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{2\kB}{t - t_0} > 0 \quad\text{for all } t > t_0.\]

The sphere grows because \(x_4\) advances at rate \(c\); the entropy
grows because the sphere grows.

\hypertarget{proof-via-parallel-channels-theorem-10-of-24}{%
\subsubsection{Proof via Parallel Channels (Theorem 10 of
{[}24{]})}\label{proof-via-parallel-channels-theorem-10-of-24}}

Photon entropy on the McGucken Sphere is doubly forced by
\(dx_4/dt = ic\): the Algebraic Channel delivers it via the unique
SO(3)-invariant probability measure on \(S^2\) combined with Shannon's
entropy formula; the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Geometric Channel delivers it via
the direct geometric area-growth of the McGucken Sphere.

\hypertarget{the-algebraic-channel-proof-algebraic-symmetry-derivation}{%
\paragraph{The Algebraic Channel Proof (Algebraic-Symmetry
Derivation)}\label{the-algebraic-channel-proof-algebraic-symmetry-derivation}}

\emph{Proof.} \textbf{Step A1 (Algebraic-symmetry photon ensemble).} An
ensemble of photons emitted isotropically from event \(p_0\) propagates
on a two-sphere of radius \(R(t) = c(t-t_0)\), with the photon
distribution invariant under the SO(3) subgroup of the
algebraic-symmetry content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) (Theorem 2 of {[}24{]}).
By Haar's 1933 uniqueness theorem applied to SO(3) acting transitively
on \(S^2\) (cf.~Theorem 5 of {[}24{]} the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Algebraic
Channel), the unique normalized SO(3)-invariant probability measure on
the photon-direction sphere is the uniform measure with density
\(1/(4\pi)\).

\textbf{Step A2 (Number of accessible spherical states).} Translated to
the radial geometry, the photon ensemble occupies a 2-sphere of total
area \(A(t) = 4\pi c^2 (t-t_0)^2\). Under the SO(3)-invariant uniform
measure, the differential entropy of the photon-direction distribution
on this 2-sphere is \(\ln(A(t)/A_0)\) for any reference area \(A_0\), by
the standard relation between differential entropy and effective volume.
The reference \(A_0\) is conventional: it sets the additive zero of the
entropy and does not affect the time-derivative \(dS/dt\). The choice
\(A_0 = 1\) in geometric units absorbs the convention into the additive
entropy constant.

\textbf{Step A3 (Shannon entropy).} The Shannon entropy of the
SO(3)-invariant uniform distribution on a region of measure \(A(t)\) is

\[S(t) = \kB \ln A(t) = \kB\ln(4\pi c^2 (t-t_0)^2).\]

Equivalently, \(S(t) = \kB[\ln(4\pi) + 2\ln(c(t-t_0))]\).

\textbf{Step A4 (Strict monotonicity).}

\[\boxed{\ \frac{dS}{dt} = \kB\cdot\frac{1}{A(t)}\cdot\frac{dA}{dt} = \kB\cdot\frac{1}{4\pi c^2(t-t_0)^2}\cdot 8\pi c^2 (t-t_0) = \frac{2\kB}{t-t_0} > 0.\ }\]

The factor 2 arises from the surface-area scaling
\(A(t)\sim (t-t_0)^2\).

\textbf{Step A5 (Convergence with the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Geometric
Channel).} Algebraic Channel delivers the photon entropy via the
Haar-uniqueness of the SO(3)-invariant measure combined with Shannon's
formula. The Geometric Channel delivers the same result via the direct
geometric area-growth of the McGucken Sphere. \(\Box\)

\hypertarget{the-geometric-channel-proof-geometric-propagation-derivation}{%
\paragraph{The Geometric Channel Proof (Geometric-Propagation
Derivation)}\label{the-geometric-channel-proof-geometric-propagation-derivation}}

\emph{Proof.} \textbf{Step B1 (Geometric setup).} From Theorem 3 of
{[}24{]}, the McGucken Sphere from spacetime event \(p_0\) has radius
\(R(t) = c(t-t_0)\) and surface area
\(A(t) = 4\pi R^2(t) = 4\pi c^2 (t-t_0)^2\). The Sphere grows
monotonically because \(x_4\) advances at \(+ic\).

\textbf{Step B2 (Photon ensemble on the wavefront).} Consider an
ensemble of photons emitted at \(p_0\). By the spherical-symmetry
content of the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Geometric Channel's wavefront expansion
(Theorem 3 of {[}24{]}), the photons spread uniformly over the surface
of the McGucken Sphere as it expands. The probability density on the
Sphere is the uniform geometric measure with density \(1/A(t)\).

\textbf{Step B3 (Direct geometric Shannon entropy).} The Shannon entropy
of the uniform distribution on a region of geometric area \(A(t)\) is

\[S(t) = -\kB \int_{\mathcal{S}_R} \frac{1}{A(t)} \ln\!\frac{1}{A(t)}\, dA = \kB\ln A(t) = \kB\ln(4\pi c^2 (t-t_0)^2).\]

\textbf{Step B4 (Strict monotonicity from McGucken Sphere area growth).}

\[\frac{dS}{dt} = \kB\,\frac{d\ln A(t)}{dt} = \kB\,\frac{A'(t)}{A(t)} = \kB\cdot\frac{8\pi c^2 (t-t_0)}{4\pi c^2 (t-t_0)^2} = \frac{2\kB}{t-t_0} > 0.\]

The strict positivity follows directly from the McGucken Sphere's
monotonic area growth, which follows from the Sphere's monotonic radial
growth, which follows from \(x_4\)'s advance at \(+ic\) (not \(-ic\)).

\textbf{Step B5 (Radiative arrow from Sphere monotonicity).} The
radiative arrow of time (radiation propagates outward, not inward) is
the direct geometric content: \(x_4\) advances at \(+ic\), the McGucken
Sphere expands monotonically, and the photon ensemble's Shannon entropy
increases monotonically with the Sphere's area.

\textbf{Step B6 (Convergence with the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Algebraic
Channel).} Geometric Channel delivers the photon entropy as the direct
area-content of the McGucken Sphere. The Algebraic Channel delivered the
same result as the Shannon entropy of the Haar-unique SO(3)-invariant
measure. The two derivations agree on
\(S(t) = \kB\ln(4\pi c^2 (t-t_0)^2)\) and \(dS/dt = 2\kB/(t-t_0)\).
\(\Box\)

\hypertarget{the-onsager-reciprocal-relations-as-a-theorem-of-the-mcgucken-principle-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-14a-of-24}{%
\paragraph{6.2.5 The Onsager reciprocal relations as a theorem of the
McGucken Principle (thermodynamics paper {[}24{]}, Theorem 14a of
{[}24{]})}\label{the-onsager-reciprocal-relations-as-a-theorem-of-the-mcgucken-principle-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-14a-of-24}}

Onsager Reciprocal Relations as a Theorem of the McGucken Principle

We now establish that the Onsager Reciprocal Relations -- celebrated by
the 1968 Nobel Prize committee as ``a further law making a thermodynamic
study of irreversible processes possible'' and described by some authors
as the ``Fourth Law of Thermodynamics'' {[}171{]} -- descend as a formal
theorem from \(dx_4/dt = ic\). Onsager's 1931 result {[}169{]}
establishes that for a thermodynamic system slightly out of equilibrium,
the linear phenomenological matrix \(L_{ij}\) relating the fluxes
\(\dot x_i\) to the conjugate thermodynamic forces \(X_j\) is
\emph{symmetric}: \(L_{ij} = L_{ji}\). This symmetry has been verified
experimentally across thermoelectricity (Peltier-Seebeck),
electrokinetics, transference in electrolytes, diffusion, heat
conduction in anisotropic solids, thermomagnetism, galvanomagnetism, and
Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation {[}170{]}; the symmetry is one of
the empirically best-confirmed relations of non-equilibrium
thermodynamics.

The orthodox derivation of Onsager reciprocity rests on three
ingredients: (i) microscopic time-reversibility of the underlying
dynamics; (ii) Boltzmann's entropy formula relating fluctuation
probability to entropy; (iii) linear-response detailed balance at
equilibrium. We now demonstrate that each of these three ingredients
descends as a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) within the McGucken framework,
with a novel additional contribution: \emph{the Onsager matrix symmetry
\(L_{ij} = L_{ji}\) is supplied by the same SO(3)-Haar measure on the
McGucken Sphere that supplies the Born rule of Theorem 7 of {[}24{]}}.
The Onsager Reciprocal Relations and the Born Rule are therefore
\emph{two consequences of the same SO(3)-rotational-symmetry of the
iterated McGucken Sphere expansion}.

\textbf{Theorem 14a of {[}24{]} (Onsager Reciprocal Relations from the
McGucken Principle).} Under the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\), the
linear phenomenological matrix \(L_{ij}\) relating fluxes \(\dot x_i\)
to conjugate thermodynamic forces \(X_j\) in a thermodynamic system
slightly out of equilibrium satisfies the Onsager Reciprocal Relations

\[L_{ij} = L_{ji} \tag{14a.1}\]

as a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\), with the three ingredients of
Onsager's 1931 derivation each descending from the McGucken framework as
follows:

\emph{(M1) Microscopic time-reversibility \textless- the
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) Algebraic Channel Schr?dinger unitarity.} The
microscopic time-reversibility Onsager invokes is precisely the
Algebraic Channel algebraic-symmetry content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) as
exhibited in Theorems 19.1, 19.3, 19.5, and 22 of {[}24{]}. The
Schr?dinger equation \(i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi\) is unitary,
time-reversible, and operator-algebraically time-symmetric (Theorem 22
of {[}24{]}); the canonical commutation relation
\([\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar\) has no preferred time direction; the
Stone-theorem unitary group generated by \(\hat H\) is reversible. The
\(+ic\) orientation of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) lives in the Geometric Channel
(Theorems 6, 9, 23a, 25, 26) and supplies the \emph{macroscopic} arrow
of time as a strict-Second-Law monotonicity, but the \emph{microscopic}
Schr?dinger dynamics is the Algebraic Channel and is fully
time-reversible. Onsager's microscopic-reversibility assumption is
therefore \emph{not in tension with} the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic
framework's \(+ic\) orientation -- it is the Algebraic Channel face of
the same principle, exhibited at the microscopic operator-algebraic
level.

\emph{(M2) Boltzmann's entropy formula \textless- Maxwell-Boltzmann
equilibrium fixed point of Theorem 14 of {[}24{]}.} The fluctuation
distribution \(P \propto \exp(\Delta S/k_B)\) near equilibrium is the
Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution derived in Theorem 14 of {[}24{]} as the
equilibrium distribution under iterated McGucken Sphere expansion at the
Compton-coupling rate \(\gamma\). The quadratic expansion of
\(\Delta S\) around the equilibrium,
\(\Delta S = -\frac{1}{2}\beta_{ij}\,x_i x_j\) with \(\beta_{ij}\) a
positive-definite symmetric matrix, follows from the Gaussian-quadratic
form of the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution near its maximum (Theorem 14
of {[}24{]}, Step 4). The Boltzmann entropy formula is therefore a
theorem of {[}24{]}'s Theorem 14 of {[}24{]}.

\emph{(M3) Detailed balance at equilibrium \textless- equilibrium fixed
point of Compton-Brownian dynamics.} Detailed balance -- the equality of
forward and reverse fluxes for every microscopic process at equilibrium
-- is the condition under which the Compton-coupled Brownian dynamics of
Theorems 4-9 of {[}24{]} reach equilibrium at the Maxwell-Boltzmann
fixed point of Theorem 14 of {[}24{]}. Each individual microscopic event
still has a \(+ic\) orientation (each inter-molecular collision is still
a Wick rotation by Theorem 26 of {[}24{]}); the macroscopic statistical
aggregation produces equal forward and reverse fluxes when the
distribution is at the Maxwell-Boltzmann fixed point. \emph{Boltzmann's
Stosszahlansatz, as diagnosed in Corollary 26.1 of {[}24{]}, is the
implicit recognition that detailed balance at equilibrium follows from
the Geometric Channel Wick rotations at every inter-molecular collision
relaxing each pre-collision molecule to the Maxwell-Boltzmann form.}
Detailed balance is therefore the equilibrium content of Theorems 6-9
and 26 of {[}24{]}.

\emph{(M4) Onsager matrix symmetry \textless- SO(3)-Haar measure on the
McGucken Sphere.} The distinctive McGucken contribution: the Onsager
matrix \(L_{ij}\) is expressible through the equilibrium correlation
function
\(L_{ij} = \int_0^\infty \langle \dot x_i(0)\,\dot x_j(t) \rangle\,dt\)
(the Green-Kubo formula). The equilibrium correlation function
\(\langle \dot x_i(0)\,\dot x_j(t) \rangle\) is computed via the
Wiener-process limit of iterated McGucken Sphere expansion (Proposition
L.2 of {[}24{]}). The SO(3)-Haar measure on each McGucken Sphere, which
supplies the Born rule of Theorem 7 of {[}24{]} via the spherical
reachability measure on iterated \(x_4\)-expansion, also supplies the
symmetry of the equilibrium correlation function under the exchange
\(i \leftrightarrow j\): the Haar measure is invariant under the
involution that swaps the two arguments, because the spherical
reachability measure on iterated \(x_4\)-expansion is symmetric under
the time-reversal involution that microscopically exchanges initial and
final endpoints on each McGucken Sphere. The Onsager matrix symmetry
\(L_{ij} = L_{ji}\) is therefore the \emph{same SO(3)-Haar-measure
symmetry that supplies the Born rule}: both are consequences of the
rotational invariance of the iterated McGucken Sphere expansion under
SO(3).

\emph{Proof.} The proof proceeds in five steps: (P1) state the
McGucken-framework setting; (P2) derive the linear phenomenological
relations from the McGucken Sphere Wiener-process limit; (P3) compute
the Onsager matrix via the Green-Kubo formula; (P4) establish the
symmetry via the SO(3)-Haar invariance; (P5) state the closure.

\emph{Step P1 (Setting).} Consider a thermodynamic system in
\(\mathbb{R}^3\) described by extensive variables \(x_i\),
\(i = 1, \ldots, n\) (e.g., energy density, mass density, charge
density). The equilibrium state is the Maxwell-Boltzmann fixed point of
Theorem 14 of {[}24{]}. Near equilibrium, the entropy admits the
quadratic expansion \(S = S_0 - \frac{1}{2}\beta_{ij}\,x_i x_j\) with
\(\beta_{ij}\) a positive-definite symmetric matrix (M2 above). The
thermodynamic forces conjugate to \(x_i\) are
\(X_i = -\partial S/\partial x_i = \beta_{ij}\,x_j\). The microscopic
dynamics is governed by the Schr?dinger equation (the Algebraic Channel
of \(dx_4/dt = ic\), M1 above) and is time-reversible at the microscopic
level.

\emph{Step P2 (Linear phenomenological relations).} For small deviations
from equilibrium, the Compton-coupled Brownian dynamics of Theorem 6 of
{[}24{]} produces, in the Wiener-process limit of Proposition L.2, a
linear-response flux \(\dot x_i\) that depends linearly on the
thermodynamic forces \(X_j\). The general form is

\[\dot x_i = \sum_j L_{ij}\,X_j \tag{14a.2}\]

with \(L_{ij}\) a phenomenological coefficient matrix to be determined.
Equation (14a.2) is the \emph{linear response form} of the McGucken
Sphere Wiener-process dynamics restricted to the slow macroscopic
variables, with the matrix \(L_{ij}\) encoding the response of each flux
to each thermodynamic force.

\emph{Step P3 (Green-Kubo formula for the Onsager matrix).} The standard
derivation of the Green-Kubo formula {[}173, 174{]} proceeds by
computing the time-integrated equilibrium correlation function of the
fluxes:

\[L_{ij} = \int_0^\infty \langle \dot x_i(0)\,\dot x_j(t) \rangle_{\rm eq}\,dt \tag{14a.3}\]

where the expectation is taken with respect to the equilibrium
fluctuation distribution (M2 above; Maxwell-Boltzmann fixed point of
Theorem 14 of {[}24{]}). Under the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the
equilibrium correlation function
\(\langle \dot x_i(0)\,\dot x_j(t) \rangle_{\rm eq}\) is computed via
the Wiener-process limit of iterated McGucken Sphere expansion
(Proposition L.2), with the Compton-coupling rate \(\gamma\) of Theorem
4 of {[}24{]} supplying the friction coefficient and the McGucken Sphere
reachability measure of Theorem 5 of {[}24{]} (the SO(3)-Haar measure on
each spherical wavefront) supplying the diffusion coefficient. Equation
(14a.3) is therefore a Green-Kubo computation entirely within the
McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework.

\emph{Step P4 (Symmetry from SO(3)-Haar invariance and microscopic
time-reversibility).} The Onsager symmetry \(L_{ij} = L_{ji}\) follows
from the equilibrium correlation function being invariant under the
exchange \(i \leftrightarrow j\), which in turn follows from two facts:

\emph{(P4a) Microscopic time-reversibility under the Algebraic Channel
Schr?dinger dynamics (M1 above)} implies that the equilibrium
correlation function
\(\langle \dot x_i(0)\,\dot x_j(t) \rangle_{\rm eq}\) satisfies

\[\langle \dot x_i(0)\,\dot x_j(t) \rangle_{\rm eq} = \langle \dot x_i(t)\,\dot x_j(0) \rangle_{\rm eq} = \langle \dot x_j(0)\,\dot x_i(t) \rangle_{\rm eq} \tag{14a.4}\]

-- the first equality by stationarity of the equilibrium state, the
second by microscopic time-reversibility (which exchanges initial and
final endpoints on each McGucken Sphere worldline, with the SO(3)-Haar
measure on each Sphere invariant under this exchange). Equation (14a.4)
is the content of Onsager's regression hypothesis.

\emph{(P4b) Integrating (14a.4) over \(t \in [0, \infty)\)} yields
\(L_{ij} = L_{ji}\). The exchange \(i \leftrightarrow j\) commutes with
the time-integration in (14a.3) because (14a.4) holds for all
\(t \geq 0\).

\emph{(P4c) The deeper identification.} The SO(3)-Haar measure on the
McGucken Sphere that supplies the equilibrium correlation function's
\(i \leftrightarrow j\) symmetry is \emph{the same SO(3)-Haar measure
that supplies the Born rule of Theorem 7 of {[}24{]}}. The Born rule is
the operational signature of this measure on a single McGucken Sphere at
a single measurement event; the Onsager symmetry is the operational
signature of the same measure on the iterated McGucken Sphere expansion
in the Green-Kubo time-integrated equilibrium correlation function.
\emph{Onsager reciprocity and the Born rule are two consequences of the
same SO(3)-Haar measure on the McGucken Sphere}, exhibited at different
scales (single Sphere for Born, iterated Sphere for Onsager) and in
different operational regimes (measurement event for Born, equilibrium
fluctuation for Onsager).

\emph{Step P5 (Closure).} Combining P1-P4: the linear phenomenological
relations (14a.2) hold near equilibrium with the matrix \(L_{ij}\) given
by the Green-Kubo formula (14a.3), and the symmetry \(L_{ij} = L_{ji}\)
follows from the microscopic time-reversibility of the Algebraic Channel
Schr?dinger dynamics combined with the SO(3)-Haar invariance of the
McGucken Sphere reachability measure. The Onsager Reciprocal Relations
are therefore a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\). \(\Box\)

\emph{Corollary 14a.1 of {[}24{]} (Onsager-Casimir and the McGucken-Wick
rotation).} Onsager 1931 himself noted that the reciprocal relations
break down in the presence of magnetic fields or Coriolis forces;
Casimir 1945 {[}172{]} established the refined relation
\(L_{ij}(\vec{B}, \vec{\Omega}) = L_{ji}(-\vec{B}, -\vec{\Omega})\) for
systems with magnetic or rotational time-reversal breaking. Under the
McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, this breakdown is diagnosable: magnetic
fields and Coriolis forces couple to the four-velocity through
pseudo-tensor combinations \(F_{\mu\nu}\) and
\(\vec{v} \times \vec{\Omega}\) that transform with odd parity under the
time-reversal involution that Step P4a relies on. Specifically, under
the McGucken-Wick rotation \(\tau = x_4/c\), the electromagnetic field
tensor \(F_{\mu\nu}\) has components \(F_{0i} = E_i\) (electric field)
that are time-even and \(F_{ij} = \epsilon_{ijk}B^k\) (magnetic field)
that are time-odd. When the McGucken-Wick rotation is applied to the
equilibrium correlation function in the presence of an external magnetic
field \(\vec{B}\), the resulting the Geometric Channel Euclidean reading
flips the sign of \(\vec{B}\) relative to the Lorentzian the Algebraic
Channel reading. The symmetry (14a.4) is therefore replaced by

\[\langle \dot x_i(0)\,\dot x_j(t) \rangle_{\rm eq}^{(\vec{B})} = \langle \dot x_j(0)\,\dot x_i(t) \rangle_{\rm eq}^{(-\vec{B})} \tag{14a.5}\]

-- the Onsager-Casimir relation as a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) via the
McGucken-Wick-rotation transformation properties of \(F_{\mu\nu}\) on
the McGucken manifold.

\emph{Proof.} Follows from the transformation of \(F_{\mu\nu}\) under
\(\tau = x_4/c\) combined with the proof of Theorem 14a of {[}24{]}
above. \(\Box\)

\hypertarget{the-refined-generalized-second-law-as-global-xux2084-flux-conservation-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-17-of-24}{%
\paragraph{6.2.6 The Refined Generalized Second Law as global x₄-flux
conservation (thermodynamics paper {[}24{]}, Theorem 17 of
{[}24{]})}\label{the-refined-generalized-second-law-as-global-xux2084-flux-conservation-thermodynamics-paper-24-theorem-17-of-24}}

\textbf{Theorem (Refined Generalized Second Law).} The Generalized
Second Law (GSL), which asserts that the total entropy of matter outside
a black hole plus the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the black hole's
horizon never decreases,

\[\frac{d}{dt}(S_{\mathrm{outside}} + S_{\mathrm{BH}}) \ge 0,\]

is refined on the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework to a conservation
statement about global \(x_4\)-flux through closed hypersurfaces. The
McGucken-refined GSL takes the form

\[\boxed{\Phi_{x_4}[\Sigma_2] - \Phi_{x_4}[\Sigma_1] \ge 0 \quad\text{for}\quad \Sigma_2 \text{ to the future of } \Sigma_1,}\]

where \(\Phi_{x_4}[\Sigma]\) is the total \(x_4\)-flux through the
closed hypersurface \(\Sigma\). This refines and generalizes Proposition
VI.1 of {[}33{]} (the GSL as the global McGucken Second Law applied to a
spacetime partitioned into an external region and a horizon-bounded
interior): the McGucken second law \(dS_{\rm total}/dt \ge 0\) holds for
the entropy summed over the entire spacetime regardless of how the
spacetime is partitioned, and the partition by the horizon gives the
standard GSL \(dS_{\rm outside} + dS_{\rm BH} \ge 0\) as a corollary.
The \(x_4\)-flux formulation makes the partition-independence manifest.
The quantum-radiation refinement of the GSL -- the case where the
horizon is shrinking due to Hawking radiation and the exterior entropy
is correspondingly growing -- is established in {[}Proposition VII.1{]}:
under Hawking radiation, \(S_{\rm ext}\) includes the entropy of
Hawking-emitted thermal radiation, \(S_{\rm BH}\) tracks the horizon
area via \(S_{\rm BH} = \kB A/(4\ell_P^2)\), and the McGucken second law
still requires \(dS_{\rm ext}/dt + dS_{\rm BH}/dt \ge 0\) at every
instant, because \(x_4\)'s expansion continues monotonically regardless
of evaporation; the entropy exchange balances out by the global
monotonicity of the McGucken second law, not by coincidence.

\hypertarget{proof-via-parallel-channels-theorem-17-of-24}{%
\subsubsection{Proof via Parallel Channels (Theorem 17 of
{[}24{]})}\label{proof-via-parallel-channels-theorem-17-of-24}}

The Refined Generalized Second Law
\(\Phi_{x_4}[\Sigma_2] - \Phi_{x_4}[\Sigma_1] \ge 0\) is doubly forced
by \(dx_4/dt = ic\), and it is the rare theorem of physics in which the
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel contribute
\emph{complementary} content rather than parallel content: the Algebraic
Channel delivers the conservation form of the law (the \(x_4\)-flux as a
Noether-like conserved current); the Geometric Channel delivers the
monotonicity sign (the \(\ge\) rather than \(=\), from the \(+ic\)
orientation of the McGucken Sphere expansion). The combination of
conservation + monotonic-sign is what makes the GSL a Second Law rather
than a First Law.

\hypertarget{the-algebraic-channel-proof-algebraic-symmetry-derivation-the-conservation-form}{%
\paragraph{The Algebraic Channel Proof (Algebraic-Symmetry Derivation:
The Conservation
Form)}\label{the-algebraic-channel-proof-algebraic-symmetry-derivation-the-conservation-form}}

\emph{Proof.} \textbf{Step A1 (Standard GSL).} The Generalized Second
Law, formulated by Bekenstein and Hawking and refined by Wall, Bousso,
and others {[}102, 103, 121, 120{]}, asserts: for any closed system
containing matter and black holes,

\[\frac{d}{dt}\left(S_{\mathrm{matter}} + \sum_i \frac{\kB A_i}{4\lP^2}\right) \ge 0.\]

\textbf{Step A2 (Definition of the \(x_4\)-flux current).} By the
moving-dimension-manifold structure of McGucken Geometry {[}5,
Defs.~5.1-5.4{]}, the McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is implemented
on \((M, F, V)\) via the future-directed timelike unit vector field
\(V\) with \(V_\mu V^\mu = -c^2\), satisfying the four
privileged-element conditions (P1)-(P4) of {[}Def.~5.4{]}, and equipped
with the active translation generator \(P_4\) in the equivalent
Cartan-geometric formulation {[}Def.~7.3{]}. The McGucken-Invariance
Lemma {[}Theorem 8.1 of {[}24{]}{]} establishes that
\(\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0\) globally on \(M\),
equivalently \(\Omega_T^4 = 0\) in Cartan-curvature form; this is the
content underwriting the construction of \(j^\mu_{x_4}\) as a
well-defined Noether-like current. The \(x_4\)-flux current is defined
as the local active-expansion density of \(x_4\):

\[j^\mu_{x_4}(p) := \rho_{x_4}(p)\, V^\mu(p),\]

where \(\rho_{x_4}(p)\) is the local density of \(x_4\)-modes (defined
as the number of independent McGucken-Sphere apex events per unit
four-volume), and \(V^\mu\) is the active-flow vector field of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) at \(p\).

\textbf{Step A3 (Conservation form via Noether 1918 plus Stokes;
Reflection positivity from \(x_4 \to -x_4\)).} By Noether's 1918 theorem
{[}86{]} applied to the temporal-uniformity content of \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
(Theorem 2 of {[}24{]} item (a) -- the rate \(ic\) is independent of
\(t\)), the corresponding Noether current \(j^\mu_{x_4}\) satisfies the
covariant conservation law

\[\nabla_\mu j^\mu_{x_4} = 0\]

\emph{at points where no McGucken-Sphere apex is added or removed}. (The
covariant divergence vanishes everywhere except at the source points of
new McGucken Spheres, where new \(x_4\)-modes enter the four-manifold
from the active-expansion process.) Applying the covariant Stokes
theorem to the closed three-surface \(\Sigma = \partial V\) bounding a
four-volume \(V\):

\[\Phi_{x_4}[\partial V] := \oint_{\partial V} j^\mu_{x_4}\, d\Sigma_\mu \;=\; \int_V \nabla_\mu j^\mu_{x_4}\, dV \;=\; \int_V \rho_{\rm source}\, dV,\]

where \(\rho_{\rm source}\) is the density of new McGucken-Sphere apex
events in \(V\). This is the conservation form of the Refined GSL: the
integrated \(x_4\)-flux through a closed three-surface equals the
integrated source content of the enclosed four-volume. The reading:
Theorem 19 of {[}19{]} (\emph{Reflection positivity from
\(x_4 \to -x_4\) symmetry}) establishes that the Euclidean action
\(S_E\) depends on \((\partial\phi/\partial x_4)^2\) rather than on the

\(x_4 \to -x_4\); equivalently, the conservation-form content of the

the asymmetry that makes it a Second-Law sign \(\ge 0\) comes from the

\hypertarget{the-algebraic-channel-proof-algebraic-symmetry-derivation-the-friedmann-constraint-route}{%
\paragraph{The Algebraic Channel Proof (Algebraic-Symmetry Derivation:
The Friedmann Constraint
Route)}\label{the-algebraic-channel-proof-algebraic-symmetry-derivation-the-friedmann-constraint-route}}

\emph{Proof.} \textbf{Step A1 (FRW from Hilbert variational principle).}
The \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Algebraic Channel derivation of the FRW metric,
established as Theorem 23 of {[}17{]}, proceeds via Hilbert's
variational principle: \(\delta S_{\mathrm{EH}}/\delta g^{\mu\nu} = 0\)
applied to the Einstein-Hilbert action with the conditions of FRW
cosmology (spatial homogeneity and isotropy at the cosmological scale,
cosmological-time foliation by the CMB rest frame as specified by
condition (P4) of {[}Def.~5.4{]}). The resulting variational equations
give the Friedmann constraints:

\[H^2 = \left(\frac{\dot a}{a}\right)^2 = \frac{8\pi G}{3}\rho - \frac{k c^2}{a^2}, \qquad \frac{\ddot a}{a} = -\frac{4\pi G}{3}\left(\rho + \frac{3p}{c^2}\right).\]

These are the Algebraic Channel algebraic-symmetry content of the
cosmological field equations, derived as theorems of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) in
the McGucken corpus.

\textbf{Step A2 (Cosmological entropy from the Algebraic Channel scaling
laws).} The Algebraic Channel scaling laws of FRW
cosmology--photon-number density \(n_\gamma \propto a^{-3}\),
matter-number density \(n_m \propto a^{-3}\), photon entropy density
\(s_\gamma \propto a^{-3}\)--combine with the comoving-volume content to
give:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Comoving photon entropy:
  \(S_{\gamma,\mathrm{comoving}} = s_\gamma \cdot a^3 V_{\mathrm{comoving}} = \text{const}\).
\item
  Photon entropy within the cosmological horizon:
  \(S_\gamma(t) = s_\gamma(t) \cdot V_{\mathrm{horizon}}(t)\). Since
  \(V_{\mathrm{horizon}}(t) \propto R_4^3(t) \propto t^3\) and
  \(s_\gamma \propto a^{-3}\) with \(a(t)\) evolving, the within-horizon
  photon entropy increases as the horizon volume grows monotonically.
\item
  Matter Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy: governed by Theorem 9 of {[}24{]}'s
  Algebraic Channel derivation, with \(dS/dt = (3/2)\kB/t > 0\) for each
  matter component.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Step A3 (de Sitter horizon entropy from Theorems 15-16 of
{[}24{]}).} In a de Sitter phase with Hubble parameter \(H\) constant,
the de Sitter horizon at proper distance \(R_{\mathrm{dS}} = c/H\) has
entropy derived through the derivation of Theorems 15 and 16 of {[}24{]}
applied to the de Sitter Killing-time generator, with the Euclidean
cigar period \(\beta_{\rm dS} = 2\pi/H\) replacing the Schwarzschild
\(\beta = 2\pi/\kappa\) but with identical Gibbons-Hawking-York
boundary-action evaluation ({[}Proposition V.1{]} adapted to the de
Sitter geometry):

\[S_{\mathrm{dS}} = \frac{\kB A_{\mathrm{dS}}}{4\lP^2} = \frac{\pi\kB c^2}{H^2 \lP^2}.\]

This is the Gibbons-Hawking de Sitter entropy {[}106{]}, derived from
the Algebraic Channel as a corollary of {[}24{]}'s Theorems 15-16.

\textbf{Step A4 (Reconstitution signature
\(\rho(t_{\rm rec}) \approx 2.6\) from the Algebraic Channel integrated
history).} The McGucken cosmological horizon is defined as the proper
radius \(R_4(t)\) of the cosmological McGucken Sphere centered at the
cosmological initial event \(p_0\), with \(R_4(t) = ct\) in the early
universe and asymptoting to \(c/H_\infty\) in late de Sitter epochs
({[}5{]}). The Hubble horizon is defined as the proper radius
\(R_H(t) = c/H(t)\). The distinguishing dimensionless ratio is

\[\rho(t) \;\equiv\; \frac{R_4(t)\cdot H(t)}{c}.\]

In the asymptotic de Sitter regime, \(R_4 \to c/H_\infty\) and
\(\rho \to 1\). In the radiation-dominated and matter-dominated eras,
\(\rho(t)\) differs from \(1\) measurably. Computing \(\rho\) at
recombination (\(z \approx 1100\)) via the McGucken-Sphere integrated
expansion combined with the Friedmann-equation integration through the
matter-dominated and \(\Lambda\)-dominated phases yields ({[}Divergence
10, IX.5{]})

\[\rho(t_{\rm rec}) \;\approx\; 2.6.\]

The McGucken-Sphere horizon entropy
\(S_{\rm McG} = \kB A_4/(4\lP^2) = \kB \pi R_4^2/(\lP^2)\) and the
Hubble-horizon entropy
\(S_{\rm Hub} = \kB A_H/(4\lP^2) = \kB \pi (c/H)^2/(\lP^2)\) stand in
the entropy ratio

\[\frac{S_{\rm McG}(t_{\rm rec})}{S_{\rm Hub}(t_{\rm rec})} \;=\; \rho^2(t_{\rm rec}) \;\approx\; 7.\]

This is the entropy-ratio empirical signature: McGucken cosmological
holography predicts an entropy reservoir on the McGucken horizon that is
approximately seven times larger than the Hubble-horizon reservoir at
recombination, with empirical consequences in the CMB power spectrum,
the Silk damping scale, and the BAO acoustic scale. The signature is
sharp, computable, and quantitative.

\textbf{Step A5 (H\(_0\) tension as the Algebraic Channel prediction,
not anomaly).} The 5\(\sigma\) Hubble tension between Planck 2018
(H\(_0 = 67.4 \pm 0.5\) km/s/Mpc inferred from CMB-anchored

recombination (larger \(\psi\)). The predicted ratio

\[\psi(t_{\rm rec})/\psi(t_0) \;\approx\; 1.083\]

matches the observed 8.3\% Planck-versus-SH0ES gap with zero free

\textbf{Step A6 (Dark-energy equation of state \(w_0 \approx -0.983\)
from cumulative spatial contraction).} The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic

\[w(z) \;=\; -1 + \frac{\Omega_m(z)}{6\pi},\]

derivable from the spatial-contraction stress-energy with no free

\(w = -1\) exactly and cannot accommodate the DESI 2024 departure
without adding fitted \(w\)-parameters; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic
framework predicted the departure from first principles before DESI
2024.

\textbf{Step A7 (Convergence with the \(dx_4/dt = ic\) Geometric
Channel).} Algebraic Channel delivers the FRW thermodynamic structure
via the Friedmann constraint, photon-number scaling laws,
Gibbons-Hawking-York Euclidean-action horizon entropy, and the
cumulative-spatial-contraction empirical signature. The Geometric
Channel will deliver the same structure via the direct geometric

channels converge on the same monotonic entropy increase, the same de
