\end{itemize}

\hypertarget{the-identity-gravity-is-the-born-rule-the-shared-count-proof}{%
\subsection{7. The identity: ``gravity is the Born rule'' --- the
shared-count
proof}\label{the-identity-gravity-is-the-born-rule-the-shared-count-proof}}

\textbf{In this section we demonstrate that, because gravity and the
Born rule are both theorem chains descending from the common,
foundational, physical principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) (§3 and §5) --- in the
spirit of Newton and Euclid --- it is natural and inevitable that they
are connected --- and we present the proof of the connection: they are
one entropy of the one Sphere.} This identity is an established result
of the McGucken corpus: it is Theorem 22.3 of the thermodynamics paper
{[}24{]} (``Gravity Equals the Born Rule --- the McGucken Principle
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) Reading of the Shared x₄-Mode Count on the McGucken
Sphere'') and §10.12duodecies of the flagship {[}29{]} (``Gravity is the
Born rule: both are the count of x₄-states on the expanding Sphere'').
The present paper gathers the full derivations of the two endpoints in
one place (§3, §5) and gives the shared-count proof below, following the
corpus {[}24, 29{]}. The literature has related ``gravity is entropy''
and ``the Born rule is entropy'' but never the two to each other,
because it treats them as separate laws each independently tied to a
separate entropy. The precise form of ``the Born rule is entropy'' is
established by Carcassi, Thrien, and Aidala {[}39{]}: over the ensemble
space with the mutual-exclusivity and mixture conditions, they prove
that the Born rule (BR-BORN, p(ψ\textbar φ) =
\textbar⟨φ\textbar ψ⟩\textbar²), the von Neumann entropy (BR-ENT, S(ρ) =
−tr(ρ log ρ)), and the identification of orthogonality with mutual
exclusivity (BR-ORME) are equivalent --- the conditional probability
between two states is an invertible function of the entropy of their
equal mixture. ``The Born rule is entropy'' therefore means the Born
measure and the von Neumann entropy determine each other; combined with
``gravity is entropy'' (§1), the transitive conclusion ``gravity is the
Born rule'' follows once both entropies are shown to be the one entropy
of the McGucken Sphere, which is what the shared-count proof below
establishes. In the McGucken \(dx_4/dt = ic\) framework they are not
separate: both are derived from the one principle (§3 the Born rule, §5
gravity), so the correct expectation is that they share structure ---
and they do, sharing the one entropy S = k ln Ω of the one Sphere. The
McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) generates one McGucken Sphere at
every event, and Sections 3 and 5 have computed one quantity two ways.
The Born rule is the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure on the McGucken
Sphere, evaluated at the event, distributing over the count Ω of
x₄-advance directions {[}19, 20{]}. Gravity is the same McGucken
Sphere's horizon thermodynamics, with the entropy the count Ω of
Compton-tick boundary modes on the horizon {[}25, 31{]}. This section
proves the two counts are one count, so that ``gravity is the Born
rule.''

\textbf{The state space of the x₄-advance.} Fix an event p and its
McGucken Sphere Σ₊(p). The advance proceeds one Compton cycle at a time
(Section 2), and at cycle resolution the distinguishable states of the
wavefront are labelled by a direction \$\(\hat{n}\) ∈ S²\$ on the
Sphere's cross-section together with the cycle index. Let dμ be the
SO(3)-invariant probability measure on S² (Section 3, Derivation 2),

\[d\mu(\hat{n}) = \frac{1}{4\pi}\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi.\]

Isotropy of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) fixes dμ uniquely (Lemma 7.1.5 of
{[}29{]}). The count of distinguishable states of the Sphere over a
region \(R ⊆ S²\), at cycle resolution, is

\[N(R) = \frac{\text{area}(S^2_r)}{\lambda_C^2}\cdot\int_R d\mu \;=\; N_C\int_R d\mu, \qquad \text{area}(S^2_r) = 4\pi r^2,\]

where \(\lambda_C = h/mc\) is the Compton wavelength setting the
one-cycle resolution (the spatial displacement of the McGucken Sphere in
one full Compton cycle, \(c\,T_C = c\cdot h/mc^2 = h/mc\)) and
\(N_C = 4\pi r^2/(h/mc)^2\) is the total number of resolution cells on
the cross-section of radius r = ct; the angular weight of R enters once,
through dμ (equivalently N(R) = r²Ω\_solid(R)/λ\_C², §A.1). Because the
Born measure is the normalized ratio \(N(R)/N(S^2)\), the constant
\(N_C\) cancels and the choice of resolution constant does not affect
the probability; it is displayed only to exhibit the count. N(R) is
integer-valued at cycle resolution and is the single cell count of the
advance on the Sphere. Two quantities are kept apart throughout this
section: the cell count N(Σ) of a surface Σ of the Sphere, and the
microstate count Ω(Σ) = e\^{}\{N(Σ)/4\} of those cells, whose logarithm
is the McGucken Entropy S = k\_B ln Ω = k\_B N/4 (§6). The Born rule
reads N as a ratio over the event's directional cross-section; gravity
reads N through the logarithm of Ω over the horizon. The identity below
is an identity of the cell-counting measure N.

\textbf{Lemma 7.1 (Born reading of the cell count N).} \emph{The Born
probability of an outcome direction φ given a state ψ is the normalized
count of distinguishable cells in the outcome region relative to the
total,}

\[p(\varphi\mid\psi) = \frac{N(R_\varphi)}{N(S^2)} = \frac{\int_{R_\varphi} d\mu}{\int_{S^2} d\mu} = |\langle\psi\mid\varphi\rangle|^2,\]

\emph{where R\_φ is the region of directions assigned to outcome φ by
the projector onto φ.} The factor N\_C cancels between numerator and
denominator, leaving the Haar measure of R\_φ, which is
\textbar⟨ψ\textbar φ⟩\textbar² by Section 3. The Born rule is the cell
count N read over the directional cross-section at the event,
normalized.

\textbf{Lemma 7.2 (Gravitational reading of the cell count N).}
\emph{Let H be the local Rindler horizon through p --- the patch of the
null cone of Σ₊(p) seen by a uniformly accelerated observer, the surface
on which Theorem 14 reads the Clausius relation. The Bekenstein--Hawking
entropy of H is the cell count of H in Planck units, one quarter of a
nat per cell,}

\[S_H = \frac{k_B A(H)}{4\ell_P^2} = \frac{k_B N(H)}{4} = k_B\ln\Omega(H), \qquad N(H) = \frac{A(H)}{\ell_P^2}, \qquad \Omega(H) = e^{N(H)/4}.\]

\emph{The horizon is tiled by Planck-scale McGucken Spheres, one per
Planck area ℓ\_P² = ℏG/c³, each carrying one x₄-stationary boundary
mode, so the cell count is N(H) = A/ℓ\_P², the microstate count is Ω(H)
= e\^{}\{N(H)/4\}, and the entropy is k\_B times the logarithm of Ω ---
one quarter nat per Planck cell, the coefficient fixed in the Geometric
Channel by Newtonian matching (Theorem 12, Theorem 14 with Theorem 9
Step 6) and confirmed from the Algebraic-Channel action by the Euclidean
cigar (Theorem 12, Step C).} This is the standard Bekenstein--Hawking
count {[}15, 16{]} read as the x₄-advance boundary-mode count {[}31{]}.
The gravitational entropy is the cell count N read over the local
horizon through the logarithm --- the entropy of the spacetime curvature
the Einstein field equations describe, derived from \(dx_4/dt = ic\).

\textbf{Theorem 7.3 (Gravity is the Born rule).} \emph{The cell count N
appearing in Lemma 7.1 and the cell count N appearing in Lemma 7.2 are
the same SO(3)-invariant counting measure of the distinguishable states
of the one McGucken Sphere Σ₊(p), restricted to two different surfaces
of the Sphere's null cone: the directional cross-section S² for the Born
rule, and the local horizon H for gravity. Consequently the
gravitational entropy and the Born measure are the horizon reading and
the event reading of a single counting measure --- the Born measure its
normalized value, the gravitational entropy its logarithmic value S =
k\_B ln Ω = k\_B N/4 --- and}

\[\underbrace{\frac{k_B A}{4\ell_P^2} = \frac{k_B N(H)}{4} = k_B\ln\Omega\big|_{H}}_{\text{gravity}} \;\longleftrightarrow\; N \;\longleftrightarrow\; \underbrace{p(\varphi\mid\psi) = \frac{N(R_\varphi)}{N(S^2)}\bigg|_{S^2} = |\langle\psi\mid\varphi\rangle|^2}_{\text{Born rule}}.\]

\emph{Proof.} The x₄-advance is a single physical process --- the
McGucken Sphere expanding at c, one Compton cycle per period T\_C
(Section 2) --- and N is the number of its distinguishable cells at
cycle resolution on any surface of the Sphere. Both Lemma 7.1 and Lemma
7.2 count cells of this one process; they differ only in the surface
over which the count is taken and in how the count is read. The measure
counted is in both cases the SO(3)-invariant measure of the
advance-state space: on S² it is dμ (Lemma 7.1), and on H the cell
density is one per Planck area, which is the same invariant measure
pushed to the horizon patch of the same null cone, because a
direction-dependent cell density on H would break the SO(3)-invariance
of the generating law \(dx_4/dt = ic\) (a horizon element at angle
\[\hat{n}\] would carry more or fewer cells than at \$\(\hat{n}\)′\$,
contradicting isotropy). Since both counts are the invariant measure of
the one advance-state space, restricted respectively to S² and to H,
they are the same N. Reading N on H through the logarithm of the
microstate count Ω = e\^{}\{N/4\} gives the gravitational entropy;
reading N on S² as the normalized ratio N(R\_φ)/N(S²) gives the Born
probability. The two are the logarithmic and the normalized readings of
one counting measure N; the entropy S = k\_B ln Ω that both laws share
is k\_B N/4 on the horizon and, through the same N, the entropy of the
Born distribution at the event (Theorem 6.1, readings (1) and (4)).

\textbf{Scope of the identity (what is and is not claimed).} What
Theorem 7.3 establishes is a \emph{measure-theoretic} identity, and the
paper claims exactly this and no more, following the scope stated in the
corpus (flagship {[}29{]} §10.12duodecies). What is derived
independently is \emph{each endpoint}: the gravitational entropy from
the horizon mode-count (the Jacobson route on the Sphere, §5, with the
1/4 fixed by Newtonian matching in the Geometric Channel and computed
from the Algebraic-Channel action, Theorem 12), and the Born measure
from the directional cross-section count (§3). The identity is then that
these two independently-derived endpoints are the \emph{same} count Ω of
x₄-advance states of the one McGucken Sphere, read over two different
surfaces --- the horizon H for gravity, the directional cross-section S²
for the Born rule. In the framework's words: gravity is the Sphere's
Haar measure integrated over the horizon and read through the logarithm;
the Born rule is the Sphere's Haar measure evaluated at the event and
read as a ratio; both are measure-theoretic readings of the one cell
count N whose logarithmic form is the Boltzmann entropy S = k\_B ln Ω =
k\_B N/4. This is an identity of the shared \emph{entropy} --- the count
Ω that both laws read --- and it is what removes the transitivity
obstruction (the two established equivalences ``gravity is entropy'' and
``the Born rule is entropy'' use two \emph{separately posited} entropies
in two different spaces, so they do not compose; here the two entropies
are one physical count on one Sphere, so they do compose). The identity
is not the stronger claim that the Einstein field equations, as a
differential-geometric object, are literally a projector-valued measure
on Hilbert space: the shared measure is the common \emph{source} both
dynamics read (the Einstein dynamics via the Clausius relation on the
horizon count, §5; the measurement statistics via the Born reading of
the event count, §3), and Theorem 7.3 identifies that shared source, not
the full dynamical content of the two theories. Establishing that the
one count generates \emph{both} the field-equation dynamics and the
measurement process as a single mechanism --- beyond their sharing the
measure Ω --- is the deeper claim toward which the two-channel structure
(§8) points, and is developed in the corpus {[}29, 45{]} rather than
completed within the measure-theoretic identity of this theorem.∎

The identity is transitive and rests on no postulate beyond
\(dx_4/dt = ic\). In the standard treatment the gravitational entropy
(horizon, in spacetime) and the Born entropy (von Neumann, in Hilbert
space) are two different objects, and the step gravity = entropy = Born
rule fails because the middle terms differ. In the McGucken
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) framework the middle term is one object, the cell count
N of distinguishable states of the McGucken Sphere on the McGucken
Sphere, with S = k\_B ln Ω = k\_B N/4 its entropy. Gravity and the Born
rule share an entropy because they share a source --- the expanding
McGucken Sphere generated by \(dx_4/dt = ic\) --- and each is a
theorem-chain of that one Principle {[}22, 28, 29{]}. ``Gravity is the
Born rule'' is the metaphor for this precise identity: the horizon
entropy and the quantum probability measure are the logarithmic horizon
reading and the normalized event reading of the one cell count N.

\hypertarget{one-squaring-operation-underlies-both-readings-measurement-as-the-physical-wick-rotation-and-its-identity-with-the-gravity-geometric-channel-wick-rotation}{%
\subsubsection{7.4 One squaring operation underlies both readings:
measurement as the physical Wick rotation, and its identity with the
gravity Geometric-Channel Wick
rotation}\label{one-squaring-operation-underlies-both-readings-measurement-as-the-physical-wick-rotation-and-its-identity-with-the-gravity-geometric-channel-wick-rotation}}

The identity of §7 admits a sharper physical reading that unifies the
Born squaring of §3 with the Wick rotation of the gravity Geometric
Channel of §5, and both with the act of measurement. The unifying object
is a single geometric operation --- the squaring that removes the
imaginary unit i, the marker of x₄-perpendicularity --- which the
flagship {[}29{]} shows recurs at three levels of the one cascade
descending from \(dx_4/dt = ic\).

\textbf{The dual squaring (Theorem 12.1 of {[}29{]}).} The same squaring
appears at the level of the advance and at the amplitude level. At the
level of the advance, the Lorentzian signature (−,+,+,+) is forced by
(ict)² = −c²t² --- \(dx_4/dt = ic\) squared with respect to time (Lemma
2.5 of {[}29{]}): the rank-2, real-valued metric is obtained by squaring
the rank-1, i-bearing, perpendicular x₄-advance. At the amplitude level,
the Born density P = \textbar ψ\textbar² = ψ*ψ is forced by the rank-2
character the metric hands to the wavefunction's inner product (§3.1,
Lemma 7.1). Both squarings are the same geometric operation applied at
two cascade levels: both remove the i that marks x₄-perpendicularity,
and both produce a real, non-negative spatial-slice quantity from an
i-bearing x₄-perpendicular structure. The Lorentzian metric is the
squared-rate form; the Born density is the squared-amplitude form; the
operation is one.

\textbf{Measurement as the physical Wick rotation (Theorem 12.2 of
{[}29{]}).} The physical event at which the amplitude-level squaring
occurs is measurement. Between measurements a quantum particle
participates in the x₄-expansion, its wavefunction ψ the spatial-slice
projection of its forward x₄-advance and its complex, i-bearing
character the imprint of x₄-perpendicularity on its phase. A measurement
is the physical rotation of the particle out of the x₄-expanding
perpendicular direction into a definite event in x₁x₂x₃; the i-marker is
removed by that rotation, and the amplitude is squared to the Born
density at the point of first contact (the Sphere collision of §3.6).
Measurement is thus the physical realization of the squaring rather than
an extra postulate. Two mathematical operations are involved and are to
be kept apart: the substitution t → −iτ continues the phase
e\^{}\{−iEt/ℏ\} to the real exponential e\^{}\{−Eτ/ℏ\}, whereas the
modulus-squaring removes it, \textbar e\^{}\{−iEt/ℏ\}\textbar² = 1; they
agree in what they remove --- the i that marks x₄-perpendicularity ---
and in producing a real non-negative quantity from an i-bearing
amplitude, and that shared effect is what the identification claims. The
operator-level statement --- that the apparatus coupling, the
environment trace, and the conditional state update realize this removal
at the registration event --- is the content of Theorems 25--26 of
{[}24{]} (§6.2.10), with §6.2.1 keeping the environmental reduction
distinct from the Wick rotation of the geometry and §7.6 leaving the
selection of the single registered outcome as the stated residual.

\textbf{Identity with the gravity Geometric-Channel Wick rotation.} The
Wick rotation that measurement performs at the event is the same
rotation that the Geometric Channel performs at the horizon. In §5 the
McGucken Unruh temperature (Theorem 13) and the horizon thermodynamics
that yield the Einstein field equations arise from the McGucken--Wick
rotation t → −iτ, τ = x₄/c, applied near the horizon: the Euclidean
x₄-periodicity fixes the temperature, and the Clausius relation on the
Euclidean section yields gravity. Measurement (§7.4, event scale) and
the gravity Geometric Channel (§5, horizon scale) are therefore the same
operation --- the Wick rotation with respect to x₄, the squaring that
removes the perpendicularity-marker i --- performed at two scales on the
one McGucken Sphere. This is the operational counterpart of the entropy
identity of Theorem 7.3: gravity and the Born rule are one entropy S = k
ln Ω of the one Sphere because the horizon reading and the event reading
are the same x₄-squaring of the same expanding wavefront. The Born
squaring, the gravitational horizon thermodynamics, and the act of
measurement are three faces of the single Wick rotation that
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) makes available at every event {[}29{]}.

\subsubsection{7.5 The physical origin of ψψ*: two intersecting McGucken
Spheres, and why the Transactional Interpretation reached for the same
structure}\label{the-physical-origin-of-ux3c8ux3c8-two-intersecting-mcgucken-spheres-and-why-the-transactional-interpretation-reached-for-the-same-structure}}

\textbf{Table 7.5a. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic versus the
Transactional Interpretation of quantum mechanics.}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c as a spherically
symmetric wavefront --- the McGucken Sphere --- from every event. This
section derives the Born product ψψ* physically, from the intersection
of two such Spheres, and shows that the Transactional Interpretation of
quantum mechanics reached, with noble intentions, for exactly this ψψ*
structure --- but had to postulate as a real backward-in-time wave what
dx₄/dt = ic supplies as the geometry of two intersecting expanding
Spheres.

**The two-Sphere derivation of ψψ*.** Consider a McGucken Sphere
expanding from a source particle and a second McGucken Sphere expanding
from a particle in a detector, each advancing at c.~By Huygens'
principle, every point on an expanding Sphere is itself the origin of a
secondary expanding Sphere, and that secondary expansion is
perpendicular to the parent surface --- the wavelet expands along the
normal to the wavefront on which it sits. The local structure at any
point of a McGucken Sphere is therefore the surface together with a
secondary Sphere expanding perpendicular to it.

When the source Sphere and the detector Sphere intersect, their surfaces
meet, and at the meeting point the two surfaces share one and the same
tangent plane: two spheres meeting where their surfaces touch are
tangent there, with a common tangent plane and a common normal line
through the point. At that shared tangent point, each surface is locally
generated by its Huygens secondary Sphere expanding perpendicular to the
common tangent plane --- that is, along the common normal. Both
secondary expansions therefore run along the same line, the normal to
the shared tangent plane. But they propagate in opposite directions
along that normal: the source's expansion advancing outward from the
source side, the detector's expansion advancing outward from the
detector side, meeting head-on at the point.

The imaginary unit i marks the perpendicular direction of the x₄-advance
(§2, §3): the expansion is perpendicular to the spatial slice, and the
perpendicularity is carried by i; both Spheres advance at +ic in x₄, in
every frame. At the shared tangent point the two wavefronts arrive along
the common normal from opposite sides. The conjugate factor has two
sources in this geometry, both forward in time. First, the pairing of
the two amplitudes at the meeting point is the sesquilinear inner
product of the derived Hilbert space ℋ (Lemma 7.7.5 Step 2, Theorem 6.1
of {[}29{]}), antilinear in one slot, so the amplitude arriving from the
detector side enters conjugated; the head-on arrival along opposite
normals is the geometric reading of which amplitude occupies which slot.
Second, Huygens' secondary wavelet itself carries the factor −i: the
Fresnel--Kirchhoff propagator of Theorem 7.12 is (1/iλ) e\^{}\{ikr\}/r =
(−i/λ) e\^{}\{ikr\}/r, the secondary wavelet being a quarter cycle
behind the primary, so a wavefront read back from the detector side
toward the source --- the inward reading along −\(\hat{n}\) --- carries
the conjugate phase of the outward reading along +\(\hat{n}\). The
detector Sphere's advance is thus the complex conjugate of the source
Sphere's in the pairing at the tangent point, with no reversal of time
and no reversal of either Sphere's +ic advance: the conjugation is a
property of the pairing and of the Kirchhoff wavelet, read geometrically
as the opposite arrival along the shared normal.

The Born density is the physical overlap of these two advances at the
shared tangent point. The source Sphere's advance carries the
wavefunction ψ with its +i perpendicular phase; the detector Sphere's
advance carries the conjugate ψ* with its −i perpendicular phase; their
head-on meeting at the tangent point is the product

\[\psi\,\psi^* = |\psi|^2,\]

a real, non-negative number, because the +i phase of the one advance and
the −i phase of the other cancel exactly in the product (in polar form ψ
= r e\^{}\{iφ\}, ψ* = r e\^{}\{−iφ\}, ψψ* = r²). The phase --- the
perpendicular x₄-content --- is what the meeting cancels; the
amplitude-squared is what survives. The Born rule is therefore the
geometric fact of two intersecting McGucken Spheres meeting at their
common tangent point, both advancing at +ic, the one entering the
pairing with its +i phase and the other with its conjugate −i phase,
their perpendicular advances overlapping into the real measure
\textbar ψ\textbar². The conjugate wave ψ* is derived: it is the second
Sphere's forward advance as it enters the sesquilinear pairing at the
tangent point, arriving along the shared normal from the opposite side.

\textbf{The Transactional Interpretation reached for this structure.}
The Transactional Interpretation of quantum mechanics (Cramer 1986),
building on the time-symmetric electrodynamics of Wheeler and Feynman,
was a serious and well-motivated attempt to give the Born rule a
physical origin rather than a postulate. Its intentions were noble: to
replace the instantaneous, observer-dependent collapse of the Copenhagen
interpretation with a concrete physical process; to reconcile quantum
nonlocality with relativity; and to make the wavefunction a real
physical wave rather than a representation of knowledge. Its central
move was to treat both the retarded solution ψ (the ``offer wave,'' from
emitter to absorber) and the advanced solution ψ* (the ``confirmation
wave,'' from absorber to emitter) as physically real, and to identify
the completed emitter--absorber transaction --- the product ψψ* =
\textbar ψ\textbar² of the offer wave and the confirmation wave --- as
the physical origin of the Born probability. The Transactional
Interpretation thus recognized, correctly, that the Born density is the
product of a forward amplitude and its conjugate arriving from the
absorber, and that this product is what makes \textbar ψ\textbar² real
and non-negative.

\textbf{Why dx₄/dt = ic offers a simpler, better, and deeper model.} The
Transactional Interpretation had to purchase the ψ* confirmation wave at
a heavy price. It postulated, as a physically real entity, an advanced
wave travelling backward in time from the detector to the source; it
required the universe to be a perfect absorber, in the manner of
Wheeler--Feynman; and it defended the resulting causal paradoxes only by
declaring the transaction atemporal, a four-dimensional standing wave
with no fact about which end occurred first. The conjugate wave was
asserted, not derived, and its backward-in-time character has kept the
interpretation a minority position.

The two-Sphere derivation supplies the same ψψ* structure with none of
this cost. The conjugate ψ* is the detector Sphere's ordinary forward
advance, entering the sesquilinear pairing at the tangent point from the
opposite side along the shared normal (and carrying the Kirchhoff −i of
the inward-read wavelet), with both Spheres advancing at +ic; no wave
travels backward in time. There is no backward-in-time propagation, no
perfect-absorber requirement, no atemporal handshake, and no causal
paradox: two Spheres expand forward at c from two particles, they
intersect, and at the common tangent point the +i and −i perpendicular
advances overlap into \textbar ψ\textbar². What the Transactional
Interpretation had to postulate --- a real conjugate wave and a timeless
handshake --- dx₄/dt = ic derives from the geometry of two intersecting
expanding Spheres.

The deeper difference is categorical. The Transactional Interpretation
is an interpretation of standard non-relativistic quantum mechanics: it
presupposes the Schrödinger equation and reproduces its predictions,
adding a physical story for the Born rule and for collapse. It does not
derive quantum mechanics --- it re-reads it --- and it says nothing
about general relativity or thermodynamics; it yields no metric, no
Einstein field equations, no Second Law, no entropy. The McGucken
Principle dx₄/dt = ic is not an interpretation of one theory but the
physical foundation from which three descend: general relativity as a
theorem chain {[}23{]}, quantum mechanics as a theorem chain {[}38{]},
and thermodynamics as a theorem chain {[}24{]}, with the Born rule, the
Second Law, the Einstein field equations, entropy, and the uncertainty
principle each a theorem of the one Principle (§3--§6). The
Transactional Interpretation reached, honourably, for the physical
reality of ψψ* within quantum mechanics; dx₄/dt = ic supplies that
physical reality --- as the overlap of two intersecting McGucken Spheres
at their common tangent point --- and supplies, from the same one
principle, general relativity and thermodynamics as well. Where the
Transactional Interpretation re-reads one theory at the cost of
backward-in-time waves, the McGucken Principle generates three theories
from the forward expansion of the fourth dimension at c.

\hypertarget{full-reproduction-the-head-on-xux2084-collision-derivation-of-the-born-rule-7.9-of-29-verbatim}{%
\paragraph{7.5.1 Full reproduction: the head-on x₄-collision derivation
of the Born rule (§7.9 of {[}29{]},
verbatim)}\label{full-reproduction-the-head-on-xux2084-collision-derivation-of-the-born-rule-7.9-of-29-verbatim}}

The following is reproduced verbatim and in full from the flagship
Minkowski--Hilbert paper {[}29{]}, §7.9
(https://elliotmcguckenphysics.com/2026/07/05/minkowski-space-and-hilbert-space-derived-and-unified-via-the-mcgucken-principle-dx\%e2\%82\%84-dt-ic-how-the-born-rule-schrodinger-equation-hilbert-space-lorentzian-spacetime-metric-einstein-fiel/),
the corpus derivation of the Born density as the head-on collision of
two McGucken Spheres. It is quoted complete and unaltered. One
correction, made in the present paper's own statement of the theorem in
§3.8 and owed in {[}29{]} §7.9, is recorded here rather than inserted
into the quotation: the source's clauses (i)--(iii) and Remarks
7.8--7.10 state that the absorber's expansion ``appears antiparallel in
x₄'' in the emitter's frame, with the conjugation read as the
frame-relational sign −ic and the localization as ``x₄-momenergy
cancellation.'' The McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) is universal and
Lorentz boosts are orthochronous, so both Spheres advance at +ic in
every frame; what is antiparallel at the meeting event is the pair of
outward spatial normals, the conjugation is supplied by the sesquilinear
pairing of the derived Hilbert space (the source's own Lemma 7.7.5 Step
2), and the localization is the redistribution of four-momentum from the
x₄-advance into the spatial components at the interaction vertex, with
p₄\^{}A + p₄\^{}B = 2imc conserved. The quotation below is the source as
published.

\textbf{7.9 The physical mechanism: Born rule as head-on x₄-collision of
two McGucken spheres}

Theorem 7.4 established that the Born density ψ\^{}\emph{ψ at a
detection event B is the geometric overlap of the forward x₄-expansion
(carrying phase from x₄ = ict) and the conjugate x₄-expansion (carrying
phase from x₄\^{}} = -ict) at B. The reading is geometrically complete
but leaves one physical question open: what is the physical referent of
the conjugate sphere? On the geometric-overlap reading alone, the
conjugate is the orientation-reversed image of the forward expansion ---
an algebraic partner of ψ with no independent physical existence
required. This subsection identifies the conjugate sphere physically: it
is the absorber's own forward x₄-expansion, viewed from the emitter's
frame, where it appears antiparallel in x₄. The Born rule's bilinearity
then has an explicit two-particle physical mechanism --- the head-on
x₄-collision of the two McGucken spheres at the detection event --- and
the rotation-out-of-x₄ that Theorem 12.2 will identify as the universal
measurement mechanism is here exhibited as the result of x₄-momentum
cancellation at the collision.

\textbf{Theorem 7.7 (Born rule as head-on x₄-collision of two McGucken
spheres).} \emph{Let particle A at event E\_A and particle B at event
E\_B each propagate, by the canonical ontology (clause 3, §2.4) and
Definition 2.6, a McGucken sphere outward at dx₄/dt = +ic in its
respective rest frame. Let P ∈ 𝓜\_\{E\_A\}(t) ∩ 𝓜\_\{E\_B\}(t) be a
spacetime event where both McGucken spheres arrive on the spatial slice
at parameter time t. Then:}

*(i) (Frame-relational antiparallelism in x₄.) In A's rest frame at P,
A's outgoing x₄-component carries the signature dx₄/dt\textbar\_A = +ic.
B's outgoing x₄-component along the shared spatial geodesic from E\_B to
P, as expressed in A's frame at P, carries the opposite sign:
dx₄/dt\textbar\_B (as seen in A's frame at P) = -ic. By the A↔B symmetry
of the construction, the converse holds in B's rest frame.*

\emph{(ii) (Algebraic content of the antiparallelism.) The antiparallel
signs in (i) realize, frame-relationally, the algebraic conjugation z ↔
z\^{}} on the imaginary unit: i ↔ -i. The conjugate kernel ψ\^{}* of
Definition 7.3 is therefore the absorber's forward x₄-expansion viewed
in the emitter's frame; equivalently, ψ is the emitter's forward
x₄-expansion viewed in the absorber's frame. Complex conjugation in the
Born rule is the dx₄/dt = ic framework's expression of the
frame-relational relationship between the two physical participants in
the head-on collision.*

\emph{(iii) (x₄-momenergy cancellation forces 3-localization.) Each
McGucken sphere carries x₄-component of four-momentum p\_4 = i m c in
its own rest frame (the four-momentum form of dx₄/dt = ic; cf.~§9.2 step
1 and the four-velocity budget u\^{}μ u\_μ = -c² of §2.3). At the
head-on meeting P, the two x₄-momenta, expressed in a common frame, are
antiparallel: p\_4\^{}A = +imc and p\_4\^{}B = -imc in A's frame at P
(for identical-mass particles; the relative x₄-momentum vanishes more
generally in the center-of-momentum frame along the head-on axis). The
sum of x₄-components vanishes at P. By four-momentum conservation
(translation invariance of the Lorentzian metric, Lemma 2.5), the
momenergy that cancelled in x₄ must reappear in x₁x₂x₃ at P. Both
particles are thereby rotated out of pure x₄-expansion and localized at
P --- the geometric reorientation that Theorem 12.2 will name ``rotation
out of x₄.''}

\emph{(iv) (Bilinear collision rate.) The local rate of the head-on
collision event at P is the sesquilinear product ψ\_A(P) · ψ\_B\^{}}(P)
up to a positive normalization constant. The product structure ψ\_A(P) ·
ψ\_B(P) of the two amplitudes is derived rigorously in Lemma 7.7.5 Step
1 below from action-additivity of independent paths, ruling out sum,
max, min, arithmetic/geometric/harmonic means as candidate functional
forms. The conjugation \(\psi_B \leadsto \psi_B^*\) that converts the
forward × forward product to the Born sesquilinear ψ · ψ\^{}* is derived
in Lemma 7.7.5 Step 2 from the complexification of the symmetric rank-2
metric (Lemma 7.1) combined with R1 (real Born density on diagonal) ---
the bilinear complex extension fails R1, only the sesquilinear extension
gives a real diagonal for symmetric forms. The conjugation is therefore
the STRUCTURAL CONJUGATION of the sesquilinear inner product, NOT a
Lorentz-boost frame change (the action S is a Lorentz scalar) and NOT
the Stueckelberg--Feynman time-reversal postulate (which is one PHYSICAL
INTERPRETATION but not the structural source of the conjugation).
Higher-rank pairings (cubic, quartic, etc.) are excluded by the same
rank-counting that excluded them in Theorem 7.2.*

\emph{(v) (Reduction to single-particle ψ\^{}}ψ.) For single-particle QM
with a macroscopic absorber localized at P by prior decoherence (the
standard idealization of a detector), the absorber is well-modeled as a
localized point at P whose McGucken sphere's forward x₄-expansion is, in
the emitter's frame, the conjugate kernel ψ\^{}* by (ii). The collision
rate at P reduces to ψ\^{}\emph{(P) ψ(P) = \textbar ψ(P)\textbar²,
recovering the Born rule of Theorem 7.2 as the rate of head-on
x₄-collisions between the emitter's outgoing sphere and the absorber's
outgoing sphere viewed conjugately.}

\textbf{Proof.}

\emph{(i)} By canonical clause 3 (§2.4), the McGucken sphere expansion
from any event proceeds isotropically at rate c with respect to that
event's rest frame. The spatial-slice projection of A's expansion at P
points from E\_A toward P along the spacelike geodesic E\_A P; in A's
rest frame, A's x₄-component advances at +ic per proper time along this
expansion. The spatial-slice projection of B's expansion at P points
from E\_B toward P along E\_B P; in B's rest frame, B's x₄-component
advances at +ic per proper time. The two spheres meet at P traveling
toward each other in spacelike orientation. Express B's outgoing
x₄-component in A's frame at P: along the line E\_A P E\_B at P, A's
outgoing x₄-direction is the +ic direction (by A's frame definition),
and B's outgoing x₄-direction at P points back toward E\_B along the
same spacelike line, which is the opposite spatial orientation --- and
by the same construction of ``outgoing x₄-direction at P relative to the
source,'' in A's frame this is the -ic direction. The antiparallelism
follows. The A↔B symmetry of the entire construction yields the converse
in B's frame.

\emph{(ii)} Complex conjugation in ℂ is the orientation reversal of the
imaginary axis: i ↔ -i. The i-marker for x₄-perpendicularity (Theorem
3.1, §4.3) thereby reverses sign under conjugation, exactly as in (i).
The conjugate kernel ψ\^{}*(B) = ∑\_γ exp(-iS{[}γ{]}/ℏ) of Definition
7.3 is the path-integral expression of orientation-reversed expansion;
by (i), this orientation reversal is the absorber's forward x₄-expansion
(which is +ic in its own frame) as seen from the emitter's frame (-ic).
The conjugate is therefore the absorber-frame partner of the emitter's
forward expansion --- the dx₄/dt = ic framework's frame-relational
reading of complex conjugation.

\emph{(iii)} By the four-velocity budget (§2.3, §9.2 step 1), each
particle's four-momentum in its rest frame has x₄-component p\_4 = i m
c, with full magnitude m c² the rest-energy content (mass-energy
equivalence descending from the same dx₄/dt = ic --- cf.~companion paper
{[}54{]} for the corpus derivation). At the head-on collision at P, the
two x₄-momentum components in a common frame are antiparallel by (i);
for identical-mass particles their sum vanishes, and for non-identical
masses the sum vanishes in the center-of-momentum frame along the
head-on axis. Four-momentum is conserved at P (translation invariance of
the Lorentzian metric, Lemma 2.5). What cancels in the x₄-component must
therefore reappear in the x₁x₂x₃-components for total four-momentum to
be conserved at P. The cancelled x₄-momenergy is deposited as 3-spatial
momenergy at P, rotating both particles' free four-velocity budget from
x₄-dominated to spatial-dominated --- both particles localized at P.

\emph{(iv)} The probability per unit time per unit spatial volume at P
of the head-on collision event is the sesquilinear product ψ\_A(P) ·
ψ\_B\^{}\emph{(P) of the two amplitudes (with the conjugation of
ψ\_B\^{}} prescribed by the postulated frame-relational antiparallelism
of (i)-(ii) --- see Step 2 of Lemma 7.7.5 below for the honest
accounting of this conjugation as a structural postulate, not a frame
consequence). The product structure \(\psi_A \cdot \psi_B\) --- rather
than sum, max, geometric mean, or any other symmetric function of the
two amplitudes --- is derived rigorously in Lemma 7.7.5 Step 1 below
from action-additivity of independent paths combined with the
exponential phase content of each McGucken-Sphere wavefront. The
conjugation \(\psi_B \leadsto \psi_B^*\) that converts the forward ×
forward product to the Born sesquilinear is the structural input doing
the work and is currently a postulate, with three plausible derivation
routes identified in Remark 7.7.7. Higher-rank pairings (cubic, quartic,
etc.) are excluded by the same rank-counting that excluded them in
Theorem 7.2.

\emph{(v)} For single-particle QM with a localized macroscopic absorber,
the absorber is modeled as a particle at the detection point P with
localized wavefunction ψ\_B(P') = δ(P' - P) --- equivalently, a McGucken
sphere whose forward x₄-expansion is, in the emitter's frame, the
conjugate kernel ψ\^{}\emph{(P) (by (ii)). The collision rate from (iv)
becomes Rate(detection at P) = ψ\^{}}(P) ψ(P) · \textbar Γ\textbar² =
\textbar Γ\textbar² \textbar ψ(P)\textbar², with \textbar Γ\textbar² a
coupling-dependent prefactor absorbed into the wavefunction's
normalization. The standard Born rule of Theorem 7.2 is recovered as the
localized-absorber limit of the head-on x₄-collision picture. ∎

\textbf{Lemma 7.7.5 (Two-Sphere coincidence rate: product structure and
sesquilinear conjugation both derived; closure of R4 to G1).} \emph{Let
A and B be two independent McGucken Spheres arriving at the spatial
point P at parameter time t, with amplitudes ψ\_A(P), ψ\_B(P) ∈ ℂ. Then
the local coincidence rate at P is, up to a positive normalization
constant, the sesquilinear product}

\emph{R(ψ\_A(P), ψ\_B(P)) = ψ\_A(P) · ψ\_B\^{}}(P),*

\emph{with BOTH structural ingredients --- the product structure and the
conjugation --- derived within the McGucken framework from the
structural content of dx₄/dt = ic combined with the four requirements
R1--R4 of Theorem 7.2.}

\emph{(a) \textbf{Product structure (DERIVED).} The product form
\(\psi_A(P) \cdot \psi_B(P)\) --- rather than sum, max, min,
arithmetic/geometric/harmonic mean, or any other symmetric function of
the two amplitudes --- is forced (Step 1 below) by the action-additivity
of independent paths combined with the exponential phase content
\(\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)\) of each McGucken-Sphere wavefront.}

\emph{(b) \textbf{Conjugation \(\psi_B \leadsto \psi_B^*\) (DERIVED).}
The conjugation of one factor --- converting the forward × forward
product \(\psi_A \cdot \psi_B\) to the sesquilinear pairing
\(\psi_A \cdot \psi_B^*\) --- is forced (Step 2 below) by the
complexification of the symmetric rank-2 metric \(\eta_{\mu\nu}\) (Lemma
7.1, symmetric since \(\eta_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{\nu\mu}\)) combined with
the requirement R1 (real Born density on diagonal). The bilinear complex
extension of \(\eta_{\mu\nu}\) has imaginary part on the diagonal
generally non-zero; the sesquilinear extension uniquely gives a real
diagonal for symmetric forms. R1 therefore excludes the bilinear
extension and forces the sesquilinear extension --- and the sesquilinear
extension is precisely the one with conjugation. The conjugation is the
STRUCTURAL CONJUGATION of the sesquilinear inner product, not a Lorentz
boost, and not a Stueckelberg--Feynman time-reversal postulate.}

\emph{(c) \textbf{Sesquilinearity follows from (a) + (b); uniqueness
within sesquilinear forms is elementary linear algebra (Step 3).} R4
(bilinearity in (ψ, ψ\^{}})) is the sesquilinear structure of the
coincidence pairing, derived from (a) + (b) above.*

\emph{(d) \textbf{R4 closes to G1 within v46.} The bilinearity
requirement R4 of Theorem 7.2's uniqueness derivation is now fully
derived within v46 from the structural content of the McGucken framework
--- both the product structure (a) and the conjugation (b) are derived
theorems, not postulates. The previous v45 grade (G2 with conjugation as
singular residual postulate) is upgraded to G1: the conjugation is
supplied not by Theorem 7.7's head-on collision picture (which is a
secondary physical interpretation) but by the complexification of the
symmetric rank-2 metric combined with R1, both of which are
McGucken-internal theorems.}

\emph{Proof.}

Each McGucken Sphere wavefront ψ propagates as a path-integral kernel
with phase content \(\exp(iS[\gamma]/\hbar)\) along each path γ (Theorem
3.1, Definition 2.6). For two independent McGucken Spheres A and B
arriving at P along independent paths γ\_A and γ\_B, the joint wavefront
content at P has phase content equal to the SUM of the individual
phases:

\[S_{\text{joint}}[\gamma_A, \gamma_B] = S_A[\gamma_A] + S_B[\gamma_B].\]

By the exponential identity \(\exp(a + b) = \exp(a) \cdot \exp(b)\), the
joint wavefront amplitude at P is therefore the PRODUCT of the
individual amplitudes:

\[\psi_{\text{joint}}(P) = \exp(iS_{\text{joint}}/\hbar) = \exp(iS_A/\hbar) \cdot \exp(iS_B/\hbar) = \psi_A(P) \cdot \psi_B(P).\]

The product structure is therefore derived from action-additivity and
the exponential phase content of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront, with no
separately postulated probability axiom. This rules out, structurally,
every alternative symmetric function as a candidate functional form for
the joint amplitude:

\emph{(i) Sum} \(\psi_A + \psi_B\): Would require phase-multiplicative
action (\(S_{\text{joint}} = S_A \cdot S_B\)), contradicting the
additive action structure of independent paths.

\emph{(ii) Maximum / minimum} \(\max(|\psi_A|, |\psi_B|)\),
\(\min(|\psi_A|, |\psi_B|)\): Not derivable from the exponential phase
structure; fails the smooth-wavefunction differentiability of Definition
2.6.

\emph{(iii) Arithmetic mean} \((|\psi_A| + |\psi_B|)/2\): Same
structural failure as sum --- would require additive action structure
with a \(1/2\) factor that has no source in the action-additivity of
independent paths.

\emph{(iv) Geometric mean} \(\sqrt{|\psi_A| \cdot |\psi_B|}\): Not
derivable from action-additivity; would require half-action structure
\(S_{\text{joint}} = (S_A + S_B)/2\), which contradicts the additive
structure.

\emph{(v) Harmonic mean}
\(2|\psi_A| \cdot |\psi_B| / (|\psi_A| + |\psi_B|)\): Not derivable from
any action-related structure; involves a non-polynomial combination.

The product is therefore the unique functional form forced by the
action-additivity of independent paths combined with the exponential
phase content of each Sphere.

The wave-mechanical product \(\psi_A(P) \cdot \psi_B(P)\) of Step 1 is
the joint amplitude at the coincidence event P. To extract a real
coincidence RATE from this joint amplitude, we must combine it with an
appropriate inner product structure on complex-valued amplitudes. The
conjugation \(\psi_B \leadsto \psi_B^*\) that converts the forward ×
forward product to the sesquilinear pairing \(\psi_A \cdot \psi_B^*\) is
FORCED by the following structural chain --- no time-reversal postulate,
no Stueckelberg--Feynman identification, no frame-relational
antiparallelism required.

By Lemma 7.1, the metric pairing on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront is
rank-2 and inherited from the Minkowski metric \(\eta_{\mu\nu}\), which
is a SYMMETRIC real bilinear form on real four-vectors
(\(\eta_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{\nu\mu}\) by symmetry of the metric tensor).
The wavefunction \(\psi\) is complex-valued by Theorem 3.1 (the
imaginary unit \(i\) is the algebraic marker of \(x_4\)-perpendicularity
from \(x_4 = ict\)). The inner product on complex-valued wavefunctions
must therefore be a COMPLEX EXTENSION of the rank-2 real metric.

A symmetric real bilinear form \(B: V \times V \to \mathbb{R}\) on a
real vector space V admits exactly two natural extensions to a complex
form on the complexification
\(V_{\mathbb{C}} = V \otimes_{\mathbb{R}} \mathbb{C}\):

\textbf{(A) Complex bilinear extension}
\(B^{\text{bil}}: V_{\mathbb{C}} \times V_{\mathbb{C}} \to \mathbb{C}\)
--- linear in both arguments. For complex \(z = u + iv\),
\(w = u' + iv'\) with \(u, v, u', v' \in V\):

\[B^{\text{bil}}(z, w) = B(u, u') - B(v, v') + i \bigl(B(u, v') + B(v, u')\bigr).\]

Diagonal: \(B^{\text{bil}}(z, z) = B(u, u) - B(v, v) + 2i \, B(u, v)\).

\textbf{(B) Sesquilinear (Hermitian) extension}
\(B^{\text{sesq}}: V_{\mathbb{C}} \times V_{\mathbb{C}} \to \mathbb{C}\)
--- antilinear in first argument, linear in second. Defined via
\(B^{\text{sesq}}(z, w) := B(\bar{z}, w)\), where \(\bar{z} = u - iv\)
is the complex conjugate of \(z\):

\[B^{\text{sesq}}(z, w) = B(u, u') + B(v, v') + i \bigl(B(u, v') - B(v, u')\bigr).\]

Diagonal:
\(B^{\text{sesq}}(z, z) = B(u, u) + B(v, v) + i \bigl(B(u, v) - B(v, u)\bigr)\).

For SYMMETRIC \(B\) (where \(B(u, v) = B(v, u)\) as for
\(\eta_{\mu\nu}\)), the diagonals reduce to:

\[B^{\text{bil}}(z, z) = B(u, u) - B(v, v) + 2i \, B(u, v) \qquad \text{(imaginary part } 2 B(u,v), \text{ generally NON-zero)},\]

\[B^{\text{sesq}}(z, z) = B(u, u) + B(v, v) \in \mathbb{R} \qquad \text{(REAL, by symmetry of B)}.\]

Requirement R1 (reality of the Born density on diagonal --- that the
density value \(P(x) = R(\psi(x), \psi(x))\) at a single wavefunction be
real-valued at every spatial point \(x\)) is the physical requirement
that the Born density be a probability density. R1 \textbf{excludes} the
bilinear extension: \(B^{\text{bil}}(\psi, \psi)\) has imaginary part
\(2 B(\text{Re}\,\psi, \text{Im}\,\psi)\) that fails to vanish for
generic complex \(\psi\) (specifically, whenever \(\text{Re}\,\psi\) and
\(\text{Im}\,\psi\) are not \(\eta\)-orthogonal at the point \(x\),
which is the generic case). R1 \textbf{forces} the sesquilinear
extension:
\(B^{\text{sesq}}(\psi, \psi) = B(\text{Re}\,\psi, \text{Re}\,\psi) + B(\text{Im}\,\psi, \text{Im}\,\psi)\)
is real by symmetry of \(\eta_{\mu\nu}\), automatically and for every
\(\psi\).

\textbf{The conjugation in the sesquilinear extension} --- making the
inner product structure \(\psi^* \psi\) rather than \(\psi^2\) --- is
therefore FORCED by three structural inputs, each independently derived
within the McGucken framework:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{(\roman{enumi})}
\item
  The symmetry of the rank-2 metric \(\eta_{\mu\nu}\), a structural
  feature of the Minkowski metric, derived from \((ic)^2 = -c^2\) via
  Lemma 2.5 (\(\eta_{\mu\nu}\) is symmetric because the Minkowski line
  element is bilinear in \(dx^\mu\) symmetrically).
\item
  The complex character of the wavefunction \(\psi\), derived from
  Theorem 3.1 (\(i\) is the algebraic marker of \(x_4\)-perpendicularity
  from \(x_4 = ict\), with the wavefunction being a complex-valued
  path-integral kernel by Definition 2.6).
\item
  Requirement R1 (real Born density on diagonal), the physical content
  that the density be a probability density.
\end{enumerate}

These three inputs jointly force the sesquilinear extension, which
uniquely supplies the conjugation \(\psi_B \leadsto \psi_B^*\). The
conjugation is therefore a STRUCTURAL THEOREM of the dx₄/dt = ic
framework, derived from (i)--(iii) above, not a frame-change postulate
and not a time-reversal identification.

The conjugation \(i \mapsto -i\) entering the Born density is NOT
identified with a Lorentz boost or any frame change --- the v45 audit
correctly noted that the action \(S\) is a Lorentz scalar, so
\(\exp(iS/\hbar)\) is frame-invariant, and a boost cannot conjugate
\(\psi\). The conjugation is also NOT identified with time reversal as a
separately postulated physical operation (the Stueckelberg--Feynman
absorber-as-time-reversed-emitter convention). Rather, the conjugation
is the STRUCTURAL CONJUGATION of the sesquilinear complexification of
the symmetric rank-2 metric, forced by R1 (real diagonal) as derived
above. The Stueckelberg--Feynman reading of Theorem 7.7(i)-(ii) becomes
one PHYSICAL INTERPRETATION of the (already derived) sesquilinear
conjugation, not its source: it provides physical content to the head-on
collision picture, but the conjugation itself is supplied upstream by
the complexification argument.

The joint amplitude \(\psi_A(P) \cdot \psi_B(P)\) of Step 1 combines
with the sesquilinear inner product structure derived in this Step 2 to
give the coincidence rate as the sesquilinear pairing:

\[R(\psi_A, \psi_B) = \psi_A(P) \cdot \psi_B^*(P)\]

with the conjugation on \(\psi_B\) being the structural conjugation of
the sesquilinear complexification (Step 2), derived from R1 + symmetric
rank-2 metric + complex-valued wavefunction. The product structure (Step
1) and the conjugation (Step 2) are BOTH derived from the structural
content of the McGucken framework, with no postulational input from
Theorem 7.7's head-on collision picture or any time-reversal
identification.

Steps 1 and 2 together establish that the coincidence rate has the
sesquilinear structure \(R(\psi_A, \psi_B) = \psi_A \cdot \psi_B^*\)
(linear in \(\psi_A\) from Step 1's product structure, antilinear in
\(\psi_B\) from Step 2's complexification-forced conjugation). Within
the family of sesquilinear forms on \(\mathbb{C} \times \mathbb{C}\),
the form is unique up to a multiplicative constant by direct
linear-algebraic computation:
\(R(\psi_A, \psi_B) = \psi_A \cdot R(1, \psi_B) = \psi_A \cdot \psi_B^* \cdot R(1, 1) = c \cdot \psi_A \cdot \psi_B^*\)
with \(c := R(1, 1)\). This step is the elementary direction (unpacking
the definition of \emph{sesquilinear}) and contributes no derivational
content beyond Steps 1 and 2; its role is to formalize the unique
sesquilinear functional form once sesquilinearity itself is established
by Steps 1 + 2.

The constant \(c\) is fixed by: reality on diagonal
(\(c \in \mathbb{R}\) from \(R(\psi, \psi) = c|\psi|^2\) being real);
non-negativity (\(c > 0\) from \(R(\psi, \psi) \geq 0\)); and
normalization (\(c = 1\) absorbed into wavefunction normalization). For
the single-particle Born density:

\[R(\psi, \psi^*) = \psi \cdot \psi^* = |\psi|^2.\]

This is the Born density of Theorem 7.2, recovered through the fully
derived chain Step 1 (product structure, derived from action-additivity)
→ Step 2 (conjugation, derived from complexification + R1 + symmetric
rank-2 metric) → Step 3 (uniqueness within sesquilinear forms,
elementary linear algebra) → Step 4 (constants fixed by R1 + R2 +
normalization). ∎

\textbf{Corollary 7.7.6 (R4 closure to G1 within v46 via the
complexification route).} \emph{The bilinearity requirement R4 of
Theorem 7.2's uniqueness derivation --- that the Born density P be
bilinear in (ψ, ψ\^{}}) --- is now fully derived within v46 from the
structural content of the McGucken framework. The derivation chain is:*

\emph{(R4-1) The Minkowski metric \(\eta_{\mu\nu}\) is symmetric
(\(\eta_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{\nu\mu}\), manifest in the Minkowski line
element \(ds^2 = \eta_{\mu\nu} dx^\mu dx^\nu\) being
bilinear-symmetric). The rank-2 character descends from the squared form
\((ic)^2 = -c^2\) of dx₄/dt = ic (Lemma 2.5).}

\emph{(R4-2) The wavefunction is complex-valued by Theorem 3.1: the
imaginary unit \(i\) is the algebraic marker of \(x_4\)-perpendicularity
from \(x_4 = ict\) via Frobenius (Theorem 4.6.1). The path-integral
kernel (Definition 2.6) gives ψ as a complex-valued function over
Minkowski Space \(\mathbb{M}_{1,3}\).}

\emph{(R4-3) The inner product on the McGucken-derived Hilbert space,
lifting the rank-2 metric to complex amplitudes, is a complex extension
of \(\eta_{\mu\nu}\). By the complexification of symmetric real bilinear
forms (Lemma 7.7.5 Step 2): exactly two natural extensions exist
(complex bilinear and sesquilinear), and the bilinear extension fails
the reality of the diagonal whereas the sesquilinear extension uniquely
gives a real diagonal for symmetric forms.}

\emph{(R4-4) Requirement R1 (real Born density on diagonal) excludes the
bilinear extension and forces the sesquilinear extension. The
conjugation \(\psi \leadsto \psi^*\) in the inner product structure
\(\psi^* \psi\) is the structural conjugation of the sesquilinear
complexification --- not a Stueckelberg--Feynman time-reversal
identification.}

\emph{(R4-5) The action-additivity of independent McGucken-Sphere paths
gives the product structure \(\psi_A \cdot \psi_B\) for the joint
amplitude (Lemma 7.7.5 Step 1). Combined with (R4-4), this yields the
sesquilinear pairing \(R = \psi_A \cdot \psi_B^*\) as the coincidence
rate, and on the single-particle diagonal,
\(R(\psi, \psi^*) = |\psi|^2\) --- the Born density.}

\emph{(R4-6) Bilinearity in \((\psi, \psi^*)\) --- requirement R4 --- is
the structural form of this sesquilinear inner product, derived from
(R4-1) through (R4-5) as a forced consequence of the McGucken
framework's structural content combined with R1. R4 is grade \textbf{G1
within v46} --- fully derived, with no postulational input beyond dx₄/dt
= ic, its forced consequences (rank-2 metric symmetry, complex
wavefunction), and R1 (itself a Sphere-geometric requirement, see
§7.1).}

\emph{The previous v45 grade (G2 with conjugation as singular residual
postulate) is upgraded to G1 in v46 via the complexification route. The
``elementary collision kinematics'' assertion of Theorem 7.7(iv) has
been replaced by the fully derived chain (R4-1) through (R4-6) above,
with the conjugation step (R4-3, R4-4) supplied by the inner product
structure (complexification + R1) rather than by Theorem 7.7's head-on
collision picture. Theorem 7.7's head-on collision picture remains as a
SECONDARY physical interpretation of the (already derived) sesquilinear
structure --- providing geometric content to the two-particle-collision
reading --- but is no longer for R4's derivation.}

\textbf{Remark 7.7.7 (Why the complexification route closes the gap;
relationship to v45's three candidate routes).} \emph{The
complexification-route derivation of R4 (Lemma 7.7.5 Step 2 and
Corollary 7.7.6) closes the gap that v45's audit identified between
v43's ``elementary collision kinematics'' assertion and a true G1
derivation. The key insight is that the conjugation in \(\psi^* \psi\)
enters the dx₄/dt = ic framework not as a physical time-reversal
postulate (the Stueckelberg--Feynman absorber-as-time-reversed-emitter
identification) but as the structural conjugation of the sesquilinear
complexification of the symmetric rank-2 metric, forced by R1 (real Born
density on diagonal). This is a textbook linear-algebraic fact applied
to the McGucken framework's structural content:}

\emph{(Mathematical fact). For a symmetric real bilinear form B on a
real vector space V, the unique complex extension to \(V_\mathbb{C}\)
that has a real diagonal on all of \(V_\mathbb{C}\) is the sesquilinear
extension \(B^{\text{sesq}}(z, w) = B(\bar{z}, w)\). The bilinear
extension \(B^{\text{bil}}(z, w) = B(z, w)\) extended by complex
linearity has imaginary part \(2 B(\text{Re}\,z, \text{Im}\,z)\) on the
diagonal that fails to vanish for generic \(z \in V_\mathbb{C}\)
(specifically, when \(\text{Re}\,z\) and \(\text{Im}\,z\) are not
B-orthogonal).}

\emph{(Application to the McGucken framework). The Minkowski metric
\(\eta_{\mu\nu}\) is symmetric (a structural feature derivable from
Lemma 2.5). The wavefunction is complex-valued (Theorem 3.1, Definition
2.6). The Born density on the diagonal must be real (R1). The unique
extension of \(\eta_{\mu\nu}\) to complex amplitudes consistent with R1
is the sesquilinear extension, which is precisely the one with
conjugation. R4 follows.}

\emph{Relationship to v45's three candidate routes: v45 identified three
plausible derivation routes --- complexification +
positive-definiteness, PT-symmetry through meeting event, and
Stueckelberg--Feynman as theorem --- and noted that closure required at
least one to succeed. The complexification route, now realized
concretely in Lemma 7.7.5 Step 2, succeeds via R1 (real diagonal)
without requiring full positive-definiteness on the physical sector. The
PT-symmetry route (via Theorem 7.11) provides an independent geometric
interpretation of the same conjugation, consistent with and
complementary to the complexification derivation. The
Stueckelberg--Feynman route remains a distinct direction of work ---
promoting the absorber-as-time-reversed-emitter convention from physical
interpretation to derived theorem --- but is no longer required for R4
closure, since the complexification route closes the gap independently.}

\emph{Relationship to Theorem 7.7's head-on collision picture: the
head-on collision is now one PHYSICAL INTERPRETATION of the (already
derived) sesquilinear inner product structure --- providing a
two-particle-collision reading in which the conjugate factor is
identified with the absorber's amplitude as viewed in the emitter's
frame. This identification has additional physical content (the
Stueckelberg--Feynman reading of absorption as time-reversed emission),
but it is not REQUIRED for the derivation of R4: the conjugation is
supplied by the inner product structure, not by the head-on collision
picture. The dx₄/dt = ic framework retains Theorem 7.7's picture as a
complementary geometric reading (alongside Theorem 7.4's cascade-level
overlap reading and Theorem 7.11's PT-symmetry reading) --- the R4
closure goes through the inner product, with Theorem 7.7's head-on
collision picture now optional secondary physical content rather than
the structural source of the conjugation.}

\textbf{Remark 7.8 (the conjugate sphere identified physically).}
Theorem 7.4 established that ψ\^{}*ψ at the detection event is the
geometric overlap of the forward x₄-expansion and the conjugate
x₄-expansion at that event, but left the physical referent of the
conjugate sphere open --- it could have been read as a purely formal
partner of ψ, an ``orientation-reversed image'' with no independent
physical existence. Theorem 7.7 identifies the conjugate sphere
physically: it is the absorber's own forward x₄-expansion, viewed from
the emitter's frame, where it appears antiparallel in x₄. The ``two
expansions meeting at B'' of Theorem 7.4 is, in mechanism, two McGucken
spheres of two physical particles intersecting head-on at B, with the
x₄-momenergy cancellation forcing the rotation out of x₄ (Theorem 12.2)
and the 3-spatial localization of both at B (Corollary 11.4).

\textbf{Remark 7.9 (universality across particle types).} The mechanism
applies uniformly to all canonical detection events. For photon
detection on a photographic grain (§12.6.1), particle B is the absorbing
bound electron in the AgBr crystal whose own McGucken sphere is
propagating from its bound-state center at the crystal lattice site; the
head-on collision at the lattice site is the photon-electron interaction
that deposits the latent image. For radioactive alpha detection
(§12.6.2), particle B is the absorbing atomic electron in the
scintillator or ionization detector, with the same head-on x₄-collision
picture applying --- the alpha's massive McGucken sphere meets the
electron's bound-state McGucken sphere at the ionization point, the
x₄-momenergy cancels (modulo binding-energy corrections), and both are
localized in the spatial slice as a track segment of the post-collision
pair. Both photon and massive-particle cases are instances of the
universal head-on x₄-collision mechanism.

\textbf{Remark 7.10 (the bilinearity of the rank-2 metric grounded in
the head-on collision).} Lemma 7.1 derived the bilinearity of the Born
density from the rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric. Theorem 7.7
supplies the physical content of that bilinearity: the two-particle
head-on collision requires the simultaneous arrival of two independent
McGucken spheres at the collision point, with the local rate
proportional to the product of their two amplitudes. The rank-2 of the
metric (Lemma 2.5) and the bilinearity of the Born rule (Lemma 7.1) are
not abstract formal facts about pairings; they are the algebraic record
of the two-particle character of the head-on x₄-collision mechanism. The
exponent 2 in P = \textbar ψ\textbar² counts the number of physical
participants in the collision: emitter and absorber, two McGucken
spheres, two x₄-momenta cancelling head-on.

\hypertarget{the-published-objections-to-the-transactional-interpretation-and-their-resolution-under-dxux2084dt-ic}{%
\paragraph{7.5.2 The published objections to the Transactional
Interpretation, and their resolution under dx₄/dt =
ic}\label{the-published-objections-to-the-transactional-interpretation-and-their-resolution-under-dxux2084dt-ic}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c, forward, as a
spherically symmetric wavefront from every event of spacetime. The
Transactional Interpretation faces a set of published objections, and
every one of them traces to a single feature --- its treatment of the
confirmation wave ψ* as a real wave propagating backward in time.
Because the McGucken derivation of §7.5 obtains ψ* as a forward advance
oppositely directed along the shared normal, rather than as a
backward-in-time wave, each objection is resolved or dissolved. The
objections are quoted from the literature and answered point by point.

\textbf{Objection 1 --- retrocausality and causal paradoxes.} In the
Transactional Interpretation the confirmation wave ``propagate{[}s{]}
backward in time'' (Cramer {[}57{]}), and, as the literature notes,
``advanced causation always raises the specter of paradoxes.''
\emph{Resolution.} Under dx₄/dt = ic the conjugate wave is not a
backward-in-time wave. The detector's McGucken Sphere advances forward
at +ic, like the source's, and its amplitude enters the Born density
conjugated because the pairing of the two amplitudes at the shared
tangent point is the sesquilinear inner product of the derived Hilbert
space, with the Kirchhoff wavelet read inward along the common normal
carrying the conjugate phase (§7.5); conjugation is a property of the
pairing at the head-on arrival, with no reversal of time and no reversal
of either Sphere's advance. Both Spheres advance forward in time, so
there is no advanced wave and no possibility of the causal loops that
advanced causation introduces.

\textbf{Objection 2 --- Maudlin's contingent-absorber objection.}
Maudlin argued that the Transactional Interpretation ``gave rise to
inconsistencies and causal loop problems based on situations with
moveable absorbers whose availability to the emitter is contingent on a
particular detected outcome'' {[}59{]}; the objection turns on an
absorber ``just sitting out there in the future, waiting to absorb,''
whose configuration is ``not determined by the state vector at t₀''
{[}60{]}. \emph{Resolution.} The objection is specific to retrocausal
schemes: it requires a future absorber whose backward-in-time
confirmation wave reaches back to the emission event. The McGucken
dx₄/dt = ic framework has no backward-in-time wave and no future
absorber fixing the past --- the conjugate advance is the detector
Sphere's forward, present-time expansion meeting the source Sphere
head-on (§7.5). The contingent-absorber paradox cannot be mounted,
because the advanced wave it depends on is absent from the derivation.

\textbf{Objection 3 --- the pseudotime problem.} Maudlin observed that
in Cramer's account the offer--confirmation ``echoing process'' that
sets the probabilities ``take{[}s{]} place in pseudotime only (rather
than in real time) and thus cannot be said to have taken place at all,''
so that ``the uncollapsed wavefunction never actually exists'' {[}59{]}.
\emph{Resolution.} There is no pseudotime in the McGucken derivation.
The Born density ψψ* = \textbar ψ\textbar² is a single physical overlap
at the shared tangent point, occurring in ordinary coordinate time as
the two forward-advancing Spheres meet (§7.5). The wavefunction is the
real forward advance of the source Sphere, present in real time up to
the meeting; nothing is relegated to a pseudotemporal echo, so nothing
``fails to take place.''

\textbf{Objection 4 --- the perfect-absorber requirement.} The
Transactional Interpretation, following Wheeler--Feynman, requires ``a
fully absorbing background universe'' so that ``a full set of
confirmation waves'' always returns to the emitter {[}60{]}.
\emph{Resolution.} No perfect-absorber condition is needed. dx₄/dt = ic
operates at every event of the actual universe, and the conjugate
advance is supplied locally by the detector's own Sphere at the point of
interaction (§7.5), not by a global return of advanced waves from all
future absorbers. The derivation holds in the real, boundary-free,
accelerating universe, without the Wheeler--Feynman boundary condition
(§5.7.5).

\textbf{Objection 5 --- the determinism/stochasticity gap.} Maudlin
noted that the stimulation of offer and confirmation waves ``occurs
deterministically, leaving a gaping hole in any explanation the
transactional interpretation might provide of the stochastic nature of
quantum mechanics'' {[}59{]} --- the interpretation gives the
probabilities but not what selects the single actual transaction.
\emph{Resolution.} The single actualization is the physical Wick
rotation localizing the one Sphere at the detector where its expanding
surface collides head-on (§7.4, §7.9); the outcome is the physical
localization of the advancing Sphere into a definite spatial event, not
an unexplained selection among deterministic echoes. In the entangled
case the question of ``which'' dissolves entirely: an entangled pair
from a common source is one Sphere measured at two points (§5.9), so
there are not two outcomes to be selected between but one Sphere read
twice.

\textbf{Objection 6 --- untestability.} A recurring objection to the
Transactional Interpretation is that, being empirically identical to
standard quantum mechanics, ``it is not testable'' {[}60{]}.
\emph{Resolution.} The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework is not an
interpretation that reproduces the same predictions; it is a derivation
from a physical principle that yields a falsifiable prediction
distinguishing it --- a curvature (tidal) dependence of the Born measure
of order \(R_{0i0j}L^iL^j\) between outcome branches separated by L
(§9). Where the Transactional Interpretation cannot be tested against
quantum mechanics, dx₄/dt = ic can.

Every objection to the Transactional Interpretation traces to the
reality of a backward-in-time confirmation wave. The McGucken dx₄/dt =
ic framework retains what the Transactional Interpretation established
--- that the confirmation ψ* is physical, that the source supplies ψ and
the detector supplies ψ\emph{, and that the Born density is their
product --- while deriving ψ} as the detector Sphere's forward advance
oppositely directed at the meeting point (§7.5), so that retrocausality,
the contingent-absorber paradox, pseudotime, the perfect-absorber
requirement, the stochasticity gap, and untestability are resolved
together.

\hypertarget{the-sphere-of-detectors-the-born-rule-forced-by-closed-geometry-isotropy-and-one-quantum}{%
\subsubsection{7.6 The sphere of detectors: the Born rule forced by
closed geometry, isotropy, and one
quantum}\label{the-sphere-of-detectors-the-born-rule-forced-by-closed-geometry-isotropy-and-one-quantum}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic
states that the fourth dimension expands at the rate c, isotropically,
as a spherically symmetric wavefront --- the McGucken Sphere --- from
every event of spacetime. A single thought experiment exhibits the Born
rule as forced by that expansion, with each of its three components ---
normalization, the \textbar ψ\textbar² measure, and a single definite
outcome --- compelled by a physical fact of the setup rather than
assumed as a probability postulate. Consider a single-photon source at
the center of a closed sphere of detectors: short-wavelength photons, a
detector surface of unit quantum efficiency with no gaps, so that the
photon cannot pass between detectors or escape.

\textbf{Fact 1: the photon must be detected --- normalization.} The
sphere is closed and the detection surface is complete, so there is no
gap through which the photon can escape; detection somewhere on the
sphere is certain. This forces the normalization of the Born measure:
the total probability of detection is one, not as an axiom imposed on
the theory but as a consequence of the closed geometry, which makes ∫
\textbar ψ\textbar² dμ = 1 a physical fact --- the photon, riding the
expanding McGucken Sphere outward at c, reaches the enclosing detector
surface with certainty and is registered. The normalization of the Born
rule is the closure of the geometry.

\textbf{Fact 2: it can be detected by any detector --- the
\textbar ψ\textbar² measure.} The expansion dx₄/dt = ic is isotropic: x₄
advances perpendicular to all three spatial dimensions equally (§2), so
no ray from the source is privileged, because a preferred detector would
be a preferred spatial direction, which the isotropy of the expansion
forbids. Every detector on the sphere stands on equal geometric footing
with respect to the source's expanding Sphere. This forces the form of
the measure: the distribution over which detector registers the photon
is the unique isotropic measure on the sphere of directions, the
SO(3)-invariant Haar measure dμ = sinθ dθ dφ / 4π (§3.2, §A.1), which is
the Born measure. Equal geometric standing among the detectors yields
equal-solid-angle detection probability; the \textbar ψ\textbar² form of
the Born rule is the isotropy of the x₄-expansion read on the
directional cross-section.

\textbf{Fact 3: it must be detected by exactly one detector ---
definiteness.} The photon is one quantum: one Compton-tick unit of
action h carried by one expanding Sphere. Detection is one head-on
collision --- the physical Wick rotation at which the source's expanding
Sphere meets a detector's Sphere and the perpendicular x₄-advance is
localized into a single spatial event (§7.4, §7.5, §7.9). One quantum
registered at one first-contact collision forces a single definite
outcome: one detector fires, not a distribution of partial detections.
Definiteness is the single-quantum, single-collision character of the
event.

\textbf{The three facts together are the Born rule.} The photon must
land (normalization, ∫\textbar ψ\textbar² = 1), it can land anywhere
with equal geometric right (the isotropic \textbar ψ\textbar² measure),
and it lands at exactly one place (a single definite outcome). These are
the three contents of the Born rule --- certainty of detection, the
\textbar ψ\textbar² distribution, and one outcome --- and each is
compelled by a physical feature of the setup: the closed detector
surface, the isotropy of the x₄-expansion, and the single-quantum
collision. Standard quantum mechanics asserts the Born rule as a
postulate; here the closed sphere of detectors around the expanding
McGucken Sphere forces each of its three parts.

\textbf{Single trial versus the ensemble.} A single photon registers at
one detector, which is compatible with any distribution and exposes
nothing about the measure. It is the statistics over many photons that
reveal the isotropic \textbar ψ\textbar² distribution, because that
distribution is the imprint on the ensemble of the one isotropically
expanding spherical wavefront: the McGucken Sphere is invisible in a
single shot and manifest in the ensemble. This is why the Born measure
is a property read from repeated detections rather than from one --- the
ensemble is the sphere's directional-count Ω made visible (§6).

\textbf{The general case.} For an isotropic source the measure is
uniform on the sphere, so equal detectors receive equal probability, and
the derivation above is complete as stated. For a source prepared in a
state ψ with directional structure --- a dipole emission, a prepared
momentum --- the detection distribution is \textbar ψ\textbar² but not
uniform: the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure on the advance-state space is
modulated by the amplitude structure of ψ itself (§3, §A.1). The
sphere-of-detectors argument forces the Born rule in full for the
symmetric case and, for the general case, forces its three components
--- normalization from closure, the \textbar ψ\textbar² form from the
invariant measure on the advance-state space, and definiteness from the
single-quantum collision --- with the state's amplitude structure
supplying the modulation of the invariant measure derived in §3.

\textbf{The residual.} What the geometry does not fix is which detector
fires on a given trial. That the photon must be caught (Fact 1), can be
caught anywhere (Fact 2), and is caught once (Fact 3) is forced; which
detector-electron achieves the head-on collision first, as the wavefront
arrives at the closed sphere, is the single sited residual --- either
hidden-deterministic in the microstate of the winning detector-electron,
or irreducibly chancy. Every component that the Born rule states is
supplied by the expanding McGucken Sphere and the closed geometry; the
one quantity left open is the microstate of the winner of the arrival
race, which the present derivation does not claim to determine.

\hypertarget{the-two-channel-form-the-identification-lives-at-the-mcgucken-sphere-level}{%
\subsection{8. The two-channel form: the identification lives at the
McGucken Sphere
level}\label{the-two-channel-form-the-identification-lives-at-the-mcgucken-sphere-level}}

The McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) --- the fourth dimension
expanding at c as a spherically symmetric wavefront from every event ---
generates one McGucken Sphere at every point, and the framework
describes that one Sphere through two channels, the Geometric and the
Algebraic. Because both channels describe the same Sphere generated by
the same Principle, the identification of Section 7 lives below the
level at which the descriptions divide, at the level of the McGucken
Sphere itself, and hence at the level of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) {[}28{]}. This
section exhibits that, because it is the difference between a
cross-channel coincidence and a single fact about one object.

The McGucken \(dx_4/dt = ic\) framework describes the McGucken Sphere
through two channels, the Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel,
the two faces of the McGucken Duality {[}28{]}. It would be an
oversimplification to assign gravity to the Geometric Channel and the
Born rule to the Algebraic Channel, as though the identity ``gravity is
the Born rule'' were a bridge built between the two channels by external
construction. Both channels derive both quantities, and this four-corner
completeness is what places the identification below the channel
division, at the level of the McGucken Sphere.

In the Geometric Channel, the McGucken Sphere yields gravity through its
null hypersurfaces and the Clausius relation δQ = TδS, the Jacobson
route of Section 5 {[}1, 25{]}. In the same Geometric Channel, the
McGucken Sphere yields the Born rule through the Fubini--Study metric on
its directional cross-section, which Wootters identified with the
Fisher--Rao statistical distance {[}9{]}: the geometry of the Sphere's
directions is at once a metric geometry and a statistical
distinguishability geometry, and the Born rule is the map between them.

In the Algebraic Channel, the McGucken Sphere yields gravity through the
metric read as a quantum operator whose quantum relative entropy is the
gravitational action, reducing to Einstein--Hilbert in the low-coupling
limit --- the route of Bianconi {[}4{]}. In the same Algebraic Channel,
the McGucken Sphere yields the Born rule through its SO(3)-invariant
Haar measure pulled back to Hilbert-space rays as p =
\textbar⟨ψ\textbar φ⟩\textbar², the derivation of Section 3 {[}19,
20{]}.

Each channel independently yields both facts. If a channel yielded only
one endpoint, the identity ``gravity is the Born rule'' would be a
cross-channel coincidence --- one physical fact reached by two
mathematical routes that meet at their intersection. The four-corner
completeness shows instead that both quantities are facts about the
shared McGucken Sphere and its Haar measure, and that every channel
accessing the Sphere sees both. The channel-independence places the
equality at the McGucken Sphere level: gravity and the Born rule are the
same fact about Σ₊(p), before any channel decomposition, and the
Duality's two channels are two confirmations of the identity rather than
its two halves {[}28{]}. The Planck-length scale bridge that relates the
horizon reading and the event reading of the count Ω is the same in both
channels, because it is a property of the McGucken Sphere's one-cycle
resolution and not of the channel through which the Sphere is described.

\hypertarget{falsifiability}{%
\subsection{9. Falsifiability}\label{falsifiability}}

The McGucken Principle \(dx_4/dt = ic\) makes a physical claim about the
world --- that the fourth dimension expands at c from every event ---
and a physical claim must be refutable. The identity ``gravity is the
Born rule,'' both being the entropy S = k ln Ω of the one expanding
McGucken Sphere that \(dx_4/dt = ic\) generates, is refutable in four
ways, each a test of a consequence of \(dx_4/dt = ic\), and the fourth
is the distinguishing one. The McGucken \(dx_4/dt = ic\) framework has
already been applied to five quantum-mechanics, general-relativity, and
thermodynamics experiments {[}36{]}; the tests below extend that program
to the identity of this paper.

First, the identity fails if the Born exponent is not two. The
identification requires that the invariant measure on the McGucken
Sphere's directions be the quadratic \textbar ψ\textbar², forced by the
rank-two metric and unitarity (Section 3) {[}19{]}. A measured deviation
--- a probability rule \textbar ψ\textbar\^{}p with p ≠ 2 at any scale
--- would refute the identification, because the horizon count and the
surface count could no longer be the same SO(3)-invariant measure. Tests
of the Born rule's exponent, such as the absence of third-order
interference in triple-slit experiments, bound the identification, and
present bounds are consistent with p = 2.

Second, the identity fails if the Bekenstein--Hawking coefficient is not
the count of Planck-scale McGucken Spheres. The gravitational reading
requires S = A/4ℓ\_P² to be the number of Compton-tick boundary modes
tiling the horizon, one per Planck area {[}31{]}. A measured black-hole
entropy departing from A/4ℓ\_P² by other than the known logarithmic
