\hypertarget{arakiuhlmann-relative-entropy-as-a-theorem-of-dx_4dt-ic-the-type-mathrmiii_1-von-neumann-algebra-generalization-of-the-step-5-umegaki-material-via-tomitatakesaki-standard-form-on-the-wedge-algebra-with-modular-conjugation-j-identified-as-pt-reflection-through-the-source-event-per-bisognanowichmann-19751976}{%
\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{22.3.9 Araki--Uhlmann relative entropy as
a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) --- the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\)
von-Neumann-algebra generalization of the Step-5 Umegaki material, via
Tomita--Takesaki standard form on the wedge algebra with modular
conjugation \(J\) identified as PT reflection through the source event
per Bisognano--Wichmann
1975/1976}{22.3.9 Araki--Uhlmann relative entropy as a theorem of dx\_4/dt = ic --- the type-\textbackslash mathrm\{III\}\_1 von-Neumann-algebra generalization of the Step-5 Umegaki material, via Tomita--Takesaki standard form on the wedge algebra with modular conjugation J identified as PT reflection through the source event per Bisognano--Wichmann 1975/1976}}\label{arakiuhlmann-relative-entropy-as-a-theorem-of-dx_4dt-ic-the-type-mathrmiii_1-von-neumann-algebra-generalization-of-the-step-5-umegaki-material-via-tomitatakesaki-standard-form-on-the-wedge-algebra-with-modular-conjugation-j-identified-as-pt-reflection-through-the-source-event-per-bisognanowichmann-19751976}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} Under \(dx_4/dt = ic\) the fourth
dimension expands at the velocity of light \(c\) in a spherically
symmetric manner from every spacetime event, with the imaginary unit
\(i\) marking perpendicularity of \(x_4\) to the three spatial axes
\(x_1, x_2, x_3\) and with the McGucken Sphere \(\Sigma_+(p)\) at every
event \(p\) carrying the Compton wavelength \(\lambda_C = h/(mc)\) that
sets the quantum of action \(h = \lambda_C \cdot mc\) per Compton-cycle
of its \(x_4\)-expansion (Theorem 22.5.4 of the present paper, the
two-bounds architecture: \(\hbar\) as entropy floor, \(c\) as speed
ceiling, both attributes of the one Sphere). Theorem 22.3's four-corner
identification of gravity \(=\) Born rule as the same
\(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-invariant Haar measure \(\mu_H\) on \(\Sigma_+(p)\)
read at two scales of integration (horizon-integrated versus
event-pointwise) covers the finite-dimensional (type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\))
case through the Umegaki 1962 relative entropy
\(S(\rho \| \sigma) = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho \log \rho - \rho \log \sigma)\)
cited at reference {[}481{]} (ContextualBornEntropy2025) in Line B of
§22.3.2 and at Bianconi 2025 reference {[}476{]} in Line A. The present
subsection lifts this identification from the type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\)
setting to the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) von-Neumann-algebra setting that
algebraic quantum field theory requires at horizons and wedges, by
deriving the Araki 1976/1977 relative entropy of states on the
Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra as a theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\), with
the Tomita--Takesaki modular conjugation \(J\) identified geometrically
through the Bisognano--Wichmann 1975/1976 theorem as PT (parity-time)
reflection through the source event \(p\). The Uhlmann 1977 monotonicity
of the Araki relative entropy under completely positive unital normal
maps --- the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) data-processing inequality that
generalizes the Lindblad 1975 monotonicity of the Umegaki relative
entropy under completely positive maps on finite-dimensional matrix
algebras --- is derived in §22.3.10 below from the
\(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-Haar-measure contraction under coarse-graining of the
McGucken Sphere via the Stinespring 1955 dilation.

\textbf{Tomita--Takesaki standard-form notation.} For a von Neumann
algebra \(\mathcal{M}\) (algebra of bounded operators on a Hilbert space
\(\mathcal{H}\) closed under weak-operator topology and containing the
identity) acting on a Hilbert space \(\mathcal{H}\), the \emph{standard
form} (Araki 1974, \emph{Pacific J. Math.} \textbf{50}, 309--354;
Haagerup 1975, \emph{Math. Scand.} \textbf{37}, 271--283) is the
quadruple \((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{H}, J, \mathcal{P})\) where: -
\(\mathcal{M}\) is the observable algebra; - \(\mathcal{H}\) is the
Hilbert space on which \(\mathcal{M}\) acts; -
\(J : \mathcal{H} \to \mathcal{H}\) is an antiunitary involution
(\(J^2 = \mathbf{1}\),
\(\langle J\xi | J\eta \rangle = \langle\eta|\xi\rangle\)), called the
\emph{modular conjugation}; - \(\mathcal{P} \subset \mathcal{H}\) is a
closed convex self-dual cone, called the \emph{natural positive cone};

satisfying: (a) \(J \mathcal{M} J = \mathcal{M}'\) where
\(\mathcal{M}'\) is the commutant of \(\mathcal{M}\); (b)
\(J \xi = \xi\) for all \(\xi \in \mathcal{P}\); (c)
\(a J a J \in \mathcal{P}\) for all \(a \in \mathcal{M}\); (d) every
normal state \(\varphi\) on \(\mathcal{M}\) is represented by a unique
vector \(\Phi \in \mathcal{P}\) with
\(\varphi(a) = \langle\Phi | a\Phi\rangle\) for all
\(a \in \mathcal{M}\). The Haagerup 1975 theorem states that the
standard form exists and is unique up to unitary equivalence for every
von Neumann algebra.

For a cyclic separating vector \(\Phi \in \mathcal{H}\) for
\(\mathcal{M}\) (meaning the subspace \(\mathcal{M}\Phi\) is dense in
\(\mathcal{H}\), and \(a\Phi = 0\) with \(a \in \mathcal{M}\) implies
\(a = 0\)), the \emph{Tomita operator} \(S_\Phi\) is the closed
antilinear operator defined by \(S_\Phi(a\Phi) = a^* \Phi\) for all
\(a \in \mathcal{M}\). Its polar decomposition
\[S_\Phi = J \Delta_\Phi^{1/2}\] defines the \emph{modular operator}
\(\Delta_\Phi\) (positive self-adjoint, generally unbounded) and the
modular conjugation \(J\). The \emph{Tomita--Takesaki theorem} (Takesaki
1970, \emph{Lecture Notes in Mathematics} \textbf{128}, Springer,
Berlin) states:
\[\Delta_\Phi^{it} \, \mathcal{M} \, \Delta_\Phi^{-it} = \mathcal{M} \quad \text{for all } t \in \mathbb{R},\]
so the \emph{modular flow}
\(\sigma_t^\varphi(a) \equiv \Delta_\Phi^{it} a \Delta_\Phi^{-it}\) is a
one-parameter group of automorphisms of \(\mathcal{M}\). The state
\(\varphi(a) = \langle\Phi | a\Phi\rangle\) is a KMS state with respect
to \(\sigma_t^\varphi\) at inverse temperature \(-1\):
\[\varphi(a \, \sigma_{-i}^\varphi(b)) = \varphi(ba) \quad \text{for } a, b \in \mathcal{M}\]
(KMS condition in the Haag--Hugenholtz--Winnink 1967 formulation,
\emph{Commun. Math. Phys.} \textbf{5}, 215--236).

\textbf{Relative modular operator.} For two faithful normal states
\(\varphi, \psi\) on \(\mathcal{M}\) with representing vectors
\(\Phi, \Psi \in \mathcal{P}\) (both cyclic separating), the
\emph{relative Tomita operator} \(S_{\Psi|\Phi}\) is defined (Araki
1973, ``Relative Hamiltonian for faithful normal states of a von Neumann
algebra,'' \emph{Publ. RIMS Kyoto Univ.} \textbf{9}, 165--209) by
closing the map
\[S_{\Psi|\Phi}(a\Phi) = a^* \Psi \quad \text{for } a \in \mathcal{M}.\]
Its polar decomposition \[S_{\Psi|\Phi} = J \Delta_{\Psi|\Phi}^{1/2}\]
defines the \emph{relative modular operator} \(\Delta_{\Psi|\Phi}\).
When \(\Psi = \Phi\), \(\Delta_{\Psi|\Phi}\) reduces to the modular
operator \(\Delta_\Phi\). The modular conjugation \(J\) in the polar
decomposition is the same \(J\) of the standard form (independent of
which state is used).

\textbf{Araki relative entropy.} The \emph{Araki relative entropy} of
\(\varphi\) with respect to \(\psi\) (Araki 1976, ``Relative entropy of
states of von Neumann algebras,'' \emph{Publ. RIMS Kyoto Univ.}
\textbf{11} (3), 809--833, Eq. (1-1), p.~809) is
\[\boxed{\; S(\varphi \| \psi) \;=\; \begin{cases} -\langle\Phi \,|\, \log \Delta_{\Psi|\Phi} \,|\, \Phi\rangle, & \text{if } \mathrm{supp}(\varphi) \leq \mathrm{supp}(\psi), \\ +\infty, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}\;}\]
Araki 1977 (\emph{Publ. RIMS Kyoto Univ.} \textbf{13}, 173--192) proves:
(a) non-negativity \(S(\varphi\|\psi) \geq 0\) with equality iff
\(\varphi = \psi\); (b) joint lower semi-continuity in
\((\varphi, \psi)\); (c) joint convexity; (d) reduction to the Umegaki
form in the type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\) case.

\textbf{Type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\) reduction.} When
\(\mathcal{M} = B(\mathcal{H})\) with \(\dim \mathcal{H} = n < \infty\)
(type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\) factor), the states \(\varphi, \psi\) are
represented by density matrices \(\rho_\varphi, \rho_\psi\), and the
relative modular operator acts on
\(\mathcal{H} \otimes \overline{\mathcal{H}}\) as the operator
\(\rho_\psi \otimes \rho_\varphi^{-1}\) (where
\(\overline{\mathcal{H}}\) is the complex-conjugate Hilbert space and
\(\mathcal{H} \otimes \overline{\mathcal{H}}\) is the Hilbert--Schmidt
representation space). The Araki entropy reduces to the Umegaki 1962
form (Umegaki, ``Conditional expectation in an operator algebra, IV
(entropy and information),'' \emph{Kodai Math. Sem. Rep.} \textbf{14},
59--85):
\[S(\varphi \| \psi) = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho_\varphi \log \rho_\varphi - \rho_\varphi \log \rho_\psi),\]
which is the Line-B entropy of Theorem 22.3 Step 5 cited at reference
{[}481{]} (ContextualBornEntropy2025, \emph{Entropy} \textbf{27}(9),
898) and the Line-A entropy cited at reference {[}476{]} (Bianconi 2025,
\emph{Phys. Rev.~D} \textbf{111}, 066001). The type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\)
reduction is what makes Theorem 22.3's four-corner identification
applicable in both the horizon-tier Bekenstein--Hawking regime and the
event-tier Born-rule regime at finite resolution.

\textbf{Theorem 22.3.9 (Araki--Uhlmann relative entropy as a theorem of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) --- standard-form derivation on the wedge algebra
generated by the McGucken Sphere).} \emph{Let \(p\) be an event of
\(\mathcal{M}_G\) with McGucken Sphere \(\Sigma_+(p)\) generated at rate
\(c\) in the \(+ic\) direction by \(dx_4/dt = ic\). Let \(W_R(p)\) be
the right Rindler wedge of \(p\) --- the maximal causal diamond of a
uniformly accelerated worldline passing through \(p\), specifically the
region \(\{x : x^1 > |x^0|\}\) with origin translated to \(p\). Then:}

\emph{(i) \textbf{(Wedge algebra, type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\))} The algebra
of local observables on \(W_R(p)\) is a von Neumann algebra
\(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\) of Murray--von Neumann type \(\mathrm{III}_1\)
(Araki 1964, ``Type of von Neumann algebra associated with free field,''
Prog. Theor. Phys. \textbf{32}, 956--965, establishing type
\(\mathrm{III}\) for the free scalar field; Fredenhagen 1985, ``On the
modular structure of local algebras of observables,'' Commun. Math.
Phys. \textbf{97} (1), 79--89, refining to type \(\mathrm{III}_1\) for
all local algebras in asymptotically scale-invariant quantum field
theories via the asymptotic-scale-invariance argument on the
modular-operator spectra; Buchholz--D'Antoni--Fredenhagen 1987, ``The
universal structure of local algebras,'' Commun. Math. Phys.
\textbf{111} (1), 123--135, extending the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\)
characterization to the universal structure of local algebras), acting
on the Sphere-cogenerated Hilbert space \(\mathcal{H}\) of the
Minkowski-space / Hilbert-space cogeneration {[}MG-Minkowski-Hilbert{]}.
The type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) character is what prevents a direct
trace-class density-matrix representation and is why the Umegaki form of
Theorem 22.3 Step 5 does not extend directly: a general
type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) relative entropy requires the modular-theoretic
formulation of Araki 1976.}

\emph{(ii) \textbf{(Reeh--Schlieder cyclic separating vacuum)} The
vacuum state \(\Omega\) is cyclic and separating for
\(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\) by the Reeh--Schlieder theorem (Reeh and Schlieder
1961, ``Bemerkungen zur Unitäräquivalenz von Lorentzinvarianten
Feldern,'' Nuovo Cimento \textbf{22}, 1051--1068). Under
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), the Reeh--Schlieder theorem is a derived consequence
of the Principle's universality at every event (Theorem 3 of the present
paper) combined with the Wightman-axiom reconstruction of the
Sphere-cogenerated Hilbert space {[}MG-Minkowski-Hilbert, §§III-IV{]}:
cyclicity follows from the density of \(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\Omega\) in
\(\mathcal{H}\) (every state is approximable by local operations in any
open region), and the separating property follows from locality (the
commutant structure of the Haag--Kastler net).}

\emph{(iii) \textbf{(Standard form existence and uniqueness)} The
standard form \((\mathcal{M}(W_R), \mathcal{H}, J, \mathcal{P})\) exists
and is unique up to unitary equivalence (Haagerup 1975, ``The standard
form of von Neumann algebras,'' Math. Scand. \textbf{37}, 271--283,
Theorem 1.6).}

\emph{(iv) \textbf{(Bisognano--Wichmann geometric identification of
modular objects)} The modular objects for the wedge algebra are
identified geometrically by the Bisognano--Wichmann theorem (Bisognano
and Wichmann 1975, ``On the duality condition for a Hermitian scalar
field,'' J. Math. Phys. \textbf{16}, 985--1007, for the Hermitian scalar
case; Bisognano and Wichmann 1976, ``On the duality condition for
quantum fields,'' J. Math. Phys. \textbf{17}, 303--321, for general
Wightman fields):}
\[\Delta_\Omega^{it} = U(\Lambda_{x^1}(-2\pi t)), \qquad J = \Theta \cdot R_1(\pi),\]
\emph{where \(U\) is the unitary representation of the Poincaré group on
\(\mathcal{H}\), \(\Lambda_{x^1}(s)\) is the Lorentz boost with rapidity
\(s\) in the \(x^1\)-direction, \(\Theta\) is CPT (charge-parity-time)
conjugation (Lüders 1954; Pauli 1955), and \(R_1(\pi)\) is the spatial
rotation by angle \(\pi\) about the \(x^1\)-axis. For a Hermitian scalar
field \(\phi(x)\) localized at spacetime point
\(x = (x^0, x^1, x^2, x^3)\), the modular conjugation acts as}
\[J \,\phi(x^0, x^1, x^2, x^3) \, J^{-1} = \phi^*(-x^0, -x^1, x^2, x^3),\]
\emph{which is a reflection in the \((x^0, x^1)\)-plane (fixing
\(x^2, x^3\)) composed with Hermitian conjugation of the field.}

\emph{(v) \textbf{(McGucken reading of \(J\) as PT reflection through
the source event \(p\))} Under the McGucken-Wick coordinate
identification \(\tau_W = x_4/c\) ({[}McWick, Theorem 30.9.2{]}) and the
Minkowski-space coordinate relation \(x_4 = ict\), the
\(x^0\)-reflection \(x^0 \mapsto -x^0\) of (iv) corresponds to the
\(x_4\)-reflection \(x_4 \mapsto -x_4\). This is the geometric operation
that would swap the forward McGucken Sphere \(\Sigma_+(p)\) and the
time-reversed Sphere \(\Sigma_-(p)\). Under \(dx_4/dt = +ic\) (sign
fixed by Theorem 3 property (c) of the present paper as a physical fact
of the Principle), the backward Sphere \(\Sigma_-(p)\) is geometrically
excluded; the modular conjugation \(J\) therefore acts at the
single-Sphere level as the formal PT reflection through \(p\) --- the
operation that, if executed on the realized Sphere \(\Sigma_+(p)\),
would produce the excluded \(\Sigma_-(p)\). This PT identification
supplies the geometry that the orthodox Bisognano--Wichmann treatment
leaves at the level of formal CPT conjugation + spatial rotation.}

\emph{(vi) \textbf{(Modular flow as Wick-rotated \(x_4\)-translation and
KMS/Unruh identification)} The modular flow
\(\sigma_t^\Omega(a) = \Delta_\Omega^{it} a \Delta_\Omega^{-it}\) is the
Lorentz boost in the \((x^0, x^1)\)-direction with boost parameter
\(-2\pi t\). Under the McGucken-Wick identification \(\tau_W = x_4/c\),
this boost is the Wick-rotated \(x_4\)-translation generator --- the
Euclidean rotation in the \((\tau_W, x^1)\)-plane by angle \(2\pi t\),
closing on itself at \(t = 1\) (period one, i.e., KMS periodicity
\(\tau_W = 2\pi/\kappa_{\text{Rindler}} = \beta \hbar\) at inverse
temperature \(\beta = 2\pi/(\hbar \kappa_{\text{Rindler}})\)). By the
Unruh effect (Unruh 1976, ``Notes on black-hole evaporation,'' Phys.
Rev.~D \textbf{14}, 870--892), the vacuum \(\Omega\) is a KMS state with
respect to the boost-generated flow at the Unruh temperature
\(T_U = \hbar a / (2\pi c k_B)\) for proper acceleration \(a\). The
modular flow identification therefore recovers the Connes--Rovelli
Thermal Time Hypothesis (Connes and Rovelli 1994, ``Von Neumann algebra
automorphisms and time-thermodynamics relation in generally covariant
quantum theories,'' Class. Quantum Grav. \textbf{11}, 2899--2917) as
derived structure --- the Wick-rotated-\(x_4\)-translation reading of
§28.6 of the present paper, with the McGucken-Wick coordinate
identification as the coordinate bridge.}

\emph{(vii) \textbf{(Relative modular operator and Araki relative
entropy on the Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra)} For any two faithful
normal states \(\varphi, \psi\) on \(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\) with
representing vectors \(\Phi, \Psi \in \mathcal{P}\), the relative
modular operator \(\Delta_{\Psi|\Phi}\) exists and is unique by the
Araki 1973 construction. The Araki relative entropy}
\[S(\varphi \| \psi) \;=\; -\langle\Phi \,|\, \log \Delta_{\Psi|\Phi} \,|\, \Phi\rangle\]
\emph{(Araki 1976, Eq. (1-1), p.~809; the finite-dimensional reduction
is Eq. (1-2) on the same page) is thereby a derived quantity on the
Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra, with all four modular objects
\((\mathcal{M}(W_R), \mathcal{H}, J, \mathcal{P})\) supplied by
\(dx_4/dt = ic\): the von-Neumann algebra of the wedge
\(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\) via the Haag--Kastler net on the Sphere-cogenerated
Hilbert space, the Hilbert space \(\mathcal{H}\) via the Minkowski-space
/ Hilbert-space cogeneration, the modular conjugation \(J\) via the
Bisognano--Wichmann identification as PT (parity-time) reflection
through \(p\), and the natural positive cone \(\mathcal{P}\) via the
standard form of Haagerup 1975. The type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\) limit
(restriction to a finite-dimensional subalgebra of \(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\))
reduces \(S(\varphi\|\psi)\) to the Umegaki form of Theorem 22.3 Step 5,
closing the extension from the finite-dimensional Line-B / Line-A
entropy to the full type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) setting that algebraic
quantum field theory requires at horizons and wedges.}

\textbf{Proof of Theorem 22.3.9.} Six steps.

\emph{Step 1 (Wedge algebra and Sphere-cogenerated Hilbert space, giving
(i)).} By the Minkowski-space / Hilbert-space cogeneration of
{[}MG-Minkowski-Hilbert, §§III-IV{]}, \(dx_4/dt = ic\) generates the
Hilbert space \(\mathcal{H}\) and the Haag--Kastler net
\(O \mapsto \mathcal{M}(O)\) of local von Neumann algebras indexed by
open spacetime regions \(O \subset \mathcal{M}_G\). For the right
Rindler wedge \(W_R(p)\), the algebra \(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\) is a factor
of Murray--von Neumann type \(\mathrm{III}\) by Araki 1964 (free-field
case: \emph{Prog. Theor. Phys.} \textbf{32}, 956--965) refined to type
\(\mathrm{III}_1\) by Fredenhagen 1985 (\emph{Commun. Math. Phys.}
\textbf{97} (1), 79--89, ``On the modular structure of local algebras of
observables''): Fredenhagen shows that in any asymptotically
scale-invariant quantum field theory the spectrum of the modular
operators \(\Delta\) of all local observable algebras equals the full
positive real line \(\mathbb{R}_+^*\) --- this is the Connes 1973
type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) invariant \(T(\mathcal{M}) = \mathbb{R}\)
characterizing the hyperfinite type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) factor. The
result is extended to the universal structure of local algebras by
Buchholz--D'Antoni--Fredenhagen 1987 (\emph{Commun. Math. Phys.}
\textbf{111} (1), 123--135, ``The universal structure of local
algebras''). The type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) character is the
Araki--Fredenhagen field-algebra classification; it is independent of
the Sphere-cogeneration route and holds in any Wightman theory with a
Reeh--Schlieder vacuum. This establishes (i).

\emph{Step 2 (Reeh--Schlieder from \(dx_4/dt = ic\), giving (ii)).} The
Reeh--Schlieder theorem (Reeh and Schlieder 1961, \emph{Nuovo Cimento}
\textbf{22}, 1051--1068, Theorem 1) states that for any Wightman theory
with vacuum \(\Omega\) invariant under the Poincaré representation
\(U\), and for any open spacetime region \(O\) with non-empty interior,
\(\mathcal{M}(O)\Omega\) is dense in \(\mathcal{H}\) and \(\Omega\) is
separating for \(\mathcal{M}(O)\). The Wightman axioms (spectrum
condition, locality, vacuum uniqueness) are derived theorems of
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) via the Minkowski-space / Hilbert-space cogeneration
{[}MG-Minkowski-Hilbert, Theorem 10{]}. The locality axiom follows from
the null-cone causal order generated by the \(x_4 = ict\) coordinate
structure (Theorem 3 of the present paper). The spectrum condition
(positive energy) follows from the \(+ic\) orientation of the Principle.
Vacuum uniqueness follows from the irreducibility of the Poincaré
representation on the Sphere-cogenerated Hilbert space. The
Reeh--Schlieder cyclic-separating property is therefore a derived
consequence of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) via these three derived axioms. This
establishes (ii).

\emph{Step 3 (Standard form, giving (iii)).} By Haagerup 1975
(\emph{Math. Scand.} \textbf{37}, 271--283, Theorem 1.6), every von
Neumann algebra admits a standard form, unique up to unitary
equivalence. Applied to \(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\) with cyclic separating
vacuum \(\Omega\) (Step 2), the standard form
\((\mathcal{M}(W_R), \mathcal{H}, J, \mathcal{P})\) exists and is
unique. The Tomita operator \(S_\Omega\) is defined by closure of
\(a\Omega \mapsto a^*\Omega\) for \(a \in \mathcal{M}(W_R)\); its polar
decomposition \(S_\Omega = J \Delta_\Omega^{1/2}\) identifies \(J\) and
\(\Delta_\Omega\) (Araki 1974, \emph{Pacific J. Math.} \textbf{50},
309--354, §3). This establishes (iii).

\emph{Step 4 (Bisognano--Wichmann identification, giving (iv) and (v)).}
The Bisognano--Wichmann theorem is proved in Bisognano and Wichmann 1975
(\emph{J. Math. Phys.} \textbf{16}, 985--1007, Theorems 1 and 2) for the
free Hermitian scalar field and extended in Bisognano and Wichmann 1976
(\emph{J. Math. Phys.} \textbf{17}, 303--321, Theorem 1) to all Wightman
fields satisfying the Wightman axioms plus the additional analyticity
condition from the Reeh--Schlieder theorem. The theorem's statement: for
the vacuum state \(\Omega\) on the right Rindler wedge algebra
\(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\), the modular operator satisfies
\(\Delta_\Omega^{it} = U(\Lambda_{x^1}(-2\pi t))\) and the modular
conjugation satisfies \(J = \Theta \cdot R_1(\pi)\), where
\(U, \Lambda_{x^1}, \Theta, R_1\) are as in (iv). Under
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), the \(x^0\)-component of the geometric reflection
\((x^0, x^1, x^2, x^3) \mapsto (-x^0, -x^1, x^2, x^3)\) embedded in
\(\Theta\) corresponds to the \(x_4\)-reflection \(x_4 \mapsto -x_4\)
via the Minkowski coordinate relation \(x_4 = ict\) and the
McGucken-Wick identification \(\tau_W = x_4/c\) ({[}McWick, Theorem
30.9.2{]}). The \(x_4 \mapsto -x_4\) reflection is the operation that
swaps \(\Sigma_+(p)\) and \(\Sigma_-(p)\); the geometric exclusion of
\(\Sigma_-(p)\) by \(+ic\) (Theorem 3 property (c) of the present paper)
renders \(J\) as the formal single-Sphere PT reflection through \(p\).
This establishes (iv) and (v).

\emph{Step 5 (Modular flow as Wick-rotated \(x_4\)-translation and Unruh
KMS, giving (vi)).} The modular flow
\(\sigma_t^\Omega(a) = \Delta_\Omega^{it} a \Delta_\Omega^{-it} = U(\Lambda_{x^1}(-2\pi t)) a U(\Lambda_{x^1}(2\pi t))\)
by Step 4. Under the McGucken-Wick coordinate identification
\(\tau_W = x_4/c\), the Minkowski boost \(\Lambda_{x^1}(s)\) in the
\((x^0, x^1)\)-plane is the Wick rotation (angle \(is\)) of the
Euclidean rotation \(R_{(\tau_W, x^1)}(s)\) in the
\((\tau_W, x^1)\)-plane. For boost parameter \(s = -2\pi t\), this is
the Euclidean rotation by angle \(2\pi t\) in the
\((\tau_W, x^1)\)-plane, closing on itself at \(t = 1\). The closure
period in \(\tau_W\) is \(\tau_W = 2\pi / \kappa_{\text{Rindler}}\)
where \(\kappa_{\text{Rindler}}\) is the surface gravity of the Rindler
horizon, giving KMS periodicity \(\tau_W = \beta \hbar\) at Unruh
inverse temperature \(\beta = 2\pi / (\hbar \kappa_{\text{Rindler}})\).
By the Unruh effect (Unruh 1976, \emph{Phys. Rev.~D} \textbf{14},
870--892; Theorem 17 of the present paper), the vacuum \(\Omega\) is a
KMS state at the Unruh temperature \(T_U = \hbar a / (2\pi c k_B)\) for
proper acceleration \(a\) of the wedge observer. The identification of
modular flow with Wick-rotated \(x_4\)-translation is the
Connes--Rovelli Thermal Time Hypothesis (\emph{Class. Quantum Grav.}
\textbf{11}, 2899--2917) recovered as derived structure per §28.6 of the
present paper, with the McGucken-Wick coordinate identification
\(\tau_W = x_4/c\) as the coordinate bridge. For a Schwarzschild
horizon, the boost reduces to the horizon-generating Killing vector and
\(T_U\) reduces to the Hawking temperature
\(T_H = \hbar c^3/(8\pi G M k_B)\) (Theorem 16 of the present paper,
independent derivation via Euclidean cigar closure under the
McGucken-Wick rotation). This establishes (vi).

\emph{Step 6 (Relative modular operator and Araki entropy on the
Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra, giving (vii)).} For two faithful
normal states \(\varphi, \psi\) on \(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\), the Araki 1973
construction (\emph{Publ. RIMS Kyoto Univ.} \textbf{9}, 165--209)
defines the relative Tomita operator \(S_{\Psi|\Phi}\) by closing the
map \(a\Phi \mapsto a^*\Psi\) for \(a \in \mathcal{M}(W_R)\) on the
cyclic subspace \(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\Phi\) (dense in \(\mathcal{H}\) by
Step 2). The polar decomposition
\(S_{\Psi|\Phi} = J \Delta_{\Psi|\Phi}^{1/2}\) (with the same \(J\) as
the standard form) defines \(\Delta_{\Psi|\Phi}\) as the positive
self-adjoint operator in the decomposition. The Araki relative entropy
\[S(\varphi\|\psi) = -\langle\Phi | \log\Delta_{\Psi|\Phi} | \Phi\rangle\]
(Araki 1976, \emph{Publ. RIMS Kyoto Univ.} \textbf{11} (3), 809--833,
Eq. (1-1), p.~809, in the Introduction §1) is then well-defined on the
Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra, with all four standard-form objects
supplied by \(dx_4/dt = ic\) via Steps 1--5. The Araki 1977 (\emph{Publ.
RIMS Kyoto Univ.} \textbf{13} (1), 173--192, ``Relative Entropy for
States of von Neumann Algebras II'') properties --- non-negativity
(Theorem 3.6(1): \(S(\varphi/\psi) \geq 0\) when
\(\varphi(1) = \psi(1) > 0\), with equality iff \(\varphi = \psi\)),
joint lower semi-continuity (Theorem 3.7(1): under norm convergence of
\(\varphi_\alpha, \psi_\alpha\),
\(\liminf S(\varphi_\alpha/\psi_\alpha) \geq S(\varphi/\psi)\)), joint
convexity (Theorem 3.8(1)), and reduction to the Umegaki form in the
type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\) case (via Eq. (1.1) and (1.2) of §1 of Araki 1976,
giving \(S(\varphi/\psi) = \varphi(\log\rho_\varphi - \log\rho_\psi)\)
in the finite-dimensional factor setting) --- follow from the Araki 1976
definition applied to the Sphere-cogenerated standard form. The
type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\) reduction yields Umegaki 1962 (\emph{Kodai Math.
Sem. Rep.} \textbf{14} (2), 59--85, ``Conditional expectation in an
operator algebra, IV (entropy and information)'')
\(S(\varphi\|\psi) = \mathrm{Tr}(\rho_\varphi \log\rho_\varphi - \rho_\varphi \log\rho_\psi)\),
the Line-B entropy of Theorem 22.3 Step 5 cited at reference {[}481{]}
and the Line-A entropy cited at reference {[}476{]}. This establishes
(vii) and completes the proof of Theorem 22.3.9. \(\blacksquare\)

\hypertarget{uhlmann-1977-monotonicity-of-the-araki-relative-entropy-under-completely-positive-unital-normal-maps-the-type-mathrmiii_1-data-processing-inequality-derived-from-the-mathrmso3-haar-measure-contraction-under-coarse-graining-of-the-mcgucken-sphere}{%
\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{22.3.10 Uhlmann 1977 monotonicity of the
Araki relative entropy under completely positive unital normal maps ---
the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) data-processing inequality derived from the
\(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-Haar-measure contraction under coarse-graining of the
McGucken
Sphere}{22.3.10 Uhlmann 1977 monotonicity of the Araki relative entropy under completely positive unital normal maps --- the type-\textbackslash mathrm\{III\}\_1 data-processing inequality derived from the \textbackslash mathrm\{SO\}(3)-Haar-measure contraction under coarse-graining of the McGucken Sphere}}\label{uhlmann-1977-monotonicity-of-the-araki-relative-entropy-under-completely-positive-unital-normal-maps-the-type-mathrmiii_1-data-processing-inequality-derived-from-the-mathrmso3-haar-measure-contraction-under-coarse-graining-of-the-mcgucken-sphere}}

\textbf{McGucken Principle anchor.} Under \(dx_4/dt = ic\) the McGucken
Sphere \(\Sigma_+(p)\) at every event \(p\) carries the unique
\(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-invariant Haar probability measure \(\mu_H\) (Theorem
7 of the present paper, via Haar's 1933 uniqueness theorem on the
homogeneous space \(S^2 = \mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)\)), with the
Compton wavelength \(\lambda_C = h/(mc)\) setting the resolution scale
at which \(x_4\)-advance modes on the Sphere are counted. Any
coarse-graining of the Sphere --- a measurable projection to a subset of
distinguishable \(x_4\)-advance modes, or more generally a completely
positive (CP) unital normal map between wedge algebras generated by
McGucken Spheres at distinct events --- contracts the
Haar-measure-weighted mode distribution to a less-informative
distribution on the coarse-grained Sphere. The Uhlmann 1977 monotonicity
of the Araki relative entropy under CP unital normal maps is the
corresponding statement at the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\)
operator-algebraic level: coarse-graining the Sphere cannot increase the
state-distinguishability measured by the Araki relative entropy of
Theorem 22.3.9 Step 6. This is the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\)
data-processing inequality generalizing the Lindblad 1975 monotonicity
of the Umegaki relative entropy under CP maps on finite-dimensional
matrix algebras.

\textbf{Uhlmann's theorem (statement).} Let \(\mathcal{M}\) and
\(\mathcal{N}\) be von Neumann algebras, and let
\(\alpha : \mathcal{N} \to \mathcal{M}\) be a 2-positive unital normal
map (every completely positive unital normal map is 2-positive unital,
so this condition is weaker than complete positivity; the full-CP case
is the operationally relevant one in quantum information). Let
\(\varphi, \psi\) be faithful normal states on \(\mathcal{M}\) with
pullbacks \(\varphi \circ \alpha, \psi \circ \alpha\) on
\(\mathcal{N}\). Then
\[\boxed{\; S(\varphi \circ \alpha \,\|\, \psi \circ \alpha) \;\leq\; S(\varphi \,\|\, \psi).\;}\]
This is Uhlmann's theorem, from Uhlmann 1977, ``Relative entropy and the
Wigner--Yanase--Dyson--Lieb concavity in an interpolation theory,''
\emph{Commun. Math. Phys.} \textbf{54} (1), 21--32, Theorem 1.2.

\textbf{Theorem 22.3.10 (Uhlmann monotonicity derived from
\(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-Haar-measure contraction under coarse-graining of the
McGucken Sphere).} \emph{Under \(dx_4/dt = ic\), any CP unital normal
map \(\alpha : \mathcal{N} \to \mathcal{M}\) between wedge algebras
generated by McGucken Spheres at events \(q, p\) respectively induces a
measure-theoretic contraction
\(\alpha^* : \mathcal{P}(\Sigma_+(p)) \to \mathcal{P}(\Sigma_+(q))\) on
the respective \(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-Haar probability measures (where
\(\mathcal{P}(\Sigma)\) denotes the space of probability measures on
\(\Sigma\) absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mu_H\)). The
contraction is monotone-decreasing on the Araki relative entropy of
state-pairs:}
\[S(\varphi \circ \alpha \,\|\, \psi \circ \alpha) \;\leq\; S(\varphi \,\|\, \psi)\]
\emph{for all faithful normal state-pairs \(\varphi, \psi\) on
\(\mathcal{M}\). The equality holds iff \(\alpha\) is a sufficient
subalgebra inclusion in the Petz 1986 sense (Petz, ``Sufficient
subalgebras and the relative entropy of states of a von Neumann
algebra,'' Commun. Math. Phys. \textbf{105}, 123--131, Theorem 2.1),
equivalently iff the Sphere-level coarse-graining preserves all
distinguishability between \(\mu_H^\varphi\) and \(\mu_H^\psi\).}

\textbf{Proof of Theorem 22.3.10.} Four steps.

\emph{Step 1 (Stinespring dilation of the CP unital normal map).} Every
CP unital normal map \(\alpha : \mathcal{N} \to \mathcal{M}\) admits a
Stinespring dilation (Stinespring 1955, ``Positive functions on
\(C^*\)-algebras,'' \emph{Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{6}, 211--216,
Theorem 1): there exist a Hilbert space \(\mathcal{K}\), a bounded
isometry
\(V : \mathcal{H}_\mathcal{M} \to \mathcal{H}_\mathcal{N} \otimes \mathcal{K}\),
and a \(*\)-representation
\(\pi : \mathcal{N} \to B(\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{N} \otimes \mathcal{K})\)
such that
\[\alpha(a) = V^* \pi(a) V \quad \text{for all } a \in \mathcal{N}.\]
Under Theorem 22.3.9 (Step 1), both \(\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{M}\) and
\(\mathcal{H}_\mathcal{N}\) are Sphere-cogenerated Hilbert spaces for
the Spheres at events \(p\) and \(q\) respectively, so the Stinespring
isometry \(V\) corresponds to a measurable embedding of the
\(x_4\)-advance mode structure of \(\Sigma_+(p)\) into the enlarged mode
structure of \(\Sigma_+(q)\) coupled to an auxiliary Hilbert space
\(\mathcal{K}\) (the ``environment'\,' in quantum-information language).

\emph{Step 2 (\(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-Haar contraction on the Sphere level).}
The Haar measure \(\mu_H\) on \(\Sigma_+(p)\) is the unique
\(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-invariant probability measure on the two-sphere
\(S^2 = \mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)\) by Haar's 1933 uniqueness
theorem (Haar, ``Der Massbegriff in der Theorie der kontinuierlichen
Gruppen,'' \emph{Ann. of Math.} \textbf{34}, 147--169). For any
measurable map \(\pi : \Sigma_+(p) \to \Sigma_+(q)\) induced by the
Stinespring dilation of Step 1 (pushforward of \(x_4\)-advance modes
from \(p\) to \(q\) composed with the auxiliary coupling), the
pushforward measures \(\pi_* \mu_H^\varphi, \pi_* \mu_H^\psi\) on
\(\Sigma_+(q)\) (defined by
\(\pi_* \mu_H^\xi(E) = \mu_H^\xi(\pi^{-1}(E))\) for measurable
\(E \subset \Sigma_+(q)\)) satisfy the classical data-processing
inequality for the Kullback--Leibler divergence (standard
measure-theoretic result; cf.~Kullback 1959, \emph{Information Theory
and Statistics}, Chapter 2):
\[D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi_* \mu_H^\varphi \,\|\, \pi_* \mu_H^\psi) \;\leq\; D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu_H^\varphi \,\|\, \mu_H^\psi),\]
where \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu \| \nu) = \int \log(d\mu/d\nu) \, d\mu\) for
mutually absolutely continuous measures \(\mu, \nu\). The inequality is
strict unless \(\pi\) is injective modulo \(\mu_H^\varphi\)-null and
\(\mu_H^\psi\)-null sets. This is the Sphere-level contraction derived
from the Haar-measure structure of \(\Sigma_+(p)\) via
\(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-invariance.

\emph{Step 3 (Lifting from Sphere-level classical measure to Araki
operator-algebraic entropy via Uhlmann's interpolation argument).}
Uhlmann 1977 (\emph{Commun. Math. Phys.} \textbf{54}, 21--32) proves
monotonicity of the Araki relative entropy under 2-positive unital
normal maps via the interpolation-theory characterization of relative
entropy --- specifically, Uhlmann shows that the Araki relative entropy
\(S(\varphi\|\psi)\) equals the Wigner--Yanase--Dyson--Lieb concave
functional (Lieb 1973, ``Convex trace functions and the
Wigner--Yanase--Dyson conjecture,'' \emph{Advances in Mathematics}
\textbf{11}, 267--288) evaluated at the Connes cocycle derivative
\((D\varphi : D\psi)_t\) of the two states. The monotonicity under
2-positive unital normal maps \(\alpha\) then follows from the
Stinespring dilation (Step 1) combined with the concavity of the Lieb
functional and the monotonicity of the classical Kullback--Leibler
divergence under the pushforward of Step 2. Specifically, Uhlmann's
argument reduces the operator-algebraic monotonicity to the classical
measure-theoretic monotonicity by passing to the Connes cocycle
derivative and applying the Lieb concavity theorem. Under
\(dx_4/dt = ic\), the classical measure-theoretic monotonicity of Step 2
is the \(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-Haar-measure contraction on the Sphere, so
Uhlmann's interpolation argument lifts the Sphere-level contraction to
the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) Araki-entropy monotonicity on the wedge
algebra:
\[S(\varphi \circ \alpha \,\|\, \psi \circ \alpha) \;\leq\; S(\varphi \,\|\, \psi).\]

\emph{Step 4 (Equality case via Petz sufficiency).} Petz 1986
(\emph{Commun. Math. Phys.} \textbf{105}, 123--131, Theorem 2.1) proves
that equality
\(S(\varphi \circ \alpha \|\psi \circ \alpha) = S(\varphi\|\psi)\) holds
iff \(\alpha\) is a sufficient subalgebra inclusion in the sense that
there exists a CP unital map \(\beta : \mathcal{M} \to \mathcal{N}\)
with \(\alpha \circ \beta = \mathrm{id}_\mathcal{M}\) on both
\(\varphi\) and \(\psi\) (equivalently, \(\alpha\) is a \(\varphi\)- and
\(\psi\)-recovery map). Under \(dx_4/dt = ic\), Petz sufficiency
corresponds to Sphere-level reversibility: the Sphere-level
coarse-graining \(\pi\) of Step 2 preserves all distinguishability
between \(\mu_H^\varphi\) and \(\mu_H^\psi\) iff \(\pi\) is injective
modulo null sets, which iff the Sphere-level KL divergence is preserved
under pushforward. The equality case therefore holds iff the
Sphere-level coarse-graining is reversible on the states in question.
This completes the proof of Theorem 22.3.10. \(\blacksquare\)

\textbf{Corollary 22.3.A (Casini 2008 Bekenstein bound as a derived
theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) via Theorem 22.3.9).} \emph{Casini 2008
(Casini, ``Relative entropy and the Bekenstein bound,'' Class. Quantum
Grav. \textbf{25}, 205021) derives the Bekenstein bound on the entropy
of a localized excitation of radius \(R\) and energy \(E\) above the
vacuum,}
\[S(\rho_V) - S(\rho_V^0) \;\leq\; \mathrm{tr}(K \rho_V) - \mathrm{tr}(K \rho_V^0) \;=\; \lambda \, R \, E / (\hbar c),\]
\emph{with \(\lambda = \pi\) for ball-shaped regions (Casini 2008, Eqs.
(1) and (9)) and \(\lambda = 2\pi\) for the orthodox Bekenstein 1981
Rindler-wedge form,} \emph{from the non-negativity of the Araki relative
entropy applied to the excited state \(\varphi\) (density matrix
\(\rho_V\)) relative to the vacuum \(\omega\) (density matrix
\(\rho_V^0\)) on a ball of radius \(R\). Casini 2008 Eq. (17),
rearranged from \(S(\rho_V \| \rho_V^0) \geq 0\) (Araki 1977, Theorem
3.6(1)) on the ball-region algebra, gives}
\[S(\rho_V) - S(\rho_V^0) \;\leq\; \mathrm{tr}(K \rho_V) - \mathrm{tr}(K \rho_V^0),\]
\emph{with \(K = -\log\rho_V^0\) the vacuum modular Hamiltonian for the
ball. Casini's Eq. (9) gives \(K\) in closed form,}
\[K \;=\; 2\pi \int_0^R dr \int r^2 \, d\Omega \; \frac{R^2 - r^2}{2R} \; H(r,\theta,\phi,0),\]
\emph{with \(H\) the CFT energy density on the ball interior (Hislop and
Longo 1982, Commun. Math. Phys. \textbf{84} (1), 71--85, DOI
10.1007/BF01208372). Under Theorem 22.3.9, every object in the
inequality --- \(S(\rho_V\|\rho_V^0)\), \(\mathcal{M}(V)\), \(\omega\),
\(K\), and the Hislop--Longo form --- is derived from \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
via the Sphere-cogenerated standard form, so the Casini derivation is a
theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) through Theorem 22.3.9. This extends Theorem
15 of the present paper: Theorem 15 derives the horizon-area form
\(S_{BH} = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)\) by Planck-sphere tiling; Corollary 22.3.A
derives the Bekenstein inequality for localized excitations by
Araki-entropy positivity.}

\textbf{Corollary 22.3.B (Faulkner--Guica--Hartman--Myers--Van Raamsdonk
2014 linearized Einstein equations from the entanglement first law as a
derived theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) via Theorem 22.3.9).}
\emph{Faulkner, Guica, Hartman, Myers, and Van Raamsdonk 2014 (JHEP
\textbf{03}, 051) derive the linearized Einstein equations from the
first-law variation of the entanglement entropy on ball-shaped regions
in a holographic conformal field theory:}
\[\delta S_{\text{EE}}(V) = \delta \langle K_V \rangle,\] \emph{where
\(K_V\) is the modular Hamiltonian for the ball-region vacuum, combined
with the Ryu--Takayanagi 2006 formula (Ryu and Takayanagi, ``Holographic
derivation of entanglement entropy from AdS/CFT,'' Phys. Rev.~Lett.
\textbf{96}, 181602)
\(S_{\text{EE}}(V) = \mathrm{Area}(\tilde V)/(4 G_N)\) relating the
boundary-CFT entanglement entropy to the bulk-AdS extremal-surface area
\(\tilde V\) with \(G_N\) the bulk Newton constant. The combined
derivation yields the linearized Einstein equations at the bulk-AdS
level from the boundary-CFT entanglement structure. Under Theorem
22.3.9, the Araki-entropy modular-Hamiltonian expectation
\(\langle K_V \rangle\) and the first-law variation
\(\delta S_{\text{EE}}(V) = \delta \langle K_V \rangle\) are derived
from the Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra. Under Theorem 15 of the
present paper and the holographic restatement of Theorem 19.4
(Hilbert--Jacobson Agreement), the Ryu--Takayanagi formula
\(S_{\text{EE}} = A/(4G_N)\) is the holographic reading of Planck-sphere
tiling. The Faulkner--Guica--Hartman--Myers--Van Raamsdonk linearized
Einstein equations are therefore a derived theorem of \(dx_4/dt = ic\)
via Theorem 22.3.9 combined with Theorems 15 and 19.4. The full
non-linear extension (Faulkner, Haehl, Hijano, Parrikar, Rabideau, and
Van Raamsdonk 2017, ``Nonlinear gravity from entanglement in CFTs,''
JHEP \textbf{08}, 057) and the Jafferis--Lewkowycz--Maldacena--Suh 2016
result (Jafferis, Lewkowycz, Maldacena, and Suh, ``Relative entropy
equals bulk relative entropy,'' JHEP \textbf{06}, 004) stating that
boundary-CFT relative entropy equals bulk-AdS relative entropy under the
holographic duality lift to the McGucken \(dx_4/dt = ic\) framework in
the same way: both are statements about the Sphere-cogenerated Araki
relative entropy's behavior under the Sphere-level duality that
generates the AdS/CFT correspondence as a derived consequence
({[}MG-Minkowski-Hilbert, §V, holographic reduction of the
Sphere-cogenerated Haag--Kastler net{]}).}

\textbf{McGucken contribution here (§§22.3.9--22.3.10).} The two
subsections together establish the Araki--Uhlmann relative entropy as
derived from \(dx_4/dt = ic\) at the full type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\)
von-Neumann-algebra level, extending Theorem 22.3's four-corner
identification from the type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\) Umegaki setting cited at
reference {[}481{]} (Line B) and reference {[}476{]} (Line A) to the
algebraic-quantum-field-theory setting that horizons and wedges require.
Theorem 22.3.9 identifies: (i) the wedge algebra \(\mathcal{M}(W_R)\) as
a type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) factor on the Sphere-cogenerated Hilbert space
via Araki 1964 (free-field type-\(\mathrm{III}\)) refined to
type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) by Fredenhagen 1985 (asymptotic-scale-invariance
argument on the modular-operator spectra), with the universal structure
established by Buchholz--D'Antoni--Fredenhagen 1987; (ii) the
Reeh--Schlieder 1961 cyclic-separating vacuum as a derived consequence
of \(dx_4/dt = ic\) via the Wightman-axiom reconstruction of
{[}MG-Minkowski-Hilbert{]}; (iii) the Haagerup 1975 standard form
existence and uniqueness on the Sphere-cogenerated algebra; (iv) the
Bisognano--Wichmann 1975/1976 modular objects
\(\Delta_\Omega^{it} = U(\Lambda_{x^1}(-2\pi t))\) and
\(J = \Theta \cdot R_1(\pi)\) as the geometry of the wedge-vacuum
structure; (v) the modular conjugation \(J\) identified under the
McGucken-Wick coordinate identification \(\tau_W = x_4/c\) as the formal
single-Sphere PT reflection through the source event \(p\) --- the
operation that would swap \(\Sigma_+(p)\) and \(\Sigma_-(p)\) if
\(\Sigma_-(p)\) were present, with \(+ic\) excluding \(\Sigma_-(p)\)
geometrically; (vi) the modular flow \(\sigma_t^\Omega\) as Wick-rotated
\(x_4\)-translation at Unruh temperature \(T_U = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)\),
recovering the Connes--Rovelli 1994 Thermal Time Hypothesis of §28.6 as
derived structure; (vii) the Araki 1976/1977 relative entropy
\(S(\varphi\|\psi) = -\langle\Phi|\log\Delta_{\Psi|\Phi}|\Phi\rangle\)
on the Sphere-cogenerated wedge algebra, with type-\(\mathrm{I}_n\)
reduction to the Umegaki 1962 form of Theorem 22.3 Step 5. Theorem
22.3.10 derives: (i) the Uhlmann 1977 monotonicity
\(S(\varphi \circ \alpha \| \psi \circ \alpha) \leq S(\varphi \| \psi)\)
under CP unital normal maps as the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\)
data-processing inequality, via Stinespring 1955 dilation combined with
Haar 1933 \(\mathrm{SO}(3)\)-Haar-measure contraction on the Sphere and
Lieb 1973 Wigner--Yanase--Dyson--Lieb concavity; (ii) the Petz 1986
sufficiency equality condition as Sphere-level reversibility. Corollary
22.3.A derives the Casini 2008 Bekenstein bound from
Araki-relative-entropy non-negativity on ball-region algebras via the
Hislop--Longo 1982 explicit modular-Hamiltonian form. Corollary 22.3.B
derives the Faulkner--Guica--Hartman--Myers--Van Raamsdonk 2014
linearized Einstein equations from the entanglement first law combined
with Ryu--Takayanagi 2006 holographic restatement of Theorem 15 of the
present paper, with the full non-linear Faulkner et al.~2017 extension
and the Jafferis--Lewkowycz--Maldacena--Suh 2016 bulk-boundary
relative-entropy duality lifting via the same Sphere-cogenerated
standard-form apparatus. The complete apparatus of modular theory
(Tomita 1967 / Takesaki 1970, Araki 1973/1974/1976/1977, Uhlmann 1977,
Haagerup 1975, Petz 1986, Bisognano--Wichmann 1975/1976, Reeh--Schlieder
1961) and its holographic-gravity consequences (Casini 2008, FGHMV 2014,
JLMS 2016, FHHPVR 2017) are thereby identified as derived from
\(dx_4/dt = ic\) via the Sphere-cogenerated wedge-algebra standard form,
rather than imported from external operator-algebraic constructions. The
identification completes the type-\(\mathrm{III}_1\) extension that
Theorem 22.3's Line-B / Umegaki material required for applicability at
horizons and wedges where the finite-dimensional density-matrix
representation fails.

\hypertarget{appendix-e.-reading-the-mcgucken-principle-a-note-on-dxux2084dt-dxux2084dux3c4-and-the-photon-clarifying-common-reader-misconceptions}{%
\subsection{Appendix E. Reading the McGucken Principle: A Note on
dx₄/dt, dx₄/dτ, and the Photon --- Clarifying Common Reader
Misconceptions}\label{appendix-e.-reading-the-mcgucken-principle-a-note-on-dxux2084dt-dxux2084dux3c4-and-the-photon-clarifying-common-reader-misconceptions}}

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension \(x_4\) is
expanding at the velocity of light: \(dx_4/dt = ic\), with
\(x_4 = ict\), as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose
wavelength sets the action \(h\) and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

\emph{This appendix is reproduced from the flagship {[}29{]}, Appendix
A. Cross-references to the flagship's own chapters are given in square
brackets, and two clauses of Remark E.0.1 are adjusted in square
brackets to the statements of Lemma 7.1 and Theorem 7.11 as they stand
in the present paper (§3.1, §3.9). Everything else is as in the source.}

\textbf{About this appendix.} Readers arriving at the McGucken Principle
from a standard graduate-relativity background bring one deep habit: the
reflex to treat per-proper-time quantities as the ``physical'' or
``covariant'' ones, and per-coordinate-time quantities as
gauge-dependent bookkeeping. That habit points the wrong way here,
because the Principle is a statement about the manifold itself --- an
expansion happening at every event, at the same rate, regardless of
which worldline crosses that event. This appendix explains the four
distinct x₄-rate quantities the paper uses, states which one is the
Principle, and shows through five worked examples how photons, horizons,
twins, and GPS clocks all read naturally once the four quantities are
kept in their proper roles.

\textbf{E.0 The Physical Fact}

Every quantity, rule, and check in this appendix descends from one
physical fact:

\emph{The fourth dimension x₄ is expanding in a spherically symmetric
manner at the rate of c from every spacetime event, or dx₄/dt = ic.}

That is the McGucken Principle. Before any of its consequences are
unpacked, its status must be stated plainly, because it is the point on
which every reading in this appendix turns: dx₄/dt = ic is an
ontological claim --- a statement about what physically is --- and not a
coordinate convention, a formal device, or a notational choice. It
asserts that the fourth dimension is a real dimension that is really
expanding, at the rate c, from every event of spacetime, now. The
expansion is the physically primary fact; everything else in the paper
is a consequence of it. Minkowski spacetime is what the expansion looks
like after its rate is integrated into the coordinate x₄ = ict and
squared into the Lorentzian metric x₄² = −c²t²; Hilbert space is what
the same expansion looks like when its per-increment imaginary rate is
read as oscillation; the light cone is the locus the expanding wavefront
traces; the metric, the causal order, the Poincaré group, the Born rule,
and the Schrödinger equation are all downstream of the one expansion.
None of these is postulated independently. They descend, by the
derivations of the body, from the single physical fact that x₄ is
expanding at c.

This is the reversal the reader must hold onto throughout. Standard
physics takes Minkowski spacetime, or the Hilbert space, or the metric,
as a starting arena and builds upon it. Here the arena is not a starting
point but a result: the starting point is the physical expansion dx₄/dt
= ic, and the arena is what that expansion generates. When the appendix
below insists that dx₄/dt = ic is primary and the per-proper-time
quantities are constructed from it, this is what is meant --- not a
preference among equivalent formalisms, but a claim about which fact is
physically prior. The rate is prior; the worldlines that share in it,
the metric that its squaring produces, and the observers that read it
are all posterior.

The imaginary unit i in dx₄/dt = ic records the algebraic
perpendicularity of the x₄-axis to the three spatial axes on which the
expansion casts its projection. Its geometric realisation at each event
p is the McGucken Sphere M\_p⁺(t) --- the spherical wavefront of radius
ct swept out around p by the x₄-expansion. The Sphere is what
distinguishes the Principle from Minkowski's constant four-velocity norm
u\^{}μ u\_μ = −c²: the norm is a scalar constraint carrying no group
action and no measure, and it survives here as a theorem of the
Principle (the chain-rule pullback of the Sphere's expansion rate).

The Sphere carries structure that supplies the Born rule downstream by
five independent routes, established in the body of the paper {[}§3 of
the present paper{]} and consolidated here. The two most fundamental are
the Metric Route (the exponent 2 is the rank of the Minkowski metric
that x₄ = ict induces; Lemma 7.1) and the Haar Route (the Sphere's
transitive SO(3) action forces a unique invariant probability measure;
Lemma 7.1.5). That these derivationally-disjoint derivations return the
same Born density \textbar ψ\textbar² is an instance of the convergent
overdetermination catalogued in Remark 7.17 {[}and §17.5bis of
{[}29{]}{]}; see Remark E.0.1.

\textbf{Remark E.0.1 (Five independent derivations of the Born rule).}
The Born density P = \textbar ψ\textbar² is derived in this framework by
five routes that share no premises beyond the McGucken Sphere itself,
each proceeding from a distinct property of the one Sphere. They are
given here in order of priority, matching the catalogue of Remark 7.17.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{(\arabic{enumi})}
\item
  \emph{Metric Route --- the Sphere's metric rank (Lemma 7.1; Theorem
  7.2).} The x₄-flux density at a detection event is the metric pairing
  of the forward +ic advance with its conjugate −ic advance. The
  Minkowski metric induced by x₄ = ict is a rank-2 tensor, so the
  pairing is bilinear in (ψ, ψ*); {[}rank-4 quartic densities are
  excluded by the unitarity of the derived evolution, which conserves
  the L² norm alone (Lemma 7.1, §3.4),{]} and U(1) phase invariance,
  reality, non-negativity, and normalization then force P =
  \textbar ψ\textbar² uniquely. The exponent 2 is the rank of the
  metric. This is the most fundamental route, because the exponent is a
  property of the metric the Principle itself induces.
\item
  \emph{Haar Route --- the Sphere's symmetry group (Lemma 7.1.5).} The
  Sphere at the detection event is a round S² ≅ SO(3)/SO(2) carrying the
  transitive SO(3) action fixed by the isotropy of the x₄-expansion. By
  the uniqueness of the invariant measure on a homogeneous space of a
  compact group, there is exactly one SO(3)-invariant probability
  measure on the Sphere, the round measure dμ = sin θ dθ dϕ / (4π), and
  this is the Born weight over detection directions. This route answers
  why a probability measure exists at all: a measure is physically
  forced only where a symmetry singles it out uniquely, and SO(3)
  singles out exactly this one. Minkowski's norm u\^{}μ u\_μ = −c²
  carries no group action and therefore no such measure --- which is why
  the Sphere, not the bare norm, is what grounds quantum probability.
\item
  \emph{Norm Route --- the Sphere's sesquilinear inner product (Lemma
  7.6).} The rank-2 sesquilinear inner product satisfies the
  parallelogram identity as a two-line algebraic consequence, giving the
  L²-norm structure on Hilbert space ℋ with no Jordan--von Neumann
  theorem needed as upstream input.
\item
  \emph{Collision Route --- two physical Spheres (Theorem 7.7; Lemma
  7.7.5).} The number of physical participants in a head-on detection
  event is exactly two --- emitter Sphere and absorber Sphere --- and
  the coincidence {[}amplitude{]} is sesquilinear in the two amplitudes,
  with sum, max, min, and arithmetic/geometric/harmonic means excluded
  by action-additivity.
\item
  \emph{PT-Symmetry Route --- the Sphere's reflection (Theorem 7.11).}
  The Sphere's discrete PT\_E-symmetry through its source event gives
  ψ*(P) = ψ(PT\_E · P) {[}exactly for time-reversal-invariant
  wavefunctions, and conjugates the propagating kernel in general
  (Theorem 7.11 (ii)){]}, so the squaring in the Born density is the
  cascade-level expression of that symmetry, and complex conjugation
  itself is grounded in it.
\end{enumerate}

Routes (1) and (2) proceed respectively from the rank of the metric and
the symmetry group of the Sphere, and are foregrounded as the two most
important: the first fixes the exponent as the metric's rank, the second
supplies the invariant measure a probability rule requires. Routes
(3)--(5) confirm the same exponent from the norm, the physical collision
count, and the reflection symmetry. No route uses another's premise ---
rank 2, the SO(3) action, the parallelogram identity, the
two-participant count, and the PT-reflection are five logically
independent facts about the same Sphere --- so their agreement on P =
\textbar ψ\textbar² is genuine convergence, not one argument told five
times. This is the sense in which the Born rule is convergently
overdetermined by dx₄/dt = ic (Remark 7.17): one downstream fact fixed
by five upstream properties of the Sphere.

\textbf{E.1 The Four x₄-Rate Quantities}

The framework uses four related quantities associated with the fourth
dimension's advance. Each has its own symbol, its own domain of
definition, and its own interpretation, and they diverge on null
worldlines.

\textbf{(R1) The coordinate rate dx₄/dt = ic,} parameter: coordinate t;
range: fixed value ic; universal --- holds at every event. The
Principle. With the integrated shadow x₄ = ict, this rate holds
identically along every worldline --- timelike, null, accelerated, at
any gravitational potential --- because x₄ is a coordinate function of t
alone. Every statement about the universality of the expansion, its
metric-independence (GR T2), or its exception-freeness is a statement in
(R1).

\textbf{(R2) The Sphere-tangent velocity component v\_x₄ ≡ √(c² − v²)}
(the worldline's share of the x₄-expansion, per coordinate time);
parameter: coordinate t; range: {[}0, c{]}; worldline-dependent. A
bounded quantity {[}Lemma 5.1.3.2 of {[}29{]}{]}. The partition v² +
v\_x₄² = c² holds for every worldline, null ones included: at spatial
rest v\_x₄ = c; on a null worldline v = c gives v\_x₄ = 0. On timelike
worldlines, v\_x₄ coincides with the standard time-dilation-related
quantities of special relativity: v\_x₄ = c dτ/dt = c/γ for 0 ≤ v
\textless{} c.~The identity v\_x₄ = c dτ/dt is a theorem about v\_x₄ ---
τ appears as output, not as the differentiation parameter. At v = c (the
null limit) all three expressions give v\_x₄ = 0: the √(c² − v²) form by
direct substitution, the c dτ/dt form as the ratio c · 0 / dt with dτ =
0, and the c/γ form as the limit γ → ∞. The framework uses v\_x₄ as the
primary symbol because it is defined by direct substitution on the null
boundary. Statements about time dilation, the photon's x₄-rest, and
horizons live here.

\textbf{(R3) The Lorentzian temporal component u⁴ = dx₄/dτ = icγ;}
parameter: proper τ; unbounded, undefined on null worldlines; a
chain-rule consequence. Derived from (R1) by the chain rule {[}Theorem
5.1.2.8 of {[}29{]}{]}: dx₄/dτ = (dx₄/dt)(dt/dτ) = icγ. Its magnitude cγ
is unbounded as v → c, and on a null worldline (dτ = 0) the quantity is
undefined --- there the affinely-parametrised null tangent dx\^{}μ/dλ
replaces it {[}Lemma 7.2.2.1a of {[}29{]}{]}.

**(R4) The accumulated x₄-advance along γ, X₄{[}γ{]} ≡ ∫\_γ ic dτ =
icτ{[}γ{]};** a worldline functional, path-dependent. Distinct from the
coordinate x₄. Two worldlines sharing endpoints share Δx₄ = ic Δt but
generally differ in X₄. Along a null worldline X₄ is constant; around
any closed curve ∮ dx₄ = 0 identically. Statements about differential
aging (the twins) live in (R4). The bridge to (R2): dX₄ = ic dτ = i
v\_x₄ dt.

\textbf{E.2 Which One Is the Principle}

The Principle is dx₄/dt = ic: the coordinate-time reading (R1). Because
x₄ is a coordinate function of t alone, the rate dx₄/dt takes the same
value ic at every event --- an expanding photon-event, a horizon event,
an event on any accelerated worldline. The reading dx₄/dτ = ic is
available too, but only where dτ = dt: on a worldline at spatial rest,
the chain rule collapses and (R1) coincides with the value of (R3). This
is Lemma 4.7 {[}of {[}29{]}{]} (the rest-frame reverse-reading
equivalence), and the qualification dτ = dt is what makes it valid. On a
moving worldline the chain rule gives icγ; on a null worldline the
quantity does not exist. The coordinate-time reading is primary because
dx₄/dt = ic is a physical fact --- the expansion itself is prior to any
worldline, and dx₄/dt = ic records it directly.

\textbf{E.3 Reading the Photon, the Horizon, and the Time-Dilation
Formula}

\textbf{E.3.1 What is the photon's x₄-rate?} The photon's share in the
expansion is zero: v\_x₄ = 0 (the v = c limit of v² + v\_x₄² = c²),
obtained by direct substitution of v = c into v\_x₄ = √(c² − v²). The
reader may be tempted to write ``dx₄/dt = 0 for the photon'' or ``dx₄/dτ
= 0.'' Neither is available. The first is the coordinate rate (R1),
which is ic at every event including the photon's --- what vanishes is
the photon's share, not the expansion. The second is 0/0: proper time is
not defined for a photon (dτ = 0 pointwise). The correct statement is
the share v\_x₄ = 0, so X₄ does not accumulate, so the photon ages not
at all. The Principle continues to hold at every event the photon
crosses.

\textbf{E.3.2 What does ``the x₄-rate at the horizon'' mean?} The rate
is gravity-rigid: ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g\_μν = 0 (GR T2). The rate dx₄/dt = ic
takes the same value near the horizon as at infinity. What varies with
potential is the share: v\_x₄(r) = c dτ/dt = c√(1 − r\_s/r) (static
Schwarzschild observer), vanishing at r = r\_s. On the infaller's own
clock dτ = dt locally and Lemma 4.7 applies: the local rate is the full
ic throughout. Gravitational time dilation is the coordinate-frame
projection of a locally invariant rate.

\textbf{E.3.3 Which identity is ``c² through spacetime''?} Sphere
partition (per coordinate time, all worldlines): v² + v\_x₄² = c²,
bounded, locus a quarter-circle. Lorentzian four-velocity norm (per
proper time, massive worldlines): u\^{}μ u\_μ = \textbar dx₄/dτ\textbar²
− \textbar d\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}/dτ\textbar² = −c², unbounded in each term, signature
difference fixing the invariant. The Euclidean per-proper-time sum
\textbar dx₄/dτ\textbar² + \textbar d\ensuremath{\mathbf{x}}/dτ\textbar² equals c² only in the
instantaneous rest frame; elsewhere c²γ². Plus-sign identities belong to
(R2); minus-sign identities to (R3).

\textbf{E.3.4 How does the twin paradox read?} Coordinate accumulation
is path-independent: both twins accumulate Δx₄ = ic Δt. Differential
ageing is read from X₄ = ∫ ic dτ, advancing at real magnitude v\_x₄ per
unit coordinate time. On the traveling leg v\_x₄ \textless{} c, so the
traveler accumulates less X₄, so less proper time. The stay-at-home twin
retains v\_x₄ = c and accumulates the maximal X₄. The CTC question
closes the same way: ∮ dx₄ = 0 identically, so a CTC cannot run on the
coordinate; the impossibility lives in X₄.

\textbf{E.3.5 γ-projection and rapidity.} A boost is hyperbolic:
rapidity ϕ with cosh ϕ = γ. The Sphere-partition projection is circular:
Sphere angle θ with sin θ = v/c, cos θ = v\_x₄/c = 1/γ. Related by the
Gudermannian, θ = gd(ϕ), so cos θ = sech ϕ. The 1/γ projection is about
θ; unbounded component growth is about ϕ.

\textbf{E.4 Why Nothing of Relativity Is Lost}

The fourth dimension advances at the same rate at every event;
worldlines differ only in how much of that advance they share in.
Massive at rest shares fully (v\_x₄ = c); moving shares less (v\_x₄ =
√(c² − v²), clock slowed by the Lorentz factor); photon does not share
at all (v\_x₄ = 0, ageless, no X₄). Lorentz invariance survives entire
because the invariant content --- the norm u\^{}μ u\_μ = −c² and the
metric --- is a theorem of the Principle (the metric is the pullback of
the Euclidean form along x₄ = ict, the −c² from (ic)²). Lorentz
transformations preserve that derived metric; γ, time dilation, length
contraction, E = γmc², the null cone, and the mass-shell all come out
unchanged. The foliation quantities v\_x₄ and X₄ are additional
bookkeeping frame-anchored to the cosmic-comoving foliation (the CMB
rest frame); the Cloaking Theorem {[}Theorem 39 of {[}29{]}{]} explains
why local metrology cannot detect them. GR survives by the
invariant/deformable split: the rate is gravity-rigid; gravity deforms
the spatial sector. Time dilation, redshift, light bending, perihelion
advance, the horizon, and the field equations are recovered exactly. The
horizon is where the share is extinguished; the expansion does not stop.

\textbf{E.5 Worked Examples}

\textbf{E.5.1 The twin paradox.} Traveler at speed v for coordinate time
Δt. Coordinate accumulation: Δx₄ = ic Δt for both. Traveler's share:
v\_x₄ = c√(1 − v²/c²). Accumulated: ΔX₄\_trav = ic √(1 − v²/c²) Δt vs
ΔX₄\_stay = ic Δt. Differential aging: Δτ\_trav − Δτ\_stay = Δt(√(1 −
v²/c²) − 1) \textless{} 0: the traveler is younger by exactly the
Lorentz factor.

\textbf{E.5.2 GPS clock rate.} Satellite at radius r, speed v, mass M.
Principle: dx₄/dt = ic. Gravitational share: v\_x₄\^{}grav/c = √(1 −
2GM/rc²); kinematic factor √(1 − v²/c²). Total: v\_x₄\^{}sat/c ≈ 1 −
GM/(rc²) − v²/(2c²). Ground: ≈ 1 − GM/(R\_⊕ c²). Fractional difference ≈
GM(1/R\_⊕ − 1/r) − v²/(2c²), matching the +4.5 × 10⁻¹⁰ pre-launch offset
at r = 26,600 km, v = 3.87 km/s.

\textbf{E.5.3 Schwarzschild gravitational redshift.} Photon from r\_1 to
r\_2 \textgreater{} r\_1. Principle: dx₄/dt = ic. Local clock rate:
v\_x₄(r)/c = √(1 − r\_s/r). Frequency ratio ν\_2/ν\_1 = √((1 −
r\_s/r\_1)/(1 − r\_s/r\_2)); weak-field Δν/ν ≈ −GM(1/r\_2 − 1/r\_1)/c²,
matching Pound--Rebka 1959. Photon: v\_x₄ = 0 throughout, no X₄. The
redshift is about the clock rates at emitter and receiver, not the
photon.

\textbf{E.5.4 Hawking temperature.} At r = r\_s, local share v\_x₄(r) →
0. Surface gravity κ = c/(2r\_s); compactification circumference L\_H =
4π r\_s = cℏβ\_H; temperature T\_H = ℏc³/(8π GM k\_B). The expansion
does not stop at the horizon; the share is extinguished on the static
foliation, and compactification of the Euclidean-section x₄-axis at L\_H
produces the thermal spectrum (Theorem 12 Steps A--B; Appendix C).

\textbf{E.5.5 Bell's spaceship.} Rockets A, B at proper distance L\_0,
accelerating identically. Coordinate rate: dx₄/dt = ic. Share: v\_x₄(t)
= c√(1 − v(t)²/c²), decreasing. Accumulated: X₄\^{}A = X₄\^{}B, so both
age identically. Launch-frame separation constant L\_0; co-moving
separation L(t) = L\_0 c/v\_x₄(t), growing without bound. The string
breaks: the budget shifts into the spatial sector identically on each
rocket, so no differential ageing; the paradox lives in the
spatial-sector geometry, the string breaking as co-moving distance grows
as 1/v\_x₄.

\textbf{E.6 Anchor Table}

The definitions and results this appendix refers to are anchored as

at Lemma 7.6 (§3.3); the Collision Route at Theorem 7.7 and Lemma 7.7.5

temperatures as x₄-compactification at Theorems 12--13 and Appendix C.
In the flagship {[}29{]}: the four-quantity notation (R1)--(R4) at
Definition 5.1.3.4-ter (Chapter 5); the Sphere-tangent share partition
v² + v\_x₄² = c² at Lemma 5.1.3.2 (Chapter 5); the reverse-reading
equivalence (dx₄/dτ = ic on rest worldlines) at Lemma 4.7 (Introduction,
after Theorem 4); the McGucken--Wick coordinate identity τ\_W = x₄/c at
Theorem 4; the null-worldline replacement for u\^{}μ at Lemma 7.2.2.1a

gravity-rigidity of the rate ∂(dx₄/dt)/∂g\_μν = 0 at GR T2 (Chapter 5,
and {[}23{]}); the chain-rule identity u⁴ = icγ at Theorem 5.1.2.8
